anywaa: 'Ba kanya pootge ni ge poot cäänö ki gø, jic nyeya moa näk odïnö aput nicäär ni ge läädö na Amaan kïthge baŋ atïya mana jiiŋ Actherri.
english: And while they were yet talking with him, came the king's chamberlains, and hasted to bring Haman unto the banquet that Esther had prepared.

anywaa: Kanyøgø nyeya ka Amaan gena put ci kuna cämge ki gwanynyø ma Acther ri riet nïne.
english: So the king and Haman came to banquet with Esther the queen.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya enge bäät maath ki kwøk nyïïomøki, nyeya acäŋ köö jï gwanynyø ma Acther, ni «?Gïn manynyï agïnaŋøøni? Di cïbö jïrï. ?Ni pïëc marï agïnaŋø? Këël miï pëënynya thääŋ ŋøøm 'moa, owëëk ïïni.»
english: And the king said again unto Esther on the second day at the banquet of wine, What is thy petition, queen Esther? and it shall be granted thee: and what is thy request? and it shall be performed, even to the half of the kingdom.

anywaa: Køøre aløk gwanynyø ma Acther ni kööe, «Wui nyeya, ni näk aano jïtö ki met ec baŋï, ni beeye gïn mo beer ki jïrï, gïn manynya ki pïëc mara beeye en: Wëëk a kwøw ki jø tuuŋwa.
english: Then Esther the queen answered and said, If I have found favour in thy sight, O king, and if it please the king, let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request:

anywaa: Kiper aani ki jø tuuŋwa, waana ŋeew, nee wa raanynyi, nee wa 'näk, nee wïthwa dïïr. Doo na waano ŋeeø na laaŋe jaak, wa na mään ki cwøw, a doo lïŋö, ni bäŋ gïn caana. Doo na beeye per luummögø keere, ba doo rømø ki man ööla ïïni ki cäänö.»
english: For we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish. But if we had been sold for bondmen and bondwomen, I had held my tongue, although the enemy could not countervail the king's damage.

anywaa: Køøre nyeya ma Ayacewëëröc aköö jï gwanynyø ma Acther, ni «?Manøgø aŋa? ?Eni bëëde kaa? ?Aŋa na tïïc teeŋ gïnögø ni raac enø ki cwïnye?»
english: Then the king Ahasuerus answered and said unto Esther the queen, Who is he, and where is he, that durst presume in his heart to do so?

anywaa: 'Ba Acther aköö, ni «Beeye Amaan man en, nyimän marwa, ŋata raac na many man caar wa!» Køøre Amaan abwøk ni put dëëre nidïk nyïm nyeya ka Acther.
english: And Esther said, The adversary and enemy is this wicked Haman. Then Haman was afraid before the king and the queen.

anywaa: Ni ö nyeya ni päny maal ki gootø ki kanya mäthge yie ki kwøk nyïïomøki, ni ci ya ajïniina mar paan dwøŋ. 'Ba Amaan adööŋ ni kwaaya gwanynyø ma Acther kiper jwïëy moe, kiper ajoode ni da gïn mo leth mo tïïc nyeya tïïö dëëre.
english: And the king arising from the banquet of wine in his wrath went into the palace garden: and Haman stood up to make request for his life to Esther the queen; for he saw that there was evil determined against him by the king.

anywaa: 'Ba na duu nyeya ki ya ajïniina, ni duu kanya mäthge yie ki kwøk nyïïomøki, Amaan ajoode no opäth bäät pëëm mana näk Acther opï bääte. Køøre nyeya aköö, na «?Aŋø, nyeni manynya gø nee gwanynyø put gøø piny nyïma naa nut yi øtø kany kiree?» 'Ba kanya ö luubö manøgø wøk ki dhi nyeya, jø tïïc täärnyïm Amaan aputge uum.
english: Then the king returned out of the palace garden into the place of the banquet of wine; and Haman was fallen upon the bed whereon Esther was. Then said the king, Will he force the queen also before me in the house? As the word went out of the king's mouth, they covered Haman's face.

anywaa: Køøre dhaanhø aciel ki røk jic nyeya moa näk odïnö mo nyeŋŋe Arböna aköö, ni «Raŋï, Amaan da jaath man wø lïër dhaanhø bääte mo ocwöth piny paare, mo bär mare jïtö ki gööye ma pïërabïïc, mo ee tïïö kiper Mördekay nee lïër bäät gø, ŋata caan gïna beer na gwøk jwïëc nyeya.» Ni kö nyeya, «Lïëru bääte.»
english: And Harbona, one of the chamberlains, said before the king, Behold also, the gallows fifty cubits high, which Haman had made for Mordecai, who had spoken good for the king, standeth in the house of Haman. Then the king said, Hang him thereon.

anywaa: Ni putge Amaan lïër bäät jaadha jiiŋŋe kiper Mördekay. Køøre nyeya wëër mare adøø piny.
english: So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then was the king's wrath pacified.

anywaa: 'Ba yi cäŋ manøgø, nyeya ma Ayacewëëröc jammi bëët moa en jï Amaan, ŋata män ki jø Juuth, aput wëëk gwanynyø ma Acther. Ni ö Mördekay ni put ci nyïm nyeya, kiper acaan Actherri jï nyeya man näk Mördekay tuuŋge.
english: On that day did the king Ahasuerus give the house of Haman the Jews' enemy unto Esther the queen. And Mordecai came before the king; for Esther had told what he was unto her.

anywaa: Kanyøgø nyeya ogut lweedø mare man wø näk ree da ŋïï man wø gøø dëër wëëlö, na lwøre baŋ Amaan, akäl wøk ni wëëk gø Mördekay. Køøre Acther jammi moa näk mo Amaan bëët aput cïp cer Mördekay.
english: And the king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it unto Mordecai. And Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.

anywaa: Køøre Acther acäŋ cäänö ki nyeya, ni päth tiet gø ni jwöŋö ni kwaya gø, nee dee gïn mo tïïe ki man wec gïna raac na tuut Amaanni na käl ri tuuŋ Agaak, na näk ee cïp piny kiper jø Juuth.
english: And Esther spake yet again before the king, and fell down at his feet, and besought him with tears to put away the mischief of Haman the Agagite, and his device that he had devised against the Jews.

anywaa: Kanyøgø nyeya athøny warkey mare aput tïŋ maal baŋ Acther; ni Acther puta päny maal ni put cuŋŋö nyïm nyeya.
english: Then the king held out the golden sceptre toward Esther. So Esther arose, and stood before the king,

anywaa: Ni kööe, «Ni näk beeye gïn mo beer ki jïrï, ni aano jïtö ki met ec baŋï, ni beeye gïn ma adïëri ki baŋï, ni yiï omïnnö ki aani møn, beerra man göötï ki wëëlö mo raanynya weeli moa cïp Amaanni piny wär Amëdatha, na käl ri tuuŋ Agaak, na gööre kiper raany jø Juuth moa en tiet mïëri moï bëët.
english: And said, If it please the king, and if I have found favour in his sight, and the thing seem right before the king, and I be pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to reverse the letters devised by Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews which are in all the king's provinces:

anywaa: ?Kiper cwïnya omaa gø nidïï ki gïnögø ni raac enø noo päth bäät jø powa, wala cwïnya omaa gø nidïï ki man neena jø tuuŋwa ni di raanynyø?»
english: For how can I endure to see the evil that shall come unto my people? or how can I endure to see the destruction of my kindred?

anywaa: Køøre nyeya ma Ayacewëëröc aköö jï gwanynyø ma Acther ki Mördekay ŋat Juuth, ni «Raŋŋu, aani jammi bëët moa en jï Amaan anø cïba jï Acther, ni ö Amaanni ni lïëri bäät jaath kiper mana caar gïn mo raac ki man 'näk jø Juuth.
english: Then the king Ahasuerus said unto Esther the queen and to Mordecai the Jew, Behold, I have given Esther the house of Haman, and him they have hanged upon the gallows, because he laid his hand upon the Jews.

anywaa: Ennø, løny ki man göötu baŋ jø Juuth ki nyeŋŋa ki jöö mano raŋŋu ni beerra eni, ni gøøc weeli moøgø ko ogut lweedø mara man wø näk ree da ŋïï man wø gøø dëër wëëlö. Kiper weeli mo awaaci mana gøø piny na göör ki nyeŋŋa, no ogøø ko ogut lweedø mara man wø näk ree da ŋïï, ba løny ki man raanynyi këët.»
english: Write ye also for the Jews, as it liketh you, in the king's name, and seal it with the king's ring: for the writing which is written in the king's name, and sealed with the king's ring, may no man reverse.

anywaa: 'Ba kar kaagø, jø wø gööt piny mo nyeya aput cwøl ni nïr dwää adäk pïërariiø kurdäk, ni beeye dwääno cwøl ni Ciban, ni göörge weeli kaawat mana caan Mördekay, ni gööra baŋ jø Juuth, ki bwöthe, ki jø kööre, ki kwääri mo mïëri moa näk dïpa ki pïërariiø ka abïriiø, ki mana täge India këël Ithiöpia. Weeli moøgø göör ka yi jöör göör mar wï jur man nø, ni gööri baŋ jiy bëët ki køør dhøk marge. Ni gööri baŋ jø Juuth thuwø ki køør yi jöör göör marge ki dhøk marge.
english: Then were the king's scribes called at that time in the third month, that is, the month Sivan, on the three and twentieth day thereof; and it was written according to all that Mordecai commanded unto the Jews, and to the lieutenants, and the deputies and rulers of the provinces which are from India unto Ethiopia, an hundred twenty and seven provinces, unto every province according to the writing thereof, and unto every people after their language, and to the Jews according to their writing, and according to their language.

anywaa: Mördekay weeli moøgøøni gööre ka nyeŋ nyeya ma Ayacewëëröc, ni gøøc ge ko ogut lweedø mar nyeya man wø näk ree da ŋïï. Ni jääŋ weeli moøgø tiet mïëri ki jiy mo cäädhi ki bäät okwëënyi mo lääy mo wø rïïŋi døc moa näk opiidhø po nyeya.
english: And he wrote in the king Ahasuerus' name, and sealed it with the king's ring, and sent letters by posts on horseback, and riders on mules, camels, and young dromedaries:

anywaa: 'Ba weeli moøgø, nyeya cäänna jø Juuth moa en yïth päänye bëët ki man dwalge dëëtge nee jwïëcge koorge, kiper ni näk da jø tøŋ wala wï jur mør mo tuga geni, nee öge maal bäät jøøka nee raanyge, ni 'näkge ge, ni dïïrge wïth jøøka, ni kuurge ko obwöre ka apoole moge, ni twierge jap jøøka;
english: Wherein the king granted the Jews which were in every city to gather themselves together, and to stand for their life, to destroy, to slay, and to cause to perish, all the power of the people and province that would assault them, both little ones and women, and to take the spoil of them for a prey,

anywaa: ni gïnögø put ka tïïc yi cäŋ manø na aciel enø yïth mïëri bëët mo nyeya ma Ayacewëëröc, kanyo tïm nïr dwää apaar kurriiø na apaar kurdäk, dwääno cwøl na Adar.
english: Upon one day in all the provinces of king Ahasuerus, namely, upon the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar.

anywaa: 'Ba weeli mo awaaci agøø piny ni tïme na ciik ni ŋäc yïth mïëri moøgø bëët, kiper nee jø Juuth bëëtge ni dëëtge ege jiiŋŋø kiper nee kwöcge coolge dëët nyïïmän moge yi cäŋ manøgø.
english: The copy of the writing for a commandment to be given in every province was published unto all people, and that the Jews should be ready against that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.

anywaa: Kar kanyøgø jøøa jääŋŋi gena put aay ni ge rwäänhnhö ki køør dwør nyeya, ni aacge wøk ni ge cäädhi ka bäät okwëënyi mo lääy mo wø rïïŋi døc, moa näk opiidhø po nyeya. 'Ba awaaci manøgø ogøø piny thuwø yi pääny Cuca paan dwøŋ.
english: So the posts that rode upon mules and camels went out, being hastened and pressed on by the king's commandment. And the decree was given at Shushan the palace.

anywaa: Køøre Mördekay aput ö wøk ki baŋ nyeya no oruyö ka abïïn nyec mo kïte caala kït dïmuuy ni kwör møøk tar, ka abïï mo ee leeŋø mo cwääc ka waac lïïna mo mïërö ni kwör møøk näga dïmuur, ni wïïe okïthö ka adun warkey mo dwøŋ; ni bëët jø pääny Cuca ni ge kwöŋŋö ki met ec.
english: And Mordecai went out from the presence of the king in royal apparel of blue and white, and with a great crown of gold, and with a garment of fine linen and purple: and the city of Shushan rejoiced and was glad.

anywaa: 'Ba gïnögø atïmö ni beeye tar kiper jø Juuth, ni känne ki kanynyø ki met ec jïge, ni tïmge ni ge di wøørø.
english: The Jews had light, and gladness, and joy, and honour.

anywaa: Kanyøgø yïth mïëri bëët,  ki yïth päänye bëët kwöra näk dwør nyeya ka awaaci mare opïï yïthge, kanynyø ki met ec aput tägö yïthakic jø Juuth, ni tïïge ka ajwöma mo dwøŋ yi cäŋ manøgø. Køøre jø møøk mo thööth moa en dï mïëri dëëtge aløkge na jø Juuth, kiper gena lwäyö ki jø Juuth.
english: And in every province, and in every city, whithersoever the king's commandment and his decree came, the Jews had joy and gladness, a feast and a good day. And many of the people of the land became Jews; for the fear of the Jews fell upon them.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya tïme na dwää apaar kurriiø, dwääy mana cwøl na Adar, ni nïre apaar kurdäk, na näk beeye cäŋ mana ö awaaci mana caan nyeya na dee thur kare yie, ni beeye cäŋ mana ŋääth nyïïmän jø Juuthi nee jø Juuth dïïmge yie, cäŋ manøgø ree aput wiil ni tïme na cäŋ mana ö jø Juuthi ki dëëtge ni dïïmge jøøa män ki geni yie.
english: Now in the twelfth month, that is, the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the same, when the king's commandment and his decree drew near to be put in execution, in the day that the enemies of the Jews hoped to have power over them, (though it was turned to the contrary, that the Jews had rule over them that hated them;)

anywaa: Kanyøgø jø Juuth dëëtge adwalge yïth päänye moge moa en tiet mïëri bëët moa bëën nyeya ma Ayacewëëröc kiper nee jiy moa many tïïc gïn mo raac dëëtge nee päth ceŋge, ni bäŋe dhaanhø mo ocuŋŋö nyïmge, kiper jiy bëët alwäyö ki geni.
english: The Jews gathered themselves together in their cities throughout all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, to lay hand on such as sought their hurt: and no man could withstand them; for the fear of them fell upon all people.

anywaa: Këël jiy moa näk jïge da kööre bäät mïëri, ki kwääri, ki bwöthe, ki jø wø tïïc tïïe mo nyeya, jø Juuth aputge køny, kiper gena lwäyö ki Mördekay.
english: And all the rulers of the provinces, and the lieutenants, and the deputies, and officers of the king, helped the Jews; because the fear of Mordecai fell upon them.

anywaa: Kiper Mördekay kare atïmö ni dwøŋ po nyeya, ni put dööŋ kar mare wïnyö yïth mïëri bëët, ni ö teeki mare ni cääth nyïme.
english: For Mordecai was great in the king's house, and his fame went out throughout all the provinces: for this man Mordecai waxed greater and greater.

anywaa: Kanyøgø jø Juuth nyïïmän moge bëët aputge 'näk ko opëëlle, ni dïïrge wïth jøøgøøni, ni tïïcge mana manyge dëëtge.
english: Thus the Jews smote all their enemies with the stroke of the sword, and slaughter, and destruction, and did what they would unto those that hated them.

anywaa: 'Ba yi pääny Cuca paan dwøŋ, jø Juuth gena nääö ki cwøw mo jïtö ki dïpe abïïc; 7-10
english: And in Shushan the palace the Jews slew and destroyed five hundred men.

anywaa: ni 'näkge wäät Amaan moa näk apaar, ni beeye Amaan wär Amëdatha, ŋata män ki jø Juuth, ni wääte moøgø beege Parcandata, ki Dalpön, ki Acpata, ki Pörata, ka Adalia, ka Aridatha, ki Parmacta, ki Aricay, ka Ariday, ki Bayjata. 'Ba bäŋ twëër mo ege tïïö.
'Ba dïcäŋögø kiree, kwään jiy moa 'näk yi pääny Cuca paan dwøŋ aput caan jï nyeya.
english: On that day the number of those that were slain in Shushan the palace was brought before the king.

anywaa: Ni kö nyeya jï gwanynyø ma Acther, ni «Jø Juuth gena nääö ki cwøw ma dïpe abïïc yi pääny Cuca paan dwøŋ, ki wäät Amaan apaar. ?A ki yïth mïëri moa näk 'moa møga nø, bëëde nidïï? ?Ennø, gïn manynyï agïnaŋøøni? Di cïbö jïrï. ?Ni pïëc marï mør agïnaŋø? Di tïïö.»
english: And the king said unto Esther the queen, The Jews have slain and destroyed five hundred men in Shushan the palace, and the ten sons of Haman; what have they done in the rest of the king's provinces? now what is thy petition? and it shall be granted thee: or what is thy request further? and it shall be done.

anywaa: Køøre Acther aköö, «Wui nyeya, ni näk beeye gïn mo beer ki jïrï, teeŋ gïna tïïc jø Juuthi yi pääny Cuca dïcäŋi ki køør awaaci marï, doo tïïö thuwø diøø, ni lïër rïŋ dëët wäät Amaan moa näk apaar bäät jenni.»
english: Then said Esther, If it please the king, let it be granted to the Jews which are in Shushan to do to morrow also according unto this day's decree, and let Haman's ten sons be hanged upon the gallows.

anywaa: Ni put nyeya cïpö ki dwøl nee tïïc kaawat manøgø. Ni put awaaci gøø piny yi Cuca, ni lïër rïŋ dëët wäät Amaan moa näk apaar.
english: And the king commanded it so to be done: and the decree was given at Shushan; and they hanged Haman's ten sons.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya tïm dwääy mana cwøl na Adar ni nïre apaar kurŋween, jø Juuth moa en pääny Cuca dëëtge adwalge ni nääge ki cwøw ma dïpe adäk yi Cuca. 'Ba bäŋ twëër mo ege tïïö.
english: For the Jews that were in Shushan gathered themselves together on the fourteenth day also of the month Adar, and slew three hundred men at Shushan; but on the prey they laid not their hand.

anywaa: 'Ba jø Juuth møga moa en yïth mïëri moa bëën nyeya dëëtge adwalge kiper nee jwïëcge gwøkge, nee jïtge ki jwöm kiper gïïa doo tïïc nyïïmän moge dëëtge, ni nääge ki jiy ma kume ma pïërabïriiø kurbïïc. 'Ba bäŋ twëër mo ege tïïö.
english: But the other Jews that were in the king's provinces gathered themselves together, and stood for their lives, and had rest from their enemies, and slew of their foes seventy and five thousand, but they laid not their hands on the prey,

anywaa: Gïïögø atïïc ni dwääy man wø cwøl na Adar nïre apaar kurdäk. 'Ba na tïm nïr dwäänögø na apaar kurŋween dëëtge ajwömge, ni tïïcge cäŋ manøgø na cäŋ ajwöma, ni beeye cäŋ met ec.
english: On the thirteenth day of the month Adar; and on the fourteenth day of the same rested they, and made it a day of feasting and gladness.

anywaa: 'Ba jø Juuth moa en Cuca dëëtge adwalge ni nääge ki jiy ri nïr dwääy apaar kurdäk ka apaar kurŋween, ni jwömge dëëtge ni nïr dwääy apaar kurbïïc, ni tïïcge cäŋ manøgø na cäŋ ajwöma, ni beeye cäŋ met ec.
english: But the Jews that were at Shushan assembled together on the thirteenth day thereof, and on the fourteenth thereof; and on the fifteenth day of the same they rested, and made it a day of feasting and gladness.

anywaa: Kiper manøgønø, jø Juuth mo wø bëëdö yïth atude moa en wøk, dwääy man wø cwøl na Adar kany wø tïm nïre na apaar kurŋween wøørge wøørø cooth na cäŋ mar met ec, ni beeye cäŋ ajwöma, man cïpge ki muuce mo caammi jï nyïïawäätge.
english: Therefore the Jews of the villages, that dwelt in the unwalled towns, made the fourteenth day of the month Adar a day of gladness and feasting, and a good day, and of sending portions one to another.

anywaa: Køøre Mördekay luup moøgø amaa piny, ni gööte ki weeli baŋ jø Juuth bëët moa karge cään ki moa karge bäyö yïth mïëri moa bëën nyeya ma Ayacewëëröc.
english: And Mordecai wrote these things, and sent letters unto all the Jews that were in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, both nigh and far,

anywaa: Ni caana gø jïge ni kany wø näk yi cwiir cooth, kanyo tïm dwääy man wø cwøl na Adar, ki mano täge ni nïre apaar kurŋween këël apaar kurbïïc, cääŋŋe moøgø doo wøørø;
english: To stablish this among them, that they should keep the fourteenth day of the month Adar, and the fifteenth day of the same, yearly,

anywaa: kiper beege cääŋŋe moa ö jø Juuthi ni jïtge ki jwöm yie, kiper gïïa doo tïïc nyïïmän moge dëëtge akääŋö, ni beeye dwääna løk pänh cwïny marge yie na met ec, ni ö kïmmö ni løø ree baŋ kanynyø; nee cääŋŋe moøgø tïïcge na mo met ec man tïïge yïthge ka ajwöm-cam ki cïp muuce mo caammi jï nyïïawäätge, ki cïp muuce jï jøøa can.
english: As the days wherein the Jews rested from their enemies, and the month which was turned unto them from sorrow to joy, and from mourning into a good day: that they should make them days of feasting and joy, and of sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor.

anywaa: Kanyøgø jø Juuth luubö mana näk ege nø täk aputge kïth bäät tïïc ki køør mana göör Mördekay jïge.
english: And the Jews undertook to do as they had begun, and as Mordecai had written unto them;

anywaa: Kiper Amaan wär Amëdatha na käl ri tuuŋ Agaak, ŋata män ki jø Juuth bëët, ena tïïö ki riek waŋ bäät jø Juuth ki man dïïr wïthge, ni leeŋ gïn mo cwøl ni pur mo caala thöör war kiper nee wïth jø Juuth kiere ni dïïr wïthge.
english: Because Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had devised against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast Pur, that is, the lot, to consume them, and to destroy them;

anywaa: 'Ba kanya ö luumma raac na tuut Amaanni ki riek waŋ kiper jø Juuth na pïïe baŋ nyeya, weeli aput göör ki køør dwør nyeya nee gïna tïïc Amaanni nee døø bääte, nee eni ki wääte lïër.
english: But when Esther came before the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked device, which he devised against the Jews, should return upon his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.

anywaa: Kiper manøgønø, cääŋŋe moøgø aputge cwøl ni Purim ni käla ri nyeŋ gïna cwøl ni pur. 'Ba ki køør luubö mana göör Mördekay yi wëëlö, ki gïïa jootge, ki gïïa tägö dëëtge,
english: Wherefore they called these days Purim after the name of Pur. Therefore for all the words of this letter, and of that which they had seen concerning this matter, and which had come unto them,

anywaa: jø Juuth aput tïïö ki ciik kiper dëëtge, ki jø oööi køørge, ki jiy mo wø many dwätö ki geni, kiper cääŋŋe moøgø na ariiø yøø nee wø wøørge kanya no ocaanø ki yi cwiir cooth ki køør luubö mana näk ogöör piny;
english: The Jews ordained, and took upon them, and upon their seed, and upon all such as joined themselves unto them, so as it should not fail, that they would keep these two days according to their writing, and according to their appointed time every year;

anywaa: ni bëët cääŋŋe moøgø ni wïc ba wïl ki man wøør ge, ki yïth beenhnhe bëët, ki paac man nø, ki yïth mïëri bëët, ki yïth päänye bëët; ni bëët cääŋŋe mo Purim moøgø na gïï mo ge paaya wïthge cooth ki ge, nee tier gïna täk ajwöma manøgø kipere nee bëëde ni ŋäc ni ba ränynyi këët ki baŋ jø Juuth, këël jø oööi køørge.
english: And that these days should be remembered and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and that these days of Purim should not fail from among the Jews, nor the memorial of them perish from their seed.

anywaa: Køøre gwanynyø ma Acther nya Abikael, ki Mördekay ŋat Juuth, gena göödö ki wëëlö mør ki teek kwär mo dwøŋ døc, ni ge meeta luubö mana kwøŋ göör kiper Purim, nee bëëde kare.
english: Then Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew, wrote with all authority, to confirm this second letter of Purim.

anywaa: Ni jääŋ weeli ni caana dwør bëët-mëër ki bëët ŋäädhe jï jø Juuth bëët moa en yïth mïëri moa näk dïpa ki pïërariiø ka abïriiø mo nyeya ma Ayacewëëröc,
english: And he sent the letters unto all the Jews, to the hundred twenty and seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, with words of peace and truth,

anywaa: kiper nee cääŋŋe mo Purim cïp piny ni teek kanya no ocaanø, kaawat mana ö Mördekay ŋat Juuth ki gwanynyø ma Acther na cïpge gø piny kiperge; ni beeye mana nø cïpge piny kiper dëëtge thuwø, ki jø oööi køørge, ni da pwöc kiper cääŋŋe mo jø ba cämö yïthge ni jø jwöŋö.
english: To confirm these days of Purim in their times appointed, according as Mordecai the Jew and Esther the queen had enjoined them, and as they had decreed for themselves and for their seed, the matters of the fastings and their cry.

anywaa: 'Ba ki køør luubö mana caan Actherri, luup mo Purim acïp piny ni teek; ni puti göör piny yi wëëlö.
english: And the decree of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim; and it was written in the book.

anywaa: Kanyøgø nyeya ma Ayacewëëröc ajwäk aput tïïc bäät mïëri moe bëët moa karge cään këël moa karge bäyö.
english: And the king Ahasuerus laid a tribute upon the land, and upon the isles of the sea.

anywaa: 'Ba tïïe bëët moa tïïe ki køør nyec mare ki teek mare, ki luup bëët moa caan kiper dööŋ kar mar Mördekay, kanya cuum gø, ogöörö yi Wëël Waac Nyeye mo Mëdön ki Parca.
english: And all the acts of his power and of his might, and the declaration of the greatness of Mordecai, whereunto the king advanced him, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?

anywaa: Kiper Mördekay ŋat Juuth beeye na nyi nyïm nyeya ma Ayacewëëröc, ni kare dwøŋ yïthakic jø Juuth, ni bëëdö ni tuuŋge bëët yïthge met ki gø, ni beeye ŋata many bëënynyö mar jø poge, na cäänö kiper wï jur mare moo ööi køøre nee jïtge ki bëët-mëër.
english: For Mordecai the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people, and speaking peace to all his seed.

anywaa: 'Ba da dhaanhø mo obëëdö yi ŋööm Uc mo nyeŋŋe cwøl ni Jööp. 'Ba dhaanhø manøgø, ena dhaanhø mo bäŋ gïn mo ogwäyö ri bëëtö mare, mo bëëtö mare tiir, ni eni lwäär ki Jwøk, ni ree ee mänö ki gïï mo reyø.
english: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and eschewed evil.

anywaa: Eni jïre da wääte abïriiø ki nyïïe adäk ma nyïïakuue,
english: And there were born unto him seven sons and three daughters.

anywaa: ni jïre da dïëk ma rööm ma kume abïriiø, ka athïrööle ma kume adäk, ki dhää puur ma kuma aciel, ka arëëni ma dïpe abïïc, ki jø tïïc mo thööth døc. 'Ba ena dhaanhø mo kare dwøŋ døc yïthakic jiy bëët moa en jï løø kur tuul-cäŋ.
english: His substance also was seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she asses, and a very great household; so that this man was the greatest of all the men of the east.

anywaa: 'Ba wäät Jööp moa näk cwøw, ge wø tïïö ka ajwöm, ni tïïcge ni leeŋge leeŋŋø yïth mïëri moge, ni nyïïmiige moa näk nyïïakuue wø cwølge cwølø kar ajwöma nee cämge nee mäthge ki geni ciel.
english: And his sons went and feasted in their houses, every one his day; and sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.

anywaa: 'Ba kanyo pööth nïr ajwöma, Jööp wø jääga baŋge nee dëëtge døøcge mo waany, ni ö Jööpi ni päny maal ka amöölla ni cïpe ko olämme mo wø waaŋ bäre ki nyeŋ nyïïe bëët, kiper ena cädö ni kööe, «Kanymør obwöre 'moa geno tïïö ki raay ni janyge Jwøk ki yïth cwïnyge.» 'Ba manøgø beeye bëëtö mar Jööp cooth.
english: And it was so, when the days of their feasting were gone about, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all: for Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.

anywaa: 'Ba dïcäŋ aciel nyïïatwiet maal gena ö kuna cuŋge nyïm Wuuö Jwøk, ni ö Ceethan thuwø ni ööe ki geni ciel.
english: Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them.

anywaa: Ni kö Wuuö Jwøki jï Ceethan, ni «?Ï kälï kaa ŋø cøøn?» Køøre aløk Ceethan jï Wuuö Jwøk, ni kööe, na «A käla kuna wïra bäät piny bäre ni jøøya gøøni.»
english: And the Lord said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? Then Satan answered the Lord, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.

anywaa: Køøre Wuuö Jwøk aköö jï Ceethan, ni «?Dhaanhnha ma Jööp ajootï? Eni, ena dhaanhø mo bäŋ ŋat mo caala gø bäät piny; ena dhaanhø mo bäŋ gïn mo ogwäyö ri bëëtö mare, mo bëëtö mare tiir, ni eni lwäär ki Jwøk, ni ree ee mänö ki gïï mo reyø.»
english: And the Lord said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil?

anywaa: 'Ba aløk Ceethanni ni kööe, «?Aŋø, Jööp Jwøk lwääre ka gïn mo bäŋ tiere jaak?
english: Then Satan answered the Lord, and said, Doth Job fear God for nought?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, paa kiper na bëëde ni eni, ki jø paare, ki jap paare bëët iï koorø jïre? Japa tïïe ki cere bëët iï gwïëdhö jïre, ni put pïïth lääc paaci moe nyaay yi ŋööm paac bäre.
english: Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side? thou hast blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.

anywaa: 'Ba ennø, tïŋ cerï maal bäät jape mø, ni raanynyï ge bëët, niï ba put janynyø täärnyïmï kiree.»
english: But put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.

anywaa: Køøre Wuuö Jwøk aköö jï Ceethan, «Wøp nø, jammi moe bëët ena cerï, 'ba kär dee gïn gutï ri dëëre.» Ni ö Ceethan ni aae nyïm Wuuö Jwøk.
english: And the Lord said unto Satan, Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand. So Satan went forth from the presence of the Lord.

anywaa: 'Ba dïcäŋ aciel, ni wäät Jööp ki nyïïe moa näk nyïïakuue ge ena bäät cam ni ge mädhö ki køøŋ nyïïomøki po cöökge mana dwøŋ,
english: And there was a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house:

anywaa: ŋat tïïc aciel aöö ni kööe jï Jööp, ni «Kanya bëëde ni dhäk purö yi pwödhö, na arëëni ge ena kar kwaath,
english: And there came a messenger unto Job, and said, The oxen were plowing, and the asses feeding beside them:

anywaa: jø Caaba gena öö ni twierge geni, ni putge jø tïïc 'näk ko opëëllö; 'ba bee aani keera na bøth kiper nee caana jïrï.»
english: And the Sabeans fell upon them, and took them away; yea, they have slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.

anywaa: 'Ba ni nyenøgø poot cäänö, ŋat tïïc mør acäŋ öö, ni kööe, ni «Maac mar Jwøk apänhnhö ki maal ni waaŋ dïëk moa näk rööm, ki jø tïïc, ni thöör geni; 'ba bee aani keera na bøth kiper nee caana jïrï.»
english: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The fire of God is fallen from heaven, and hath burned up the sheep, and the servants, and consumed them; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.

anywaa: 'Ba ni nyenøgø poot cäänö, ŋat tïïc mør acäŋ öö, ni kööe, ni «Jø Kaldia gena öö ni pääŋge dëëtge na dhøgi adäk, ni twierge athïrööle, ni putge jø tïïc 'näk ko opëëllö; 'ba bee aani keera na bøth kiper nee caana jïrï.»
english: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The Chaldeans made out three bands, and fell upon the camels, and have carried them away, yea, and slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.

anywaa: 'Ba ni nyenøgø poot cäänö, ŋat tïïc mør acäŋ öö, ni kööe, ni «Wäätï ki nyïïï ni ge ena po cöökge mana dwøŋ ni ge cämö ni ge mädhö,
english: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, Thy sons and thy daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house:

anywaa: jamø mo teek døc akwönnö ki dïpaap ni cwöba røk, ni gøøc tuk øtø karge ŋweeni, ni put päth bäätge ni thøwge; 'ba bee aani keera na bøth kiper nee caana jïrï.»
english: And, behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and smote the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men, and they are dead; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.

anywaa: Kanyøgø Jööp aput ö maal ni jeeya abïïne, ni gwäär jïëye wøk. Køøre Jööp dëëre aleeŋ piny yïth ŋøøm, ni wøør Jwøk,
english: Then Job arose, and rent his mantle, and shaved his head, and fell down upon the ground, and worshipped,

anywaa: ni kööe, «Aana ö wøk ki yi mera ni bäŋ gïrpiny jïra; aano døøk ni bäŋ gïrpiny jïra. Gena cïp Wuuö Jwøki jïra ni cäŋ ge lwørrø; kiper manøgønø, pwøc en ri nyeŋ Wuuö Jwøk.»
english: And said, Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.

anywaa: 'Ba ki yïth gïïögø bëët na leth na tägö, Jööp kär bääyö ri Jwøk, ni käre gø jäälö.
english: In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.

anywaa: 'Ba da dïcäŋ mør thuwø mo nyïïatwiet maal geno ö kuna cuŋge nyïm Wuuö Jwøk, ni ö Ceethan thuwø ni ööe ki geni na aciel nee cuŋŋe nyïme.
english: Again there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them to present himself before the Lord.

anywaa: Kanyøgø Wuuö Jwøk aköö jï Ceethan, ni «?Ï kälï kaa ŋø cøøn?» Køøre aløk Ceethanni jï Wuuö Jwøk, ni kööe, na «A käla kuna wïra bäät piny bäre ni jøøya gøøni.»
english: And the Lord said unto Satan, From whence comest thou? And Satan answered the Lord, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.

anywaa: Køøre Wuuö Jwøk aköö jï Ceethan, ni «?Dhaanhnha ma Jööp ajootï? Eni, ena dhaanhø mo bäŋ ŋat mo caala gø bäät piny; ena dhaanhø mo bäŋ gïn mo ogwäyö ri bëëtö mare, mo bëëtö mare tiir, ni eni lwäär ki Jwøk, ni ree ee mänö ki gïï mo reyø. 'Ba këël na bëëdï niï tuuŋŋa aani bääte kiper nee eni raanynya ki gïn mo bäŋ tiere, eni poot bëëdö ra adïëri mare.»
english: And the Lord said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil? and still he holdeth fast his integrity, although thou movedst me against him, to destroy him without cause.

anywaa: 'Ba aløk Ceethanni ni kööe, ni «Ŋati man nø jwøra gïno pïï dëëre. 'Ba dhaanhø løny jïre ki man cïp jap kwøwe bëët kiper jwïëye.
english: And Satan answered the Lord, and said, Skin for skin, yea, all that a man hath will he give for his life.

anywaa: 'Ba ni näk mo cerï iï tïŋ maal bääte, ni ö rïŋ dëëre ki cuu moe ni jïte ki täw, ka adïëri møn, ï pute ka janynyø täärnyïmï kiree.»
english: But put forth thine hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will curse thee to thy face.

anywaa: Køøre Wuuö Jwøk aköö jï Ceethan, «Wøp, tïïc gïna manynyï jaak dëëre, 'ba jwïëye keere kär gutï.»
english: And the Lord said unto Satan, Behold, he is in thine hand; but save his life.

anywaa: Kanyøgø Ceethan aay nyïm Wuuö Jwøk, ni kïth dëër Jööp ka ajøra mo dwøŋ døc, ni beeye ki mana täge ki thäny tiete këël dï wïïe.
english: So went Satan forth from the presence of the Lord, and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown.

anywaa: Køøre Jööp alwötö ka abat nee dëëre gøønynye ki gø, ni eno pï piny yi bur.
english: And he took him a potsherd to scrape himself withal; and he sat down among the ashes.

anywaa: 'Ba cïïe aköö jïre, na «?Aŋø ni poot bëëdï ra adïëri marï en? Jaany Jwøk nø; ni thøwï!»
english: Then said his wife unto him, Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die.

anywaa: 'Ba aløøe jï cïïe ni kööe, ni «Ïïni, ï cäänö kaamar dhaagø ma bøøl. ?Aŋø, ø doo bëëdö ni ø joota gïn mo beer keere ki baŋ Jwøk, ni bäŋ gïn mo raac?» 'Ba ki yïth japøgø bëët, Jööp kär bääyö ki yïth luup moe bëët moa caane.
english: But he said unto her, Thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh. What? shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips.

anywaa: 'Ba nyïïawäät Jööp ma adäk, ni beege Elipath nyï Tëman, ki Bildat nyï Cuua, ki Cöpar nyï Nayma, kanya wïnyge gïïa leth bëët na tägö dëër Jööp, gena cïp piny ki cäŋ man røømge yie nee cige kuna cømge cwïny Jööp.
english: Now when Job's three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place; Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite: for they had made an appointment together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya cige na lwiithge gø ni karge poot bäär, eni kärge ŋiiø, ni putge tägö ko oduuru ni döötge ege tïŋ maal døc; ni jeecge abïïe moge, ni jøøpge tør wïthge ki pänh cwïny.
english: And when they lifted up their eyes afar off, and knew him not, they lifted up their voice, and wept; and they rent every one his mantle, and sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven.

anywaa: Køøre gena put pï piny yïth ŋøøm ki eni ciel ki nïne abïriiø ki wärre abïriiø. 'Ba bäŋ dhaanhø aciel dëëtge mo dhee ee tuuö ki eni, kiper bëëtö mana jootge na leth na en yie.
english: So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great.

anywaa: 'Ba køør gïnögø, Jööp dhee ajabe ni cien dïcäŋ mana lwaarø yie ki gø.
english: After this opened Job his mouth, and cursed his day.

anywaa: Ni kööe,
english: And Job spake, and said,

anywaa: ni «Beerra man ö dïcäŋŋi mana lwaarø yie ki aani ni ränynye, ge ki wäär mana cään jiyi yie kipera, ni ‹Nyilaar dïcwøø alwaarø ki gø!›
english: Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived.

anywaa: Beerra man ö dïcäŋŋi manøgø ni tïme na muudhö, ni ö Jwøki ni en maal ni bäŋe gïn caare kiper gø; beerra man bäŋe tar mo rieny bääte.
english: Let that day be darkness; let not God regard it from above, neither let the light shine upon it.

anywaa: Beerra man mayi ya muudhö ki lwøc mo cøl; beerra man rïëpi ya pöölö; beerra man ö dïcäŋögø ni wëëgi ya muunhnhögø lwär.
english: Let darkness and the shadow of death stain it; let a cloud dwell upon it; let the blackness of the day terrify it.

anywaa: Beerra man ö wäärri manøgø ni mayi ya muudhö mo cøl døc; beerra man ba mïn yie ki man dwali røk nïne mo cwiir, ni dööŋe wøk ni bäŋ kwäänne ki røk nïr dwäde.
english: As for that night, let darkness seize upon it; let it not be joined unto the days of the year, let it not come into the number of the months.

anywaa: Ka adïëri møn, beerra man ö wäärri manøgø ni dööŋe ni bäŋ gïrpiny yie; beerra man tïme ni bäŋ dwør met ec mo wïnynyi yie.
english: Lo, let that night be solitary, let no joyful voice come therein.

anywaa: Beerra man ö jø wø ceen cääŋŋe ni cienge dïcäŋ manøgø; ni beege jøøa näk rege ege jiiŋŋø ki man wëëkge lään wø cwøl ni Lëëwatan ööny maal.
english: Let them curse it that curse the day, who are ready to raise up their mourning.

anywaa: Beerra man ö ceerri mo amöölla mar dïcäŋögø ni tïmge ni cøl; beerra man ö eni ni koor tar mar dïcäŋ ni ba joot gø, ni ö eni ni ba joot tiet-cäŋ ka amöölla;
english: Let the stars of the twilight thereof be dark; let it look for light, but have none; neither let it see the dawning of the day:

anywaa: kiper eni mera käre mänö ki man lwaare ki aani, ni käre japa leth gëëŋö ki aani nee ba jooda ki nyeŋŋa.
english: Because it shut not up the doors of my mother's womb, nor hid sorrow from mine eyes.

anywaa: «?Aŋø ni ba puta thøø en kanya lwaarø ki aani, ni beeye kanya ööa wøk ki yi mera kiree?
english: Why died I not from the womb? why did I not give up the ghost when I came out of the belly?

anywaa: ?Aperŋø na cïp a käw ni pïr aani, ni wëëk aani dhøødhø ki thunh mera?
english: Why did the knees prevent me? or why the breasts that I should suck?

anywaa: Kiper doo na aano thøw, dee na aano butö ni aano nikïïl en; ni aano butö ni raa yaa jwömö,
english: For now should I have lain still and been quiet, I should have slept: then had I been at rest,

anywaa: kaamar nyeye ki jøøa wïthge leer na käär mïëri na gëën dëëtge ki päänye moi no oränynyö dïcäŋi en.
english: With kings and counsellors of the earth, which built desolate places for themselves;

anywaa: Aani doo na rewa ewa jwömö na aciel en ki kwääri moa näk jïge da warkie, na näk uudi moge ege pääŋö ki gwet-bïrö.
english: Or with princes that had gold, who filled their houses with silver:

anywaa: ?Wui, aŋø ni ba bwönna wøk en ki yi mera ni kan aani yi bwörö kaamar nyilaal mo tac cäŋ käre joodø na bäre?
english: Or as an hidden untimely birth I had not been; as infants which never saw light.

anywaa: Yi bwörö kaace, jøøa reyø japa reyø na wara tïïcge ba tïïcge këët; ni ö jøøa wara bëëdö no oööl ki tïïc ni jïtge ki jwöm.
english: There the wicked cease from troubling; and there the weary be at rest.

anywaa: Jiy moa no otwöö ge bëët, ge dööŋ wøk tier tööc, ni bëëtge ni bäŋ dwør kwäärö mo wïnyge bäätge këët mo köömma geni ki tïïc.
english: There the prisoners rest together; they hear not the voice of the oppressor.

anywaa: Jøøa kwörge therø ki moa kwörge døøŋŋø ge ena yi bwörö, ni laŋŋø bëëdö no opädö ni bäŋ teek kwääye bääte.
english: The small and great are there; and the servant is free from his master.

anywaa: «?Aperŋø na cïp tar jï jø wø en yïth gïï mo leth, ni wëëk jiy kwøw moa näk kïmmö ki yïth cwïnyge?
english: Wherefore is light given to him that is in misery, and life unto the bitter in soul;

anywaa: Ni beege jø wø bëëdö ni køya thøø, 'ba thøø ba ööi; ni wø cac thøø døc ni kaala man wø cac jap kwärö mo okoony piny,
english: Which long for death, but it cometh not; and dig for it more than for hid treasures;

anywaa: jøøa näk mïn ec marge ki kanynyø jootge ka kanyo pïïcge yi bwörö.
english: Which rejoice exceedingly, and are glad, when they can find the grave?

anywaa: ?Aperŋø na cïp kwøw jï dhaanhø mo jööre orwäänyö, mo jööre odëët Jwøki en?
english: Why is light given to a man whose way is hid, and whom God hath hedged in?

anywaa: Kiper kïmmö atïmö na cam mara;  ni bëët dwør cooyø mara ni lwör kaamar pïï.
english: For my sighing cometh before I eat, and my roarings are poured out like the waters.

anywaa: Gïna lwäära ki gø aö bääta; gïna naa lwäär ki gø døc apänh bääta.
english: For the thing which I greatly feared is come upon me, and that which I was afraid of is come unto me.

anywaa: Aani bäŋ bëëtö mo beer ki bëët jwöm jïra; aani bäŋ jwöm jïra møn, 'ba beege jwør gïï mo leth keerge.»
english: I was not in safety, neither had I rest, neither was I quiet; yet trouble came.

anywaa: Køøre aløk Elipathi nyï Tëman jïre ni kööe,
english: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said,

anywaa: ni «?Ni näk da dhaanhø mo mak cwïnye ni cääne ki ïïni, yiï ränynyö ki gø? ?'Ba aŋa ni løny jïre ki man bëëde ni lïŋö ni ba cäänö?
english: If we assay to commune with thee, wilt thou be grieved? but who can withhold himself from speaking?

anywaa: Ka adïëri møn, jiy mo thööth apwönynyï, ni wëëgï bäädi moa no onilway tëënnö.
english: Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands.

anywaa: Jiy moa näk bøømmø, dëëtge awëëgï tëënnö ki luup moï, ni wëëgï cøŋŋi moa no jöönyö nithïk.
english: Thy words have upholden him that was falling, and thou hast strengthened the feeble knees.

anywaa: 'Ba ennø, gïï mo leth aläw öö bäätï, ni put yiï ränynyö, ni pïïcge dëërï, ni put cwïnyï bwøk.
english: But now it is come upon thee, and thou faintest; it toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, lwär marï ki Jwøk paa beeye cøm cwïny jïrï, ni ö bëëtö marï na tiir ni näk ŋäädhe marï?
english: Is not this thy fear, thy confidence, thy hope, and the uprightness of thy ways?

anywaa: «Raŋï døc mø; ?aŋø, da ŋat mo bëëdö ki bëëtö mo beer ni rwäänye? ?Aŋø, da ŋat mo bëëdö ki bëëtö mo tiir ni ränynye na bäre?
english: Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished, being innocent? or where were the righteous cut off?

anywaa: 'Ba mana ŋääa, jø wø bëëdö ni ge puura raay, ki jø wø bëëdö ni ge piitha gïï mo reyø, nyïï gø kacge kaaø.
english: Even as I have seen, they that plow iniquity, and sow wickedness, reap the same.

anywaa: Geni, ge di raany jamø mano ö wøk ki dhi Jwøk, ni thøwge ki wëër mare ni wø liel kaamar maac.
english: By the blast of God they perish, and by the breath of his nostrils are they consumed.

anywaa: Ŋuuwe ge märö ni ŋärge, 'ba lak ŋuuwe moa teek otøyi.
english: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, and the teeth of the young lions, are broken.

anywaa: Ŋuu thøw kiper mana käre jïtö ki cam, ni ö nyïï ŋuuwe moa thenh thenh ni keethge.
english: The old lion perisheth for lack of prey, and the stout lion's whelps are scattered abroad.

anywaa: «Da luubö maa caan jïra no omooŋø, ni beeye luubö mo mooŋa ïtha.
english: Now a thing was secretly brought to me, and mine ear received a little thereof.

anywaa: 'Ba ni aano butö døc ki niine mo dëëra kuua, aana lägö ki gïn mo cwïnya pärö ki gø,
english: In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falleth on men,

anywaa: ni ö lwärri ki dïkwany dëël mo dwøŋ ni ö bääta, ni put cuuwi 'moa tïmö ni nhønhnhi.
english: Fear came upon me, and trembling, which made all my bones to shake.

anywaa: Ni ö gïn mo keda jamø ni pöödhe ki täärnyïma, ni ö dëëra ni neejuk ki lwär.
english: Then a spirit passed before my face; the hair of my flesh stood up:

anywaa: Ni jooda gïnögø ni cuŋŋö, 'ba ba løny ki man ŋiia gø ni kööa ni bee gïn, 'ba gïnögø abëëdö ni cuŋŋö nyïma, ni wïnynya dwøl mo muuŋö mo köö,
english: It stood still, but I could not discern the form thereof: an image was before mine eyes, there was silence, and I heard a voice, saying,

anywaa: na ‹?Aŋø, løny jï dhaanhø ki man tïme ni bëëtö mare tiir ni kaala Jwøk? ?Eni løny jïre ki man tïme ni waany ni kaala ŋata cwääc gø?›
english: Shall mortal man be more just than God? shall a man be more pure than his maker?

anywaa: 'Ba ni näk Jwøk këël jø wø tïny gø ba ŋäädhe, ni eni wø jïtö ki gïï mo obaac nyïïatwieli moe,
english: Behold, he put no trust in his servants; and his angels he charged with folly:

anywaa: a tugi ki dhaanhø nø, ni bëëdö yi øtø mo tïïc ko odhöönh en, ni tiere kanya käl yie bee yi tør, ni bee gïn wø laar dweny kaamar alweela.
english: How much less in them that dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, which are crushed before the moth?

anywaa: 'Ba wø tïme na akiya amöölla ka abøøya, put gïn mørri ka nyath, ni thøøe na bäre bäre ni bäŋ ŋat mo caar wïïe ki gø.
english: They are destroyed from morning to evening: they perish for ever without any regarding it.

anywaa: ?Moøge paa beege teeŋ jøøa näk oduŋkaare moge oputh wøk ni putge thøø ni bäŋ leec wïc jïge?
english: Doth not their excellency which is in them go away? they die, even without wisdom.

anywaa: «Cwötï ennø mø. ?Da ŋat mo wïnynya dwørï? ?A nyïïatwiel maal mane nø noo göögï ree?
english: Call now, if there be any that will answer thee; and to which of the saints wilt thou turn?

anywaa: Kiper keec cwïny, dhaanhø mo wïïe ba leer nääe nääö, ni ö gootø ni 'näk dhaanhø ma acaaye thiinh.
english: For wrath killeth the foolish man, and envy slayeth the silly one.

anywaa: Aana jïtö ki dhaanhø mo wïïe ba leer, mo bëëtö mare cäätha maal ni beer, 'ba paare alaar cien.
english: I have seen the foolish taking root: but suddenly I cursed his habitation.

anywaa: Eni nyïïe bëëdö ni kär gwøø, ni geno caarø kar løøk, ni bäŋ ŋat mo cwak geni.
english: His children are far from safety, and they are crushed in the gate, neither is there any to deliver them.

anywaa: Caammi moe athöör jiyi moa no onäk käci, këël mana këët baŋ moa ciek yïth koodhi; ni ö jap kwärö moe ni thööri ya jøøa näk owär.
english: Whose harvest the hungry eateth up, and taketh it even out of the thorns, and the robber swalloweth up their substance.

anywaa: Kiper caannø ba ö wøk ka yi tør, ni jwør gïï mo leth ba tuya yïth ŋøøm;
english: Although affliction cometh not forth of the dust, neither doth trouble spring out of the ground;

anywaa: 'ba dhaanhø nyöönna jwør gïï mo leth kaawat man wø ö akaraaci mo otal wø gami ya maaci.
english: Yet man is born unto trouble, as the sparks fly upward.

anywaa: «'Ba ki baŋa, beeye man manynya Jwøk; aani luubö mara cïba nyïm Jwøk,
english: I would seek unto God, and unto God would I commit my cause:

anywaa: ŋat wø tïïc gïï mo ec thäŋŋö ki ge mo tietge ba løny ki kwany, ni beege gïï mo rëëma ec mo ba thum ki kwaan.
english: Which doeth great things and unsearchable; marvellous things without number:

anywaa: Eni køth wø cïbe cïbö bäät piny, ni jääŋ pïï yïth pwöth.
english: Who giveth rain upon the earth, and sendeth waters upon the fields:

anywaa: Eni jøøa kwörge therø wø cïbe kwör mo døøŋŋø, ni ö jø wø kïmmi ni tïŋ ge maal nee bëëtge no ogwøø.
english: To set up on high those that be low; that those which mourn may be exalted to safety.

anywaa: Eni luup mo wø tuut jø wø nyeŋge reegø wø raanynye raanynyø, ni tïme ni bäŋ gïn mo thura kare këët ri tïïe moge.
english: He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform their enterprise.

anywaa: Eni jø wø ŋääth leec wïc marge keerge wø wëëge mak ka abïëp riek waŋ marge, ni ö japa tuutge ni laar tïmö ni bäŋ tietge.
english: He taketh the wise in their own craftiness: and the counsel of the froward is carried headlong.

anywaa: Muudhö wø nijïïm bäätge ko okaan cäŋ, ni thäämge ki dhöör cäŋ keda pinynya wäär.
english: They meet with darkness in the daytime, and grope in the noonday as in the night.

anywaa: Eni jiy moa many køny wø pieme piemø yïth luup riek waŋ mo jøøa reyø, ni piem jøøa can ceŋ jøøa teek.
english: But he saveth the poor from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty.

anywaa: Kiper manøgønø, jøøa can wø jïtö ki ŋäädhe, ni ö tïïe moa reyø ni cuŋge.
english: So the poor hath hope, and iniquity stoppeth her mouth.

anywaa: «Meta yi ŋat wø jook Jwøki; kiper manøgønø, kär pwöc Jwøk na en teeki jïre taagï.
english: Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth: therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty:

anywaa: Kiper eni dhaanhø wø kïthe yi gïn mo leth, 'ba eni cïpö ki cøm cwïny; ni kïth dëër dhaanhø ki ŋwiili, 'ba cäŋe ka wëëk caŋŋø ki ceŋŋe.
english: For he maketh sore, and bindeth up: he woundeth, and his hands make whole.

anywaa: Eni ï käle wøk ki yïth gïï mo leth mo pïï ra abïciel, 'ba këël doo pïï ri bïrietge bäŋ gïn mo leth mo gut ïïni.
english: He shall deliver thee in six troubles: yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee.

anywaa: Eni ï gwøe gwøø ki thøø cer käc, ni gwøk ïïni ki thøø ri leny.
english: In famine he shall redeem thee from death: and in war from the power of the sword.

anywaa: Ïïni ï dööŋ wøk ra ajäla mar dhøk, ni bëëdï niï ba lwäär kany wø täk gïï mo lethi.
english: Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue: neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh.

anywaa: Ïïno bëëdö niï ŋeethø bäät gïï mo leth ki kany wø näk ri käc, ni bëëdï niï ba lwäär ki lääc paap moa no owär.
english: At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh: neither shalt thou be afraid of the beasts of the earth.

anywaa: Kiper pwödhö marï otïmö ni bäŋ kïte yie,  ni ö lääc paapi ni bëëtge ki bëëtmëër ki ïïni.
english: For thou shalt be in league with the stones of the field: and the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee.

anywaa: Ïïno bëëdö ni iï ŋäädhö ki man näk mo kar bëëtö marï bëëdö no ogwøø, ni raŋï kaal marï ni bäŋ gïrpiny aciel mo orwäänyö yie.
english: And thou shalt know that thy tabernacle shall be in peace; and thou shalt visit thy habitation, and shalt not sin.

anywaa: Otïmö ni ŋäyï thuwø ki man näk miï jïtö ko obwöre mo thööth, ni tïm nyïïkwaayï kaamar luum mar bäät piny.
english: Thou shalt know also that thy seed shall be great, and thine offspring as the grass of the earth.

anywaa: Ïïno ci yi bwörö ni ïïno røm ki cwiiri kaawat man wø kac caammi ki yi caa marge mana näk kare.
english: Thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age, like as a shock of corn cometh in in his season.

anywaa: «Ka adïëri møn, luubö man anø raŋwa ni jootwa gø na adïëri; kiper manøgønø, wïnynyï, ni kwanyï tiere ï keerï.»
english: Lo this, we have searched it, so it is; hear it, and know thou it for thy good.

anywaa: Køøre aløk Jööpi ni kööe,
english: But Job answered and said,

anywaa: ni «Wui, pänh cwïny mara na dii rømø møn no okïth bäät gïr røm no odwalø ki gïïa leth moa tägö dëëra bëët,
english: Oh that my grief were thoroughly weighed, and my calamity laid in the balances together!

anywaa: peek marge doo tïmö ni kaala akwöö mo näpa døøŋŋø, ni beeye tiere ni bëëda ni dhaa cara dhwöle naa ba cädö na wøp en.
english: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the sea: therefore my words are swallowed up.

anywaa: Kiper athëëre mo Jwøk na en teeki jïre atïmö ni cööba aani, ni ö cïmmi marge ni ci dëëra. Gïna leth na kïth Jwøki bääta caala jø leny mo cööba aani.
english: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me, the poison whereof drinketh up my spirit: the terrors of God do set themselves in array against me.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, løny jï arëën paap ki man jwöŋe ki käc ni da luum jïre? ?Wala løny jï dhieŋ ki man jwöŋe ni jïre da cam?
english: Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? or loweth the ox over his fodder?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, cam mo bäth jaak di camø ni bäŋ acäbö ree? ?Wala løø tøŋ-gwienø mana tar wø jwør dhøki jwørø ni met?
english: Can that which is unsavoury be eaten without salt? or is there any taste in the white of an egg?

anywaa: Aani teeŋ caammi moøgø a kweer ki man guda ge; gena caammi maa män ki ge.
english: The things that my soul refused to touch are as my sorrowful meat.

anywaa: «Wui, gïna pëënynya thur kare wäne nø, nee gïna manynya cïp Jwøki jïra,
english: Oh that I might have my request; and that God would grant me the thing that I long for!

anywaa: nee jïëe ki man 'näk aani, ni ö eni ni wëëk cere leeŋ bääta ni thøøa!
english: Even that it would please God to destroy me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!

anywaa: 'Ba gïn mo poot cïpa cøm-cwïny jïra, këël ni bëëda naa ena yïth gïï mo leth døc en, aani, a kär kweer ki luup Jwøa en kur keere.
english: Then should I yet have comfort; yea, I would harden myself in sorrow: let him not spare; for I have not concealed the words of the Holy One.

anywaa: «?Aŋø, teek mara nyïëdi røk nø, mo doo løny jïra ki man kura? ?Aŋuun bëëtö mara en kaa këët nø, mo doo løny ki man maa cwïnya?
english: What is my strength, that I should hope? and what is mine end, that I should prolong my life?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, dëëra teek kaamar kïdi, ni rïŋ dëëra caala nywïënyö ma jwïël?
english: Is my strength the strength of stones? or is my flesh of brass?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, da teek jïra mo løny ki man kønya dëëra ki gø këët, ni gïna daa dëëra kønyø ki gø onø käl?
english: Is not my help in me? and is wisdom driven quite from me?

anywaa: «Ŋat mo kweer ki man nyooth mëër mare jï nyawati mo ena yi gïn mo leth, lwär man lwäärö ki Jwøa en teeki jïre ee wiiø.
english: To him that is afflicted pity should be shewed from his friend; but he forsaketh the fear of the Almighty.

anywaa: 'Ba u na nyïïawäädi 'moa, aana cøøgu kaamar nyeŋ näm mo cøøga jiy, mo kany wø manynyi nee öömmö yïthge ki pïï, ge di cwänö no otal.
english: My brethren have dealt deceitfully as a brook, and as the stream of brooks they pass away;

anywaa: Ni beege nyeŋ näm mo pïge rege cwödhö ki køør pey mo oløy yïthge.
english: Which are blackish by reason of the ice, and wherein the snow is hid:

anywaa: Kany wø bëëtge ni bäŋ pïï yïthge, ge bëëdö ni geno nikïïl; ni kany wäro tïme ni piny lïëth, ge dööŋ ni bäŋ gïrpiny yïthge.
english: What time they wax warm, they vanish: when it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.

anywaa: Jiy mo wø cäädhi ki bäät athïrööle, kany wø gakge nee ge jïtge ki pïï yïthge,  ge tïmö ni marge thääyö dïpaap jaak ni thøwge.
english: The paths of their way are turned aside; they go to nothing, and perish.

anywaa: Jø Tëma mo wø cäädhi ki bäät athïrööle gena määnyö, ni ö jøøa öö ki Cïïba ni öge ni ge ŋäätha ge.
english: The troops of Tema looked, the companies of Sheba waited for them.

anywaa: 'Ba yïthge acwat jaak ni gïna ŋääthge kärge joodø; gena ci yïth nyeŋ näpögø ni tïm gïna ŋääthge ni bäŋ tiere.
english: They were confounded because they had hoped; they came thither, and were ashamed.

anywaa: 'Ba ennø, uuna tïmö nou caala nyeŋ näpögø ki jïra; gïn mo di lwäyö ki gø ajootu ni putu lwäyö.
english: For now ye are nothing; ye see my casting down, and are afraid.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, aana cäänö cøøn na bëëde, ni ‹Cïpu jïra ki gïrpiny, ni mooyu aani røk jammi mou ki muuy man wø cïp ki piny,
english: Did I say, Bring unto me? or, Give a reward for me of your substance?

anywaa: ni piemmu aani ceŋ jiy mo wø män ki aani, ni kälu aani wøk ceŋ jiy mo wø caan aani›?
english: Or, Deliver me from the enemy's hand? or, Redeem me from the hand of the mighty?

anywaa: «Pwönynyu aani, aano bëëdö ni aano nikïïl, ni ööu ni nyoothu bëëtö mara jïra mana raac.
english: Teach me, and I will hold my tongue: and cause me to understand wherein I have erred.

anywaa: Wui, ateeŋ køny mo nyïëdi ni joot ki køør luup ma adïëri! ?'Ba agïnaŋø na duu cäänö maru?
english: How forcible are right words! but what doth your arguing reprove?

anywaa: ?U manynya gø nee luubö mana caana tiirru, ni you caarø ni luup mo ŋat mo bääte opädhö bäŋ tietge?
english: Do ye imagine to reprove words, and the speeches of one that is desperate, which are as wind?

anywaa: Uuni, uuna jiy mo løny ki man tïïu ki gïï mo reyø dëët obwöre moa näk kïïe ki køør ŋïïce mo wø tïïc ki ri kwääk ki baw, ni pïëmmu bäät gät nyïïawäädi mou nou gatha ge na laaŋe.
english: Yea, ye overwhelm the fatherless, and ye dig a pit for your friend.

anywaa: 'Ba ennø, beerra man raŋŋu jïra mø. ?Aŋø, a cäänö ki luup tööt nyïmmu?
english: Now therefore be content, look upon me; for it is evident unto you if I lie.

anywaa: Ennø, a caana jïïu nee ŋethu wiillu ni bäŋe gïn mo patha kare mo caannu këët. Weyu luupögø nø, kiper bëëtö mara poot bëëdö ni tiir kare.
english: Return, I pray you, let it not be iniquity; yea, return again, my righteousness is in it.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, aani a ŋäc cäänö ki luup mo patha kare? ?Aŋø, luup mo reyø ba daa ŋiiø a keera?
english: Is there iniquity in my tongue? cannot my taste discern perverse things?

anywaa: «?Aŋø, bëëtö mar dhaanhø bäät piny kany patha tïïc mo teek keere cøøn? ?Aŋø, nïr kwøw moe ba thööre ka tïïc mo teek kaamar ŋat mo tïïö ka gwel?
english: Is there not an appointed time to man upon earth? are not his days also like the days of an hireling?

anywaa: Kaawat man wø bëët dhaanhø ma laŋŋø ni lääŋŋa tïpö, wala ŋat tïïc mo køya gät tïïc mare,
english: As a servant earnestly desireth the shadow, and as an hireling looketh for the reward of his work:

anywaa: aana bëëdö ni da dwäde mo okwaan bääta ni gïna koora bäŋ tiere mo yaa joodø, 'ba beeye kïmmö ki yïth wärre keere na ŋøl bääta.
english: So am I made to possess months of vanity, and wearisome nights are appointed to me.

anywaa: 'Ba kany wø nyaaŋŋa dëëra piny, a cädö ni kööa, na ‹?A yi wäne nø noo ööa maal?› 'Ba yi wäär puta tïmö ni bäär, ni puta bëëtö naa løøŋŋa raa jaak këël kanyo ruu øwi.
english: When I lie down, I say, When shall I arise, and the night be gone? and I am full of tossings to and fro unto the dawning of the day.

anywaa: Tør bëëdö no omägö rïŋ dëëra bäre, ni jïte ki twöŋi, ni ö atwøti ni nigedheeth, ni bëët tuuti ni muulö jaak.
english: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; my skin is broken, and become loathsome.

anywaa: Nïr kwøw 'moa atïmö ni läädö døc ni kaala man wø läät cwääy abïï; nïr kwøw 'moa apïï ya aŋuudi ni bäŋ ŋäädhe kipere këët.
english: My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and are spent without hope.

anywaa: «Wui Jwøk! Par wïïï ki man näk kwøw mara beeye jam dhøk jaak, ni nyeŋŋa bäŋ gïn mo beer mo neenge këët.
english: O remember that my life is wind: mine eye shall no more see good.

anywaa: Jiy mo wø raŋ aani a ba cäŋge neennø këët; ïïni, a manynyï manynyø, 'ba a ba jootï këët.
english: The eye of him that hath seen me shall see me no more: thine eyes are upon me, and I am not.

anywaa: Kaawat man wø ö pööle wø neebay ni rwäänye, ŋat mo okïth yi bwörö, eni ba cäŋ duu wøk këët.
english: As the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away: so he that goeth down to the grave shall come up no more.

anywaa: Eni ba duu paare këët, eno tïmö ni kuc kanya bëëde yie.
english: He shall return no more to his house, neither shall his place know him any more.

anywaa: «Kiper manøgønø, aani a ba lïŋi; aani, a cäänö ni cwïnya opädhö ki pänh cwïny mar jwïëy 'moa, ni dwaalla ni cwïnya okëënynyö.
english: Therefore I will not refrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, aana naama dwøŋ, wala lääna dwøŋ ni wø bëëdö yi kut, ni bëëdï naa iï määnynyö ki ŋat koor en?
english: Am I a sea, or a whale, that thou settest a watch over me?

anywaa: Kany wø kööa ni pëëm mara cwïnya ocøme, ni ö kar niine mara ni tïïc ŋurö mara ni jööt,
english: When I say, My bed shall comfort me, my couch shall ease my complaint;

anywaa: a putï ka wëëk bwøk ki lääk mo teek, ni wëëgï aani lwär ki gïï wø neen ki yi wïc.
english: Then thou scarest me with dreams, and terrifiest me through visions:

anywaa: Kiper manøgønø, jwïëy 'moa, møt-dëël pute ka par, ni theemma thøø ki bëët dëël mara man.
english: So that my soul chooseth strangling, and death rather than my life.

anywaa: Aani, aana männö ki bëët kwøw mara, naa ba many bëëtö naa kwøw këët. Beerra man wec aani keera, kiper nïr kwøw 'moa caala jam dhøk.
english: I loathe it; I would not live alway: let me alone; for my days are vanity.

anywaa: «?Aperŋø ni bëët dhaanhe en ni kare iï tïïö ni dwøŋ ki baŋï, ï na Jwøk, ni bëëdï niï lääŋŋa gø en,
english: What is man, that thou shouldest magnify him? and that thou shouldest set thine heart upon him?

anywaa: ni eni raŋŋï raŋŋø ka amöölla cooth, niï bëëdö niï päänynya gø cooth?
english: And that thou shouldest visit him every morning, and try him every moment?

anywaa: ?Aŋø ni ba løøï waŋï wøk bääta en, wala ki man weyï aani ki nyi kany mo caala mwøny laaw?
english: How long wilt thou not depart from me, nor let me alone till I swallow down my spittle?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, ni näk mo aano bääyö, agïnaŋø na baaa dëërï, ï na dïkuri mar dhaanhø? ?Aperŋø ni bëëdï ni wïïï iï këël raa en, ni tïma kaamar tëër bäätï?
english: I have sinned; what shall I do unto thee, O thou preserver of men? why hast thou set me as a mark against thee, so that I am a burden to myself?

anywaa: ?Aperŋø ni ba weyï gïïa baaa en, ni wëënnï raay 'moa? Kiper ki kany mo cään a buta piny tiet ŋøøm; 'ba ïïni, aano manynyï, 'ba a tïmö naa tøør këët.»
english: And why dost thou not pardon my transgression, and take away mine iniquity? for now shall I sleep in the dust; and thou shalt seek me in the morning, but I shall not be.

anywaa: Køøre aløk Bildati nyï Cuua ni kööe,
english: Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,

anywaa: na «?A kany mo nyïëdi noo carï luupögø, noo tïm luupï moo ö wøk ki dhiï ni caala jamø mo teek?
english: How long wilt thou speak these things? and how long shall the words of thy mouth be like a strong wind?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, Jwøk luup wø ŋøle ŋølø no oköömmö, wala Jwøa en teeki jïre luubö mo tiir wëëge kööm?
english: Doth God pervert judgment? or doth the Almighty pervert justice?

anywaa: Ni näk mo obwöre moï obääyö dëëre, eni bääyö marge ee nø dwøk wïthge.
english: If thy children have sinned against him, and he have cast them away for their transgression;

anywaa: 'Ba ïïni, ni näk mo Jwøk iï manynyø, ni kwayï eni na en teeki jïre,
english: If thou wouldest seek unto God betimes, and make thy supplication to the Almighty;

anywaa: ni bëëtö marï beer ni tiir, ka adïëri møn, eni ree dee nyoodhø jïrï, ni dwøk bëëtö marï mana beer kare.
english: If thou wert pure and upright; surely now he would awake for thee, and make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous.

anywaa: Këël na bëëdï ni täk bëëtö marï nëëni ni thiinh, bëët yi nyïm marï døøye mo dwøŋ.
english: Though thy beginning was small, yet thy latter end should greatly increase.

anywaa: «Beerra man pëënynyï beenhnhe moa pöödhö, nee jammi moa kwany kwäcge nee caange jïrï nee ŋäyï.
english: For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers:

anywaa: Kiper øøna jiy mo ø nywøl ka awääre en, ni bäŋ gïn mo ŋääø døøc, ni nïr bëëtö marø bäät piny kany laara pöödhö kaamar tïpö.
english: (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days upon earth are a shadow:)

anywaa: ?Aŋø, ï ba pwönyge ni cäänge ïïni ki luup leec wïc ki køør kwänynyö marge?
english: Shall not they teach thee, and tell thee, and utter words out of their heart?

anywaa: «?Aŋø, otöök døøŋŋø ni bäär jaak kany mo otal? ?Løny jï obøw ki man tuue kany mo bäŋ naam yie?
english: Can the rush grow up without mire? can the flag grow without water?

anywaa: Geni kanyo pootge ni marge tuuö ni mar ni ge poot kär nyaarø, ge laara talø ni ränyge ni kaala lumme møga bëët.
english: Whilst it is yet in his greenness, and not cut down, it withereth before any other herb.

anywaa: Kaawat manøgønø, uutjïëthe mo jiy bëët moa näk wïthge owïl ki Jwøk, ki ŋäädhe mar ŋat mo tøør ri Jwøk, laara ränynyö.
english: So are the paths of all that forget God; and the hypocrite's hope shall perish:

anywaa: Eni ŋäätha gïn mo ba ruu, ni gööga ri gïn mo laara ränynyö kaamar øt-othïënhö.
english: Whose hope shall be cut off, and whose trust shall be a spider's web.

anywaa: Gïna caal øt-othïënhö wø ŋäädhe ŋäädhö, 'ba bäŋ wø cuŋŋi kare; ni mak gø ni teek, 'ba bäŋ wø bëëdö ki kany mo bäär.
english: He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand: he shall hold it fast, but it shall not endure.

anywaa: Eni bëëdö kaamar jaath mo oløth mo ena yi böön-cäŋ, mo bäädi moe olaak ya ajïniina bäre,
english: He is green before the sun, and his branch shooteth forth in his garden.

anywaa: ni lweedi moe tuya yïthakic kïte, ni ge rïïö ki karge yïth kïte.
english: His roots are wrapped about the heap, and seeth the place of stones.

anywaa: 'Ba kany wø näk mo eni di daa, kare oköö, ni ‹Ï kuua cøøn.›
english: If he destroy him from his place, then it shall deny him, saying, I have not seen thee.

anywaa: 'Ba ka adïëri møn, met ec mar jøøgø ba bëëdö ki kany mo bäär, 'ba jø møøk oööi ni läwge karge.
english: Behold, this is the joy of his way, and out of the earth shall others grow.

anywaa: «Ka adïëri møn, dhaanhø mo bëëdö ni bäŋ gïn jøøŋŋi ri bëëtö mare ba kwier Jwøki; ni Jwøk thuwø jiy mo wø tïïc gïïa reyø ba cwaae.
english: Behold, God will not cast away a perfect man, neither will he help the evil doers:

anywaa: 'Ba eni dhiï poot tïïe tïïö ni bëënna ŋeethø, ni wëëk ïïni kwöŋŋö ki met ec ki dhiï.
english: Till he fill thy mouth with laughing, and thy lips with rejoicing.

anywaa: Nyïïmän moï geno bëëdö ni geno rïëp lään wïci; ni ö kwör bëëte mo jøøa reyø ni tïmge ni bäŋgø këët.»
english: They that hate thee shall be clothed with shame; and the dwelling place of the wicked shall come to nought.

anywaa: 'Ba aløk Jööpi ni kööe,
english: Then Job answered and said,

anywaa: na «Adïëri møn, ŋääa ni manøgø bee gïn ma kare, ?'ba ennø, bëëtö mar dhaanhø tïme ni tiir nidïï nyïm Jwøk?
english: I know it is so of a truth: but how should man be just with God?

anywaa: Këël da dhaanhø mo manynya man pïëme ki gø, ki røk luupe ma kuma moo care, eni bäŋ aciel mo duue.
english: If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one of a thousand.

anywaa: Jwøk wïïe leer døc ni teek mare okadhø. ?Aŋa ni cäänö ki gø ni waŋe teek, ni bäŋ gïn mo tägi dëëre?
english: He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who hath hardened himself against him, and hath prospered?

anywaa: Eni kïte wø daae daaø ni bäŋ gïn mo ŋäcge, ni jaal geni ki wëër mare.
english: Which removeth the mountains, and they know not: which overturneth them in his anger.

anywaa: Eni tier piny di nëëŋö ni jäŋ gø, ni tïïc were mo gø ni kwanynyi.
english: Which shaketh the earth out of her place, and the pillars thereof tremble.

anywaa: Eni cäŋ wø di cäännö nee ba rienye, ni tïïc ceer nee ba cïpge ki tar.
english: Which commandeth the sun, and it riseth not; and sealeth up the stars.

anywaa: Eni keere maal apeere, ni bee eni ni wø cäädhi ki bäät athaŋ naama dwøŋ.
english: Which alone spreadeth out the heavens, and treadeth upon the waves of the sea.

anywaa: Bee eni na cwääc ceer mo wø cwøl ni liec ki ceer mo wø cwøl ni wäät-odäki, ki ceer mo wø cwøl ni joonni, ki ceer mo wø en jï løø tier piny.
english: Which maketh Arcturus, Orion, and Pleiades, and the chambers of the south.

anywaa: Eni wø tïïö ki gïï mo ec thäŋŋö ki ge mo tietge ba løny ki kwany, ni tïïe ki gïï mo rëëma ec mo ba thum ki kwaan.
english: Which doeth great things past finding out; yea, and wonders without number.

anywaa: Kany wø cur buuta, eni ba jooda, ni kany wø pöödhe, eni ba løny ki man ŋääa gø.
english: Lo, he goeth by me, and I see him not: he passeth on also, but I perceive him not.

anywaa: Kany wø juth gïrpiny, ?aŋa ni løny jïre ki man män gø,  na aŋa ni köö ki eni, na ‹Agïnaŋø ni tïïyï enø?›
english: Behold, he taketh away, who can hinder him? who will say unto him, What doest thou?

anywaa: «Jwøk wëër mare ba dwøk piny, ni jø wø ö maal bääte na no odwätö ki Reeyap opäth piny tiete.
english: If God will not withdraw his anger, the proud helpers do stoop under him.

anywaa: ?A aani nø, aana ŋa no dwöga baŋe en? Na a luupa ŋø ni løny jïra ki man caana gø jïre?
english: How much less shall I answer him, and choose out my words to reason with him?

anywaa: Këël na bëëda ni bëëtö mara tiir, a ba løny ki man dwöga baŋe, 'ba gïna daa tïïö bee ki man kwaa gø, eni ni wø ŋøl luumma, kiper nee bäth ec mare nyoodhe jïra.
english: Whom, though I were righteous, yet would I not answer, but I would make supplication to my judge.

anywaa: Këël daa cwølø nee duunne jïra, kära ŋäädhö ki man näk ïthe di ciiø ki luumma.
english: If I had called, and he had answered me; yet would I not believe that he had hearkened unto my voice.

anywaa: Eni, a wø tøye tøyø ki jamø mo teek, ni kïth dëëra ki ŋwiili mo thööth ki gïn mo bäŋ tiere.
english: For he breaketh me with a tempest, and multiplieth my wounds without cause.

anywaa: Eni a ba wëëk jwöm ki man jwïëa ki jamø, 'ba eni bëëdö ni caama aani ki gïï mo keec.
english: He will not suffer me to take my breath, but filleth me with bitterness.

anywaa: Ni näk mo gïn mo tïïc ka teek, teek mare dwøŋŋa eni. ?'Ba ni näk mo gïn mo tïïc ka løøk, aŋa noo cwøl eni kar løøk?
english: If I speak of strength, lo, he is strong: and if of judgment, who shall set me a time to plead?

anywaa: Këël na bëëda ni bëëtö mara tiir, dhøk mara a wø di jäälö. Këël na bëëda ni bäŋ gïn mo jøøŋŋi ri bëëtö mara, luup mo wø cara, raaya wø dige nyoodhø.
english: If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me: if I say, I am perfect, it shall also prove me perverse.

anywaa: «Këël na bëëda ni bäŋ gïn mo jøøŋŋi ri bëëtö mara, bäŋ gïn mo caana kiper dëëra, kiper bëëtö mara yaa taaø.
english: Though I were perfect, yet would I not know my soul: I would despise my life.

anywaa: Gïïögø röömi bëët, ni bee tiere na kööa, ni ‹Eni ŋata näk bäŋ gïn jøøŋŋi ri bëëtö mare, ki ŋata näk bëëtö mare raac, ge raanynye raanynyø na aciel bëët.›
english: This is one thing, therefore I said it, He destroyeth the perfect and the wicked.

anywaa: Kany wø dee thøø mo tägö ni cwöba røk dëët jøøa bëëtge beyø, eni wø ŋeethø bäät gïïa leth na jwørge.
english: If the scourge slay suddenly, he will laugh at the trial of the innocent.

anywaa: ?'Ba ni näk piny onø cïp ceŋ jø raay, ni dïŋut luup onø tïïc na cööye, ni näk mo patha eni na tïïc gø, ŋat mør aŋa?
english: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof; if not, where, and who is he?

anywaa: «Nïne 'moa atïmö ni läädö døc ni kaala ŋat ŋwïëy; gena laar pöödhö ni bäŋ met ec mo ege joodø.
english: Now my days are swifter than a post: they flee away, they see no good.

anywaa: Gena cäädhö ni jööt døc kaamar jää naam mo otïïö ka abääpa, ni neewïïw kaamar olwiith mo cwietha gïrpiny.
english: They are passed away as the swift ships: as the eagle that hasteth to the prey.

anywaa: Kany wø kööa ni wïïa wëëga wïlö ki gïïa leth, ni kööa ni cwïnya cøma cømø naa ŋeetha,
english: If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will leave off my heaviness, and comfort myself:

anywaa: a poot bëëdö naa lwäär kiper gïïo leth noo tägi dëëra, kiper ŋääa naa ba ŋunnï.
english: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that thou wilt not hold me innocent.

anywaa: Aani, luubö anø ŋøl bääta ni aano bääyö; ?aperŋø nø noo bëëda ni raa öölö ki ŋaap jaak en?
english: If I be wicked, why then labour I in vain?

anywaa: Këël mo dëëra yaa lwøø ki caabuun, ni lwøa ceŋŋa ki thöö nee tïmge ni waany,
english: If I wash myself with snow water, and make my hands never so clean;

anywaa: a poot leeŋï yi buur mo yie da gïï mo reyø, na abïïe 'moa dëëtge puta tïmö ni jeey ki aani.
english: Yet shalt thou plunge me in the ditch, and mine own clothes shall abhor me.

anywaa: «Kiper Jwøk patha dhaanhø kaamar aani mo løny ki man dwöga jïre,  nee wa ciwa kar løøk ni cäänwa yïthakicwa.
english: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, and we should come together in judgment.

anywaa: Wui, doo naa da dïŋut luup mo ci dïwa, ni dee cuŋŋö yïthakicwa bëët,
english: Neither is there any daysman betwixt us, that might lay his hand upon us both.

anywaa: ni daa jïtö ki dhaanhø mo tïŋa athøra mar Jwøk maal bääta, naa puta tïmö naa ba bööi ki køør mana lwäära ki gø,
english: Let him take his rod away from me, and let not his fear terrify me:

anywaa: køøre nø, a doo cäänö ki eni ni bäŋ lwär; 'ba ba løny ki man tïïa gïnögø ki teek mara.
english: Then would I speak, and not fear him; but it is not so with me.

anywaa: «Aani, aana männö ki bëët kwøw mara; kiper manøgønø, a bëëdö naa dwaalli jaak nø, ni cääna ki køør këëny cwïny mara.
english: My soul is weary of my life; I will leave my complaint upon myself; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.

anywaa: Aani caana caanø jï Jwøk ni kööa, ni ‹Kär aani jäälï, 'ba gïna kïthï bääta en caan tiere nee ŋääa.
english: I will say unto God, Do not condemn me; shew me wherefore thou contendest with me.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, beeye gïn mo beer jïrï ki man caannï aani, niï kwiera gïna tïïyï ki cerï, ni tïmï niï wëëga uutjïëthe mo jøøa reyø bëënynyö?
english: Is it good unto thee that thou shouldest oppress, that thou shouldest despise the work of thine hands, and shine upon the counsel of the wicked?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, nyeŋ mo dhaanhø dagø jïrï? ?Aŋø, ï rääŋö kaawat man wø räŋ dhaanhe?
english: Hast thou eyes of flesh? or seest thou as man seeth?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, nïr kwøw moï caala nïr kwøw mo dhaanhø, wala cwiic kwøw moï caala mo dhaanhø,
english: Are thy days as the days of man? are thy years as man's days,

anywaa: ni tïmï niï manynya bääyö mara keere en, niï caya raay 'moa?
english: That thou enquirest after mine iniquity, and searchest after my sin?

anywaa: Ïïni, ŋäyï ni bäŋ gïn mo yaa baa; ni bäŋ ŋat mo løny jïre ki man piem aani cerï.
english: Thou knowest that I am not wicked; and there is none that can deliver out of thine hand.

anywaa: « ‹Ceŋŋï beege na cwääc aani na tïïc aani. ?Aŋø, ennø ï cäŋa duu kuna raanynyï aani?
english: Thine hands have made me and fashioned me together round about; yet thou dost destroy me.

anywaa: Par wïïï mø, ïïni aana nø cwääyï ki ro odhöönh; ?aŋø, a cäŋï ka raanynyø naa cäŋa døø ri tør?
english: Remember, I beseech thee, that thou hast made me as the clay; and wilt thou bring me into dust again?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, a kärï thii yi mera kaamar caak, ni wëëgï dëëra mägö kaamar caak ma dïïle, ni tïma ni aana dhaanhø?
english: Hast thou not poured me out as milk, and curdled me like cheese?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, dëëra kärï rïëbö ki buyö ki rïŋö, ni wëëgï dëëra mak na aciel ki cuu ki läär?
english: Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh, and hast fenced me with bones and sinews.

anywaa: Bëët kwøw acïpï jïra, ni nyoothï mëëyï jïra ni wø ba jøøl, ni ö gööki marï ni koor jwïëya.
english: Thou hast granted me life and favour, and thy visitation hath preserved my spirit.

anywaa: « ‹'Ba gïïögø beege gïïa näk iï kan cwïnyï, ni ŋääa ni beege gïïa caarï kipera.
english: And these things hast thou hid in thine heart: I know that this is with thee.

anywaa: Ni näk mo aano tïïö ki raay, a diï joodø, ni ba diï a wiiø ki jääl ki køør bääyö mara.
english: If I sin, then thou markest me, and thou wilt not acquit me from mine iniquity.

anywaa: Wui, ni näk mo aano bääyö, otïmö ni leth jïra! 'Ba këël bëëtö mara doo tiir, wïïa ba daa tïŋ maal, kiper a ena yi laac wïc mo dwøŋ døc, naa raŋŋa gïna leth na ena yie.
english: If I be wicked, woe unto me; and if I be righteous, yet will I not lift up my head. I am full of confusion; therefore see thou mine affliction;

anywaa: Ni näk mo wïïa tïŋa maal, a diï dwarø kaawat man wø tïïc ŋuuwi, ni diï cäŋ teek marï nyoothø bääta.
english: For it increaseth. Thou huntest me as a fierce lion: and again thou shewest thyself marvellous upon me.

anywaa: Ïïna kännö ki luup møøk mo nyärö mo jääla aani, ni ö wëërri marï ni meet ree bääta; gïï mo leth awëëgï ööny bääta ni rege lwöbö.
english: Thou renewest thy witnesses against me, and increasest thine indignation upon me; changes and war are against me.

anywaa: « ‹?Aperŋø ni wëëgï aani nywöl wøk en?  Wui! doo beer ki mana daa thøw cøøn ni poot bäŋ waŋ mo oneen aani.
english: Wherefore then hast thou brought me forth out of the womb? Oh that I had given up the ghost, and no eye had seen me!

anywaa: Aŋø, kanya ööa wøk ki yi mera, daa put pööth yi bwörö ni keda a kär cwääö, doo beer!
english: I should have been as though I had not been; I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, nïra na nøk poot ba wëëgï thöör bääta nø? Wec aani nø naa jïta ki met ec mo thiinh,
english: Are not my days few? cease then, and let me alone, that I may take comfort a little,

anywaa: kanyo poode naa poot kär ci kanya näk bäŋ duun wøk yie, ni beeye kanya näk muudhö mo cøl døc,
english: Before I go whence I shall not return, even to the land of darkness and the shadow of death;

anywaa: kanya näk bëëdö na wäär ni näga muudhö, ni wïc ee kierø ni tar mare poot na muudhö.› »
english: A land of darkness, as darkness itself; and of the shadow of death, without any order, and where the light is as darkness.

anywaa: Køøre aløk Cöparri nyï Nayma ni kööe,
english: Then answered Zophar the Naamathite, and said,

anywaa: «?Aŋø, luup mo thööth di carø jaak ni ba dwøgi? ?Aŋø, ki man cäänö ki luup mo thööth, luup dhaanhø døøye mo beyø?
english: Should not the multitude of words be answered? and should a man full of talk be justified?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, luup moï na näk bäŋ tietge, jiy wëëge lïŋŋö? ?Aŋø, bäŋ dhaanhø mo jooga ïïni kany wø näk miï tïïö ka abuua?
english: Should thy lies make men hold their peace? and when thou mockest, shall no man make thee ashamed?

anywaa: Kiper ïïna köö, na ‹A cara gïï ma adïëri, ni bëëtö mara beer ki nyïm Jwøk.›
english: For thou hast said, My doctrine is pure, and I am clean in thine eyes.

anywaa: Wui, doo beer na di Jwøki cäännö, ni jap dhee ni jääl ïïni,
english: But oh that God would speak, and open his lips against thee;

anywaa: ni nyooth leec wïc jïrï mana näk tiere okanø; kiper leec wïc mana näk adïëri di joodø ki uutjïëthe ma teeŋi. 'Ba gïn wär ŋäyï: Jwøk ïïna jääle ka ajäla mo thiinhnha eni ki mana diï joodø.
english: And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is! Know therefore that God exacteth of thee less than thine iniquity deserveth.

anywaa: «?Aŋø, jap Jwøk moa näk tietge okanø løny ki man ŋäyï ge? ?Aŋø, eni na Jwøk na en teeki jïre, løny ki man ŋäyï tiet japa tïïe ki leec wïïe këël aŋuunne?
english: Canst thou by searching find out God? canst thou find out the Almighty unto perfection?

anywaa: Kiper gena gïï mo ena maal døc mo kwörge bäyö ni kaala jap maal. ?Aŋø, agïnaŋø ni løny ki tïïc jïrï? Geni, gena gïï mo ena piny kuya døc ni kaala kar bëët jwïëc jøøa no othøw. ?Aŋø, løny ki man ŋäyï ge?
english: It is as high as heaven; what canst thou do? deeper than hell; what canst thou know?

anywaa: Bär mar rumi marge kaala ŋøøm, ni ö dööŋ-eci marge ni kaal naama dwøŋ.
english: The measure thereof is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.

anywaa: «?Aŋø, ni näk mo Jwøk öö ni leeŋ ïïni øt twöc, ni ŋun bäätï ki luubö, aŋa noo män gø?
english: If he cut off, and shut up, or gather together, then who can hinder him?

anywaa: Kiper eni jø cwøk wø ŋääe ŋääö, ni kany wø joot gïn mo raac, ba wiie jaak ni bäŋ gïn caare kiper gø.
english: For he knoweth vain men: he seeth wickedness also; will he not then consider it?

anywaa: Ki man ö ŋat mo wïïe bäŋ acaara ni lëëny wïïe, jööta eni jï arëën-paap ki man lwaare ki dhaanhø.
english: For vain man would be wise, though man be born like a wild ass's colt.

anywaa: «Ni näk mo cwïnyï iï wëëk Jwøk, ni thaaŋï ceŋŋï jïre,
english: If thou prepare thine heart, and stretch out thine hands toward him;

anywaa: ni ö raayï moa en cerï ni leeŋï ge wøk, ni bäŋe raay mo jïëyï ki man duny kar bëëtö marï,
english: If iniquity be in thine hand, put it far away, and let not wickedness dwell in thy tabernacles.

anywaa: ïïni, ïïno bëëdö ni wïïï iï tïŋ maal ni bäŋ laac wïc, ni cuŋŋï niï teek ni bäŋ lwär.
english: For then shalt thou lift up thy face without spot; yea, thou shalt be stedfast, and shalt not fear:

anywaa: Ka adïëri møn, wïïï 'owïl ki gïna leth na jwørï, ni kwaanï gø kaamar pïï ni wø kwönni ni puta pöödhö.
english: Because thou shalt forget thy misery, and remember it as waters that pass away:

anywaa: Bëët kwøw marï orieny ni kaala dhöör-cäŋ, ni ö muudhö marï ni tïme kaamar amöölla.
