english: When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder:

anywaa: kar kanyaca leec wïc aneene ni kwaan bëëtö mar gø, ni këël tier gø piny, ni pääny gø.
english: Then did he see it, and declare it; he prepared it, yea, and searched it out.

anywaa: Køøre ena köö jï dhaanhø, ni ‹Ka adïëri møn, ki man lwäär Wuuö Jwøk beeye leec wïca eni; ni man kwier gïn mo raac beeye ŋäc tiet jammi eni.› »
english: And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding.

anywaa: 'Ba Jööp ena bëëdö ni poot cäänö ni kööe,
english: Moreover Job continued his parable, and said,

anywaa: na «Aŋø ni ba tïme keda a ena yïth nïne moa pöödhö en, kanya bëët Jwøki ni waŋe ena bääta,
english: Oh that I were as in months past, as in the days when God preserved me;

anywaa: ni lamba mare orieny bääta, ni yi muudhö caadha ka tar mare!
english: When his candle shined upon my head, and when by his light I walked through darkness;

anywaa: Nïne moøgø beege nïne moa beyø jïra, ni beeye kanya bëët Jwøki na nyawat mara ni koora kar bëëtö mara.
english: As I was in the days of my youth, when the secret of God was upon my tabernacle;

anywaa: Ni beeye kanya poot Jwøa en teeki jïre ni ena buuta, no obwöre 'moa ge bëëdö deŋŋa;
english: When the Almighty was yet with me, when my children were about me;

anywaa: kanya bëët waŋjöö mara ni thec ki caak, ni maaw bëëdö ni kwönna wøk jïra ki yi kïdi man wø biic nyïïjenni yie.
english: When I washed my steps with butter, and the rock poured me out rivers of oil;

anywaa: «'Ba kanya wara cøøa dhi kiir mar pääny, naa pïïa piny kar acooŋa ki dïbwöthe mo pääny,
english: When I went out to the gate through the city, when I prepared my seat in the street!

anywaa: obwöc cwøw a wø jootge joodø ni jämge aani ki kara, ni ö jø døøŋŋø ni öge maal ni cuŋge.
english: The young men saw me, and hid themselves: and the aged arose, and stood up.

anywaa: Kanyøgø dïbwöthe wø puta nidut, ni cïpge ceŋge dhøkge,
english: The princes refrained talking, and laid their hand on their mouth.

anywaa: ni ö kwääri ni micge dhøkge, ni dhäthge ki cäänö.
english: The nobles held their peace, and their tongue cleaved to the roof of their mouth.

anywaa: Kiper jiy moa wïny luumma aana pwøcge, ni ö jiyi moa joot aani ni køpge gïra.
english: When the ear heard me, then it blessed me; and when the eye saw me, it gave witness to me:

anywaa: Kiper aani jiy moa can ni wø many køny, ki kïïe moa näk bäŋ jø göökge rege gena kønya.
english: Because I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and him that had none to help him.

anywaa: Ŋata en um thøø aana gwïëthe, ni wëëga cwïny määr thuunhnhi mïnnö ni wärge ki dudi.
english: The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me: and I caused the widow's heart to sing for joy.

anywaa: Bëënynyö arøøa dëëra kaamar abïï, ni tïïa ŋøl luup ma kare kaamar aleeŋŋa ka abïï man wø loop wïc.
english: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me: my judgment was as a robe and a diadem.

anywaa: Aana bëëdö na waŋ kiper cööye, ni bëëda ni aana tielø kiper ŋööte.
english: I was eyes to the blind, and feet was I to the lame.

anywaa: Aana bëëdö na wuuö kiper jø wø many køny, ni bëëda naa cwaga wëëlle kar løøk.
english: I was a father to the poor: and the cause which I knew not I searched out.

anywaa: Lëëmmi mo jø raay atøya, ni ö cam mana en dhøkge ni käla gø wøk.
english: And I brake the jaws of the wicked, and plucked the spoil out of his teeth.

anywaa: «Aana cädö ni nïr kwøw 'moa thöönhnhö kaamar nyeŋ akwöö, ni thøøa ya abïla mara ki met ec.
english: Then I said, I shall die in my nest, and I shall multiply my days as the sand.

anywaa: Aana bëëdö kaamar jaath mo lweedi moe okar ni pïïcge yïth pïï, mo bääte bëëdö no oninør ki thööy ki yi wäär bäre.
english: My root was spread out by the waters, and the dew lay all night upon my branch.

anywaa: Wödö mara bëëdö ni nyään jïra cooth, ni ö teek dëëra ni bëëde ni nyään.
english: My glory was fresh in me, and my bow was renewed in my hand.

anywaa: «Jiy abëëdö ni ge wïnynya luumma ni ge raŋŋa jïra, ni ge wø bëëdö ni ge lïŋö ni ïthge wø cekge ciiø ki luup pwöc 'moa.
english: Unto me men gave ear, and waited, and kept silence at my counsel.

anywaa: Kany wø näk mo aano cäännö, ge ba cäänni køøra këët; luup 'moa putge ka wïnynyö na kare.
english: After my words they spake not again; and my speech dropped upon them.

anywaa: Gena bëëdö ni ge køya aani kaawat man wø koor køth, ni ge bëëdö ni dhøkge ege löö jïra kaawat man wø tïïc jiyi mo lääŋŋa køth.
english: And they waited for me as for the rain; and they opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain.

anywaa: Aani jïge wø raŋa raŋø ni met ec yaa nyoodhø jïge kany wø bëëtge ni cwïnyge opädhö, ni jïtge ki cøm cwïny kany wø raŋge täärnyïma ni leer.
english: If I laughed on them, they believed it not; and the light of my countenance they cast not down.

anywaa: Aana bëëdö ni aana bwödhi marge, ni jëënna geni ki jöör bëëtö man bëëtge ki gø. Aana bëëdö kaamar nyeya yïthakic jø leny, naa bëëdö naa caala ŋat wø cïpi ki cøm cwïny jï jø wø näk cwïnyge opädhö.
english: I chose out their way, and sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners.

anywaa: «'Ba ennø, jiy moa näk therø geni ki aani a wø buuge buuö, ni beege jøøa wëëkge kwiera ki man kønyge guu 'moa, nee pïïth dïëga koorge na aciel.
english: But now they that are younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I would have disdained to have set with the dogs of my flock.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, teek marge agïne ni dee duuö jïra, ni bäätge onø jöönyö?
english: Yea, whereto might the strength of their hands profit me, in whom old age was perished?

anywaa: Gena jiy mo odwat ki køør can ki käc. Geni, wø tïme na wäär, ge wø göönna wøk ki lweet jenni yïth ŋøøpa näk otal na en yi ŋöömma näk oränynyö.
english: For want and famine they were solitary; fleeing into the wilderness in former time desolate and waste.

anywaa: Jenni moa näk otuy dïtëën wø puthge wøk ni camge ge, ni tïm cam marge ni beege lweet jenni.
english: Who cut up mallows by the bushes, and juniper roots for their meat.

anywaa: Ge wø rïëma wøk ki yïthakic jiy, ni kwöŋ jøwi bäätge kede gena kuuwe.
english: They were driven forth from among men, (they cried after them as after a thief;)

anywaa: Gena cöör wøk nee bëëtge nyeŋ näm moa no otal, ki yïth agäp-kïte ki yïth buri.
english: To dwell in the cliffs of the valleys, in caves of the earth, and in the rocks.

anywaa: Ge bëëdö ni ge jwöŋö yïth atøge ni dëëtge ege diil tiet koodhi.
english: Among the bushes they brayed; under the nettles they were gathered together.

anywaa: Ge bëëdö ni gena bøøre ni gena jiy mo bäŋ nyeŋge, ni geno rïëm wøk ki yi ŋööm paac.
english: They were children of fools, yea, children of base men: they were viler than the earth.

anywaa: «'Ba ennø, nyeŋŋa ege kïth yi duut ni ge kwääk ka gø, ni nyeŋŋa ege tïïö ni beeye gïn wacge yïthakicge.
english: And now am I their song, yea, I am their byword.

anywaa: Geni ge män ki aani, ni ge bëëdö ni karge ege jädhö ki aani; ni nyeŋŋa ba wecge ki man ŋuutge gø ki laaw.
english: They abhor me, they flee far from me, and spare not to spit in my face.

anywaa: Kiper Jwøk thøør atum mara awëëk nilwak ni tïïc aani naa jääk, ni ö geni ni putge tïmö ni dëëtge ba mänge këët ki man buuge aani.
english: Because he hath loosed my cord, and afflicted me, they have also let loose the bridle before me.

anywaa: Ge wø öö ki bäät cwïïa ni gena lwaak ni tukge aani, ni cekge abïëp nyïma naa makge ki tieta; ni kunyge ki buri mo leny deŋŋa nee këëtge ki aani.
english: Upon my right hand rise the youth; they push away my feet, and they raise up against me the ways of their destruction.

anywaa: Geni waŋjööra wø dëëtge dëëdö; ni wëëkge aani ränynyö ni bäŋ ŋat mo jooga geni.
english: They mar my path, they set forward my calamity, they have no helper.

anywaa: Gena öö kede ge dunynyi ka kany mo otuc mo dwøŋ dëër øtø, ni putge rïŋ baŋa,
english: They came upon me as a wide breaking in of waters: in the desolation they rolled themselves upon me.

anywaa: ni ö dëëra ni tïme ni rïïŋö ki lwär, ni ö wödö mara ni cööri wøk bääta kaawat man wø tïïc jamø, ni ö bëët-gööki mara ni pöödhe kaamar pöölö.
english: Terrors are turned upon me: they pursue my soul as the wind: and my welfare passeth away as a cloud.

anywaa: «'Ba ennø, cwïnya apädhö; ni ö nïne mo jwør gïï mo leth ni bëëtge naa ege maa.
english: And now my soul is poured out upon me; the days of affliction have taken hold upon me.

anywaa: Kany wø tïme na wäär, cuu 'moa puta tïmö ni möödö ni rämö; ni rääm mara bëëdö dëëra ni ba maar cuŋŋö.
english: My bones are pierced in me in the night season: and my sinews take no rest.

anywaa: Jwøk abïï mara amaae ki teek mare na dwøŋ, ni møt aani ki lieŋ koothi mara.
english: By the great force of my disease is my garment changed: it bindeth me about as the collar of my coat.

anywaa: Eni aana leeŋ yo odhöönh, ni puta tïmö kaamar tør ki bur.
english: He hath cast me into the mire, and I am become like dust and ashes.

anywaa: «Wui, ï na Jwøk, aana jwöŋö riï kiper køny, 'ba ï kär duunnö jïra;  ni cuŋŋa nyïmï, ni bëëdï ni waŋï iï këël dëëra jaak.
english: I cry unto thee, and thou dost not hear me: I stand up, and thou regardest me not.

anywaa: Ïïna tïïö dëëra ki gïn mo raac, ni ö bëëtö mara ni døøyï gø mo leth ki badï na teek.
english: Thou art become cruel to me: with thy strong hand thou opposest thyself against me.

anywaa: Ïïni, aana leeŋï maal yi jamø, ni ö jamø ni køøl aani; ni ö ïïni ni cäŋï aani leeŋ ya atuunna.
english: Thou liftest me up to the wind; thou causest me to ride upon it, and dissolvest my substance.

anywaa: Aani ŋääa naa kïthï piny kar thøø, ni beeye kanya no ojiiŋŋø na kar røømmø kiper gïïa kwøw bëët.
english: For I know that thou wilt bring me to death, and to the house appointed for all living.

anywaa: «Ka adïëri møn, cenø bäŋ wø tïŋ maal bäät dhaanhø mo oränynyö kany wø jwöŋe kiper køny yi bëëtö mare na leth.
english: Howbeit he will not stretch out his hand to the grave, though they cry in his destruction.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, a bäŋ wø jwöŋi kaper jøøa en yi bëëtö mo leth? ?Aŋø, cwïnya bäŋ wø kïmmi kaper jøøa can?
english: Did not I weep for him that was in trouble? was not my soul grieved for the poor?

anywaa: 'Ba kanya bëëda ni cwïnya da ŋäädhe ni da gïn mo beer mo öö, atïmö ni ööa gïn mo raac; ni ö kanya bëëda naa køya tar ni tïme ni ööa muudhö.
english: When I looked for good, then evil came unto me: and when I waited for light, there came darkness.

anywaa: Aani cwïnya bëëdö no oränynyö jaak ni bäŋ jwöm mo jooda; ni ö jwør gïï mo lethi ni bëëtge ni ena nyïma.
english: My bowels boiled, and rested not: the days of affliction prevented me.

anywaa: A bëëdö naa kïmmö ni bäŋ cøm cwïny mo jooda; naa wø cuŋŋö dï lwaak naa jwöŋö kiper køny.
english: I went mourning without the sun: I stood up, and I cried in the congregation.

anywaa: Dwør oduuru mara atïmö kaamar dwør othöö, ni ö dwør kïmmö mara ni tïme kaamar dwør tula.
english: I am a brother to dragons, and a companion to owls.

anywaa: Buny dëëra atïmö ni cøl; ni tïm dëëra ki cuu 'moa ni waŋŋi ka adïrïgi.
english: My skin is black upon me, and my bones are burned with heat.

anywaa: Kiper manøgønø, thoom mara dwøl mare aniida baŋ dwør kïmmö, ni ö dwør opelø mara ni wiila gø baŋ dwør oduuru.
english: My harp also is turned to mourning, and my organ into the voice of them that weep.

anywaa: «Aani nyeŋŋa amäna ki man neena nyakøø ni cwïnya pärö ki gø.
english: I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?

anywaa: ?Agïnaŋø noo cïp Jwøki mana en maal jï dhaanhø, ni beeye mano tïmö na kure ki baŋ Jwøa en teeki jïre na en maalø?
english: For what portion of God is there from above? and what inheritance of the Almighty from on high?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, patha ränynyö kiper jø wø tïïc raay, ki ööny gïn mo leth bäät jø wø tïïc gïï mo reyø?
english: Is not destruction to the wicked? and a strange punishment to the workers of iniquity?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, Jwøk, uutjïëth bëëte 'moa bäŋ wø raŋŋe, ni kwar kwör cääthe mo tieta bëët?
english: Doth not he see my ways, and count all my steps?

anywaa: «Ni näk maa caatha øtjöör tööt, ni tieta løpa køør luup cwøk,
english: If I have walked with vanity, or if my foot hath hasted to deceit;

anywaa: doo beerra man ö Jwøki ni kïth gïïa tïïa bäät gïr røm mana näk kare, nee joode ki man näk mo bëëtö mara tiir.
english: Let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know mine integrity.

anywaa: 'Ba ni näk mo aano gaa wøk ki øtjöö, ni tïm cwïnya ni bwøtha nyeŋŋa, wala ceŋŋa bëëdö ni ba waany,
english: If my step hath turned out of the way, and mine heart walked after mine eyes, and if any blot hath cleaved to mine hands;

anywaa: doo beerra man ö japa piidha ni cami ya jø møøki, ni ö gïïa piidha ni pudhi wøk.
english: Then let me sow, and let another eat; yea, let my offspring be rooted out.

anywaa: «Ni näk mo aano pätö ki dhaagø mør ki cwïnya, wala a leewa dhi øtø mar cï ŋat atut mara,
english: If mine heart have been deceived by a woman, or if I have laid wait at my neighbour's door;

anywaa: doo beerra man ö dhaagø mara ni tïme na ŋat tïïc jï dïcwøø mør, ni buut cwøwi møøk ki gø.
english: Then let my wife grind unto another, and let others bow down upon her.

anywaa: Kiper gïnögø doo tïmö na bääyö mo raac døc, ni tïme na raay mo duunnö ka ajäla.
english: For this is an heinous crime; yea, it is an iniquity to be punished by the judges.

anywaa: Ni tïme na maac mo wääŋö, ni räänyö këël mano këët kar bëët jwïëc jøøa näk othøw,  ni dee japa moa näk yaa joodø bëët raanynyø.
english: For it is a fire that consumeth to destruction, and would root out all mine increase.

anywaa: «Doo naa cwøw ki mään moa näk jø tïïc 'moa luup moge yaa taaø, kanya dwaalge ki nyeŋŋa,
english: If I did despise the cause of my manservant or of my maidservant, when they contended with me;

anywaa: ?agïnaŋø ni daa dwøgø jï Jwøk kanyo pëëny aani? ?Na agïnaŋø ni daa løø jïre kanyo cwøl aani kar løøk?
english: What then shall I do when God riseth up? and when he visiteth, what shall I answer him?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, Jwøk na cwääc aani ec, paa eni na cwääc jøøgø thuwø? ?Aŋø, ba poot na eni na cwääc waani yïth mëëkwa?
english: Did not he that made me in the womb make him? and did not one fashion us in the womb?

anywaa: «'Ba aani, gïïa many jøøa canni kära mänö, ni waŋ cï thøø kära tïïö ni can;
english: If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail;

anywaa: aani cam mara kära camø na a keera, ni ba pääŋŋa ko obwöre moa näk kïïe.
english: Or have eaten my morsel myself alone, and the fatherless hath not eaten thereof;

anywaa: 'Ba ki mana täge ki yïth nïr thïnhö mara, a wø pïïdhö ki kïïe, naa bëëdö kaamar wääge, naa bëëdö naa gwøga määr thuunhnhi cooth.
english: (For from my youth he was brought up with me, as with a father, and I have guided her from my mother's womb;)

anywaa: Ni näk mo da dhaanhø mo yaa joodø mo manynya thøø ki can abïï, wala dhaanhø mo cäädhi ka dëëre,
english: If I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or any poor without covering;

anywaa: ni käre aani gwïëdhö ki yi cwïnye, kiper mana kära dëëre wëëk murrö ki jïëc rööm 'moa;
english: If his loins have not blessed me, and if he were not warmed with the fleece of my sheep;

anywaa: ni cera yaa tïŋ maal bäät obwöre moa näk kïïe, kiper mana ŋääa gø naa di cwaaø kar løøk,
english: If I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, when I saw my help in the gate:

anywaa: doo beerra man ö bada ni pudhi wøk göönna, ni put toor ki waŋ mutö.
english: Then let mine arm fall from my shoulder blade, and mine arm be broken from the bone.

anywaa: Kiper a lwäär ki ränynyö man wø ööi ki baŋ Jwøk, ni ba løny ki man tïïa ki gïn mo raac kiper a lwäär ki dööŋ-kar mare.
english: For destruction from God was a terror to me, and by reason of his highness I could not endure.

anywaa: «Doo na cwïnya bëëdö ni ŋäätha warkey, ni aano köö ni warkey mana tøŋ beeye kar gwøk røk mara;
english: If I have made gold my hope, or have said to the fine gold, Thou art my confidence;

anywaa: ni yia omïnnö ki jap kwärö 'moa na thööth, ni beege japa tïïa ki ceŋŋa;
english: If I rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because mine hand had gotten much;

anywaa: ni aano lwïthö baŋ cäŋ ni jooda gø no orieny, wala dwääy yaa lwiidhø ni cäädhi ka ajiem mare,
english: If I beheld the sun when it shined, or the moon walking in brightness;

anywaa: ni tïm cwïnya ni ena køørge, ni nuuma cera ki dhaa, ni mara wøør ge,
english: And my heart hath been secretly enticed, or my mouth hath kissed my hand:

anywaa: gïïögø thuwø doo tïmö na raay ni känne ka ajäla bääta, kiper doo tïmö naa kwiera Jwøk na en maal.
english: This also were an iniquity to be punished by the judge: for I should have denied the God that is above.

anywaa: «?Aŋø, aani, yia wø mïnnö wø bëëde ki gïn mo leth mo tägö dëër nyimänna, wala a wø kanynyø kiper gïna leth na ö bääte?
english: If I rejoiced at the destruction of him that hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him:

anywaa: Ba doo løny; aani, dhaa wø köömma köömmö nee ba cääne ki raay, ki man ciena jwïëc ŋatøgø.
english: Neither have I suffered my mouth to sin by wishing a curse to his soul.

anywaa: ?A jø wø bëëdö paara, ge bäŋ wø köö na bëëde, na ‹?Aŋa ni kär jäŋ ki cam mo met po Jööp?›?
english: If the men of my tabernacle said not, Oh that we had of his flesh! we cannot be satisfied.

anywaa: Bäŋ wëëllö mo yaa wëëk but thääŋ jöö ki wäär, kiper dhi øtø mara bëëdö ni yaa jabø jaak kiper wëëlle.
english: The stranger did not lodge in the street: but I opened my doors to the traveller.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, raay 'moa yaa kanø kaawat man wø tïïc jiyi, ni gïï mo reyø yaa kan cwïnya,
english: If I covered my transgressions as Adam, by hiding mine iniquity in my bosom:

anywaa: kiper mana lwäära ki jiy døc, ni aano bwøk ka ataa mar tuuŋa, ni puta bëëtö en ni aano nikïïl naa ba døny wøk?
english: Did I fear a great multitude, or did the contempt of families terrify me, that I kept silence, and went not out of the door?

anywaa: «Wui! ?Aŋø ni bäŋe ŋat wïny dwøra en? Raŋï, ŋïï mara kee en, beerra man ö Jwøa en teeki jïre ni duunne jïra! Beerra man ö ŋati ni löö ki aani en ni göör luupa piny.
english: Oh that one would hear me! behold, my desire is, that the Almighty would answer me, and that mine adversary had written a book.

anywaa: Ka adïëri møn, daa käärö ki göönna, ni kïtha gø wïïa kaamar aduda.
english: Surely I would take it upon my shoulder, and bind it as a crown to me.

anywaa: Aani kwör cääthe mo tieta daa caanø jïre, ni daa cäänö nyïme kaawat man wø cään kwäärö.
english: I would declare unto him the number of my steps; as a prince would I go near unto him.

anywaa: «'Ba ni näk mo pwöth 'moa a ege jäälö, ni kwöra no opuurö 'moa ge jwöŋö ni pï nyeŋge øya piny,
english: If my land cry against me, or that the furrows likewise thereof complain;

anywaa: ni jap wø ciek yi pwödhö cama ni jø tïïc ba cunna, ni cwïny jø tïïc wø raanynya raanynyø,
english: If I have eaten the fruits thereof without money, or have caused the owners thereof to lose their life:

anywaa: doo beerra man tuc koodhi kar beek wø cwøl ni cïndë, ni tuc luummi kar beek wø cwøl ni gäbci.» Luup Jööp gena ŋuudö kaagø nø.
english: Let thistles grow instead of wheat, and cockle instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.

anywaa: Kanyøgø jøøgø na adäk yøø gena lïŋö ki man dwökge ki luubö jï Jööp, kiper mana kööe ni bëëtö mare tiir ki baŋe.
english: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.

anywaa: 'Ba Eliyu wär Barakel nyï Buc, na käl dhi øt Ram, yie awaaŋ ki gootø døc ki Jööp kiper mana kööe ni bëëtö mare tiir ki nyïm Jwøk.
english: Then was kindled the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the kindred of Ram: against Job was his wrath kindled, because he justified himself rather than God.

anywaa: Eni thuwø, yie awaaŋ ki gootø ki nyïïawääte moa na adäk kiper mana dhäthe jïge ki man dwökge ki luubö ma kare jï Jööp, këël na bëëtge ni Jööp ege jäälö.
english: Also against his three friends was his wrath kindled, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.

anywaa: 'Ba Eliyu, kiper mana näk mo eni thiinh, jøøgø akoore nee kwøŋge cäänö ki Jööp.
english: Now Elihu had waited till Job had spoken, because they were elder than he.

anywaa: 'Ba Eliyu, kanya joot jøøgø na adäk yøø ni bäŋ luubö ma kare mo ege dwøgø, yie awaaŋ ki gootø.
english: When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, then his wrath was kindled.

anywaa: Kanyøgønø, Eliyu wär Barakel nyï Buc ena köö, ni «Aani, a thiinh ki cwiiri, 'ba uuni u døøŋŋø; kiper manøgønø, aana lwäyö ki man caana acaara mara jïïu.
english: And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, I am young, and ye are very old; wherefore I was afraid, and durst not shew you mine opinion.

anywaa: Aani, aana cädö ni ‹Dhaanhø mo dwøŋ beeye na doo cäänö, ni ö dhaanhe mo cwiiri moe thööth ni dee pöö ki luup leec wïc.›
english: I said, Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom.

anywaa: 'Ba beeye Jwïëc Jwøk ni wø en dëër dhaanhø, ni beeye jam dhi Jwøa en teeki jïre ni wø cïp kwany tiet luup jï gø.
english: But there is a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding.

anywaa: 'Ba patha ŋata dwøŋ keere ni wø wïïe leer, ni patha ŋata cwiiye thööth keere ni wø kwany tier gïrpiny ma kare.
english: Great men are not always wise: neither do the aged understand judgment.

anywaa: Kiper manøgønø, aana köö, ni ‹Cegu ïthu jïra; aani thuwø acaara mara caana caanø jïïu.›
english: Therefore I said, Hearken to me; I also will shew mine opinion.

anywaa: «'Ba ka adïëri møn, aani uuna køya ki cäänö maru, naa bëëdö ni ïtha yaa ciiø kanya bëëdu nou määnyö ki luup leec wïc mo caannu.
english: Behold, I waited for your words; I gave ear to your reasons, whilst ye searched out what to say.

anywaa: Aana bëëdö ni ïtha yaa ciiø døc baŋu; 'ba bäŋ dhaanhø dëëtu mo bääyö mar Jööp ee joodø, ni bäŋgø thuwø mo luup Jööp ee løø na adïëri.
english: Yea, I attended unto you, and, behold, there was none of you that convinced Job, or that answered his words:

anywaa: Käru köö, ni ‹Waana jiy mo wïthwa leer; beerra man ö Jwøki ni bööt Jööp, ni patha dhaanhø.›
english: Lest ye should say, We have found out wisdom: God thrusteth him down, not man.

anywaa: 'Ba Jööp na cääne, ba cäänö ka aani, naa ba dwök baŋe thuwø ki luubö kaawat mana caannu.
english: Now he hath not directed his words against me: neither will I answer him with your speeches.

anywaa: «'Ba jøøgø yïthge athäŋŋö, ni bäŋe gïn mo ege dwøgø këët;  ni tïmge ni bäŋ gïn mo maar lønyø jïge ki caan.
english: They were amazed, they answered no more: they left off speaking.

anywaa: ?A aani, løny ki man kura këët? Kee ge bëëdö ni geno nikïïl, ni ge cuŋŋö kaace jaak ni bäŋ dhaanhø mo dwögi.
english: When I had waited, (for they spake not, but stood still, and answered no more;)

anywaa: 'Ba aani thuwø, mara løøa løø; aani thuwø, acaara mara caana caanø.
english: I said, I will answer also my part, I also will shew mine opinion.

anywaa: Kiper aani jïra da luup mo thööth mo caana caanø; jwïëy moi ni dëëra en a ege wëëk cäänö.
english: For I am full of matter, the spirit within me constraineth me.

anywaa: Yia bëëdö kaamar opïr pïën mo päŋ ki køøŋø, mo manynya man cööde.
english: Behold, my belly is as wine which hath no vent; it is ready to burst like new bottles.

anywaa: Aani, a cäänö naa jïta ki jwöm; aani, dhaa jaba jabø ni dwöga ki luubö.
english: I will speak, that I may be refreshed: I will open my lips and answer.

anywaa: Aani, bäŋ dhaanhø mo jeenya, ni bäŋ dhaanhø mo mwødha;
english: Let me not, I pray you, accept any man's person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man.

anywaa: kiper doo na aana ŋat mwøth, ŋata cwääc aani doo laar öö ni dee aani kälö.
english: For I know not to give flattering titles; in so doing my maker would soon take me away.

anywaa: «'Ba ennø, ï na Jööp, cek ïthï ki luup 'moa, ni wïnynyï luup moi bëët ni caana jïrï en.
english: Wherefore, Job, I pray thee, hear my speeches, and hearken to all my words.

anywaa: Ennø, aani a ena bäät man jaba dhaa naa cääna, ni luup oløny ni ena bäät buny dhaa kiree.
english: Behold, now I have opened my mouth, my tongue hath spoken in my mouth.

anywaa: Ni luupa moi ni caana ii käla yi cwïny mo thïïŋ, ni luup mo wø ö wøk ki dhaa beege gïï mo ŋääa ni gena adïëri.
english: My words shall be of the uprightness of my heart: and my lips shall utter knowledge clearly.

anywaa: Jwïëc Jwøk bee na cwääc aani, ni ö jam jwïëy mar Jwøa en teeki jïre ni wëëk aani kwøw.
english: The Spirit of God hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life.

anywaa: 'Ba ni näk mo løny jïrï, duunnï jïra ni mø, jek riï nø, ni ööï ni cuŋŋï nyïma ki luup moï.
english: If thou canst answer me, set thy words in order before me, stand up.

anywaa: Aani cøøn, a rööma ïïni ki nyïm Jwøk, naa käla ro odhöönh thuwø.
english: Behold, I am according to thy wish in God's stead: I also am formed out of the clay.

anywaa: 'Ba ennø, ï ba doo lwäyö ki aani, kiper cera ba tïmö ni peek bäätï.
english: Behold, my terror shall not make thee afraid, neither shall my hand be heavy upon thee.

anywaa: «'Ba ka adïëri møn, ïïna cäänö ni wïnyö jïra, ni luup moa caanï aputa wïnynyö kiree.
english: Surely thou hast spoken in mine hearing, and I have heard the voice of thy words, saying,

anywaa: Ïïna köö, ‹Ni bëëtö mara beer, ni bäŋ gïn mo ogwäyö jïra, naa bëëdö naa waany ni bäŋ raay mo yaa tïïö.
english: I am clean without transgression, I am innocent; neither is there iniquity in me.

anywaa: 'Ba Jwøk anø määnyö ki jöö mør man jääl aani ki gø, naa ee nø kwaan kaamar nyimän mare.
english: Behold, he findeth occasions against me, he counteth me for his enemy,

anywaa: Eni tieta akïth yïth orøge, ni bëëdö ni neeta uutjïëthe 'moa bëët, naa jääle.›
english: He putteth my feet in the stocks, he marketh all my paths.

anywaa: «'Ba ennø, ï na Jööp, a cäänna ïïni, marï patha kare, kiper Jwøk dwøŋ døc ni kaala dhaanhø.
english: Behold, in this thou art not just: I will answer thee, that God is greater than man.

anywaa: ?Aperŋø ni pïëmï ki Jwøk en, ni kööï ni luup moï ba duue?
english: Why dost thou strive against him? for he giveth not account of any of his matters.

anywaa: Kiper Jwøk løny jïre ki man cääne ki luup ki uutjïëthe ma teeŋi, 'ba dhaanhø wïïe ba caare ki luup mo gø.
english: For God speaketh once, yea twice, yet man perceiveth it not.

anywaa: Kany wø tïme na wäär ni jiy obutö døc kwör niine moge, Jwøk cäänö ki jiy ki yïth lääk ki ri jammi mo wø nyooth ki yi wïc ki wäär,
english: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falleth upon men, in slumberings upon the bed;

anywaa: ni jap ïthge ki man wïnyge dwøre, ni wëëk geni bwøk ki köömmö mare,
english: Then he openeth the ears of men, and sealeth their instruction,

anywaa: ni mare duu geni wøk ki uutjïëthe moge na reyø, ni mäna geni ki bëët atöör;
english: That he may withdraw man from his purpose, and hide pride from man.

anywaa: kiper nee jwïëcge pieme dhi buur, ni gwøk jwïëy moge ki thøw opëëllö.
english: He keepeth back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.

anywaa: 'Ba Jwøk løny jïre thuwø ki man jook dhaanhø ki täw,  ni wëëk gø but bäät pëëm ni rämö, ni cuu moe ojøøny.
english: He is chastened also with pain upon his bed, and the multitude of his bones with strong pain:

anywaa: Ni put tïmö ni cwïnye ba many cam, ni cwïnye bëëdö ni cøl ki caammi moa no ojierø.
english: So that his life abhorreth bread, and his soul dainty meat.

anywaa: Ni ö dëëre ni dwade døc, ni tïm cuuwe ni nëënö wøk jaak.
english: His flesh is consumed away, that it cannot be seen; and his bones that were not seen stick out.

anywaa: Ni tïm kare ni cään ki thøø, ni ö bëët kwøw mare ni tïme ni ena cer nyïïatwiel mar thøø.
english: Yea, his soul draweth near unto the grave, and his life to the destroyers.

anywaa: «'Ba ki røk nyïïatwiet maal ma kuma, doo na da aciel mo ena løøe mo cäänö kipere, ni para wï gø ki gïna dee tïïö,
english: If there be a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to shew unto man his uprightness:

anywaa: ni nyootha bäth ec mare jïgø, ni kööe, ni ‹Piem eni dhi thøø, kiper aana jïtö ki gïn mo wïïla eni wøk,›
english: Then he is gracious unto him, and saith, Deliver him from going down to the pit: I have found a ransom.

anywaa: kanyøgønø, rïŋ dëëre doo cäŋa tïmö kaamar rïŋ dëër nyilaal mo poot thiinh, ni dee døø kare ni teek ni caala yïth nïr wøp moe.
english: His flesh shall be fresher than a child's: he shall return to the days of his youth:

anywaa: Ni läme jï Jwøk, ni ö Jwøki ni jïëc mare, ni neen täärnyïm Jwøk ni put kwöŋŋö ki met ec, kiper mana dwøgi ya Jwøki kare ri bëëtö mare mana tiir dïkwøŋ.
english: He shall pray unto God, and he will be favourable unto him: and he shall see his face with joy: for he will render unto man his righteousness.

anywaa: Køøre nø, eni wär ki duut nyïm jiy, ni kööe, ni ‹Aana bääyö møn, ni raanynya gïna näk adïëri, 'ba ajäla mana dee aani jäälö ki gø kär tïïc Jwøki.
english: He looketh upon men, and if any say, I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, and it profited me not;

anywaa: 'Ba eni jwïëya apieme cer thøø; 'ba ennø, a puta bëëtö yi tac kwøw.›
english: He will deliver his soul from going into the pit, and his life shall see the light.

anywaa: «'Ba ka adïëri møn, Jwøk teeŋ gïïögø bëët wø tïïe tïïö jï jiy ki kwör møøk,
english: Lo, all these things worketh God oftentimes with man,

anywaa: ni mare piem jwïëy mo dhaanhø dhi thøø, kiper nee dhaanhø bëëde yi tac kwøw.
english: To bring back his soul from the pit, to be enlightened with the light of the living.

anywaa: «'Ba ennø, ï na Jööp, cek ïthï ni wïnynyï luumma; niïkïïl, naa cäänna.
english: Mark well, O Job, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I will speak.

anywaa: 'Ba nee da gïn mo løgï løø, caanï jïra; cäänï, kiper a manynya gø niï ŋunni ni marï beer.
english: If thou hast any thing to say, answer me: speak, for I desire to justify thee.

anywaa: 'Ba ni näk mo bäŋgø, cek ïthï jïra; niïkïïl, kiper niï läwa pwönynyö ki luup leec wïc.»
english: If not, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I shall teach thee wisdom.

anywaa: Køøre Eliyu ena bëëdö ni poot cäänö ni kööe,
english: Furthermore Elihu answered and said,

anywaa: ni «U ni wø köö ni wïthu leer, wïnynyu luup 'moa; cegu ïthu jïra, u ni wø köö ni uuno kwänynyö;
english: Hear my words, O ye wise men; and give ear unto me, ye that have knowledge.

anywaa: kiper ïth beeye ni wø jier luup, kaawat man wø ö leepi wø bel cam.
english: For the ear trieth words, as the mouth tasteth meat.

anywaa: Beerra man jierø gïna tiir kiper dëëtø, ni tïmø bëët ni ø kwanya gïna beer kiper dëëtø.
english: Let us choose to us judgment: let us know among ourselves what is good.

anywaa: «'Ba ennø, Jööp aköö, ni ‹Aana dhaanhø mo bëëtö mare tiir; 'ba Jwøk akweer ki man tïïc ŋøl luup ma kare bääta.
english: For Job hath said, I am righteous: and God hath taken away my judgment.

anywaa: Këël na bëëda ni bëëtö mara tiir, aana kwaan kaamar twöt; këël na bëëda naa ba bääö, aana jïtö ki ŋwiili mo ba caŋŋi.›
english: Should I lie against my right? my wound is incurable without transgression.

anywaa: ?Wui, aŋa ni caal Jööp en, mo luup abuua care ni jööt jaak kaawat man wø maath pïï?
english: What man is like Job, who drinketh up scorning like water?

anywaa: Eni wø bëëdö ka jø wø tïïc gïï mo reyø, ni eni wø dwätö na aciel ki jø raay.
english: Which goeth in company with the workers of iniquity, and walketh with wicked men.

anywaa: Kiper ena köö, ni ‹Ki man bëëdö ni døøya yi Jwøk mo met bäŋ gïn mo duue dëër dhaanhø.›
english: For he hath said, It profiteth a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.

anywaa: «Kiper manøgønø, cegu ïthu jïra, u ni wø köö ni tiet luup laaru ka kwany.  Jwøk kare bäär ki tïïc gïn mo raac; ni eni na Jwøa en teeki jïre kare bäär ki tïïc gïn mo patha adïëri.
english: Therefore hearken unto me, ye men of understanding: far be it from God, that he should do wickedness; and from the Almighty, that he should commit iniquity.

anywaa: Kiper eni, ŋati man nø cunne cunnö ki køør gïna tïïe; ni ö ŋati man nø ni dwøk japa tïïe wï gø ki køør bëëtö mar gø.
english: For the work of a man shall he render unto him, and cause every man to find according to his ways.

anywaa: Ka adïëri møn, Jwøk ba tïïö ki gïn mo patha adïëri, ni eni na en teeki jïre luup ba ŋøle no oköömmö.
english: Yea, surely God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert judgment.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, da ŋat mo Jwøk ee mooø ki teek bäät piny? ?Aŋø, bäät piny bäre ocïba ŋa cere nee bëëde ni koora eni?
english: Who hath given him a charge over the earth? or who hath disposed the whole world?

anywaa: Doo na Jwøk cädö kaper dëëre keere, ni war jwïëy moe ki jam jwïëy mare,
english: If he set his heart upon man, if he gather unto himself his spirit and his breath;

anywaa: gïïa kwøw bëët doo puta thøø, ni ö dhaanhe ni dee døø ri tør.
english: All flesh shall perish together, and man shall turn again unto dust.

anywaa: «'Ba ï na Jööp, ni näk mo tiet luup cøøa wïïï, wïny gïn, ni cegï ïthï ki luummo caana.
english: If now thou hast understanding, hear this: hearken to the voice of my words.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, ŋat wø män ki ŋøl luup ma adïëri, løny jïre ki man käär jiy? ?Aŋø, Jwøa teek na bëëtö mare tiir, jäälï jäälö?
english: Shall even he that hateth right govern? and wilt thou condemn him that is most just?

anywaa: Eni na Jwøk wø köö jï nyeya, ni ‹Ïïni, wïïï raac,› ni kööe jï kwääri, ni ‹Uuna jiy mo reyø.›
english: Is it fit to say to a king, Thou art wicked? and to princes, Ye are ungodly?

anywaa: Eni ba bëëdö ni ena løø dïbwöthe, ni jøøa näk okwär ba lääŋŋe døc ni kaala jøøa can, kiper mana näk mo geni bëët beege japa tïïe ki cere.
english: How much less to him that accepteth not the persons of princes, nor regardeth the rich more than the poor? for they all are the work of his hands.

anywaa: Jøøgø bëët, ge laara thøø ki kany mo cään. Kany wø tïme na dhöör-wäär, ge laara thøø ni pööth karge. Jøøa teek, jwïëcge laara pöödhö ni ge kär gudö ki cenø.
english: In a moment shall they die, and the people shall be troubled at midnight, and pass away: and the mighty shall be taken away without hand.

anywaa: «Kiper Jwøk raŋŋa yi jöör bëëtö mar dhaanhø; ni waŋe neeta kwör cääthe mo tiet gø.
english: For his eyes are upon the ways of man, and he seeth all his goings.

anywaa: Bäŋ kany mo cøl wala tier tïpö mo dhïïth mo løny ki man ö jø wø tïïc gïï mo reyø ni kange rege yie.
english: There is no darkness, nor shadow of death, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.

anywaa: Jwøk ba mak ki teek ki man cïp dhaanhø nyïme, nee luum gø ŋøle.
english: For he will not lay upon man more than right; that he should enter into judgment with God.

anywaa: Eni jiy moa teek pete petø ni thenh thenh ni bäŋ tier gïn mo pëënynye, ni kïth jø møøk kwörge.
english: He shall break in pieces mighty men without number, and set others in their stead.

anywaa: Ka adïëri møn, eni tïïe mo jøøgø ŋääe, ni raany geni ki wäär, ni putge ränynyö.
english: Therefore he knoweth their works, and he overturneth them in the night, so that they are destroyed.

anywaa: Geni, ge jääl Jwøki jäälö kiper raay moge, ni nëënö nyïm jiy bëët.
english: He striketh them as wicked men in the open sight of others;

anywaa: Kiper gena gaa wøk ki man caathge køør Jwøk, ni bäŋ gïn mo caarge kiper uutjïëth tïïe moe.
english: Because they turned back from him, and would not consider any of his ways:

anywaa: Geni, jøøa can ki jøøa no ocaannø atïïcge nee jwöŋge dëër Jwøk kiper køny, ni ö Jwøki ni wïny oduuru marge.
english: So that they cause the cry of the poor to come unto him, and he heareth the cry of the afflicted.

anywaa: ?'Ba ni näk mo eno lïŋö, aŋa noo köö ni eno bääyö? ?A ni näk mo täärnyïme ee kanø, aŋa noo joot gø? Eni, jiy ki wïth juurre bëët ena tiere,
english: When he giveth quietness, who then can make trouble? and when he hideth his face, who then can behold him? whether it be done against a nation, or against a man only:

anywaa: kiper nee dhaanhø mo tøør ri Jwøk nee jiy ba kääre, nee ba tïme na abïëp mo jiy pätha yie.
english: That the hypocrite reign not, lest the people be ensnared.

anywaa: «Kanymør da dhaanhø mo köö jï Jwøk,  ni ‹Gïï mo leth ajwøra, 'ba ennø, a ba bääyi këët.
english: Surely it is meet to be said unto God, I have borne chastisement, I will not offend any more:

anywaa: Beerra man pwönynyï aani ki japa näk kuua; 'ba ni näk mo aano bääyö, naa ba cäŋa bääyö këët.›
english: That which I see not teach thou me: if I have done iniquity, I will do no more.

anywaa: ?Aŋø Jööp, løny jï Jwøk ki man duunne jïrï kaawat man wø manynyï, kany wø näk mo ïïno kweer ki mare? Beeye ïïni na doo ŋøl luummögø ni patha aani; kiper manøgønø, mana ŋäyï caanï.
english: Should it be according to thy mind? he will recompense it, whether thou refuse, or whether thou choose; and not I: therefore speak what thou knowest.

anywaa: «Jøøa näk tiet luup cøøa wïthge, ki ŋato wïny luumma ni wø wïïe leer, geno köö,
english: Let men of understanding tell me, and let a wise man hearken unto me.

anywaa: ni ‹Jööp cara luup mo patha mo kwänynyö; ni luup mo care bäŋ leec wïc rege.
english: Job hath spoken without knowledge, and his words were without wisdom.

anywaa: Doo beer ki man tet Jööp døc kar løøk, nee luup bëët caane, kiper luup mo wø dwøge caala mo ŋat raay.
english: My desire is that Job may be tried unto the end because of his answers for wicked men.

anywaa: Kiper eni bäät raaye amëënne ka ageem, ni paŋ ceŋŋe yïthakiyø ni mare abuua, ni car luup mo thööth dëër Jwøk.› »
english: For he addeth rebellion unto his sin, he clappeth his hands among us, and multiplieth his words against God.

anywaa: Køøre Eliyu abëëdö ni poot cäänö ni kööe jï Jööp,
english: Elihu spake moreover, and said,

anywaa: na «?Aŋø, iï caarø ni beeye gïn ma kare ki man kööï ni bëëtö marï tiir ki nyïm Jwøk?
english: Thinkest thou this to be right, that thou saidst, My righteousness is more than God's?

anywaa: Kiper ïïna köö jïre, na ‹?Agïnaŋø noo jooda wala noo duue jïra ki køør mano bëëda ni raa yaa mänö ki raay?›
english: For thou saidst, What advantage will it be unto thee? and, What profit shall I have, if I be cleansed from my sin?

anywaa: «'Ba ennø, løøa løø jïrï, ni bee ïïni ki nyïïawäätï moø ni buutï yøø.
english: I will answer thee, and thy companions with thee.

anywaa: Lwïthï maal mø ni raŋï gø; raŋ pøøl moø ni en maal kuya yøøke ki ïïni.
english: Look unto the heavens, and see; and behold the clouds which are higher than thou.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, ni näk mo ïïno bääyö, da gïn mo raanynye dëër Jwøk? ?A ni näk mo da gïï mo reyø mo thööth mo iï tïïö, agïnaŋø noo raanynye dëër Jwøk?
english: If thou sinnest, what doest thou against him? or if thy transgressions be multiplied, what doest thou unto him?

anywaa: ?'Ba ni näk mo bëëtö marï tiir, agïnaŋø na cïpï jï Jwøk, wala agïnaŋø na joode baŋï?
english: If thou be righteous, what givest thou him? or what receiveth he of thine hand?

anywaa: Rääö marï guta jiy mo caala ïïni, ni ö bëënynyö marï ni gut teeŋ jøøgø thuwø.
english: Thy wickedness may hurt a man as thou art; and thy righteousness may profit the son of man.

anywaa: «Jiy ge jwöŋö kiper caannø mana päl bäätge. Geni, ge jwöŋö kiper køny nee bøthge ceŋ jøøa en teeki ceŋge.
english: By reason of the multitude of oppressions they make the oppressed to cry: they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty.

anywaa: 'Ba bäŋ dhaanhø mo pëëö, ni ‹?Jwøk en kaa na cwääc aani, Jwø wø wëëk wa wär dudi ki wäär,
english: But none saith, Where is God my maker, who giveth songs in the night;

anywaa: ni wø pwöny wa døc ni kaala man pwöny lääy mo bäät piny, ni wïthwa ee tïïö ni leer ni kaala weny mo maal?›
english: Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth, and maketh us wiser than the fowls of heaven?

anywaa: Eni, kany wø bëët jøøgø ni jwöŋö, bäŋ gïn mo løøe, kiper atöör mana en cwïnyge, ge na jø raay.
english: There they cry, but none giveth answer, because of the pride of evil men.

anywaa: 'Ba ka adïëri møn, Jwøk ïthe ba ciie ko oduuru mo bäŋ tiere; ni eni na en teeki jïre bäŋ gïn caare kiper teeŋ gïnögø.
english: Surely God will not hear vanity, neither will the Almighty regard it.

anywaa: A ïïni nø, ï na Jööp, dwørï owïny Jwøki nidïï, ni kööï ni eni kärï joodø en, ni luubö marï ena nyïme niï koora eni!
english: Although thou sayest thou shalt not see him, yet judgment is before him; therefore trust thou in him.

anywaa: 'Ba kiper mana bëët Jwøki ni gootø mare ee jooø ki man tïïy ajäla, ni raac jiy ba raŋŋe døc,
english: But now, because it is not so, he hath visited in his anger; yet he knoweth it not in great extremity:

anywaa: ï na Jööp, dhiï aŋammï ki luup mo bäŋ tietge;  ni kaathï cäänö marï ki luup mo tøør ri leec wïc.»
english: Therefore doth Job open his mouth in vain; he multiplieth words without knowledge.

anywaa: Køøre Eliyu ena bëëdö ni poot cäänö ni kööe,
english: Elihu also proceeded, and said,

anywaa: ni «Koor aani ki kany mo thiinh, nee luup møøk cäŋa caannø kiper Jwøk.
english: Suffer me a little, and I will shew thee that I have yet to speak on God's behalf.

anywaa: Aani jammi moa kwanya käla kwör ma teeŋi; ennø, a caana gø ki man näk mo Jwøk na cwääc aani, mare beer.
english: I will fetch my knowledge from afar, and will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.

anywaa: 'Ba ka adïëri møn, luup 'moa patha luup tööt; ŋata wïïe leer na näk okwänynyö na kare bee aani ni en dïïu en.
english: For truly my words shall not be false: he that is perfect in knowledge is with thee.

anywaa: «'Ba ka adïëri møn, Jwøk beeye na teek ni bäŋ dhaanhø mo raŋe ni ee taaø; ni teek mare ki man ŋäc tiet jammi opöödhö.
english: Behold, God is mighty, and despiseth not any: he is mighty in strength and wisdom.

anywaa: Eni jø wø tïïc gïïa reyø ba wiie ni kwøw; 'ba jøøa no ocaarø, luup moge wø ŋøle ŋølø na kare.
english: He preserveth not the life of the wicked: but giveth right to the poor.

anywaa: Ni eni waŋe ba daae bäät jøøa bëëtge tiir; 'ba ge cïbe bäät wälu na aciel ki nyeye, ni bëëtge no owøørø na bäre bäre.
english: He withdraweth not his eyes from the righteous: but with kings are they on the throne; yea, he doth establish them for ever, and they are exalted.

anywaa: Kany wø tööc jiy ki tiimme, ni päthge yïth thøøli mo jwør gïï mo leth,
english: And if they be bound in fetters, and be holden in cords of affliction;

anywaa: Jwøk nyootha tïïe moge jïge ki raay moge, ni beege japa töötge kiperge.
english: Then he sheweth them their work, and their transgressions that they have exceeded.

anywaa: Eni ge wø tïïe tïïö nee ïthge cekge ki pwöc, ni kööm geni ki man løkge cwïnyge yïth raay moge.
english: He openeth also their ear to discipline, and commandeth that they return from iniquity.

anywaa: 'Ba geni, ni näk mo ge jïëy ni tïnyge eni, nïr kwøw moge moa dööŋ dege thöörö ni bëëtö marge orømø, ni thöörge cwiiri moge ni ge ena yi met ec.
english: If they obey and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.

anywaa: 'Ba ni näk mo ïthge ba cekge, ge di nääö ko opëëllö, ni thøwge ni ge kär kwänynyö.
english: But if they obey not, they shall perish by the sword, and they shall die without knowledge.

anywaa: «'Ba jøøa näk cwïnyge tøør ri Jwøk, ge bëëdö ni geno gootø; geni ge ba jwöŋi kiper køny kany wø ö Jwøki wø wëëk ge twöc.
english: But the hypocrites in heart heap up wrath: they cry not when he bindeth them.

anywaa: Geni, ge wø laara thøø ni ge poot kär jal. Aŋuun kwøw marge wø laara cuuŋö, ni beege ki cwøw mo wø tïïc tïï käp yïth uut juu moa näk patha adïëri.
english: They die in youth, and their life is among the unclean.

anywaa: 'Ba Jwøk jiy moa en yïth gïï mo leth wø käle wøk ki yïth gïïa leth na enge yïthge; ni tïïc geni nee ïthge cekge ki pwöc moe, kany wø enge yïth gïïa leth.
english: He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.

anywaa: «'Ba ï na Jööp, Jwøk ïïna käl wøk ki dhøk gïïa leth, ni cïp ïïni kany mo laac miï bëëdö ni ïïno pädö yie, ni buutï päŋ ki caammi.
english: Even so would he have removed thee out of the strait into a broad place, where there is no straitness; and that which should be set on thy table should be full of fatness.

anywaa: 'Ba ennø, bäätï ajïtö ki teeŋ ajäla man wø ö bäät jøøa bëëtge reyø; ni ö ajäla ki ŋøl luup ni ciel ïïni.
english: But thou hast fulfilled the judgment of the wicked: judgment and justice take hold on thee.

anywaa: Beerra man gwøgï riï nee wïïï ba maaŋ jap kwärri; ni ba løøï wïïï wøk ki køør jap wø thööth ni wø cïp ki piny.
english: Because there is wrath, beware lest he take thee away with his stroke: then a great ransom cannot deliver thee.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, iï caarø ni jap kwärö moï ki teek marï bäre, niï mäne mänö ki man pïïc gïï mo lethi bäätï?
english: Will he esteem thy riches? no, not gold, nor all the forces of strength.

anywaa: Kär muudhö parï ki man ööe, ni wø rïëm jiy wøk ki yïth mïëri moge.
english: Desire not the night, when people are cut off in their place.

anywaa: Gwøk riï ni ba døøï yïth raay, kiper beeye ki køør raay ni jwørï gïï mo leth en.
english: Take heed, regard not iniquity: for this hast thou chosen rather than affliction.

anywaa: «Ka adïëri møn, Jwøk bëëdö no owøørø ki teek mare. ?A dïpööy mane ni caal eni?
english: Behold, God exalteth by his power: who teacheth like him?

anywaa: ?Aŋa ni wø nyooth uutjïëth tïïe moe mo wø tïïe, wala mo oköö jïgø ni ‹Ïïna bääyö›?
english: Who hath enjoined him his way? or who can say, Thou hast wrought iniquity?

anywaa: Par wïïï ki man tïŋï nyeŋŋe maal kiper tïïe moe na näk ocäŋ jiyi ki dudi.
english: Remember that thou magnify his work, which men behold.

anywaa: Tïïe moe ajoot wïth juurre bëët, ni jooti ya jiyi moa kwörge bäyö.
english: Every man may see it; man may behold it afar off.

anywaa: Ka adïëri møn, Jwøk dwøŋ ni ba løny ki man ŋääø bëëtö mare bäre; ni ba løny jïïø ki man ŋääø cwiic kwøw moe.
english: Behold, God is great, and we know him not, neither can the number of his years be searched out.

anywaa: «Eni, ŋiith pïï ajääŋ maal, nee tïme na pøøl,
english: For he maketh small the drops of water: they pour down rain according to the vapour thereof:

anywaa: ni wëëk gø løø ni lwör piny na køth, ni tïm køthi ni pätha bäät jiy ni päl døc.
english: Which the clouds do drop and distil upon man abundantly.

anywaa: ?Aŋa ni ŋäc yi jöö mana ö eni na peer pøøl ki gø, ki yi jöö man wø wëëk odäru köö ki gø yi kar bëëtö mare maal?
english: Also can any understand the spreadings of the clouds, or the noise of his tabernacle?

anywaa: Raŋï, eni agaackøth mare wø keethe keethø deŋŋe, ni ö kudi mo naama dwøŋ ni pääŋ ge ki pïï.
english: Behold, he spreadeth his light upon it, and covereth the bottom of the sea.

anywaa: Moøgø beege uutjïëthe mo wø käär wïth juurre ki ge, ni eni wø cïpö ki cam mo päl jïge.
english: For by them judgeth he the people; he giveth meat in abundance.

anywaa: Eni cere wø wëëge pääŋö ka agaackøth, ni kööm gø ki man gööye kanya manynye.
english: With clouds he covereth the light; and commandeth it not to shine by the cloud that cometh betwixt.

anywaa: Odäru mare nyootha öönynye, ni ö lääc paaci thuwø ni ŋäcge öö mare.
english: The noise thereof sheweth concerning it, the cattle also concerning the vapour.

anywaa: «Wui! Gïnögø wenyø mara atïïe ni pöödö døc, ni manynya pär wøk kare.
english: At this also my heart trembleth, and is moved out of his place.

anywaa: Cegu ïthu, ni wïnynyu märö mar dwør Jwøk man ni ö wøk ki dhee ni lwör døc en.
english: Hear attentively the noise of his voice, and the sound that goeth out of his mouth.

anywaa: Eni agaackøth mare di meenyø ki maal, ni put tac gø jääŋŋö yïth tuk piny.
english: He directeth it under the whole heaven, and his lightning unto the ends of the earth.

anywaa: 'Ba noo tïme na køøre, dwør Jwøk wø märö, eni määr døc ki dwøl mo dwøŋ. 'Ba kany wø wëëk dwøre märö, agaackøth ba jooe.
english: After it a voice roareth: he thundereth with the voice of his excellency; and he will not stay them when his voice is heard.

anywaa: Dwør Jwøk wø märö, ni tïïe ki gïï mo døøŋŋø mo ec thäŋŋö ki ge; eni gïï mo døøŋŋø wø di tïïö ni bäŋ ŋat mo kwany tietge.
english: God thundereth marvellously with his voice; great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend.

anywaa: Kiper eni wø köö jï pey, ni ‹Pänhnhu bäät piny,› ni kööe jï køth, ni ‹Lwörï døc ni øyï piny ni teek.›
english: For he saith to the snow, Be thou on the earth; likewise to the small rain, and to the great rain of his strength.

anywaa: Ni put tïïe mo jiy wëëk cuŋŋö, ni ö jiyi bëët ni ŋäcge tïïe mo gø.
english: He sealeth up the hand of every man; that all men may know his work.

anywaa: Ni ö lääyi mo paap ni kaange rege, ni putge bëëtö kwörge ni ge ba ö wøk.
english: Then the beasts go into dens, and remain in their places.

anywaa: Atuunna wëëge kwön wøk ki kar kän mare, ni put kännö ki köö ki yi jamø mo teek døc.
english: Out of the south cometh the whirlwind: and cold out of the north.

anywaa: Jam jwïëy mar Jwøk piiø di tïïö, ni ö pïïyi ni makge rege ni teek døc.
english: By the breath of God frost is given: and the breadth of the waters is straitened.

anywaa: Eni pøøl wø pääŋe pääŋö ki pïï, ni wëëk agaackøth mare nigaaŋ ni put keethø yïthakicge.
english: Also by watering he wearieth the thick cloud: he scattereth his bright cloud:

anywaa: Eni pøøl tïïe tïïö nee cääthge bäät piny bäre ki køør dwøre, nee gïïa kööm ge ki ge tïïcge.
english: And it is turned round about by his counsels: that they may do whatsoever he commandeth them upon the face of the world in the earth.

anywaa: Eni køth wø wëëge pädhö bäät piny, ni ki kwör møøk mare ajäla, wala eni jwøya piny ni mare nyooth mëër mare ni wø ba jøøl.
english: He causeth it to come, whether for correction, or for his land, or for mercy.

anywaa: «'Ba ï na Jööp, cek ïthï ki gïn, ni cuŋŋï ni caarï tiet luup mo Jwøk moi ni thääŋ ec ii.
english: Hearken unto this, O Job: stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, da gïn mo ŋäyï kiper yi jöö man wø ö Jwøki wø kööm pøøl ki gø, ki kany wø meeny agaackøth mare ki yïthakic pøøl?
english: Dost thou know when God disposed them, and caused the light of his cloud to shine?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, da gïn mo ŋäyï kiper yi jöö man bëët pøølli ni lïïrö maal en, ni bee gïï mo rëëma ec ni wø tïïc Jwøki, eni ni wø ŋäc tiet jammi bëët?
english: Dost thou know the balancings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him which is perfect in knowledge?

anywaa: ?A ïïni, ï ni wø dëërï tïmö ni lïëth tier abïïnï, kany wø näk piny onikïïl ki jamø man wø kwönni ki tier-piny,
english: How thy garments are warm, when he quieteth the earth by the south wind?

anywaa: løny jïrï ki man kønyï Jwøk ki tïïc kany wø peer maal, ni ee tïïö ni tøŋ ni paŋŋi kaamar cïläälca?
english: Hast thou with him spread out the sky, which is strong, and as a molten looking glass?

anywaa: «Aŋø, ï pwönynyï waani wäne nø, nee wa jïtwa ki luubö mo caanwa jï Jwøk; waani bäŋ gïn mo løny ki man caanwa gø, kiper wa bëëdö yi muudhö.
english: Teach us what we shall say unto him; for we cannot order our speech by reason of darkness.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, løny ki man kööï jï Jwøk, na ‹A manynya gø naa cäänna›? ?Aŋø, da ŋat mo doo pëëö nee eni raany Jwøki?
english: Shall it be told him that I speak? if a man speak, surely he shall be swallowed up.

anywaa: Bäŋ ŋat mo løny jïre ki man raŋ jï cäŋ kany wø näk mo orieny ni tar døc, ni waŋe otïïc jamø ni tøŋ.
english: And now men see not the bright light which is in the clouds: but the wind passeth, and cleanseth them.

anywaa: Jwøk öö ki wï-piny ka ajiem mo ec thäŋŋö ki gø, mo caala warkey mo tøŋ døc.
english: Fair weather cometh out of the north: with God is terrible majesty.

anywaa: Jwøa en teeki jïre kaala wïthø, ni teek mare opöödhö; 'ba ki køør ŋøl luup mana näk adïëri, ki bëët bëënynyö mare, bäŋ ŋat manynye nee thiel piny.
english: Touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out: he is excellent in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice: he will not afflict.

anywaa: Kiper manøgønø, jiy lwäär ki eni, kiper eni bäŋ wø lwïthi baŋ jø wø köö ki yïth cwïnyge ni wïthge leer.»
english: Men do therefore fear him: he respecteth not any that are wise of heart.

anywaa: Køøre Wuuö Jwøk luubö aløøe jï Jööp ki ya atuunna, ni kööe,
english: Then the Lord answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said,

anywaa: ni «?Man aŋa ni rïëp pwöc 'moa ki muudhö en ki luup mo bäŋ kwänynyö rege?
english: Who is this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge?

anywaa: 'Ba ennø, jek riï kaawat man wø tïïc dïcwøø. Aani, ï pëënynya pëënynyö ki pïëc nee løgï jïra.
english: Gird up now thy loins like a man; for I will demand of thee, and answer thou me.

anywaa: «?Ïïni ee, kanya caa tier piny ki cwääc, ï nutö? Caanï jïra, ni näk mo ïïna dhaanhø mo tiet luup ŋäyï.
english: Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.

anywaa: ?Aŋa na tïïc yi lïŋ yi dööŋö mar gø? ?Aŋø, bee ïïni? ?Na aŋa na røm gøøni?
english: Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest? or who hath stretched the line upon it?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, tier piny ocwää bäät ŋø, wala aŋa na kwøŋ kït gøøt mar gø cwääc,
english: Whereupon are the foundations thereof fastened? or who laid the corner stone thereof;

anywaa: kanya bëët ceerri mo amöölla ni ge wär na aciel, ni nyïïatwiet maal bëët ge kwöŋŋö ki met ec?
english: When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?

anywaa: «?Aŋa na cïëk dhøgi mo kwör wø tuul pïïyi ki yïthge mo naama dwøŋ, kanya kwönge wøk ki tiet ŋøøm kuya?
english: Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it brake forth, as if it had issued out of the womb?

anywaa: Aani, pøøl atïïa na abïï man uum dëëre ki gø, ni wïra deŋŋe ki muudhö mo cøl døc.
english: When I made the cloud the garment thereof, and thick darkness a swaddlingband for it,

anywaa: Ni tïïa ki nyeŋ kee mo ba løny ki man kaal ge, ni määnynya dhee ko odhuule ki dïdëëdi.
english: And brake up for it my decreed place, and set bars and doors,

anywaa: Køøre aana köö, ni ‹Ï na naama dwøŋ, løny ki man tïŋï riï maal ennø, 'ba kany ba kaalï këët; athaga marï na dwøŋ ŋøl kany nø.›
english: And said, Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further: and here shall thy proud waves be stayed?

anywaa: «?Aŋø, ki mana bëëdï cøøn, amöölla tïïya ïïni nee wø ööe,  wala øw wø wëëga ï niwaany,
english: Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days; and caused the dayspring to know his place;

anywaa: nee bäät piny nee wø maae bäre, ni wëëk jø raay riem wøk yi gø?
english: That it might take hold of the ends of the earth, that the wicked might be shaken out of it?

anywaa: Thuuri ka amädi mo bäät piny tïmö ni nëënö kaamar käde mo ena ri dak.
english: It is turned as clay to the seal; and they stand as a garment.

anywaa: Jø wø tïïc gïïa reyø tar marge abïp, ni ö ceŋ moge moa dege tïŋ maal kiper tïïc gïï mo reyø ni tøcge.
english: And from the wicked their light is withholden, and the high arm shall be broken.

anywaa: «?Ïïni, ïïno nø ci yïth jøør mo naama dwøŋ, wala ki man cäädhï tiet pïï yi kut?
english: Hast thou entered into the springs of the sea? or hast thou walked in the search of the depth?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, dhi kal mar kar bëët jwïëc jøøa no othøw anyooth jïrï? ?Aŋø, dhi kal manøgø ni cøl enø anø jootï?
english: Have the gates of death been opened unto thee? or hast thou seen the doors of the shadow of death?

anywaa: ?A dööŋö mar bäät piny bäre ŋäyï? Caanï jïra, ni näk mo gïïögø bëët ŋäyï.
english: Hast thou perceived the breadth of the earth? declare if thou knowest it all.

anywaa: «?A jöö man wø coony kar bëëtö mar tar en kaa? ?Kar bëët muudhö en kaa?
english: Where is the way where light dwelleth? and as for darkness, where is the place thereof,

anywaa: ?Aŋø, løny jïrï ki man kïthï ge kwörge? ?Uutjïëthe mo wø ci kwör bëëte moge ŋäyï?
english: That thou shouldest take it to the bound thereof, and that thou shouldest know the paths to the house thereof?

anywaa: Ka adïëri møn, ŋäyï, kiper ïïno nø nywøl kar kanyaca. Ïïni, ïïno bëëdö ki cwiiri mo thööth.
english: Knowest thou it, because thou wast then born? or because the number of thy days is great?

anywaa: «?Aŋø, ïïna døny yïth uut kän moa näk pey okan yïthge, wala ki man jootï uut kän moøgø,
english: Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow? or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail,

anywaa: na näk yaa kanø kiper cääŋŋe mo jwør gïï mo leth, ni beege cääŋŋe mo lenye ki mänye?
english: Which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war?

anywaa: ?A jööra ŋø ni wø ci kanya näk tar okeethø yie, wala kanya näk jam wø ööi ki kur tuul-cäŋ okeethø yie bäät piny?
english: By what way is the light parted, which scattereth the east wind upon the earth?

anywaa: ?Aŋa ni wø koony aŋaak man wø pööth pï køthi ki yie, ni wø jiiŋ jöö man wø määr køthi ki yie,
english: Who hath divided a watercourse for the overflowing of waters, or a way for the lightning of thunder;

anywaa: nee ŋöömma näk bäŋ jiy yie jïte ki pïï, ni beeye kanya näk otal na näk bäŋ dhaanhø yie,
english: To cause it to rain on the earth, where no man is; on the wilderness, wherein there is no man;

anywaa: nee ŋöömma näk oränynyö na näk bäŋ gïrpiny yie bëënynye, ni wëëk gø tuuö ki luum?
english: To satisfy the desolate and waste ground; and to cause the bud of the tender herb to spring forth?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, køth da wänni? ?Aŋa na tïïc ŋïth thööy?
english: Hath the rain a father? or who hath begotten the drops of dew?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, rwöc okäla ri ŋø? ?Aŋa na tïïc pey mo wø ööi ki maal,
english: Out of whose womb came the ice? and the hoary frost of heaven, who hath gendered it?

anywaa: kany wø mäk pïïyi ni teek kaamar kïdi, ni bäät pï naama dwøŋ bëëdö no orïëp rwöci?
english: The waters are hid as with a stone, and the face of the deep is frozen.

anywaa: «?Aŋø, løny jïrï ki man twöyï ceeya cwøl ni joonni? ?Aŋø, løny ki man pätï ceer mo wø cwøl ni wäät-odäki?
english: Canst thou bind the sweet influences of Pleiades, or loose the bands of Orion?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, ceer moa näk rege ege cooŋø løny jïrï ki man bwøthï ge kanya näk karge, wala ceey wø cwøl ni liec løny jïrï ki man bwøthï gø ki jø wø caath køøre?
english: Canst thou bring forth Mazzaroth in his season? or canst thou guide Arcturus with his sons?

anywaa: ?A ïïni, ciik mo jap maal ŋäyï? ?Løny jïrï ki man tïïyï ge nee bäät piny kääri ki ge?
english: Knowest thou the ordinances of heaven? canst thou set the dominion thereof in the earth?

anywaa: «?Aŋø, løny jïrï ki man cwötï nee dwørï pïïe yïth pøøl, nee køth mo päl päth bäätï?
english: Canst thou lift up thy voice to the clouds, that abundance of waters may cover thee?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, løny jïrï ki man köömmï agaackøth nee cige kanya manynyï, ni köge jïrï, ni ‹Wa ena kany ennø›?
english: Canst thou send lightnings, that they may go, and say unto thee, Here we are?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, aŋa na mooc cwïny ka acaara? ?A kwany tiet luup ocïpa ŋa jï ŋeth?
english: Who hath put wisdom in the inward parts? or who hath given understanding to the heart?

anywaa: ?Aŋa ni jïre da leec wïc mo løny ki man kwaan pøøl, wala ki man wëëk køth pädhö keda pïï mo kuny piny ka maal,
english: Who can number the clouds in wisdom? or who can stay the bottles of heaven,

anywaa: ni tïm tørri no odhöönh mo ree ee maa na aciel, ni ö pølli ni mecge rege na aciel?
english: When the dust groweth into hardness, and the clods cleave fast together?

anywaa: «?Aŋø, ŋuu dwänynyï dwänynyö ki lääy man came, ni wëëgï nyïï ŋuu moa näk onäk käci jäŋö ki cam,
english: Wilt thou hunt the prey for the lion? or fill the appetite of the young lions,

anywaa: kany wø bëëtge ni geno butö kwör bëëte moge, ni geno møør piny ya abuŋŋö?
english: When they couch in their dens, and abide in the covert to lie in wait?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, aŋa ni wø mooc agaak ki cam, kany wø bëët nyïïe ni ge jwöŋö jï Jwøk, ni ge thääyö kiper bäŋ-cam?
english: Who provideth for the raven his food? when his young ones cry unto God, they wander for lack of meat.

anywaa: «?Aŋø, da gïn mo ŋäyï kiper kany wø ö adëëlli wø nywølge? ?Aŋø, løny jïrï ki man raŋï aŋer kany wø nywøle ki nyïïe?
english: Knowest thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth? or canst thou mark when the hinds do calve?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, løny jïrï ki man kwarï dwäde marge këël kany wø pïïcge ri lwaar marge? ?Aŋø, da gïn mo ŋäyï kiper caae mo lwaar moge?
english: Canst thou number the months that they fulfil? or knowest thou the time when they bring forth?

anywaa: Geni cøŋge wø këëlge piny ni nywølge nyïïge, ni put mäc lwaarri nijwöm dëëtge.
english: They bow themselves, they bring forth their young ones, they cast out their sorrows.

anywaa: Dëët nyïïge døøŋŋø ni putge tïmö ni teek dïpaap, ni putge aay ni ge ba duu baŋ mëëkge.
english: Their young ones are in good liking, they grow up with corn; they go forth, and return not unto them.

anywaa: «?Aŋø, aŋa na tïïc arëëni mo paap nee bëëtge ki wïthge? ?Na aŋa na tïïc ge nee bëëtge ni geno pädö?
english: Who hath sent out the wild ass free? or who hath loosed the bands of the wild ass?

anywaa: Geni, paap acïba jïge na kar bëëtö marge, ni tïm kar bëëtö marge ni bee yi ŋöömma näk bäŋ gïn tuy yie.
english: Whose house I have made the wilderness, and the barren land his dwellings.

anywaa: Ge ŋeethø bäät pääny kiper okiera man wø tägi yie, ni bäŋ dwør ŋat mo kwør geni mo wïnyge.
english: He scorneth the multitude of the city, neither regardeth he the crying of the driver.

anywaa: Geni bäät kïte wø neetge neetø nee jïtge ki kar kwaath kiper dëëtge, ni bëëtge ni ge manynya luum mana mar.
english: The range of the mountains is his pasture, and he searcheth after every green thing.

anywaa: «?Aŋø, løny jïrï ki man pwönynyï jööbi niï tïnynye? ?Aŋø, løny jïrï ki man kïthï gø yi lwaaga marï nee but yie ki wäär?
english: Will the unicorn be willing to serve thee, or abide by thy crib?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, løny jïrï ki man magï gø nee pwödhö marï puure? ?Aŋø, løny jïre ki man kuk gool jïrï?
english: Canst thou bind the unicorn with his band in the furrow? or will he harrow the valleys after thee?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, løny jïrï ki man ŋääthï gø kiper teek mare na dwøŋ? ?Aŋø, tïïc marï na teek løny jïrï ki man leeŋï gø bääte?
english: Wilt thou trust him, because his strength is great? or wilt thou leave thy labour to him?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, løny jïrï ki man ŋääthï gø nee beel moï cooŋe ni kïth ge kar dïn?
english: Wilt thou believe him, that he will bring home thy seed, and gather it into thy barn?

anywaa: «Uudö bwöpe wø tuuŋŋe tuuŋŋö jaak ni yie met, 'ba bwöm moe ko okwöre moe ba caal mo aliil.
english: Gavest thou the goodly wings unto the peacocks? or wings and feathers unto the ostrich?

anywaa: Eni tøŋ moe nywøle yi ŋøøm ni wii gø piny jaak, ni tïm tøŋŋi moe ni lïëth yi tør.
english: Which leaveth her eggs in the earth, and warmeth them in dust,

anywaa: 'Ba ba caare ki man näk mo ge di nyørø ki tiel ni tøcge, wala ki man ö lääc paapi ni cääthge ki bäätge.
english: And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, or that the wild beast may break them.

anywaa: Eni cwïnye ba pädhi kiper nyïïe, ni ge ba maar kwaan kaamar nyïïe, ni ba caare man näk öölö mare ocam paapi jaak.
english: She is hardened against her young ones, as though they were not hers: her labour is in vain without fear;

anywaa: Kiper eni kär mooc Jwøki ki leec wïc, ni bäŋ gïr kwany tiet jammi mo ocïbö jïre.
english: Because God hath deprived her of wisdom, neither hath he imparted to her understanding.

anywaa: 'Ba kany wø peer bwöpe nee reeŋe, eni puta ŋeethø bäät okweeny lääy ki ŋat wø kiiw gø.
english: What time she lifteth up herself on high, she scorneth the horse and his rider.

anywaa: «?Aŋø, løny jïrï ki man cïpï ki teek jï okweeny lääy, wala man kïthï ŋut gø ki gööl?
english: Hast thou given the horse strength? hast thou clothed his neck with thunder?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, eni løny jïrï ki man tïïyï gø nee päre kaamar bäänyö? 'Ba kany wø kudhe ni mare ŋwøc, kännö ki lwär.
english: Canst thou make him afraid as a grasshopper? the glory of his nostrils is terrible.

anywaa: Eni ŋøøm cäye cäyö ki tiete, ni put yie mïnnö ki teek mare, ni put reŋ kar leny.
english: He paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in his strength: he goeth on to meet the armed men.

anywaa: Eni ŋeethø bäät lwär, ni bäŋ gïn mo eni bwøk ki gø, ni eni ba døøa ŋääe ni mare lwär ko opëëllö.
english: He mocketh at fear, and is not affrighted; neither turneth he back from the sword.

anywaa: Eni dööt athëëre mo ena yi køp di wïnynyö, ki tøøŋi moa no opaaø na näk bëëdö ni paŋŋi.
english: The quiver rattleth against him, the glittering spear and the shield.

anywaa: Kany wø wïny dwør tuuŋ mar leny, dëëre puta tïmö ni rïïŋö, ni reeŋe døc ni ŋøøm di källö, ni ba cuŋŋi.
english: He swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage: neither believeth he that it is the sound of the trumpet.

anywaa: 'Ba noo wïny dwør tuuŋ mar leny, eni puta twäätö, ni ŋwääc leny ni kare poot bäär, ni wïny dïŋaŋ mar kwääri mo leny.
english: He saith among the trumpets, Ha, ha; and he smelleth the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.

anywaa: «?Aŋø, akäna wëëgï määtö ki køør leec wïc marï, wala man tïïyï gø nee bwöpe peere ni ee løø tier-piny?
english: Doth the hawk fly by thy wisdom, and stretch her wings toward the south?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, bee ïïni ni wø kööm olwiith nee määt maal kuya, ni geer øde bäät kïte mo ena maal døc?
english: Doth the eagle mount up at thy command, and make her nest on high?

anywaa: Eni bëëdö wï kïdi maal ni buuta yie ki wäär, ni beeye bäät kïdi mana näk kar gwøk røk.
english: She dwelleth and abideth on the rock, upon the crag of the rock, and the strong place.

anywaa: 'Ba ki kaace eni määnyö ki cam, ni këël waŋe ri gø ni kare bäär.
english: From thence she seeketh the prey, and her eyes behold afar off.

anywaa: Nyïïe wø cämö ki rïŋö mo ree poot da remø, ni kany wø dee dëël mo othøw, eni di joodø yie.»
english: Her young ones also suck up blood: and where the slain are, there is she.

anywaa: Køøre Wuuö Jwøk aköö jï Jööp,
english: Moreover the Lord answered Job, and said,

anywaa: na «?Aŋø, ŋat wø jook jiy, pïëmö ki Jwøa en teeki jïre? Beerra man ö ŋat wø car luup mo teek dëër Jwøk ni løk pïëc manøgø!»
english: Shall he that contendeth with the Almighty instruct him? he that reproveth God, let him answer it.

anywaa: Køøre aløk Jööpi jï Wuuö Jwøk ni kööe,
english: Then Job answered the Lord, and said,

anywaa: ni «Aani, aana dhaanhø jaak mo bäŋ kare. ?Olønye jïra nidïï ki man dwöga baŋï ki luubö? Aani dhaa miia miiø ki cera.
english: Behold, I am vile; what shall I answer thee? I will lay mine hand upon my mouth.

anywaa: Aani, aana nø cäännö yie aciel, 'ba a ba cäänni këët; këël na nø cääna ki luup mo thööth, bäŋ luubö mør mo caana këët.»
english: Once have I spoken; but I will not answer: yea, twice; but I will proceed no further.

anywaa: Køøre Wuuö Jwøk Jööp acäänne ki ya atuunna, ni kööe,
english: Then answered the Lord unto Job out of the whirlwind, and said,

anywaa: ni «Jek riï kaawat man wø tïïc dïcwøø; aani ï pëënynya pëënynyö nee løgï jïra.
english: Gird up thy loins now like a man: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.

anywaa: «?Aŋø, ï köö møn ni luup mo wø ŋøla patha adïëri? ?Aŋø, a jällï jällö ni aano bääyö ni keda beerra marï keere?
english: Wilt thou also disannul my judgment? wilt thou condemn me, that thou mayest be righteous?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, cerï teek ni caala mar Jwøk? ?A ïïni, ï määr ki dwøl mo caala mare?
english: Hast thou an arm like God? or canst thou thunder with a voice like him?

anywaa: Ïïni, runy dëërï ka ajiem ki dööŋ-kar, ni rïëpï riï ki wödö ki teek.
english: Deck thyself now with majesty and excellency; and array thyself with glory and beauty.

anywaa: Køny wëër marï wøk kaamar naam mo kwödö døc,  ni raŋŋï jøøgø bëët ni töödö yøø ni wëëgï ge lään wïc.
english: Cast abroad the rage of thy wrath: and behold every one that is proud, and abase him.

anywaa: Jøøgø bëët ni töödö yøø raŋŋï ni dwøgï wïthge piny; ni ö jø wø tïïc gïï mo reyø ni raanynyï geni kwör wø bëëtge yïthge.
english: Look on every one that is proud, and bring him low; and tread down the wicked in their place.

anywaa: Koony geni yïth ŋøøm ge bëët; ni cïëgï geni yïth bwör.
english: Hide them in the dust together; and bind their faces in secret.

anywaa: Køøre aani ki dëëra a öö ni caana gø jïrï ki man näk mo riï piemï piemø ki cer cwïïï na teek.
english: Then will I also confess unto thee that thine own right hand can save thee.

anywaa: «Raŋ lään wø caal ray, na näk yaa cwääö kaawat marï, ni wø bëëdö ni cama luum kaamar dhieŋ.
english: Behold now behemoth, which I made with thee; he eateth grass as an ox.

anywaa: Raŋï mø, eni teek mare ena røk läär mo piere, ni läär mo bäp yie teek døc.
english: Lo now, his strength is in his loins, and his force is in the navel of his belly.

anywaa: Eni jïbe cuŋŋö ni teek kaamar jaath, ni läär mo tiete otïïö ni teek døc.
english: He moveth his tail like a cedar: the sinews of his stones are wrapped together.

anywaa: Ni cuu moe caala nywïënyö mana näk jwïël, ni tiete teek kaamar athøc nywïëny.
english: His bones are as strong pieces of brass; his bones are like bars of iron.

anywaa: Ni cwääc mana cwääy ki gø, ec di thääŋö ni kaala lääy bëët moa cwääc Jwøki; 'ba beeye Jwøk na cwääc gø keere noo bööt gø.
english: He is the chief of the ways of God: he that made him can make his sword to approach unto him.

anywaa: Eni cam mare joode bäät thuuri, kany wø kwääk lääyi yie bëët mo paap.
english: Surely the mountains bring him forth food, where all the beasts of the field play.

anywaa: Ni eni wø buuta tier abøw, ni ree wø kane yo otöök.
english: He lieth under the shady trees, in the covert of the reed, and fens.

anywaa: Eni ree wø kane tier tïpö mar abøw, ni eni bëëdö no ociel ageeta dïër.
english: The shady trees cover him with their shadow; the willows of the brook compass him about.

anywaa: 'Ba kany wø pänh naammi ki bääte, eni ba lwäyi; eni bëëdö kare ni bäŋ gïn lääŋŋe, këël na bëët Naam Jördanni ni kwöta dhi gø.
english: Behold, he drinketh up a river, and hasteth not: he trusteth that he can draw up Jordan into his mouth.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, aŋa ni løny jïre ki man mak gø kany wø näk mo eni rääŋö, wala bïtha gø ni gän gø ki um gø?
english: He taketh it with his eyes: his nose pierceth through snares.

anywaa: «?Aŋø, løny jïrï ki man tuudï lään wø cwøl ni Lëëwatan wøk ko obïth, wala ki man twöyï leebe ki thøøl?
english: Canst thou draw out leviathan with an hook? or his tongue with a cord which thou lettest down?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, løny jïrï ki man rwaagï thøøl ume, wala ki man magï gø ki lëëmme ko obïth?
english: Canst thou put an hook into his nose? or bore his jaw through with a thorn?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, løny jïre ki man kwaac ïïni nee bäth ec marï nyoothï jïre? ?Aŋø, løny jïre ki man mwøth ïïni ki luup mo met?
english: Will he make many supplications unto thee? will he speak soft words unto thee?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, løny ki man jïëc luup moï, kiper nee tïme na laŋŋø jïrï na bäre bäre?
english: Will he make a covenant with thee? wilt thou take him for a servant for ever?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, løny jïrï ki man kwäägï ki gø kaamar wenyø, wala ki man twöï gø piny jï laaŋe moï moa näk nyïïakuue nee kwääkge ki gø?
english: Wilt thou play with him as with a bird? or wilt thou bind him for thy maidens?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, løny jï dïgäthe ki man pïëmge kiper gäte nee ŋeewge? ?Aŋø, løny ki man pääŋge gø yïthakicge?
english: Shall the companions make a banquet of him? shall they part him among the merchants?

anywaa: ?Aŋø, løny jïrï ki man cööbï kwöt dëëre ka arøøc, wala ki man cööbï wïïe ki waragööy?
english: Canst thou fill his skin with barbed irons? or his head with fish spears?

anywaa: 'Ba noo kïthï cerï bääte, wär put ŋäc ni leny dagø, ni eni ba cäŋï nwøyø këët na bäre bäre.
english: Lay thine hand upon him, remember the battle, do no more.

anywaa: Ŋato päär gø ki man mak gø, ba løny jïre, këël ki man neeni ki waŋ bee lwär mo dwøŋ døc;
english: Behold, the hope of him is in vain: shall not one be cast down even at the sight of him?

anywaa: ni bäŋ ŋat mo kam gø, kiper eni wïnni døc. ?A ennø, aŋa ni løny jïre ki man gëëme ki aani?
english: None is so fierce that dare stir him up: who then is able to stand before me?

anywaa: ?Aŋa ni bääta da pïïdö mare nee eni cunna? Kiper jammi moi bëët ni en tier maal en beege 'moa.
english: Who hath prevented me, that I should repay him? whatsoever is under the whole heaven is mine.

anywaa: «Aani, a ba lïŋi ki man cääna kiper tiet läänögø, wala teek mare wala yi cwääc mare.
english: I will not conceal his parts, nor his power, nor his comely proportion.

anywaa: ?Aŋa ni løny jïre ki man gööny koothi mare wøk dëëre? ?Aŋa ni løny jïre ki man daŋ kwöt dëëre wøk man ni ree dwalø na ariiø en?
english: Who can discover the face of his garment? or who can come to him with his double bridle?

anywaa: ?Aŋa ni many man jap dhi gø, kiper nyämme moe bee gïï mo di lwäyö ki ge.
english: Who can open the doors of his face? his teeth are terrible round about.

anywaa: Dïŋääe otïïö keda kööt leny mo ocaanø, ni ge bëëdö ni rege gääbö na aciel;
english: His scales are his pride, shut up together as with a close seal.

anywaa: ni man nø kare cään ki maya, ni bäŋ jamø mo pöödhi ki yïthakicge.
english: One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.

anywaa: Geni, ge bëëdö ni rege gääbö ki møga, ni ge bëëdö ni rege ege maa ni bäŋ gïn mo pää ge.
english: They are joined one to another, they stick together, that they cannot be sundered.

anywaa: Kany wø kweere ki tham, tar puta nikwiil, ni put nyeŋŋe mëënynyö kaamar däär cäŋ mar amöölla.
english: By his neesings a light doth shine, and his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.

anywaa: Maac mo liel wø ööa wøk ki dhee, ni ö piit maaci ni pele.
english: Out of his mouth go burning lamps, and sparks of fire leap out.

anywaa: Eni jïrö nitul ki ume, ni tïme kaamar daa thaal mo twak mo othäänhö bäät moonni.
english: Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, as out of a seething pot or caldron.

anywaa: Jam jwïëy mare, bel di äbö, ni ö maaci mo liel ni ö wøk ki dhee.
english: His breath kindleth coals, and a flame goeth out of his mouth.

anywaa: Ŋute bëëdö ni teek døc, ni ŋat wø joot gø puta lwäyö ki gø.
english: In his neck remaineth strength, and sorrow is turned into joy before him.

anywaa: Rïŋ dëëre teek, ni ree döötö no ogääbö, ni bëëdö ni teek kaamar nywïënyö.
english: The flakes of his flesh are joined together: they are firm in themselves; they cannot be moved.

anywaa: Cwïnye teek kaamar kïdi ni ba lwäär, ni bëëdö kaamar kïn guur.
english: His heart is as firm as a stone; yea, as hard as a piece of the nether millstone.

anywaa: Kanyo näk mo eno ö maal, jøøa teek ge puta lwäyö, ni putge bwøk ni døøge ŋäthge kany wø tuuŋ ree.
english: When he raiseth up himself, the mighty are afraid: by reason of breakings they purify themselves.

anywaa: Këël da opëëllö, wala tøŋ, wala atheerø, wala waragööy mo ööa baŋe, bäŋgø mo bööt gø.
english: The sword of him that layeth at him cannot hold: the spear, the dart, nor the habergeon.

anywaa: Nywïënyö mana näk bääŋ kwaane kaamar theeŋ bëëlö, ni kwaan nywïënyö mana näk jwïël kaamar jaath mo otøp.
english: He esteemeth iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood.

anywaa: Eni ba reŋi ka atheerø, ni kïdi man wø thööri ki gø nëëni keda lethø ki jïre.
english: The arrow cannot make him flee: slingstones are turned with him into stubble.

anywaa: Na athøra neete keda luum mo otal, ni eni wø ŋeethø bäät ŋat wø thöör gø ki tøŋ.
english: Darts are counted as stubble: he laugheth at the shaking of a spear.

anywaa: Ni kwök mo wø en bäp yie beth kaamar piit dak mo othøw, ni kew ŋøøm kaamar gïr dïn man wø tuut dhäki.
english: Sharp stones are under him: he spreadeth sharp pointed things upon the mire.

anywaa: Eni kut di tïïö ni wälli kaamar pïï mo twak yi dak, ni tïïc pï naama dwøŋ ni dhulli kaamar maaw mo twak yi dak.
english: He maketh the deep to boil like a pot: he maketh the sea like a pot of ointment.

anywaa: Ni kany wø pöödhe ki yie puta nitwääc ni tar, ni put nëënö kaamar jïër mo tar.
english: He maketh a path to shine after him; one would think the deep to be hoary.

anywaa: Eni bäŋ gïn mo rööma gø bäät piny, ni eno cwääö ni bäŋ gïn mo lwääre.
english: Upon earth there is not his like, who is made without fear.

anywaa: Eni wø lwïthö baŋ lääy mo wø töödö bëët ni raŋ ge ni ee taaø, ni bëëdö ni ena nyeya bäätge.»
english: He beholdeth all high things: he is a king over all the children of pride.

anywaa: Køøre aløk Jööpi jï Wuuö Jwøk ni kööe,
english: Then Job answered the Lord, and said,

anywaa: ni «Aani, ŋääa ni jammi bëët løny ki tïïc jïrï; ni tïïe moï moa näk iï cïp piny, bäŋgø mo kääŋi rege ni ba tïïc.
english: I know that thou canst do every thing, and that no thought can be withholden from thee.

anywaa: Ïïni, ïïna pëëö, na ‹?Aŋa ni rïëp pwöc 'moa ki muudhö en ki luup mo bäŋ kwänynyö rege?› Ka adïëri møn, aana cäänö ki luup mo tietge kära kwanyø na karge, ni beege luup mo rëëma ec mo kaala acaara mara.
english: Who is he that hideth counsel without knowledge? therefore have I uttered that I understood not; things too wonderful for me, which I knew not.

anywaa: Ïïna köö, ni ‹Cek ïthï naa cäänna; aani ï pëënynya pëënynyö nee løgï jïra.›
english: Hear, I beseech thee, and I will speak: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.

anywaa: 'Ba aani, luup moï awïnynya ki ïtha, 'ba ennø ïïna jooda ki waŋa kiree.
english: I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee.

anywaa: Kiper manøgønø, aani dëëra ajääla, ni køba raay 'moa naa bëëdö yi tør ki yi bur.»
english: Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.

anywaa: 'Ba Wuuö Jwøk kanya nø caan luupögø jï Jööp, ena köö ki Elipath nyï Tëman, ni «Aana gootø ki ïïni ki nyïïawäätï moa na ariiø, kiper bäŋ luup mo karge mo you caanø kipera kaawat mana tïïc dhaanhnha ma Jööp.
english: And it was so, that after the Lord had spoken these words unto Job, the Lord said to Eliphaz the Temanite, My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends: for ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath.

anywaa: Kiper manøgønø, lwötu ki rwädhe abïriiø ki nyöök rööm abïriiø, ni cou baŋ dhaanhnha ma Jööp ni cïpu ge no olämme mo wø waaŋ bäre kiper dëëtu. 'Ba dhaanhnha ma Jööp olämö kiperu, ni ööa ni jïëa lam mare, ni bäŋe gïn mo tïïa dëëtu këët ki køør bøøl maru. Uuni, bäŋ luup mo karge mo you caanø kipera kaawat mana tïïc dhaanhnha ma Jööp.»
english: Therefore take unto you now seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you: for him will I accept: lest I deal with you after your folly, in that ye have not spoken of me the thing which is right, like my servant Job.

anywaa: Køøre Elipath nyï Tëman, ki Bildat nyï Cuua, ki Cöpar nyï Nayma, gïna caan Wuuö Jwøki jïge atïïcge; ni ö Wuuö Jwøki ni jïëc lam mar Jööp.
english: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did according as the Lord commanded them: the Lord also accepted Job.

anywaa: 'Ba køør kanya läm Jööpi kiper nyïïawääte, bëëtö mare adwøk Wuuö Jwøki kare, ni mooc gø ki jammi mo opöödhö ni kaala moa nut jïre dïkwøŋ.
english: And the Lord turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before.

anywaa: Nyïïmenni bëët moa näk cwøw ki moa näk mään, ki jiy bëët moa ŋäc eni dïkwøŋ, gena öö ni cämge ki eni paare.
