anywaa: Kär iï mïnnö kany wø päth nyimänni marï, ni kär cwïnyï døøc mo met kany wø cwany tiere;
english: Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth:

anywaa: nee gïna tïïyï ba tïme ni raac jï Wuuö Jwøk noo neen gø, ni paany wëër mare bäät ŋatøgø.
english: Lest the Lord see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.

anywaa: Kär wïïï kierï ka acaara kiper bëët jøøa reyø, ni ba keeyï per bëët jø raay;
english: Fret not thyself because of evil men, neither be thou envious at the wicked;

anywaa: kiper ŋat raay, aŋuun bëëtö mare gööya piny ni raac, ni tïm jøøa reyø ni caala lamba mo cäätha baŋ thøø.
english: For there shall be no reward to the evil man; the candle of the wicked shall be put out.

anywaa: Nyie wääda, lwäär Wuuö Jwøk ki nyeya, ni ba dwätï ki jø wø many ageem;
english: My son, fear thou the Lord and the king: and meddle not with them that are given to change:

anywaa: kiper gïï mo leth ocwöp dëëtge, ?Aŋa ni ŋäc ränynyö mano ööi ki baŋ Wuuö Jwøk ki nyeya?
english: For their calamity shall rise suddenly; and who knoweth the ruin of them both?

anywaa: Moi thuwø beege luup pwöc mo jøøa wïthge leer: Ki man ŋøl luup mo rege da ajeeny ba beer.
english: These things also belong to the wise. It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment.

anywaa: Ŋat wø köö jï ŋat raay, ni «Marï beer,» eno cien jiyi, ni jääli ya lwaaki bäre;
english: He that saith unto the wicked, Thou art righteous; him shall the people curse, nations shall abhor him:

anywaa: 'ba jø wø jääl jøøa reyø, otïmö ni beer jïge, ni ö gwïëthi mana beer ni en bäätge.
english: But to them that rebuke him shall be delight, and a good blessing shall come upon them.

anywaa: Ŋat wø dwögi ki luubö ma adïëri wø nyootha mëër mare mana näk kare.
english: Every man shall kiss his lips that giveth a right answer.

anywaa: Jiiŋ dëërï dïkwøŋ kiper tïï lak paac, ni jiiŋŋï pwödhö marï, køøre nø, paac marï ogeerï.
english: Prepare thy work without, and make it fit for thyself in the field; and afterwards build thine house.

anywaa: Kär luubö mo bäŋ tiere kïth bäät wadu kar løøk, ni ba maaŋŋï wïth jiy ki luup mo ocur dhiï.
english: Be not a witness against thy neighbour without cause; and deceive not with thy lips.

anywaa: Kär niï köö, na «A tïïö dëëre ki gïrpiny kaa mana tïïe dëëra, naa coola gø dëëre ki køør mana tïïe dëëra.»
english: Say not, I will do so to him as he hath done to me: I will render to the man according to his work.

anywaa: Aana cør buut pwöth beel mar ŋata dëëre leth, ki buut pwöth omøki mar ŋata näk ba cädö,
english: I went by the field of the slothful, and by the vineyard of the man void of understanding;

anywaa: ni neena pwöth no otuy ki koodhi bäre, ni dï pwödhö bäre ouum akatanyøŋŋi, ni kiir kïdi mana en lakge opädhö.
english: And, lo, it was all grown over with thorns, and nettles had covered the face thereof, and the stone wall thereof was broken down.

anywaa: Køøre aneena ni caara gø døøc ki cwïnya, ni raŋa tiere ni jïta ki pwöc.
english: Then I saw, and considered it well: I looked upon it, and received instruction.

anywaa: Ï ni wø laar butö ki nyi kany mo thiinh, ni wø laarï narø ki nyi kany mo thiinh; ï ni wø laar thäänhö ki ceŋŋï nee riï jwömï ki nyi kany mo thiinh,
english: Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:

anywaa: bëët can ööa bäätï kaamar kuu, ni pïïc ränynyö bäätï kaamar ŋat twëër.
english: So shall thy poverty come as one that travelleth; and thy want as an armed man.

anywaa: Moi thuwø beege pwöc leec wïc mo Cølöman, moa ŋwaal jic Edhekaya piny, eni na nyeny Juuda.
english: These are also proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.

anywaa: Ki man bëët Jwøki ni tiet luup møøk ee kanø beeye ajiem jïre, ni ki man many tiet luup beeye ajiem jï nyeye.
english: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings is to search out a matter.

anywaa: Acaac nyeye karge bäär ni tietge ba joot, kaawat man wø bëët maalli ni kare bäär, kaawat man wø bëët tiet ŋøømmi ni kare bäär.
english: The heaven for height, and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings is unsearchable.

anywaa: Noo leenyï gwel-bïrö, käl apøk nyal wøk, køøre løny jï dïthädhi ki man tïïe ki gïn mo mïërö ki gø;
english: Take away the dross from the silver, and there shall come forth a vessel for the finer.

anywaa: jøøa reyø käl wøk nyïm nyeya, køøre wälu mare tiere okëët piny ki køør bëënynyö.
english: Take away the wicked from before the king, and his throne shall be established in righteousness.

anywaa: Kär dëërï døøc mo dwøŋ nyïm nyeya, ni ba kööï ni da karï dï jøøa kwörge døøŋŋø;
english: Put not forth thyself in the presence of the king, and stand not in the place of great men:

anywaa: kiper beerra eni ki man køøi ki ïïni, ni «Dää kany,» ni kaala man dwøk ï piny nyïm ŋata kare dwøŋ. Gïn mo iï nø joot ki waŋï,
english: For better it is that it be said unto thee, Come up hither; than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince whom thine eyes have seen.

anywaa: kärï laar läät baŋ løøk ki gø, ?kiper agïnaŋø noo tïïyï ya aŋuunne, kanyo näk mo wadu wïïï ee lääö?
english: Go not forth hastily to strive, lest thou know not what to do in the end thereof, when thy neighbour hath put thee to shame.

anywaa: Caan luubö marï keerï ki wadu, ni ba dhääï luup ŋat mør wøk;
english: Debate thy cause with thy neighbour himself; and discover not a secret to another:

anywaa: niï ba jøøŋ ŋato wïny gø, ni ö gïna raaci noo caan kiperï ni ba cuŋŋe.
english: Lest he that heareth it put thee to shame, and thine infamy turn not away.

anywaa: Luubö mo caan no orømø mïërö kaamar warkey mo othiiø ni caala nyïïoleem mo ocïp ya athaanh gwel-bïrö.
english: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver.

anywaa: Juuk mar ŋat mo wïïe leer mïërö jï ïth mo wïnyö, kaawat man wø mïër gwel ïthi mar warkey ki jap mïërö ma warkey.
english: As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, so is a wise reprover upon an obedient ear.

anywaa: Ŋat mo oŋäädhö man wø jääŋŋi caala pïï mo ŋec kany wø tïme na kar kac, kiper jwïëc kwäärö mare wø wëëge duuö.
english: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to them that send him: for he refresheth the soul of his masters.

anywaa: Ŋat wø buuk muuy mo ba cïbe, caala pøøl ki jamø mo öö mo ba cïpi ki køth.
english: Whoso boasteth himself of a false gift is like clouds and wind without rain.

anywaa: Cäänö ni cwïny ocïp piny acaac kwäärö wø di wiilø, ni ö leepi mo jööm ni dwøk luubö piny mo teek.
english: By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.

anywaa: Kany wø jootï maar kïc, cam mana näk orømø keere, 'ba ni näk mo iï puudhö, ï ŋøøk ki gø.
english: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.

anywaa: Nook tierï ki wääth po wadu, nee ba jøøme ni männe ki ïïni.
english: Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour's house; lest he be weary of thee, and so hate thee.

anywaa: Ŋat wø kïth luum tööt bäät watge tïïya gïn mo leth kaamar opëëllö ka athøc leny ka atheerø mo beth.
english: A man that beareth false witness against his neighbour is a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.

anywaa: Dhaanhø man wø tïïö ki gïï mo reyø ki piny, ki man ŋääth eni cäŋ gïï mo leth caala lëëö mo ocam akøøgø, ni caal tielø mo obäp.
english: Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble is like a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.

anywaa: Ki man wärö ki dudi jï ŋat mo cwïnye peek caala man wø bëët dhaanhø yi köö na aleeŋŋa mare okäl wøk, ni caala atwøda mo okïthö ki nyïjaa.
english: As he that taketh away a garment in cold weather, and as vinegar upon nitre, so is he that singeth songs to an heavy heart.

anywaa: Ni näk mo nyimännï obup, wär mooyï ki cam nee came; ni näk mo ree da riew, wär mooyï ki pïï nee maadhe;
english: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:

anywaa: kiper noo tïïyï gïnögø, ï cooŋa cuk mo oäpö dï wïïe, 'ba Wuuö Jwøk ïïno cunne.
english: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord shall reward thee.

anywaa: Da jamø mo kwödö mo wø kännö ki køth, ni leep mo waya nyeŋ wø duua agääde.
english: The north wind driveth away rain: so doth an angry countenance a backbiting tongue.

anywaa: Ki man bëët dhaanhe thaŋ agööla, beerra eni ni kaala man bëëdö yi øtø aciel ki dhaagø ma ŋat pïëm.
english: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house.

anywaa: Luubö mo nyään mo met mo käla kany mo bäär caala man wø met pïïyi mo ŋec jï ŋat mo oööl ki riew,
english: As cold waters to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.

anywaa: Ŋat mo mare beer man wø jøøm ni jïëe ki mar ŋat raay, beeye gïn mo raac kaamar pï jøøro mo oduubö.
english: A righteous man falling down before the wicked is as a troubled fountain, and a corrupt spring.

anywaa: Patha gïn mo beer ki man cam maar kïc ni päl, ni patha gïn mo beer ki man many wödö kiper dëël.
english: It is not good to eat much honey: so for men to search their own glory is not glory.

anywaa: Dhaanhø mo dëëre ba jooe keere caala pääny mo kiir mare onyaa piny.
english: He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.

anywaa: Kaawat man wø bëët peyi ki öörö, ni bëët køthi ni kär rømø ki kar kac, wödö thuwø kär rømø ki ŋat mo wïïe känni.
english: As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honour is not seemly for a fool.

anywaa: Acïëni mo bäŋ tiere ba pïï bäät dhaanhø; tïmö ni caala man wø määt adhieŋŋi ka agweec jaak.
english: As the bird by wandering, as the swallow by flying, so the curse causeless shall not come.

anywaa: Acwäät rømi ka ŋat mo wïïe känni, ni caala man bëëde na alaŋŋa rømi ko okweeny, ni kaw rømi ka arëën.
english: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool's back.

anywaa: Kär niï dwøga luum ŋat mo wïïe känni ki køør luup bøøl moe, niï ba tïmï niï caala eni.
english: Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest thou also be like unto him.

anywaa: Dwøk luum ŋat mo wïïe känni no orømø ki luup bøøl moe, nee ba kööe ni wïïe leer ki jïre.
english: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own conceit.

anywaa: Ŋat wø jääŋ dwøl ki dhaanhø mo wïïe känni, wø ŋøra tiete keere, ni maath ränynyö kaamar pïï.
english: He that sendeth a message by the hand of a fool cutteth off the feet, and drinketh damage.

anywaa: Pwöc man wø cur dhøk jøøa wïthge känni caala tier dhaanhø ma puuth man wø lïëri jaak.
english: The legs of the lame are not equal: so is a parable in the mouth of fools.

anywaa: Ŋat wø wøør ŋat mo wïïe känni caala ŋat wø twöö baarø ro okwat leethïk nee ba reeŋe.
english: As he that bindeth a stone in a sling, so is he that giveth honour to a fool.

anywaa: Pwöc man wø cur dhøk jøøa wïthge känni caala koodhi mo wø käär ŋat mo omeerri ki cere.
english: As a thorn goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.

anywaa: Ŋat wø kïth ŋat mo wïïe känni yi tïïc ni wø røøth ŋat mo cäädhö jöö jaak nee kïth yi tïïc, caala ŋat mo thöödhö jaak ka athëëre ni mooc dëët jiy ki ŋwiili.
english: The great God that formed all things both rewardeth the fool, and rewardeth transgressors.

anywaa: Ŋat mo wïïe känni man wø nøøc bëët bøølø mare, caala gwök ni wø døø baŋ ŋwøge.
english: As a dog returneth to his vomit, so a fool returneth to his folly.

anywaa: ?Dhaanhø mo köö ni wïïe leer ki jïre ajootï? Da ŋäädhe mo thiinh kiper ŋat mo wïïe känni ni kaala teeŋ ŋatøgø.
english: Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? there is more hope of a fool than of him.

anywaa: Ŋat leth dëël cwïnye wø di thwølø ni kööe, ni «Da ŋuu øtjöö, ni da ŋuu dï thwørø.»
english: The slothful man saith, There is a lion in the way; a lion is in the streets.

anywaa: Ŋat leth dëël wø bëëdö ni løøŋŋa ree kar niine mare, kaawat man wø ö balbala wø løøŋ ree kare.
english: As the door turneth upon his hinges, so doth the slothful upon his bed.

anywaa: Ŋat leth dëël cere wø rwaage ya awal baŋ kwön, 'ba eni dëëre jääk ki man kïth cere dhee.
english: The slothful hideth his hand in his bosom; it grieveth him to bring it again to his mouth.

anywaa: Ŋat leth dëël ki jïre ni leerra wïïe keere ni kaala jiy abïriiø mo luup wø dwøkge ni ege caarø.
english: The sluggard is wiser in his own conceit than seven men that can render a reason.

anywaa: Ŋat wø dier pïëm mo paa mare caala ŋat mo maga gwök mo path ki ïth gø. 18-19
english: He that passeth by, and meddleth with strife belonging not to him, is like one that taketh a dog by the ears.

anywaa: Ŋat wø cøøk watge, ka aŋuudi ni kööe, ni «Mara kwääk jaak,» caala dhaanhø ma bøøl man wø thöödhö ki dhøk jenni mo rege da mäc, ka athëëre, ki gïï wø duunni ki thøø.
Kany mo bäŋ dïwääc nyeŋ yie, pïëm wø døøa piny yie, kaawat man wø thøw maaci kany wø thum jer maaci.
english: Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: so where there is no talebearer, the strife ceaseth.

anywaa: Ŋat pïëm, pïëm wø di nyebø kaamar maac, kaawat man ö belli ni wø tïïcge cuk ni kwayø, ni ö jenni ni wø tïïcge maac ni liel.
english: As coals are to burning coals, and wood to fire; so is a contentious man to kindle strife.

anywaa: Luup dïwääc nyeŋ caala cam mo met, ni wø dønynya yi cwïny dhaanhø bäre.
english: The words of a talebearer are as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.

anywaa: Ŋat mo dhee cara mëër ni cwïnye raac caala dak mo jøørra dï ŋääe keere ki warkey.
english: Burning lips and a wicked heart are like a potsherd covered with silver dross.

anywaa: Nyimän luupe wø di tøøtø ki dhee, 'ba cwïnye wø kaanna jap cwøk.
english: He that hateth dissembleth with his lips, and layeth up deceit within him;

anywaa: Kany wø cääne ni luup ee døøc mo met, kär niï ŋäätha gø, kiper da gïïpinyi abïriiø yi cwïnye mo ec raac ki ge døc.
english: When he speaketh fair, believe him not: for there are seven abominations in his heart.

anywaa: Këël män mare dee kanø ki køør cwøk mare, rääö mare tïmö ni ŋäc dï acooŋa bäre.
english: Whose hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shewed before the whole congregation.

anywaa: Ŋat wø koony buur kiper watge, eni ki dëëre pätha yie, ni ŋat wø cöör kïdi bäät watge, oduu bääte keere.
english: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him.

anywaa: Leep mo cara tööt män ki jiy moa näk ee caannø, ni dhøk mo tøøta luup wø wëëga jiy ränynyö.
english: A lying tongue hateth those that are afflicted by it; and a flattering mouth worketh ruin.

anywaa: Kärï ŋwöö kiper gïno tïïyï diøø, kiper gïno tägi yi cäŋ mar diøø kuyï.
english: Boast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.

anywaa: Beerra man tïme niï pwøya ŋat mørri, ni paa ï ki dhiï keerï, ni beerra man tïmï niï pwøya ŋat mo pathi, ni paa ï ki leebï keerï.
english: Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips.

anywaa: Ŋäc ni kïdi peek, na akwöö peek thuwø, 'ba amena mar ŋat mo wïïe känni kaala gïïögø karge riet.
english: A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fool's wrath is heavier than them both.

anywaa: Wëër cïïmma tïïc gïï mo reyø ni räänyö kaamar jwïïö. ?'Ba aŋa ni maar cuŋŋö nyïm ŋat mo cwïnye okëënynyö?
english: Wrath is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before envy?

anywaa: Juuk mo onyoodhø beerra eni ni kaala mëër mo juuk mare kär nyoodhø.
english: Open rebuke is better than secret love.

anywaa: Wat wø tïïya adïëri kany wø pwöny ïïni ki pwöc mo jwørï jwørø, 'ba nyimän, këël dhøk dee nuumö, mare cwøk.
english: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.

anywaa: Ŋat mo ojäŋ wø kweer ki maar kïc, 'ba ki jï ŋat mo obup, këël gïn mo keec wø tïmö ni ŋweeth.
english: The full soul loatheth an honeycomb; but to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.

anywaa: Ŋat wø wïdi jaak ni wec paare caala wenyø man wø wec øde ni määde jaak.
english: As a bird that wandereth from her nest, so is a man that wandereth from his place.

anywaa: Maar riia ki gïn wø jïye ŋwääi ni met, cwïny wø døøcge mo met; kaawat manøgø thuwø, pwöc nyawat ec wø døøye mo met.
english: Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart: so doth the sweetness of a man's friend by hearty counsel.

anywaa: Kär niï weya nyawadu ki nyawat wäru, ni kany wø enï yïth gïï mo leth, kärï many køny baŋ cöögu na kare bäär; theemma wat mo kare cään ni kaala cöögö mo kare bäär.
english: Thine own friend, and thy father's friend, forsake not; neither go into thy brother's house in the day of thy calamity: for better is a neighbour that is near than a brother far off.

anywaa: Nyie wääda, bëëdï ni wïïï leer, ni døøyï cwïnya mo met, kiper nee lønye jïra ki man dwöga ki luubö jï ŋat wø jøøŋ aani.
english: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, that I may answer him that reproacheth me.

anywaa: Ŋat mo waŋe riek, gïna raac wø di joodø ni kan ree, 'ba ŋat ma acaara mare thiinh wø pätha yi gø, ni jwør gïï mo leth.
english: A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself; but the simple pass on, and are punished.

anywaa: Ŋat mo ojïëy na kar ŋat pïïdö marï ma wëëllö, abïïne wär lwørï, ni magï eni na dïgïti kanyo cïp ree na kar dhaanhø mo path.
english: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger, and take a pledge of him for a strange woman.

anywaa: Ŋat wø laar pää ki bäc øw ni gwïëth watge ni dwøre ee tïŋ maal, mare di kwaanø na acïëni.
english: He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him.

anywaa: Dhaagø ma ŋat pïëm kännö ki öölö kaamar øtø mo cwïër dïcäŋ wø bëët køthi ni pädhö.
english: A continual dropping in a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike.

anywaa: Ki man jook dhaagø ma ŋat pïëm nëëna man jook jamø, ni caala man mec maaw ki cenø.
english: Whosoever hideth her hideth the wind, and the ointment of his right hand, which bewrayeth itself.

anywaa: Nywïënyö wø paak ka nywïënyö watge; kaawat manøgø thuwø, dhaanhø wø bëënynyi ka ri watge.
english: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.

anywaa: Ŋat wø gwøk olaam, nyïï gø came camø, ni ŋat wø gwøk kwäärö mare jïtö ki wödö.
english: Whoso keepeth the fig tree shall eat the fruit thereof: so he that waiteth on his master shall be honoured.

anywaa: Kaawat man wø nëën täärnyïm dhaanhø na kare ki yïth pïï, cwïny dhaanhø thuwø wø nyootha bëëtö mar dhaanhø.
english: As in water face answereth to face, so the heart of man to man.

anywaa: Kaawat man wø bëët kar bëët jwïëc jøøa no othøw ni ba jäŋ ki jiy, waŋ dhaanhø thuwø ba jäŋ ki jap bäät piny.
english: Hell and destruction are never full; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.

anywaa: Gwel-bïrö ki warkey beeye maa thäth ni wø raŋi ki gø; ni mana en cwïny dhaanhø wø raŋ ka køør man wø pwøc eni.
english: As the fining pot for silver, and the furnace for gold; so is a man to his praise.

anywaa: Ŋat dïkät wïc këël diï wälö ki leek yi pany kaamar beel, bëët bøøl mare bäŋ doo aay dëëre.
english: Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar among wheat with a pestle, yet will not his foolishness depart from him.

anywaa: Bëëdï ni bëët dïëk moï ŋäyï na wøp, ni këëllï wïïï dëët dhäk moï,
english: Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.

anywaa: kiper jap kwärö bäŋ wø bëëdö na bäre bäre, ni dööŋ kar mar dhaanhø bäŋ wø bëëdö ni nut ki yïth beenhnhe bëët.
english: For riches are not for ever: and doth the crown endure to every generation?

anywaa: Kany wø waaŋ luummi, ni ö mana nyäänni ni lødhe, ni nyaar luum mana en lak thuuri, ni cooŋi piny kiper dhäk,
english: The hay appeareth, and the tender grass sheweth itself, and herbs of the mountains are gathered.

anywaa: ïïni, ï jïtö ki dum dëërï ki røk rööm moï, ni ö atëëe moï ni duunge ki gät pwödhö.
english: The lambs are for thy clothing, and the goats are the price of the field.

anywaa: Ni bëët caa atëëe no orømø kiper cam marï ki paarï bäre, këël kiper jø tïïc moï thuwø.
english: And thou shalt have goats' milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, and for the maintenance for thy maidens.

anywaa: Ŋat raay wø böö jaak ni bäŋ ŋat mo oŋwiec køøre, 'ba ŋata mare beer cwïnye da cer ni caala ŋuu.
english: The wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion.

anywaa: Kany wø bëët paaci ki bëëtö mo raac, kwääri mo tïïö ka ageeme wø tïmö ni thööth, 'ba paac mo käära ŋat mo cädö ni wïïe leer ruu ki kany mo bäär.
english: For the transgression of a land many are the princes thereof: but by a man of understanding and knowledge the state thereof shall be prolonged.

anywaa: Dhaanhø mo can man wø caar ŋata can, caala køth man wø raany caammi.
english: A poor man that oppresseth the poor is like a sweeping rain which leaveth no food.

anywaa: Jø wø wec ciik Jwøk wø bëëdö ni pwøya jøøa reyø, 'ba jø wø gwøk ciik wø pïëmö ki jøøa reyø.
english: They that forsake the law praise the wicked: but such as keep the law contend with them.

anywaa: Jøøa reyø tier ŋøl ma adïëri bäŋ wø ci cwïnyge, 'ba jø wø many Wuuö Jwøk tier gø wø cøøa cwïnyge bäre.
english: Evil men understand not judgment: but they that seek the Lord understand all things.

anywaa: Beerra eni ki man bëët dhaanhe ni can mo caatha jöö mo thïïŋ, ni kaala ŋat mo okwär mo caatha jöö mo oköömmö.
english: Better is the poor that walketh in his uprightness, than he that is perverse in his ways, though he be rich.

anywaa: Nyilaal man wø gwøk ciik Jwøk, gïna beer ki gïna raac ŋääe, 'ba nyilaal man wø cäädhi ki jø wärö wø duua lään wïc jï wänni.
english: Whoso keepeth the law is a wise son: but he that is a companion of riotous men shameth his father.

anywaa: Ŋat wø wëëk jape mac nee cool ni da wïthge wø cooŋa geni nee dööŋge jï ŋat wø nyooth mëër jï jøøa can.
english: He that by usury and unjust gain increaseth his substance, he shall gather it for him that will pity the poor.

anywaa: Ŋat wø løø ïthe wøk ki man ba wïny ciik Jwøk, këël lam mare kiree tïmö na gïn mo yi Jwøk raac ki gø.
english: He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination.

anywaa: Ŋat wø bwøth jøøa marge thïïŋ nee gaage wøk jöör raay, pätha yi buur mare keere; 'ba jø wø bëëtö marge thïïŋ, gïn mo beer odööŋ jïge.
english: Whoso causeth the righteous to go astray in an evil way, he shall fall himself into his own pit: but the upright shall have good things in possession.

anywaa: Ŋat mo okwär wø cädö ni wïïe leer ki jïre, 'ba ŋat mo can mo wïïe da acaara, gïïa en cwïny ŋatøgø di joodø.
english: The rich man is wise in his own conceit; but the poor that hath understanding searcheth him out.

anywaa: Kany wø tïm paaci ni ena ceŋ jøøa beyø, wø da ajiem mo päl, 'ba kany wø ö jøøa reyø maal, jiy rege wø kaange kaannø.
english: When righteous men do rejoice, there is great glory: but when the wicked rise, a man is hidden.

anywaa: Ŋat wø kaan bääyö mare ba bëënynyi, 'ba ŋat wø køp raay moe ni wec geni, mëëy Jwøk di joodø.
english: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.

anywaa: Gwïëth en bäät ŋat wø bëëdö ni lwäära Wuuö Jwøk cooth, 'ba ŋat wø døøc cwïnye mo teek pätha yïth gïï mo leth.
english: Happy is the man that feareth alway: but he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief.

anywaa: Ŋat mo raac mo bëëdö na kwäärö bäät jøøa can caala ŋuu man wø ŋäri, ni caal odïëk mo owär.
english: As a roaring lion, and a ranging bear; so is a wicked ruler over the poor people.

anywaa: Kwäärö man wø caar jiy, wïïe bäŋ acaara, 'ba ŋat wø kwier jammi mo joot ki jöö mo patha adïëri wø døøya nïr kwøw moe mo thööth.
english: The prince that wanteth understanding is also a great oppressor: but he that hateth covetousness shall prolong his days.

anywaa: Ŋat mo dëëre da kwör dhaanhø mo rem gø ee køny piny bëëdö ni bëënna böö këël aŋuun thøø mare; eni, kär dee ŋat køny gø.
english: A man that doeth violence to the blood of any person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him.

anywaa: Ŋat wø bëëdö ni caatha jöö mo thïïŋ di piemø, 'ba ŋat wø bëëdö ni caatha jöö mo oköömmö laara päth yi ränynyö.
english: Whoso walketh uprightly shall be saved: but he that is perverse in his ways shall fall at once.

anywaa: Ŋat wø puur ŋöömö mare jïtö ki cam mo päl, 'ba ŋat wø løp køør gïï mo oballe jaak wø joota bëët can mo dwøŋ døc.
english: He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread: but he that followeth after vain persons shall have poverty enough.

anywaa: Ŋat mo oŋäädhö okwär ki gwïëth, 'ba ŋat wø jalli døc nee laar kwärö ba kääŋi ka ajäla.
english: A faithful man shall abound with blessings: but he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent.

anywaa: Ki man nyooth bëët ajeeny paa gïn mo beer, 'ba dhaanhø wø poot jëënyö kiper nyi thääŋ møø mana cïp jïre.
english: To have respect of persons is not good: for for a piece of bread that man will transgress.

anywaa: Ŋat mo cere teek wø jalli døc nee laar kwärö, 'ba bëët can mano ö bääte kuue.
english: He that hasteth to be rich hath an evil eye, and considereth not that poverty shall come upon him.

anywaa: Ŋat wø jook dhaanhø jïtö ki pwøc yi nyïme ni kaala ŋat wø tøøt luup ki dhee.
english: He that rebuketh a man afterwards shall find more favour than he that flattereth with the tongue.

anywaa: Ŋat wø kwal jap wänni ki menni, ni kööe, ni «Man patha bääyö,» ena wat ŋat wø räänyö.
english: Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith, It is no transgression; the same is the companion of a destroyer.

anywaa: Ŋat mo cwïnye päl, pïëm wø di tääö, 'ba ŋat wø bëëdö ni ŋäätha Wuuö Jwøk, bëëtö mare bëënynyö.
english: He that is of a proud heart stirreth up strife: but he that putteth his trust in the Lord shall be made fat.

anywaa: Ŋat wø bëëdö ni ŋäätha acaara mare keere, ena bøøl, 'ba ŋat wø cäädhi ki køør leec wïc di piemø.
english: He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool: but whoso walketh wisely, he shall be delivered.

anywaa: Ŋat wø cïpi jï jøøa can ba cänni, 'ba ŋat wø mec waŋe jïtö ka acëënne mo thööth.
english: He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack: but he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse.

anywaa: Kany wø ö jøøa reyø maal, jiy rege wø kaange kaannø, 'ba kany wø ränyge, jøøa marge beer tïmö ni thööth.
english: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves: but when they perish, the righteous increase.

anywaa: Ŋat wø jøgi cooth, ni luup poot di dhalø, ränynyö ocwöp dëëre, ni bäŋ gïn køny gø.
english: He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.

anywaa: Kany wø thöönh jøøa marge beer ni jïge da teek, jiy yïthge wø mïnnö, 'ba kanyo en teeki cer ŋata raac, jiy wø cooyø.
english: When the righteous are in authority, the people rejoice: but when the wicked beareth rule, the people mourn.

anywaa: Ŋat wø mëër ki leec wïc wø duua met ec jï wänni, 'ba ŋat wø cäädhi ki kääpe raanynya jape.
english: Whoso loveth wisdom rejoiceth his father: but he that keepeth company with harlots spendeth his substance.

anywaa: Nyeya paac wø këël piny ka køør ŋøl ma adïëri, 'ba nyeya man wø jwäk jiy ki teek wø raanynya paac.
english: The king by judgment establisheth the land: but he that receiveth gifts overthroweth it.

anywaa: Ŋat wø cäänö kiper watge ni ee tøøtø, wø ciia abïëp kwör tiet watge.
english: A man that flattereth his neighbour spreadeth a net for his feet.

anywaa: Ŋat mo raac wø pätha ya abïëbe keere ki køør gïïa baye, 'ba ŋata mare beer wø bëëdö ni wär ki dudi ni yie met.
english: In the transgression of an evil man there is a snare: but the righteous doth sing and rejoice.

anywaa: Ŋat mo mare beer pïëmö kiper ŋøl mar jøøa can, 'ba ŋata raac teeŋ acaara ma enønø ba ci wïïe.
english: The righteous considereth the cause of the poor: but the wicked regardeth not to know it.

anywaa: Jø abuua wëër wø dhäya ge dï pääny, 'ba jøøa wïthge leer wëër wø jookge jooø.
english: Scornful men bring a city into a snare: but wise men turn away wrath.

anywaa: Kany wø ö ŋat mo wïïe leer wø cige kar løøk ki ŋat mo wïïe känni, ŋata wïïe känni wø wëëyö ni ŋïëre bäät ŋatøgø, ni luubö ba caan ni beer.
english: If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man, whether he rage or laugh, there is no rest.

anywaa: Jø wø køny rem jiy piny män ki ŋat mo mare tiir, ni ge manynya jwïëc jøøa marge thïïŋ.
english: The bloodthirsty hate the upright: but the just seek his soul.

anywaa: Ŋat mo wïïe känni wëër mare wø pute ka nyooth, 'ba ŋat mo wïïe leer wëër mare wø di kanø.
english: A fool uttereth all his mind: but a wise man keepeth it in till afterwards.

anywaa: Ni näk kwäärö ïthe di ciiø ki luup tööt, jøøa kwörge døøŋŋø bëët moa en tiere tïmö ni reyø.
english: If a ruler hearken to lies, all his servants are wicked.

anywaa: Gïn mo rwöpa ŋata can ki ŋat wø caar jiy beeye en, geni bëët nyeŋge amooc Wuuö Jwøki ki tar.
english: The poor and the deceitful man meet together: the Lord lighteneth both their eyes.

anywaa: Ni näk nyeya luup jøøa can di ŋølø na karge, wälu mare këëta piny na bäre bäre.
english: The king that faithfully judgeth the poor, his throne shall be established for ever.

anywaa: Acwäät ki juuk cïpö ki leec wïc, 'ba nyilaal mo bëëdö ka wïïe wø duua lään wïc jï menni.
english: The rod and reproof give wisdom: but a child left to himself bringeth his mother to shame.

anywaa: Kany wø tïm jøøa reyø ni thööth, gïï wø bac jiyi tïmö ni thööth thuwø, 'ba jøøa marge beer, ränynyö mar jøøa reyø oneenge.
english: When the wicked are multiplied, transgression increaseth: but the righteous shall see their fall.

anywaa: Pwöny wäädï, køøre ïïno jïti ki jwöm ki køøre, ni døøc cwïnyï mo met.
english: Correct thy son, and he shall give thee rest; yea, he shall give delight unto thy soul.

anywaa: Kany mo køp dwør Jwøk ocuŋŋö yie, jiy wø bëëdö ka wïthge jaak, 'ba jø wø gwøk ciik Jwøk, gwïëth ena bäätge.
english: Where there is no vision, the people perish: but he that keepeth the law, happy is he.

anywaa: Ŋat tïïc bäŋ wø köömmi ki luubö keere, kiper këël dee wïnynyö, eni bäŋ wø jïëy.
english: A servant will not be corrected by words: for though he understand he will not answer.

anywaa: ?Ŋat wø laar luubö jøl dhi dhaanhø ajootï? Da ŋäädhe mo thiinh kiper ŋat mo wïïe känni ni kaala teeŋ ŋatøgø.
english: Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? there is more hope of a fool than of him.

anywaa: Ŋat wø gool ŋat tïïc mare ni ba luumme, ka aŋuudi beeye pänh cwïny noo joot.
english: He that delicately bringeth up his servant from a child shall have him become his son at the length.

anywaa: Ŋat wëëye pïëm wø di tääö, ni ö ŋat wø laar wëër ni bac gïï mo thööth.
english: An angry man stirreth up strife, and a furious man aboundeth in transgression.

anywaa: Atöör mar dhaanhø, dhaanhø wø dwøge piny, 'ba ŋat mo bëëdö ni dëëre ee dwøk piny wø jïtö ki wödö.
english: A man's pride shall bring him low: but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit.

anywaa: Ŋat ma nyawat kuuwi, mare män ki jwïëy moe, ni eni ba kööŋ ki man caan gïna ŋääe.
english: Whoso is partner with a thief hateth his own soul: he heareth cursing, and bewrayeth it not.

anywaa: Ki man lwäärö ki dhaanhø beeye abïëp jï dhaanhø, 'ba ŋat wø ŋääth Wuuö Jwøk bëëdö no ogwøø.
english: The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the Lord shall be safe.

anywaa: Jiy mo thööth wø manynya leec nyïm baŋ kwäärö, 'ba ŋøl ma adïëri wø joot dhaanhe baŋ Wuuö Jwøk.
english: Many seek the ruler's favour; but every man's judgment cometh from the Lord.

anywaa: Jøøa marge beer yïthge reyø ki jø wø tïïc gïï mo reyø, ni ö jøøa reyø ni raac yïthge ki jøøa marge thïïŋ.
english: An unjust man is an abomination to the just: and he that is upright in the way is abomination to the wicked.

anywaa: Moi beege luup moa perge leth moa car Aguurri o Jake, ena köö, «Wui Jwøk, aano ööl, aano ööl møn, ni bäŋ gïn mo løny jïra.
english: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh, even the prophecy: the man spake unto Ithiel, even unto Ithiel and Ucal,

anywaa: Ka adïëri møn, aani, aana tïmö naa kaala jiy bëët ni bäŋ gïn mo ŋääa, ni bäŋ acaara jïra kaamar jiy bëët.
english: Surely I am more brutish than any man, and have not the understanding of a man.

anywaa: Aani, leec wïc kära kwanyø, ni mana daa ŋääö kiper Jwøa en kur keere kuua.
english: I neither learned wisdom, nor have the knowledge of the holy.

anywaa: ?Ŋata aa maal ni duu piny aŋa? ?Ŋata mak jamø ki cere aŋa? ?Ŋata bäc pï naama dwøŋ ka aleeŋŋa mare aŋa? ?Ŋata tïïc piny ni teek këël teegi moe aŋa? ?Nyeŋŋe aŋa? ?A nyeŋ wääde aŋa? Ni näk mo ŋäyï, caanï jïra.
english: Who hath ascended up into heaven, or descended? who hath gathered the wind in his fists? who hath bound the waters in a garment? who hath established all the ends of the earth? what is his name, and what is his son's name, if thou canst tell?

anywaa: «Luup Jwøk bëët oraŋø ni joodi na adïëri; ena kwöt leny jï jø wø kan røkge buute.
english: Every word of God is pure: he is a shield unto them that put their trust in him.

anywaa: Kär niï mëëta bäät luup moe, niï ba jääle ni tïm tööti marï ni ŋäc.
english: Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar.

anywaa: «Wui Wuuö Jwøk, a kwaya ïïni ki jammi ariiø; kär niï mäna geni ki aani kanyo pooda naa kär thøw.
english: Two things have I required of thee; deny me them not before I die:

anywaa: Cwøk ki tööt tïïc karge ni bäär ki aani, ni ba wëëgï aani can wala ni ba wëëgï aani kwärö; cïp cam jïra mana näk orømø ki aani,
english: Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me:

anywaa: kiper naa ba jääŋa ni mooŋa ïïni, ni kööa, ni ‹?Wuuö Jwøk aŋa?› wala naa ba tïma naa can ni kwäta, naa raanynya nyeŋŋï, ï na Jwøk mara.»
english: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.

anywaa: Kär niï waya nyeŋ ŋat tïïc nyïm kwäärö mare, niï ba ciene, ni jïtï ka ajäla.
english: Accuse not a servant unto his master, lest he curse thee, and thou be found guilty.

anywaa: Da jiy mo wëëkge wø päcge gïï mo reyø, ni mëëkge ba pwøcge.
english: There is a generation that curseth their father, and doth not bless their mother.

anywaa: Da jiy mo cädö ni ge waany ki jïge, kaamane ge poot kär tïmö ni waany yïth raay moge.
english: There is a generation that are pure in their own eyes, and yet is not washed from their filthiness.

anywaa: Da jiy mo wø raŋa jiy piny, na atöör marge wø di joodø nyeŋge.
english: There is a generation, O how lofty are their eyes! and their eyelids are lifted up.

anywaa: Da jiy mo lakge otïïö ni beth kaamar opëëllö, ni nyämme moge otïïö ni caala caakïïne, nee jøøa can ki jøøa näk ocaarø løønyge yïthakic jiy bäät piny.
english: There is a generation, whose teeth are as swords, and their jaw teeth as knives, to devour the poor from off the earth, and the needy from among men.

anywaa: Da nyïëdi ariiø jï cwiiø, mo wø jwöŋö, ni «Wa mooc, wa mooc.» Da gïïpinyi adäk mo ba jäŋ, ni ŋweerge ba maar köö, ni «Aana rømø.»
english: The horseleach hath two daughters, crying, Give, give. There are three things that are never satisfied, yea, four things say not, It is enough:

anywaa: Ni gïïögø beege kar bëët jwïëc jøøa no othøw, ki dhaagø ma bwøc, ki ŋøøm mo ba røm ki pïï, ki maac ni wø ba maar köö, ni «Aana rømø.»
english: The grave; and the barren womb; the earth that is not filled with water; and the fire that saith not, It is enough.

anywaa: Ŋat mo waŋe ena dëër wänni ni buua gø, ni taak ciik mo menni, nyeŋŋe ogöön agääe wøk moa en ya agäm-kïte, ni cami ya cøre.
english: The eye that mocketh at his father, and despiseth to obey his mother, the ravens of the valley shall pick it out, and the young eagles shall eat it.

anywaa: Da gïïpinyi adäk mo yia ege thääŋö døc, ni ŋweerge tiere ba ci wïïa;
english: There be three things which are too wonderful for me, yea, four which I know not:

anywaa: ni gïïögø beege jöör odhuuth ni wø määt maal nyeŋ pøøl, ki køør thwöl man wø cør bäät kïdi, ki jöör baabuur kany wø cäädhe yi naama dwøŋ, ki jöör dïcwøø ki dhaagø man wø mëëre ki gø.
english: The way of an eagle in the air; the way of a serpent upon a rock; the way of a ship in the midst of the sea; and the way of a man with a maid.

anywaa: Man beeye bëët dhaagø ma kääbi; eni wø käbö ni pooc dhee, ni kööe, ni «Bäŋ gïn mo raac mo yaa tïïö.»
english: Such is the way of an adulterous woman; she eateth, and wipeth her mouth, and saith, I have done no wickedness.

anywaa: Da gïïpinyi adäk mo piny yie othäŋŋö ki ge, ni ŋweerge ba løny ki käärö jïre;
english: For three things the earth is disquieted, and for four which it cannot bear:

anywaa: ni gïïögø beeye kany wø tïm laŋŋø na nyeya, ki kany wø jäŋ ŋat mo wïïe raaci ki cam,
english: For a servant when he reigneth; and a fool when he is filled with meat;

anywaa: ki kany wø jït dhaagø mo okweeyø ki dïcwøø, ki kany wø läw dhaage ma ŋat tïïc kar nyijø wø tïnynye.
english: For an odious woman when she is married; and an handmaid that is heir to her mistress.

anywaa: Da gïïpinyi aŋween mo therø bäät piny, 'ba wïthge leer døc:
english: There be four things which are little upon the earth, but they are exceeding wise:

anywaa: ŋiinynyi beege wï twöŋö mo dëëtge ba teek, 'ba caammi moge wø poot cooŋge piny kany wø ciek caammi.
english: The ants are a people not strong, yet they prepare their meat in the summer;

anywaa: Athinaaki beege lääy mo jïge bäŋ teek, 'ba ge wø poot tïïö ki uudi yïthakic kïte.
english: The conies are but a feeble folk, yet make they their houses in the rocks;

anywaa: Bäänyö bëëdö ni bäŋ nyeya jïge, 'ba geni bëët wø poot cäädhö na lwaae.
english: The locusts have no king, yet go they forth all of them by bands;

anywaa: Dïgwey beeye gïn mo magï maaø ki cerï jaak, 'ba eni wø poot di joodø paan dwøŋ.
english: The spider taketh hold with her hands, and is in kings' palaces.

anywaa: Da gïïpinyi adäk, ni kany wø cääthge, ge naayyø, ni ŋweerge cäädhi ni naayyø døc;
english: There be three things which go well, yea, four are comely in going:

anywaa: ni gïïögø beeye ŋuu na teek døc dï lääy bëët, ni ŋääe bäŋ wø løøe ki gïrpiny jaak;
english: A lion which is strongest among beasts, and turneth not away for any;

anywaa: ki thwønh gwienø, ki nywø ateea, ki nyeya man wø cäädhi ki jø leny moe.
english: A greyhound; an he goat also; and a king, against whom there is no rising up.

anywaa: Ni näk mo ïïno bëëdö ni wïïï raac, ni dëërï iï tïŋ maal, wala ïïno bëëdö niï caara acaare mo reyø, cïëk dhiï ki cerï.
english: If thou hast done foolishly in lifting up thyself, or if thou hast thought evil, lay thine hand upon thy mouth.

anywaa: Kiper wëër mo di tuuŋŋö duunnö ki wëër mo dwøŋ, kaawat man wø puuc caak ni pääre ki maaw, ni ö ummi mo di dwiinynyø ni cwïëre ki remø.
english: Surely the churning of milk bringeth forth butter, and the wringing of the nose bringeth forth blood: so the forcing of wrath bringeth forth strife.

anywaa: Moi beege luup mo perge leth mo nyeya ma Lemuël, moa ö menni na pwöny eni ki geni.
english: The words of king Lemuel, the prophecy that his mother taught him.

anywaa: Ena köö, ni «Wui wääda, ï na nyi yia, ï na jooda ki køør mana kööŋa jï Jwøk,
english: What, my son? and what, the son of my womb? and what, the son of my vows?

anywaa: kär niï raanynya teek marï ki mään, ni kär niï cïpa riï jïge, ge ni wø raany nyeye.
english: Give not thy strength unto women, nor thy ways to that which destroyeth kings.

anywaa: «Wui Lemuël, patha gïn mo orømø ki man mäth nyeye ki køøŋ nyïïomøki, ni patha gïn mo orømø ki man ö kwääri ni paacge kwøŋ mo keec;
english: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine; nor for princes strong drink:

anywaa: nee ba mäthge ni wïl wïthge ki ciik, ni wecge man ŋølge luup na karge mo jøøa can.
english: Lest they drink, and forget the law, and pervert the judgment of any of the afflicted.

anywaa: Køøŋø mo keec wär wëëk ŋat mo kare cään ki thøø, ni cïpï køøŋ nyïïomøki jï ŋat mo cwïnye okëënynyö ki køør bëëtö mare.
english: Give strong drink unto him that is ready to perish, and wine unto those that be of heavy hearts.

anywaa: Wëëk eni maath ni wïl wïïe ki can mare, nee ba cäde ki leth bëëtö mare.
english: Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.

anywaa: «Jap dhiï kiper jø wø ba løny ki man cäänge kiper dëëtge keerge, kiper adïëri thuwø mar jøøa no oööl bëët.
english: Open thy mouth for the dumb in the cause of all such as are appointed to destruction.

anywaa: Jap dhiï, ni ŋølï luup na karge, ni cuŋŋï kiper adïëri mar jøøa no ocaarø ki jøøa can.»
english: Open thy mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.

anywaa: Joot dhaagø mo beer teek døc! Teeŋ dhaaŋŋøgø pere leth ni kaala tii mo perge leth døc.
english: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.

anywaa: Cwøre wø ŋäätha eni ki cwïnye bäre, ni bëëde ni ba can ki gïï mo perge leth.
english: The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her, so that he shall have no need of spoil.

anywaa: Dhaaŋŋøgø wø tïïya gïï mo beyø cooth kiper cwøre ki yïth nïr kwøw moe bëët, ni bäŋ gïn mo raac mo tïïe kiper gø.
english: She will do him good and not evil all the days of her life.

anywaa: Eni wø määnyö ki jïëc rööm ki waare, ni cwääc geni na abïïe, ni eni ceŋŋe wø rweenhnhi ri tïïc ni yie met.
english: She seeketh wool, and flax, and worketh willingly with her hands.

anywaa: Eni caala baabuur mar ŋat wø gädhö; cam mare wø di øømmø kany mo bäär.
english: She is like the merchants' ships; she bringeth her food from afar.

anywaa: Eni wø laara päny maal ni piny poot cøl, ni jiiŋ cam kiper jic paare, ni cïp kur mään mo wø tïïö jïre.
english: She riseth also while it is yet night, and giveth meat to her household, and a portion to her maidens.

anywaa: Eni wø cädö bäät pwödhö ni ŋeew gø, ni piith pwöth omøki ki jammi moa joode ki køør tïïc mare.
english: She considereth a field, and buyeth it: with the fruit of her hands she planteth a vineyard.

anywaa: Eni tïïc mare wø di tïïö ni cwïnye ee cïbö bäre, ni bääte ee maaø ni teek døc.
english: She girdeth her loins with strength, and strengtheneth her arms.

anywaa: Eni gïï wø gadhe wø di joodø ni duunnö, ni maac mare bäŋ wø laar thøø ki wäär.
english: She perceiveth that her merchandise is good: her candle goeth not out by night.

anywaa: Eni waarø wø di biidhø ni weny gø, ni cwäny dëëre ka abïï.
english: She layeth her hands to the spindle, and her hands hold the distaff.

anywaa: Eni cere wø di peerø baŋ jøøa can, ni jap cere jï jø wø many køny.
english: She stretcheth out her hand to the poor; yea, she reacheth forth her hands to the needy.

anywaa: Eni cwïnye ba päri kiper jic paare, kany wø tïme na ri kööny aŋalakiir, kiper jic paare bëët orööbö ka abïïk köö.
english: She is not afraid of the snow for her household: for all her household are clothed with scarlet.

anywaa: Eni dëëre wø di cwänynyö ka abïï rïëp, ni eni wø käära abïïe mo pøøth mo tïïc ka lïïna.
english: She maketh herself coverings of tapestry; her clothing is silk and purple.

anywaa: Eni, cwøre bëëdö ni ŋäc ki kar acooŋa, kany wø bëëde ni eno pï piny dï jø døøk paac.
english: Her husband is known in the gates, when he sitteth among the elders of the land.

anywaa: Nyijøøgø wø kwöö ka abïïe ma lïïne ni gath geni, ni nyuuŋe ki kaae ni dwøk ge pwödhö ki jø wø gädhö.
english: She maketh fine linen, and selleth it; and delivereth girdles unto the merchant.

anywaa: Eni, mak paac ni teek ki wøør røk bëëdö dëëre kaamar abïï, ni yie wø bëëdö ni met kiper cääŋŋe mo oööi.
english: Strength and honour are her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come.

anywaa: Eni dhee wø cara luup leec wïc, ni ö pwöc mëërri ni wø ba jøøl ni en leebe.
english: She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness.

anywaa: Eni, bëët jic paare wø di neetø na wøp, ni ba many gø nee cäme jaak ni ba tïïö.
english: She looketh well to the ways of her household, and eateth not the bread of idleness.

anywaa: Eni, obwöre moe wø ööa maal ni pwøcge eni, ni ö cwøre thuwø ni pwøc eni, ni kööe,
english: Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praiseth her.

anywaa: «Da mään mo thööth mo tïïö ki gïï mo perge leth, 'ba ïïni, ceŋge bëët akaalï.»
english: Many daughters have done virtuously, but thou excellest them all.

anywaa: Wøp jaak dhaanhø wø di cøøgø, ni mïërö keere bäŋ gïn mo duue, 'ba dhaagø man wø lwäär Wuuö Jwøk wø di pwøø.
english: Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the Lord, she shall be praised.

anywaa: Cïpu pwøc jïre ki køør gïïa tïïe ki cere, ni pøøc eni yïth acooŋe ki køør tïïe moe.
english: Give her of the fruit of her hands; and let her own works praise her in the gates.

anywaa: Moi beege luup Dïpööy ma o Deebit, ni beeye Dïpööy mana bëëdö na nyeya yi Jerucalem.
english: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.

anywaa: Dïpööy aköö, ni «Bëëtö bäŋ tiere! Bëëtö bäŋ tiere! Bëëtö bäŋ tiere na bäre! Jammi bëët bäŋ tietge!»
english: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all is vanity.

anywaa: ?Agïnaŋø ni wø joot dhaanhe ki yïth tïïe moe bëët ni bëëde ni ree ee öölö ki tïïc tier cäŋ piny kany en?
english: What profit hath a man of all his labour which he taketh under the sun?

anywaa: Beenhnhe di nywølø ni ge pöödhö, ba piny poot bëëdö ni nut kare na bäre bäre.
english: One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh: but the earth abideth for ever.

anywaa: Cäŋ wø tuulö ni pädhe, ni laar døø køøre kanya tuule ki yie.
english: The sun also ariseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to his place where he arose.

anywaa: Jamø wø kwöta tier-piny, ni cäŋ ree løgø ni kwöt wï-piny; ni bëëdö ni piny jøøye jøøyø ni cäŋa døø kanya täge ki yie.
english: The wind goeth toward the south, and turneth about unto the north; it whirleth about continually, and the wind returneth again according to his circuits.

anywaa: Näm bëët ge bëëdö ni ge kwöta yi naama dwøŋ, 'ba naama dwøŋ poot bëëdö ni ba päŋ. Pïï bëëdö ni ge døøa tiet näm, ni ge wø cäŋa kwönnö.
english: All the rivers run into the sea; yet the sea is not full; unto the place from whence the rivers come, thither they return again.

anywaa: Jammi bëët mo wø tïïc duua öölö bäät jiy, ni beeye öölö mo opöödhö mo ba løny ki caan ki dhøk. Waŋ bëëdö ni ba jäŋ ki raŋ, ni ïth bëëdö ni ba päŋ ki luup mo wø wïnynye.
english: All things are full of labour; man cannot utter it: the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.

anywaa: Japa tägö ya acääŋŋe cäŋ ka jootø ni tägö, ni japa tïïc ya acääŋŋe cäŋ ka tïïyö; bäŋ gïrpiny mo nyään tier cäŋ piny kany.
english: The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, da gïrpiny mo løny man cään dhaanhe kipere, ni «Raŋï, man beeye gïn mo nyään»? Gïnögø kee oløny ni nut piny kany kanya poode ni ø poot kär cwääö.
english: Is there any thing whereof it may be said, See, this is new? it hath been already of old time, which was before us.

anywaa: Wïc ba par ki jiy moa bëëdö ya acääŋŋe, ni këël beenhnhe moo ööi yi nyïm, jø wø caath køørge wïthge ba parge ki geni.
english: There is no remembrance of former things; neither shall there be any remembrance of things that are to come with those that shall come after.

anywaa: A na Dïpööy, aana bëëdö na nyeya yi Jerucalem bäät jø Icriel.
english: I the Preacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

anywaa: Aani, jammi moi bëët ni wø tïïc tier maal piny kany en, aana cädö kiperge ni raŋa ge døøc, ni kwaana ge ki køør leec wïc. 'Ba beeye tëër mo peek døc na kïth Jwøki bäät jiy nee jwørge!
english: And I gave my heart to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all things that are done under heaven: this sore travail hath God given to the sons of man to be exercised therewith.

anywaa: 'Ba na raŋa jammi bëët moi ni wø tïïc tier cäŋ piny kany en, ka adïëri møn, gena tïmö bëët ni bäŋ tietge, ni caala man many jamø nee mak.
english: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and, behold, all is vanity and vexation of spirit.

anywaa: Gïn mo omeenø ba døø kare; ni gïn mo bäŋgø ba løny ki kwaan.
english: That which is crooked cannot be made straight: and that which is wanting cannot be numbered.

anywaa: Aani, aana cädö ki cwïnya, ni kööa, ni «Ka adïëri møn, ŋeth mara adøøŋŋø ni cääth maal ki leec wïc mo kaala leec wïc mar jiy bëët moa kwøŋ Jerucalem käärö naa poodi; aani, jammi mo thööth mo leec wïc ki kwänynyö ajooda.»
english: I communed with mine own heart, saying, Lo, I am come to great estate, and have gotten more wisdom than all they that have been before me in Jerusalem: yea, my heart had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.

anywaa: Køøre aana cädö nee tier leec wïc kwanya, këël bøøl, ki bäŋ acaara thuwø, 'ba moøgø thuwø, acäŋa jootø ni caala man many jamø nee mak.
english: And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also is vexation of spirit.

anywaa: Kiper leec wïc mo dwøŋ duua pänh cwïny mo dwøŋ; ni ki man meet kwänynyö, meeta cooyø.
english: For in much wisdom is much grief: and he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow.

anywaa: Aana cädö ki cwïnya naa cäänna raa ni kööa, ni «Neenï, ennø ï päära päärö ki man jïtï ki met ec; beerra man mïn yiï nø.» 'Ba ka adïëri møn, acäŋ tïmö na gïn mo bäŋ tiere.
english: I said in mine heart, Go to now, I will prove thee with mirth, therefore enjoy pleasure: and, behold, this also is vanity.

anywaa: Ni kööa, ni «Ŋeethø beeye gïr bøølø jaak; ni met ec, ?agïnaŋø noo duue?»
english: I said of laughter, It is mad: and of mirth, What doeth it?

anywaa: Aana määnyö døc ki ya acaara mara naa manynya man tïïa yia ni met ki køøŋø, ki man këëlla wïïa thuwø ri bëët bäŋ acaara, na acaara mara poot bwøtha aani ki leec wïc, këël mano jooda gïn mo beer mo tïïc jiyi tïïö moi ni bëëdö tier maal piny kany en, ki yïth cwiiri moi ni nøk noo beetge ii.
english: I sought in mine heart to give myself unto wine, yet acquainting mine heart with wisdom; and to lay hold on folly, till I might see what was that good for the sons of men, which they should do under the heaven all the days of their life.

anywaa: Aana tïïö ki tïïe mo thööth. Aana gëëdö ki uudi kiper dëëra, ni pïïdha ki jer omøki kiper dëëra;
english: I made me great works; I builded me houses; I planted me vineyards:

anywaa: aana tïïö ka ajïniine ki kwör jwöm røk mo opïïthö ki jenni kiper dëëra, ni piidha teeŋ jenni bëët yïthge mo wø nyïïge cam;
english: I made me gardens and orchards, and I planted trees in them of all kind of fruits:

anywaa: ni tïïa ka aguule mo pïï na mo jwøc pwöth jenni ki ge.
english: I made me pools of water, to water therewith the wood that bringeth forth trees:

anywaa: Aana ŋëëö ki laaŋe ma cwøw ki mään, ni jïra da laaŋe møøk mo nywølla paara. Aani thuwø jïra da dïëk ki dhäk mo thööth døc, ni bäŋ dhaanhø mo da japøgø jïre mo kaala aani yi Jerucalem.
english: I got me servants and maidens, and had servants born in my house; also I had great possessions of great and small cattle above all that were in Jerusalem before me:

anywaa: Aani, dëëra amäänynya ki gwel-bïrö ki warkey mo päl, ki jap kwär mo nyeye ki mo mïëri. Aani, dëëra amäänynya ki jø wär dudi ma cwøw ki mään, ni käla mään mo thööth paara, ni beeye gïn wø wëëk yïth cwøw mïnnö.
english: I gathered me also silver and gold, and the peculiar treasure of kings and of the provinces: I gat me men singers and women singers, and the delights of the sons of men, as musical instruments, and that of all sorts.

anywaa: Køøre kara atïmö ni dwøŋ døc naa kaala cuumme bëët moa kwøŋ Jerucalem käärö naa poodi. Naa bëëdö ni leec wïc mara poot nut kare.
english: So I was great, and increased more than all that were before me in Jerusalem: also my wisdom remained with me.

anywaa: Jammi bëët moa mïërö ki waŋa, bäŋgø mo yaa kwierø. Aani, bäŋ gïn mo cwïnya okweer ki gø røk jap met ec, kiper cwïnya bëëdö ni met kiper jammi bëët moa tïïa, ni manøgø beeye gïna duu tïïe moa tïïa bëët.
english: And whatsoever mine eyes desired I kept not from them, I withheld not my heart from any joy; for my heart rejoiced in all my labour: and this was my portion of all my labour.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya neena jammi bëët moa tïïa ki cera, ki tïïc bäre mana ööla ki gø, ka adïëri møn, ajooda ni jammi bëët bäŋ tietge, ni caala man many jamø nee mak, ni bäŋ gïn mo duu jammi moi ni tier cäŋ piny kany en.
english: Then I looked on all the works that my hands had wrought, and on the labour that I had laboured to do: and, behold, all was vanity and vexation of spirit, and there was no profit under the sun.

anywaa: Køøre aana tägö ki man cäda kiper leec wïc, ki bøøl, ki bäŋ acaara, ?kiper agïnaŋø noo tïïc ŋato läw kara, a na nyeya, ni näk mo paa gïïa näk onø tïïc dïkwøŋ?
english: And I turned myself to behold wisdom, and madness, and folly: for what can the man do that cometh after the king? even that which hath been already done.

anywaa: 'Ba ajooda ni leec wïc beerra eni ki bäŋ acaara, kaawat man bëëde en ni tar beerra eni ki muudhö.
english: Then I saw that wisdom excelleth folly, as far as light excelleth darkness.

anywaa: Ŋat mo wïïe leer, jammi nëënö jïre na karge; 'ba ŋat mo wïïe bäŋ acaara,  eni cäädha yi muudhö. 'Ba ajooda na aŋuun jøøgø bëët poot na aciel.
english: The wise man's eyes are in his head; but the fool walketh in darkness: and I myself perceived also that one event happeneth to them all.

anywaa: Køøre aana cädö ki cwïnya ni kööa, ni «Gïn wø tägi dëër ŋat mo wïïe bäŋ acaara poot tägö dëëra thuwø. ?Aŋø, tiere aŋø ni tïm wïïa ni leer døc en?» Ni cääna ki cwïnya ni kööa, ni «Manøgø thuwø poot na gïn mo bäŋ tiere.»
english: Then said I in my heart, As it happeneth to the fool, so it happeneth even to me; and why was I then more wise? Then I said in my heart, that this also is vanity.

anywaa: Kiper ŋat mo wïïe leer poot caala ŋat mo wïïe bäŋ acaara, ni wïc ba paayi ki geni ki kany mo bäär. Ki yïth nïne bëët moo ööi, wïc wïl ki geni bëët. Kaawat man bëëde en ni ŋat mo wïïe bäŋ acaara thøw, ŋat mo wïïe leer thuwø thøw.
english: For there is no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool for ever; seeing that which now is in the days to come shall all be forgotten. And how dieth the wise man? as the fool.

anywaa: Kiper manøgø nø, aana tïmö naa män ki kwøw, kiper jammi bëët mo wø tïïc tier cäŋ piny kany en, duua rääm dëëra; kiper gïïögø bëët bäŋ tietge; caala man many jamø nee mak.
english: Therefore I hated life; because the work that is wrought under the sun is grievous unto me: for all is vanity and vexation of spirit.

anywaa: Aani, aana männö ki gïïa duu gïïa tïïa bëët tier cäŋ piny kany en, kiper gïïögø dööŋ jï ŋato ööi køøra.
english: Yea, I hated all my labour which I had taken under the sun: because I should leave it unto the man that shall be after me.

anywaa: 'Ba ŋäyi ŋa, kanymør ŋatøgø beeye ŋat mo wïïe leer, wala ŋat mo wïïe bäŋ acaara. 'Ba eni jammi moa tïïa ki leec wïc na ööla kiperge tier cäŋ piny kany en, dööŋ jïre. Manøgø thuwø poot na gïn mo bäŋ tiere.
english: And who knoweth whether he shall be a wise man or a fool? yet shall he have rule over all my labour wherein I have laboured, and wherein I have shewed myself wise under the sun. This is also vanity.

anywaa: Kiper manøgø nø, ŋäädhe mara aŋøla bäät gïïa duu gïïa tïïa bëët tier cäŋ piny kany en.
english: Therefore I went about to cause my heart to despair of all the labour which I took under the sun.

anywaa: Kiper dhaanhø jammi tïïe tïïö ki leec wïc, ki kwänynyö, ki riek waŋ. 'Ba gïïögø bëët dööŋ jï ŋat mør mo gïïögø käre tïïö. Manøgø thuwø poot na gïn mo bäŋ tiere ni beeye gïn mo raac døc.
english: For there is a man whose labour is in wisdom, and in knowledge, and in equity; yet to a man that hath not laboured therein shall he leave it for his portion. This also is vanity and a great evil.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, agïnaŋø noo joot dhaanhe røk jammi moa tïïe bëët na ööle kiperge ni wïïe ee kierø tier cäŋ piny kany en?
english: For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun?

anywaa: Kiper ki yïth nïne mo dhaanhø bëët tïïc mare beeye rääm ki cooyø; këël ki wäär, ŋedhe bëëdö ni ba jwöm. Manøgø thuwø poot na gïn mo bäŋ tiere.
english: For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.

anywaa: Bäŋ gïn mo beerra eni jï dhaanhø ni näk mo paa cam ki maath ki man raŋ tïïc mare na gïn mo beer. Manøgø thuwø ajooda ni beeye gïn mo cer Jwøk ena ree.
english: There is nothing better for a man, than that he should eat and drink, and that he should make his soul enjoy good in his labour. This also I saw, that it was from the hand of God.

anywaa: ?Kiper aŋa ni løny jïre ki man cäme ni mïn yie ni näk paa Jwøk noo tïïc gø?
english: For who can eat, or who else can hasten hereunto, more than I?

anywaa: Kiper ŋat mo bëëtö mare beer ki nyïm Jwøk, eni mooe mooø ki leec wïc, ki kwänynyö, ki met ec; 'ba ŋat ma ŋat raay tïïe tïïö nee jïte ki jammi ni cooŋ geni piny nee dööŋge jï ŋata bëëtö mare beer ki nyïm Jwøk. Manøgø thuwø poot na gïn mo bäŋ tiere ni caala man many jamø nee mak.
english: For God giveth to a man that is good in his sight wisdom, and knowledge, and joy: but to the sinner he giveth travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him that is good before God. This also is vanity and vexation of spirit.

anywaa: Da caae mo ocïp piny kiper jammi bëët. Tïïe bëët mo wø tïïc tier maal piny kany, man nø da caa kipere.
english: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:

anywaa: Da caa mar nyöödö, ki caa mar thøø. da caa man piith jammi yie, ki caa man puth ge wøk yie.
english: A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted;

anywaa: Da caa mar 'näk, ki caa man wëëk jiy kwøw yie; da caa man toor uudi piny yie, ki caa man geer uudi yie.
english: A time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;

anywaa: Da caa mo dhaanhø jwöŋö yie, ki caa mo dhaanhø ŋeethø yie; da caa ma mar kïmmö, ki caa ma mar meeŋ.
english: A time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;

anywaa: Da caa man leeŋ kïte wøk yie, ki caa man cooŋ geni yie; da caa man gääm dëël yie ki mëër, ki caa man ba gääm dëël yie.
english: A time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;

anywaa: Da caa man many gïrpiny yie, ki caa man cwat eci yie ni ba joot; da caa man gwøk gïrpiny yie, ki caa man leeŋi wøk yie.
english: A time to get, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;

anywaa: Da caa ma abïï di jeeyø yie, ki caa man kwøy yie; da caa mar lïŋŋö, ki caa mar cäänö.
english: A time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;

anywaa: Da caa mar mëër, ki caa mar män; da caa mar leny, ki caa mar bëët-mëër.
english: A time to love, and a time to hate; a time of war, and a time of peace.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, agïnaŋø nø, noo joot ŋat tïïci ki køør öölö mare?
english: What profit hath he that worketh in that wherein he laboureth?

anywaa: Aani, ajooda ki  man näk mo da tïïc mo teek mo okïth Jwøki bäät jiy na baa bäätge.
english: I have seen the travail, which God hath given to the sons of men to be exercised in it.

anywaa: Jwøk jammi bëët ee tïïö ni beyø ki yïth caae moge. Ni eni thuwø dhaanhø ee mooø ka acaara man ŋäc bëëtö mo bäŋ cuŋŋe, 'ba poot bäŋ gïn mo kwany dhaanhe kiper tïïe mo Jwøk moa tïïe ki mana täge wïlöölö këël mano këët ya aŋuudi.
english: He hath made every thing beautiful in his time: also he hath set the world in their heart, so that no man can find out the work that God maketh from the beginning to the end.

anywaa: Aani, ajooda ni bäŋ gïn mo beerra eni kiper dhaanhø mo kaala man mïn yie, ki man tïïe ki gïn mo beer yïth nïr kwøw moe.
english: I know that there is no good in them, but for a man to rejoice, and to do good in his life.

anywaa: Ŋati man nø doo cämö ni mädhe ni mïn yie ki køør japa tïïe bëët ki öölö mare, ni manøgø beeye muuy mana cïp Jwøki.
english: And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labour, it is the gift of God.

anywaa: Aani, ŋääa ni jammi mo wø tïïc Jwøki bëëdö na bäre bäre; ni bäŋ gïrpiny mo løny man meedi bäätge wala mo käla wøk ki rege, kiper jammi moa tïïc Jwøki beeye kiper nee jiy lwäärge ki eni.
english: I know that, whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God doeth it, that men should fear before him.

anywaa: Gïï no onø tägö ii ki moo cäŋ tägö yi nyïm beege japa tägö dïkwøŋ, kiper poot na japøge ni wø cäŋ Jwøki tïïyö nee täkge.
english: That which hath been is now; and that which is to be hath already been; and God requireth that which is past.

anywaa: Aani thuwø gïn mør mo yaa cäŋ jootø tier cäŋ piny kany bee en; kanya doo nää kar ŋøl luup ma kare, atïmö ni nuta rääö yie, ni ö kanya doo nää kar ŋøl luup ma adïëri ni tïme thuwø ni nuta rääö yie.
english: And moreover I saw under the sun the place of judgment, that wickedness was there; and the place of righteousness, that iniquity was there.

anywaa: Aani, aana cädö ki cwïnya ni kööa, ni «Jwøk luup jiy bëët moa bëëtge tiir, ki moa bëëtge raac, ŋøle ŋølø na kare, kiper jammi bëët ki tïïe bëët da caa marge mo öö.»
english: I said in mine heart, God shall judge the righteous and the wicked: for there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.

anywaa: Ni cäŋa cädö ki cwïnya ni kööa, ni «Ka adïëri møn, Jwøk jiy apäänynye nee joot jiyi ki man näk mo ge röömi ki lääy.»
english: I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.

anywaa: Kiper gïn wø tägi dëër dhaanhø ki gïn wø tägi dëër lääy poot na teeŋ gïrpiny aciel. Dhaanhø thøw ni lääy thøw thuwø; ni ge bëët dëëtge da jwïëy ma teeŋ aciel, ni ba løny ki man cät dhaanhe ni pöödha eni ki lääy, kiper bëëtö bäŋ tiere kiperge bëët.
english: For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other; yea, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no preeminence above a beast: for all is vanity.

anywaa: Geni bëët, dëëtge cøøa kanya aciel; ni ge bëët ge käla yi tør, ni ge poot døøa yi tør bëët.
english: All go unto one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again.

anywaa: ?Aŋa ni ŋäc gø ki man näk mo jwïëc dhaanhø cøøa maal ni jwïëc lääy cøøa tiet ŋøøm?
english: Who knoweth the spirit of man that goeth upward, and the spirit of the beast that goeth downward to the earth?

anywaa: 'Ba aani, ajooda ni bäŋ gïn mo beerra eni kiper dhaanhø mo kaala man mïn yie ki køør jammi moe mo wø tïïe, kiper beeye gïna dööŋ jïre na kure. Kiper kanyo thøøe ba løny ki man duue ni joot japa tägö køøre.
english: Wherefore I perceive that there is nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his own works; for that is his portion: for who shall bring him to see what shall be after him?

anywaa: Køøre aana cäŋ nëënnö ni jooda tïïe moa näk mo ocaarø bëët moi ni tïïc tier cäŋ piny kany en. 'Ba ka adïëri møn, jiy moa no ocaarø, pï nyeŋge ajooda, ni ge bëëdö ni bäŋ ŋat mo cøma cwïnyge, ni teek ena ceŋ jøøa caar geni. 'Ba geni, ge na no ocaarø, bäŋ ŋat mo cøma cwïnyge.
english: So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power; but they had no comforter.

anywaa: Ni puta jiy moa no othøw pwøc ni beerra marge ki jiy moi ni poot kwøw ii.
english: Wherefore I praised the dead which are already dead more than the living which are yet alive.

anywaa: 'Ba ki røk gïïögø na ariiø yøø, beerra dhaanhø mo kär nywølø mo jammi moi ni reyø ni temmi tier cäŋ piny kany en käre kam joot.
english: Yea, better is he than both they, which hath not yet been, who hath not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.

anywaa: 'Ba ajooda møn ni jammi bëët mo wø tïïc ki öölö ki mo wø tïïc bëët ki køør riek waŋ, ööi ka ri këëyö man wø tägi yïthakic dhaanhø ki wati. Manøgø thuwø poot na gïn mo bäŋ tiere ni caala man many jamø nee mak.
english: Again, I considered all travail, and every right work, that for this a man is envied of his neighbour. This is also vanity and vexation of spirit.

anywaa: Dhaanhø mo wïïe bäŋ acaara bëëdö jaak ni ceŋŋe ee dwödö, ni eni raanynya dëëre keere.
english: The fool foldeth his hands together, and eateth his own flesh.

anywaa: Beerra joot gïn mo thiinh mo ree da jwöm, ni kaala gïn mo dwøŋ mo joot ka tïïc mo teek mo dëël oöölö ki gø ni wø caal man many jamø nee mak.
english: Better is an handful with quietness, than both the hands full with travail and vexation of spirit.

anywaa: Køøre gïn mør mo bäŋ tiere ma acäŋa jootø tier cäŋ piny kany beeye en.
english: Then I returned, and I saw vanity under the sun.

anywaa: Da dhaanhø mo bëëdö eni keere ni bäŋ wääde ni bäŋ coki. 'Ba eni bëëdö ni  dëëre ee öölö ki tïïc mo teek mo bäŋ cuŋŋe. Ni eni bëëdö ni waŋe poot ba jäŋ ki jap kwär, ni dëëre ba pëënynye ki man kööe, na «?Aŋa ni ööla dëëra kipere en, ni bëëda naa tïïya tïïc man ni teek en ni dëëra yaa mänö ki man tïïa yia ni met?» Manøgø thuwø poot na gïn mo bäŋ tiere ni beeye tïïc ma tïï rääm.
english: There is one alone, and there is not a second; yea, he hath neither child nor brother: yet is there no end of all his labour; neither is his eye satisfied with riches; neither saith he, For whom do I labour, and bereave my soul of good? This is also vanity, yea, it is a sore travail.

anywaa: Beerra jiy ariiø mo bëëdö na aciel ni kaala dhaanhø aciel mo bëëdö eni keere. Kiper gïno duu tïïci marge ki køør öölö beeye gïn mo beer.
english: Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.

anywaa: Kiper ni näk mo dhaanhø aciel pädhö, dhaanhø maya wati tïŋe maal. 'Ba otïmö ni leth jï ŋat opädhi na eni keere ni bäŋ ŋat mo tïŋ gø maal!
english: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up.

anywaa: Maya thuwø, ni näk mo jiy ariiø obutö na aciel, dëëtge tïmö ni mør. ?'Ba dhaanhø aciel ma eni keere, dëëre otïme ni mør nidïï?
english: Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone?

anywaa: Ni näk mo dhaanhø aciel teek ni løny jïre ki man bööt dhaanhø mo bëëdö eni keere, jiy ariiø ba løny ki böötö jïre. Thøøli mo orwöbö na nyeŋ adäk, ba jööt ki man laar cöödö.
english: And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.

anywaa: Beerra dhaanhø mo poot thiinh mo can mo wïïe leer, ni kaala nyeya ma jaal mo wïïe bäŋ acaara mo ba jïëy ki pwöc mo wø caan jïre.
english: Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.

anywaa: Kiper dhaanhø løny ki man tïme na nyeya, këël mo eni käla øt twöc, wala eni nywöli ni can na o paac.
english: For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor.

anywaa: 'Ba ajooda ni jiy moi bëët ni bëëdö ni kwøw tier cäŋ piny kany en, ge caatha køør nyilaal manøgø na thiinh enø kanyo läw kar nyeya.
english: I considered all the living which walk under the sun, with the second child that shall stand up in his stead.

anywaa: Ni jiy bëët mo wø en nyïme ba thum ki kwaan. 'Ba jiy moa lämmö cään yïthge kär met ki ŋata läw kar nyeya. Manøgø thuwø poot na gïn mo bäŋ tiere ni caala man many jamø nee mak.
english: There is no end of all the people, even of all that have been before them: they also that come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and vexation of spirit.

anywaa: Gwøk riï ki bëëtö marï kany wø ciï yi Øt Jwøk. Wär tïme niï ciï kaper cek ïth døc ni patha man cïpï ko olämme jaak kaawat man wø tïïc jøøa näk wïthge bäŋ acaara; kiper kucge ni gïna tïïcge bee gïn mo raac.
english: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.

anywaa: Kärï laar päth ri cäänö jaak, ni ba läädï ki cwïnyï ki man laarï kööŋ nyïm Jwøk. Kiper Jwøk ena maal niï ena piny. Kiper manøgø nø, beerra man bëëdï niï cara luup mo nøk.
english: Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter any thing before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.

anywaa: Kiper cäänö mar dhaanhø mo wïïe bäŋ acaara joot ka køør luupe na thööth, ni caala man wø lägö ki lääk ki køør acaare mo thööth.
english: For a dream cometh through the multitude of business; and a fool's voice is known by multitude of words.

anywaa: Kany wø kööŋï nyïm Jwøk, kärï ruu ki man tïïyï gïna kööŋï kipere. Kiper Jwøk yie ba mïnni ki ŋat mo wïïe bäŋ acaara. Tïïc gïna kööŋï kipere!
english: When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.

anywaa: Beerra eni ki man ba kööŋï, ki man kööŋï ni gïna kööŋï kipere ba tïïyï.
english: Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.

anywaa: Kär cäänö marï tïïyï na cäänö mo bwødha ïïni yïth raay, niï ba cäŋï köö nyïm dïlämi mar Wuuö Jwøk, ni «Luumma caana abøth.» ?Aŋø, Jwøk diï wëëga gootø ki luup moï nee gïna tïïyï cäŋ raanynyø?
english: Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?

anywaa: Kany wø tïm lääki ni thööth, kännö ki luup mo thööth mo bäŋ tietge; kiper manøgø, lwäärï ki Jwøk.
english: For in the multitude of dreams and many words there are also divers vanities: but fear thou God.

anywaa: Ni näk miï jïtö ki dhaanhø mo can mo di caarø yi paayø mo ŋøl ma adïëri ki bëëtö ma kare orwäänyö yie, kär cwïnyï thäŋŋö kanyo jootï gø; kiper kwäärö man nø da kwäärö mør bääte mo raŋŋa gø, ni kwääri moøgø thuwø poot da kwääri møøk bäätge mo raŋŋa ge.
english: If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter: for he that is higher than the highest regardeth; and there be higher than they.

anywaa: Gïï wø joot ki ri ŋøøm wø cøøa jï jiy bëët, 'ba beeye nyeya døc ni wø køny dëëre ki jap wø puur yi ŋöömö mare.
english: Moreover the profit of the earth is for all: the king himself is served by the field.

anywaa: Ŋat wø mëër ki gwel wø bëëdö ni ba jäŋ ki gwel, ni ŋat wø mëër ki jap kwärö wø bëëdö ni eni ba rømi ki jap kwärö moa joode. 'Ba manøgø thuwø poot na gïn mo bäŋ tiere.
english: He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance with increase: this is also vanity.

anywaa: Kany wø näk mo jap kwärö othöönhnhö, jø wø cam geni thuwø ge thöönhnhö. ?'Ba agïnaŋø noo kønye jï wëëk japøge ni näk mo patha man neetge ge ki nyeŋge  jaak?
english: When goods increase, they are increased that eat them: and what good is there to the owners thereof, saving the beholding of them with their eyes?

anywaa: Dhaanhø mo tïïö ki tïïc mo teek wø butö ki niine mo beer, këël eni cama gïn mo thiinh wala gïn mo dwøŋ. 'Ba ŋat mo okwär, mo jïre da jammi mo thööth, nyeŋŋe ba gämmi.
english: The sleep of a labouring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much: but the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.

anywaa: 'Ba gïn mo raac døc mo yaa joodø tier cäŋ piny kany bee en. Ŋat wø many kwärö ni wø cooŋ jammi mo thööth wø cäŋa ränynyö ki køørge.
english: There is a sore evil which I have seen under the sun, namely, riches kept for the owners thereof to their hurt.

anywaa: 'Ba kanyo räny jap kwärö moøgø ki køør gïn mør mo tägö jaak, ŋata no okwär ni näk mo da wääde tïmö ni bäŋ gïn mo dööŋ jï wääde këët mo køny ree ki gø.
english: But those riches perish by evil travail: and he begetteth a son, and there is nothing in his hand.

anywaa: Eni no okwär enø, kaa mana ö wøk ki yi menni ni bäŋ abïï dëëre, puta døø kaa mana ööe. Eni døøk ni bäŋ gïn mo kwöge këët ri japa tïïe ki öölö mare.
english: As he came forth of his mother's womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.

anywaa: 'Ba manøgø beeye gïn mo raac døc thuwø. Kaawat mana ö eni na nywøli ni bäŋ gïrpiny jïre, eni poot thøw thuwø na ennø nø. ?Aŋø, agïnaŋø noo duue nø ki man ö dhaanhe ni ööl ree jaak ki tïïc en, ni caala man many jamø nee mak?
english: And this also is a sore evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go: and what profit hath he that hath laboured for the wind?

anywaa: Teeŋ ŋatøgø nø, ki yïth nïr kwøw moe bëët eni bëëdö ni ena yi muudhö ni kïmmö døc, ni täwö ni cooyø.
english: All his days also he eateth in darkness, and he hath much sorrow and wrath with his sickness.

anywaa: 'Ba ennø, mana jooda ni beerra eni bee en. Dhaanhø doo cämö, ni mädhe, ni mïn yie ki køør japa tïïe bëët ki öölö mare tier cäŋ piny kany ki yïth nïr kwøw moe moi ni nøk no ocïp Jwøki jïre en; kiper manøgø beeye mana cïp jïre na kure.
english: Behold that which I have seen: it is good and comely for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labour that he taketh under the sun all the days of his life, which God giveth him: for it is his portion.

anywaa: Maya thuwø, kaawat man bëëde en ni Jwøk ŋati man nø ee mooø ki jap kwär ki jammi mo beyø, eni thuwø dhaanhø ee mooø ki teek bäät japøge ki man cäm dhaanhe rege na kure, ni jïte ki met ec ki køør öölö mare; ni manøgø beeye muuy mana cïp Jwøki.
english: Every man also to whom God hath given riches and wealth, and hath given him power to eat thereof, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labour; this is the gift of God.

anywaa: Kiper mana ö Jwøki na koor dhaanhø ki man bëët dhaanhe ni cwïnye met, dhaanhø atïmö ni ba cädö kiper nïr kwøw moe.
english: For he shall not much remember the days of his life; because God answereth him in the joy of his heart.

anywaa: 'Ba da gïn ma ajooda mo raac døc tier cäŋ piny kany, ni beeye gïn mo jiy ee öölö døc.
english: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is common among men:

anywaa: Jwøk løny ki man mooc dhaanhø ki jap kwär, ki gwel, ki dööŋ kar, nee dhaanhø bëëde ni bäŋ gïn cane røk jammi bëët mo wø manynye ki cwïnye; 'ba Jwøk ŋatøgø ba tïïe nee yie mïnne ki japøge, kiper beeye ŋat mo path noo yie mïnni ki japøge. Manøgø beeye gïn mo bäŋ tiere ni beeye rääm mo raac døc.
english: A man to whom God hath given riches, wealth, and honour, so that he wanteth nothing for his soul of all that he desireth, yet God giveth him not power to eat thereof, but a stranger eateth it: this is vanity, and it is an evil disease.

anywaa: Dhaanhø løny ki man näk mo jïre da obwöre ma dïpa, ni ö eni ni bëëde ki cwiiri mo thööth ni eni kwøw; 'ba këël cwiiri moa beede doo thööth, ni näk mo yie kär mïnnö ki japa beyø na joode, ni eni ba koony ki koony ma kare, aani, a doo köö, ni «Beerra dhaanhø mo obwön wøk ni kaala eni.
english: If a man beget an hundred children, and live many years, so that the days of his years be many, and his soul be not filled with good, and also that he have no burial; I say, that an untimely birth is better than he.

anywaa: Kiper dhaanhø mo obwön wøk caala gïn mo bäŋ tiere ni pöötha yi muudhö; ni ö nyeŋŋe ni put nibäc yi muudhö.
english: For he cometh in with vanity, and departeth in darkness, and his name shall be covered with darkness.

anywaa: Eni na bwön wøk enø, cäŋ ba neene, ni bäŋ gïn mo ŋääe na bäre. 'Ba eni, beerra mare ki dhaanhø maya.
english: Moreover he hath not seen the sun, nor known any thing: this hath more rest than the other.

anywaa: Këël dhaanhø doo bëëdö ni kwøw ki cwiiri ma kuma kwöre ariiø, ni näk mo yie kär mïnnö ki japa beyø na joode, ?aŋø, jiy bëët ba ci kaagø na aciel enø?»
english: Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?

anywaa: Öölö mar dhaanhø ki tïïc, beeye kiper yie; 'ba eni poot bëëdö ni ba jäŋ.
english: All the labour of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, ŋat mo wïïe leer beere nidïï ni kaala ŋat mo wïïe bäŋ acaara? ?Agïnaŋø ni duue dëër ŋat mo can ki man tïïc bëëtö mare ni beer nyïm jiy?
english: For what hath the wise more than the fool? what hath the poor, that knoweth to walk before the living?

anywaa: Beerra gïn mo oneenø ki waŋ ni kaala gïn mo di parø ki cwïny. Manøgø thuwø poot na gïn mo bäŋ tiere ni caala man many jamø nee mak.
english: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire: this is also vanity and vexation of spirit.

anywaa: Gïn wø nut, nyeŋŋe oløny ni ŋäc, ni dhaanhø oløny ni ŋäc ki man näk mo ena dhaanhø. 'Ba dhaanhø ba løny jïre ki man pïëme ki Jwøk na teek na näk kaala eni.
english: That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he.

anywaa: Kiper da luup mo thööth mo wø di carø ni bäŋ tietge. ?'Ba agïnaŋø noo duue nø dëër dhaanhø?
english: Seeing there be many things that increase vanity, what is man the better?

anywaa: ?Kiper,  aŋa ni wø ŋäc gïna beer kiper dhaanhø kany wø poode ni kwøw ki yïth nïrögø ni nøk yøø ni wø bäŋ tietge? Nïrögø wø laara pöödhö kaamar tïpö. ?Kiper aŋa ni løny jïre ki man caan gïno tägi køør thøø mar dhaanhø tier cäŋ piny kany?
english: For who knoweth what is good for man in this life, all the days of his vain life which he spendeth as a shadow? for who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?

anywaa: Beerra wïny nyeŋ mo beer ni kaala maar riia mo ŋwäänynye met. Ni beerra dïcäŋ thøø mar dhaanhø ni kaala dïcäŋ man wø nywøl dhaanhø yie.
english: A good name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one's birth.

anywaa: Beerra eni ki man lïïmmö paac mo yie da thøø ni kaala man ci paac mo yie da ajwöma, kiper thøø beeye aŋuun dhaanhø; ni jiy moa kwøw gïnögø dege kïtha cwïnyge.
english: It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men; and the living will lay it to his heart.

anywaa: Beerra pänh cwïny ni kaala ŋeethø, kiper kany wø bëët dhaanhø ni täärnyïme cøl ki køør kïmmö mare, løny ki man jïte ka acaara mo beer ki yi cwïnye.
english: Sorrow is better than laughter: for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made better.

anywaa: Dhaanhø mo wïïe leer, cwïnye ena paac mo yie da thøø, 'ba jiy mo wïthge bäŋ acaara, cwïnyge ena paac mo jiy bëëdö ni yïthge met jaak.
english: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.

anywaa: Beerra man wïny juuk mar dhaanhø mo wïïe leer ni kaala man wïny dudi mo jiy mo wïthge bäŋ acaara.
english: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.

anywaa: Kiper ŋeethø mar ŋat mo wïïe bäŋ acaara, caala dööt moonni mo liel tier dak, ni manøgø thuwø poot na gïn mo bäŋ tiere.
english: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool: this also is vanity.

anywaa: 'Ba tïïe mo caarø, ŋat mo wïïe leer tïïe tïïö ni wïïe bäŋ acaara, ni ö jammi mo wø cïp ki piny ni raany acaare moa beyø cwïny gø.
english: Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad; and a gift destroyeth the heart.

anywaa: Aŋuudi mar luubö beerra eni ni kaala tägö mar luubö. Cïp cwïny piny beerra eni ni kaala atöör.
english: Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof: and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
