anywaa: Kär cwïnyï läädö ki man laarï wëër, kiper wëër bëëdö tier jwöth ŋat mo wïïe bäŋ acaara.
english: Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.

anywaa: Kärï cäänö ni kööï, na «?Aperŋø ni tïme ni beyø nïne moa acääŋŋe ni kaala nïne mo dïcäŋi ii?» Kiper manøgø paa leec wïc ki man pëëny teeŋ pïëc ma enøgønø.
english: Say not thou, What is the cause that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not enquire wisely concerning this.

anywaa: Leec wïc beer ni caala gïn wø dööŋ jï dhaanhø, ni kunynyö jï jiy moi ni kwøw ii ni wø neen cäŋ.
english: Wisdom is good with an inheritance: and by it there is profit to them that see the sun.

anywaa: Kiper leec wïc, dhaanhø di gwøø ni caala man wø ö gwelli wø gwøk dhaanhø. 'Ba gïn wø duu ŋäc jammi ki leec wïc beeye ki man gwøk jwïëc ŋat wø en jï gø.
english: For wisdom is a defence, and money is a defence: but the excellency of knowledge is, that wisdom giveth life to them that have it.

anywaa: Caar wïïï ki tïïc mar Jwøk. ?Kiper aŋa ni løny jïre ki man twieny gïn mo ee nø meen?
english: Consider the work of God: for who can make that straight, which he hath made crooked?

anywaa: Ki yïth nïne mo wø bëët jammi ni beyø, bëëdï ni yiï met. 'Ba ki yïth nïne mo wø bëët jammi ni reyø, cädï ki man näk mo beeye Jwøk na tïïc manøgø ki maya. Kiper manøgø nø, dhaanhø bäŋ gïn mo løny jïre ki man ŋäc gø kiper bëëtö mare mano en nyïm bäre.
english: In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: God also hath set the one over against the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him.

anywaa: Ki yi bëëtö mana beeda bäre na näk bäŋ tiere, jammi bëët ajooda. Ajooda ni ŋat mo bëëtö mare beer laara thøø  yi bëëtö mare na beer; ni ö ŋat wø tïïö ki raay ni bëëde ki cwiiri mo thööth yïth gïï wø reyø ni wø temme.
english: All things have I seen in the days of my vanity: there is a just man that perisheth in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man that prolongeth his life in his wickedness.

anywaa: Kär beer marï kaathï, ni ba kaathï leec wïc marï. ?Aŋø, ï raanynyï riï jaak kiper ŋø?
english: Be not righteous over much; neither make thyself over wise: why shouldest thou destroy thyself?

anywaa: Kär rääö marï kaathï, ni ba bëëdï ni wïïï bäŋ acaara. ?Aŋø, ni layï riï ki man laarï thøø ni paa kar thøø marï en?
english: Be not over much wicked, neither be thou foolish: why shouldest thou die before thy time?

anywaa: Beerra man magï luubö mana na aciel, ni ba weyï luubö maya thuwø; kiper ŋat wø lwäär ki Jwøk luup moøgø bëët kwanye kwanyø.
english: It is good that thou shouldest take hold of this; yea, also from this withdraw not thine hand: for he that feareth God shall come forth of them all.

anywaa: Leec wïc cïpö ki teek jï ŋat mo wïïe leer ni kaala teek mar cuumme apaar mo ena yi pääny.
english: Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty men which are in the city.

anywaa: Ka adïëri møn, bäŋ dhaanhø mo mare adïëri bäät piny kany, mo bëëdö ni tïïya gïn mo beer cooth, ni ba bääyi.
english: For there is not a just man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.

anywaa: Kär luup mo wø car jiyi lwørï na luup mo perge leth bëët; kanymør ŋat tïïc marï wïnynyï wïnynyö ni janynya ïïni.
english: Also take no heed unto all words that are spoken; lest thou hear thy servant curse thee:

anywaa: Kiper ïïni, ŋäyï ki yi cwïnyï ni ki kwöre mo thööth da jiy møøk mo iï janynyø thuwø.
english: For oftentimes also thine own heart knoweth that thou thyself likewise hast cursed others.

anywaa: 'Ba aani, gïïögø bëët araŋa ki køør leec wïc ni kööa, ni «Aano tïmö ni wïïa leer,» 'ba atïmö ni kare bäär ki aani.
english: All this have I proved by wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it was far from me.

anywaa: Leec wïc mana nut bëëdö ni kare bäär, ni tiere okan piny døc. ?Aŋø, da ŋat mo joota tier gø?
english: That which is far off, and exceeding deep, who can find it out?

anywaa: Aani, aana cäŋ cädö ki cwïnya ki man kwanya tier leec wïc, naa manynya man ŋääa gø naa caya tiere, nee rääö mar bäŋ acaara ki bøøl nee ŋääa.
english: I applied mine heart to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom, and the reason of things, and to know the wickedness of folly, even of foolishness and madness:

anywaa: 'Ba gïn mør ma ajooda mo di jwørø ni leth døc ni kaala thøø, beeye dhaagø mo cwïnye da acaare mo reyø mo caala abëëbe ka ajääpi, mo ceŋŋe bëëdö ni caala tiimme. Ŋat mo bëëtö mare beer ki nyïm Jwøk bøth cer teeŋ dhaagø manøgø. 'Ba ŋat ma ŋat raay tuude tuudö.
english: And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.

anywaa: 'Ba Dïpööy aköö, ni «Ka adïëri møn, gïrpiny aciel ajooda kanya dwala jammi bëët na aciel ki man kwanya tier bëëtö marge,
english: Behold, this have I found, saith the preacher, counting one by one, to find out the account:

anywaa: naa poot bëëdö naa manynya gø këël kar kany ennø, 'ba kära joodø. 'Ba aana jïtö ki dïcwøø aciel keere mo wïïe leer yïthakic jiy ma kuma, 'ba bäŋ dhaagø mo wïïe leer mo yaa joodø dëët jøøgø bëët.
english: Which yet my soul seeketh, but I find not: one man among a thousand have I found; but a woman among all those have I not found.

anywaa: Ka adïëri møn, gïna jooda keere beeye en. Jwøk jiy acwääe ni cwïnyge waany, 'ba jiy atïmö ni ge manynya tïïe mo thööth mo riek waŋ.»
english: Lo, this only have I found, that God hath made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, aŋa ni rööm ŋati ni wïïe leer en? ?Aŋø, aŋa ni ŋäc jammi bëët ki man pät tietge? Leec wïc täärnyïm dhaanhø døøye mo leer, ni wiila cøl nyïm.
english: Who is as the wise man? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? a man's wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed.

anywaa: Aani, a cäänna ïïni, «Gwøk luum nyeya kiper kööŋ mana kööŋï ki gø nyïm Jwøk.
english: I counsel thee to keep the king's commandment, and that in regard of the oath of God.

anywaa: Kärï läädö ki man paanyï dëërï buut nyeya. Kärï dwätö ki jiy mo tïïya gïn mo raac, kiper løny jï nyeya ki man tïïc gïna met yie ki gø jaak.»
english: Be not hasty to go out of his sight: stand not in an evil thing; for he doeth whatsoever pleaseth him.

anywaa: Kiper mana näk mo dwør nyeya teek, ?aŋa ni løny jïre ki man kööe jïgø, na «Agïnaŋø ni tïïyï en?»
english: Where the word of a king is, there is power: and who may say unto him, What doest thou?

anywaa: Ŋat wø gwøk dwør nyeya bäŋ gïn mo leth mo tïïc dëëre, ni ŋat mo wïïe leer da caa ma kare mo ŋääe ki man tïïc gïrpiny yie ki jöö ma kare.
english: Whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing: and a wise man's heart discerneth both time and judgment.

anywaa: Kiper këël ni bëëde ni jiy oööl jaak en, da caa ma kare ki man tïïc gïrpiny man nø yie ki jöö ma kare.
english: Because to every purpose there is time and judgment, therefore the misery of man is great upon him.

anywaa: Kaawat man bëëde en ni bäŋ dhaanhø mo ŋäc jap nyïm, ?aŋa nø, noo caan japo tägi yi nyïm jï dhaanhø?
english: For he knoweth not that which shall be: for who can tell him when it shall be?

anywaa: Bäŋ dhaanhø mo jïre da teek bäät jamø ki man jook gø, ni bäŋ dhaanhø mo løny jïre ki man män ree ki thøø dïcäŋ thøø mare. Ni bäŋ ŋat leny mo wec kwääy lenynyi nee aae jaak kany wø näk ri leny, ni gïn mo leth ba kääŋi ki man täge dëët jø wø tïïc gïï mo reyø.
english: There is no man that hath power over the spirit to retain the spirit; neither hath he power in the day of death: and there is no discharge in that war; neither shall wickedness deliver those that are given to it.

anywaa: Aani, gïnögø bäre ajooda, kanya cäda bäät jammi moi bëët ni wø tïïc tier cäŋ piny kany en, ni da jiy mo geno ö maal bäät jø møøk ni ge caara ge.
english: All this have I seen, and applied my heart unto every work that is done under the sun: there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt.

anywaa: Maya thuwø, aana jïtö ki jø raay mo othøw, ni di koonyø no owøørø, ni  beege jøøa wara bëëdö ni ge dønynya Øt Lam mana en kur keere ni ge duua wøk ki yie, ge na wara jïtö ka ajiem yi pääny kanya wara tïïge ki raay. 'Ba manøgø thuwø poot na gïn mo bäŋ tiere.
english: And so I saw the wicked buried, who had come and gone from the place of the holy, and they were forgotten in the city where they had so done: this is also vanity.

anywaa: 'Ba kany wø bëëde ni luum ŋat mo otïïö ki gïï mo reyø kär laar ŋøl, cwïny jiy bëëdö ni päŋ ki man tïïge ki gïï mo reyø thuwø.
english: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.

anywaa: 'Ba këël ŋat raay doo bëëdö ni tïïö ki gïï mo reyø ki kwöre ma dïpa ni poot bëëdö ni kwøw ki cwiiri mo thööth jaak, aani, ŋääa ni jø wø lwäär Jwøk ki cwïnyge na adïëri poot beerra marge.
english: Though a sinner do evil an hundred times, and his days be prolonged, yet surely I know that it shall be well with them that fear God, which fear before him:

anywaa: 'Ba kiper ŋat wø tïïc gïn mo raac ni wø bëëdö ni ba lwäär ki Jwøk, tïmö ni ba beer kipere. Eni nïr kwøw moe tïmö kaamar tïpö ni wø ba ruu ki kany mo bäär.
english: But it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he prolong his days, which are as a shadow; because he feareth not before God.

anywaa: 'Ba da gïn mør thuwø mo bäŋ tiere mo wø tägö bäät piny kany en, ni gïnaca bee en. Da jiy mo bëëtge beyø mo gïïa doo tägö dëët jøøa bëëtge reyø tïmö ni täga dëëtge, ni ö gïïa doo rømø ki man täkge dëët jøøa bëëtge reyø ni tïme ni täga dëët jøøa bëëtge beyø. 'Ba manøgø thuwø a caana ni poot na gïn mo bäŋ tiere.
english: There is a vanity which is done upon the earth; that there be just men, unto whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked; again, there be wicked men, to whom it happeneth according to the work of the righteous: I said that this also is vanity.

anywaa: 'Ba aana köö ni dhaanhø doo bëëdö ki met ec, kiper bäŋ gïrpiny mo beerra eni kiper dhaanhø tier cäŋ piny kany, ni näk mo patha man cäme, ni mädhe ni mïn yie. 'Ba eno bëëdö no ojøl met eci ri tïïc mare na teek ki yïth nïr kwøw moe bëët moa cïp Jwøki jïre tier cäŋ piny kany.
english: Then I commended mirth, because a man hath no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry: for that shall abide with him of his labour the days of his life, which God giveth him under the sun.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya cäda ki cwïnya ki man kwanya tier leec wïc nee tïïe moi ni wø tïïc bäät piny en nee jooda, ni jooda gø ni dhaanhø ba buti ki waŋcäŋ ki wäär ki køør tïïc man wø tïïe,
english: When I applied mine heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done upon the earth: (for also there is that neither day nor night seeth sleep with his eyes:)

anywaa: køøre aani, tïïc bäre mar Jwøk aputa joot; ni puta gø ŋäc ni bäŋ dhaanhø mo løny jïre ki man kwany tiet jammi moi bëët ni wø tïïc tier cäŋ piny kany en. Këël dhaanhø doo ŋäbö ki man joot gø, dhäthö jïre. Këël ŋat mo wïïe leer doo köö, ni «Aani, ŋääa,» ba løny ki man ŋäc gø.
english: Then I beheld all the work of God, that a man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun: because though a man labour to seek it out, yet he shall not find it; yea further; though a wise man think to know it, yet shall he not be able to find it.

anywaa: 'Ba aani, luup moøgø bëët akïtha cwïnya ni cäda kiper jiy moa bëëtge beyø ki jiy moa wïthge leer, ki man näk mo tïïe moge ena cer Jwøk. 'Ba kuc dhaanhe ki man näk mo beeye mëër wala män ni koor eni yi nyïm.
english: For all this I considered in my heart even to declare all this, that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God: no man knoweth either love or hatred by all that is before them.

anywaa: Jiy bëët, ge cøøa kanya ciel. Ni beege jøøa bëëtge beyø ki jø wø tïïö ki gïï mo reyø, ki jøøa beyø, ki jøøa waany ki jøøa näk ba waany, ki jø wø cïpi ko olämme, ki jø wø ba cïpi. Kiper gïn wø tägi dëër dhaanhø mo beer poot tägö dëër ŋat raay; ni gïn wø tägi dëër ŋat wø kööŋ nyïm Jwøk poot tägö dëër ŋat wø lwäär ki man kööŋe.
english: All things come alike to all: there is one event to the righteous, and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean, and to the unclean; to him that sacrificeth, and to him that sacrificeth not: as is the good, so is the sinner; and he that sweareth, as he that feareth an oath.

anywaa: Gïn wø raac ni wø tägi tier cäŋ piny kany beeye man wø tïm jiyi bëët ni cøra jöörögø na aciel enø. Maya thuwø, cwïny jiy bëëdö ni päŋ ki gïï mo reyø, no okiera bëëdö ni ena cwïnyge ki ri bëëtö marge bäre. 'Ba ya aŋuudi ge poot thøw bëët.
english: This is an evil among all things that are done under the sun, that there is one event unto all: yea, also the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that they go to the dead.

anywaa: Kiper jø wø bëëdö ni kwøw da ŋäädhe kiperge. Ka adïëri møn, beerra gwök mo kwøw ki ŋuu mo othøw.
english: For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope: for a living dog is better than a dead lion.

anywaa: Kiper jiy mo kwøw ŋäcge ni ge thøw; 'ba jiy mo othøw bäŋ gïn mo ŋäcge, ni bäŋ gïn mo beer mo jootge, ni wïc ba par ki geni këët.
english: For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know not any thing, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten.

anywaa: Mëër marge, ki män marge, ki keec marge, onø aay ki geni ciel; ni bäŋ karge këët na bäre dëët jammi bëët mo wø tägi tier cäŋ piny kany en.
english: Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, is now perished; neither have they any more a portion for ever in any thing that is done under the sun.

anywaa: 'Ba ennø, ciï ni camï cam marï ki met ec, ni maathï køøŋø marï ni cwïnyï met; kiper Jwøk yie onø mïnnö ki tïïe moï.
english: Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart; for God now accepteth thy works.

anywaa: Beerra man bëët abïïe moï ni tar cooth ni bëëdï ni wïïï iï wïïrö ki maaw cooth.
english: Let thy garments be always white; and let thy head lack no ointment.

anywaa: Bëëdï ni iï met ki dhaagø marï na mëërï ki gø ki yïth nïr kwøw moï bëët, moi ni bäŋ tietge ii na cïp Jwøki jïrï tier cäŋ piny kany en. Kiper manøgø beeye kuna dööŋ na marï ki yïth nïr kwøw moï, ki køør tïïc marï mana öölï ki gø tier cäŋ piny kany en.
english: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity: for that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.

anywaa: Gïn wäro magï ki cerï ki man tïïyï  gø put tïïc ki cwïnyï bäre; kiper bäŋ acaare, wala kwänynyö wala leec wïc ki tïïc mo di tïïö këët kar bëët jwïëc jøøa no othøw noo ciï yie.
english: Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest.

anywaa: Aani, da gïn mør ma acäŋa jootø tier cäŋ piny kany en. Ŋat mo ŋäc ŋwiec da kany ba käädhe ri ŋwïëy, no oteeø da kany ba bööde ri leny, ni ŋat wø wïïe leer da kany ba jïte ki cam, ni ŋat wø waŋe riek da kany ba jïte ki jap kwärö, ni ŋat wø ŋäc jammi da kany ba jïte ki pwøc. 'Ba da kany mo öö ki gum dëël mo tägö kiperge bëët.
english: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.

anywaa: Maya thuwø, bäŋ dhaanhø mo gïno tägi dëëre ŋääe. Kaawat man bëëde en ni rëëö di maaø ka ajääp, ni wenyø di maaø ka abïëp, jiy thuwø pätha yïth gïï mo reyø ki kany mo kucge ni cwöba rege jaak.
english: For man also knoweth not his time: as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare; so are the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falleth suddenly upon them.

anywaa: Aani thuwø da gïn ma ajooda tier cäŋ piny kany ni beeye nyuudhi mar leec wïc mo yia othäŋŋö ki gø døc.
english: This wisdom have I seen also under the sun, and it seemed great unto me:

anywaa: Da nyi pääny mo thiinh mo bëëdö jiy mo nøk yie. 'Ba nyeya mo teek døc aöö nee këëde ki jiy moa en yi nyi pääny manøgø, ni cielge gø dïër ni tïïge ki gïn ethge bäät kiir ki gø.
english: There was a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it:

anywaa: 'Ba yi nyi päänyögø da dhaanhø mo can mo wïïe leer, ni piem jiy moa en yi nyi päänyögø ki køør leec wïc mare. 'Ba ya aŋuudi, bäŋ dhaanhø mo opar wïïe ki ŋatøgø ni can enø.
english: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man.

anywaa: Køøre aana köö, ni «Beerra leec wïc ni kaala teek mar dhaanhø.» 'Ba leec wïc mar ŋata can ataak ni luup moe kär leŋø.
english: Then said I, Wisdom is better than strength: nevertheless the poor man's wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.

anywaa: Beerra luup ŋat mo wïïe leer ki man wïnynyi mëëth ni kaala dilweel mar cuumi mo ena dï bøøre.
english: The words of wise men are heard in quiet more than the cry of him that ruleth among fools.

anywaa: Leec wïc beerra eni ni kaala jap leny. 'Ba ŋat raay aciel keere gïï mo beyø døc di raanynyø.
english: Wisdom is better than weapons of war: but one sinner destroyeth much good.

anywaa: Kaawat man wø thøø lwaŋŋi yi maaw mo ŋwäänynye met ni wø tïïcge maaw bäre ni ŋwääö no okwäk, gïn mo thiinh thuwø mo tïïc ni wïc kär caarø, leec wïc ki wödö raanynye raanynyø bäre.
english: Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour: so doth a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom and honour.

anywaa: Dhaanhø mo wïïe leer, wø bwøth cwïnye baŋ tïïe moa beyø, ni ö dhaanhø mo wïïe bäŋ acaara ni bwødhi ya cwïnye baŋ tïïe moa reyø.
english: A wise man's heart is at his right hand; but a fool's heart at his left.

anywaa: Dhaanhø mo wïïe bäŋ acaara, këël kany wø cäädhe waŋjöö, ki man näk mo wïïe ba leer put jiyi bëët ka ŋec ni wïïe bäŋ acaara møn.
english: Yea also, when he that is a fool walketh by the way, his wisdom faileth him, and he saith to every one that he is a fool.

anywaa: Ni näk mo kwäärö wëër ki ïïni, cwïnyï kär ränynyö ni daagï riï kar tïïc mana no ocïbö jïrï, kiper cïp cwïny piny gïï mo thööth mo reyø mo doo tïïö wëëge kääŋö.
english: If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, leave not thy place; for yielding pacifieth great offences.

anywaa: Aani da gïï mo reyø mo yaa joodø tier cäŋ piny kany, ni beege jap wø reyø ni wø tïïc kwääri.
english: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, as an error which proceedeth from the ruler:

anywaa: Jiy mo wïthge bäŋ acaara ge di cuumö kwör mo døøŋŋø; ni ö jiyi moa no okwär ni cïp geni kwör mo otaaø.
english: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in low place.

anywaa: Aani laaŋe ajooda ni ge cäädhi ka bäät okwëëc lääy, ni ö kwääri ni jooda ge ni ge cäädhi ka piny ki tietge kaamar laaŋe.
english: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.

anywaa: Ŋato koony buur, løny ki man tïme ni pätha eni yie, ni ö ŋato toor kiir nee døny yi gø, ni tïme ni bee eni noo dwøŋ thwölli.
english: He that diggeth a pit shall fall into it; and whoso breaketh an hedge, a serpent shall bite him.

anywaa: Ŋat wø tøk kïte, eni wø jïtö ki gïn mo leth ki køørge, ni ö ŋat wø kääö ki jenni ni jït dëëre ki gïï mo leth ki køørge.
english: Whoso removeth stones shall be hurt therewith; and he that cleaveth wood shall be endangered thereby.

anywaa: Ni näk mo ley pööl ni dhee kär paa, tïmö ni manynya teek mo dwøŋ man ŋudö ki gø. 'Ba leec wïc pere leth ki man wëëk tïïc thur kare.
english: If the iron be blunt, and he do not whet the edge, then must he put to more strength: but wisdom is profitable to direct.

anywaa: Ni näk mo thwöl laara käyö ni yie poot kär tïïö ni met, tïmö ni bäŋ gïn mo duue jï ŋata døøc yi gø mo met.
english: Surely the serpent will bite without enchantment; and a babbler is no better.

anywaa: Luup mo wø ö wøk ki dhi dhaanhø mo wïïe leer beege luup mo beyø, 'ba luup mo wø cur leep dhaanhø mo wïïe bäŋ acaara käla ränynyö bääte.
english: The words of a wise man's mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.

anywaa: Eni, tägö mar luup moe bëët, bee luup mo bäŋ tietge, ni ö aŋuun luup moe ni putge tïmö ni beeye rääö ki bøøl.
english: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness: and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.

anywaa: 'Ba eni na wïïe bäŋ acaara enø, cäänö mare poot  kaadhe kaadhø jaak. Bäŋ dhaanhø mo ŋäc gïno tägi yi nyïm, ni bäŋ dhaanhø mo løny jïre ki man cään gø ki gïno tägi køør thøø mar gø.
english: A fool also is full of words: a man cannot tell what shall be; and what shall be after him, who can tell him?

anywaa: Tïïc mar ŋat mo wïïe bäŋ acaara kännö ki öölö bääte, këël mano tïme ni ba løny jïre ki man ŋäc jöö man ci dï pääny.
english: The labour of the foolish wearieth every one of them, because he knoweth not how to go to the city.

anywaa: Otïmö ni leth jïrï, ï na paana näk nyeya marï bëëdö ka acaac lal, ni wø bwöthe moï møøl ri cam ka amöölla.
english: Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and thy princes eat in the morning!

anywaa: 'Ba ï na paana näk nyeya marï käla ri tuuŋ nyec, gwïëth en jïrï, ni bee ï ni wø bwöthe moï cämö ka yi caa ma kare, kiper nee jïtge ki teek dëël ni patha man bëënge meerø.
english: Blessed art thou, O land, when thy king is the son of nobles, and thy princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!

anywaa: Ni näk mo dhaanhø jääk ki man tïïc wï øde, wï øde pätha piny; ni ö bëët jäk mare ni wëëk øtø cwïër.
english: By much slothfulness the building decayeth; and through idleness of the hands the house droppeth through.

anywaa: Jiy cam mar ajwöma wø jiiŋge jiiŋŋø kiper met ec, ni ö køøŋe ni tïïc yi dhaanhø ni met. 'Ba gwel beeye wø tïïc teeŋ japøgø bëët.
english: A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh merry: but money answereth all things.

anywaa: 'Ba ïïni, kär nyeya cienï, këël ki yïth acaare moï; ni ba cienï ŋat mo okwär kanyo enï kar niine marï; kiper wec maal luup moï juthge judhö ni aacge ki gø, ni ö geni na näk ocwääö ni da bwöm ni waacge luubö marï.
english: Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.

anywaa: Bëëdï ni iï bäth ki man cïpï, kiper dïcäŋ aciel ï di duunnö.
english: Cast thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days.

anywaa: Pääŋ jammi moï ki kwöre abïriiø wala kwöre abära, kiper gïn mo raac mo løny ki man täge bäät piny kuyï.
english: Give a portion to seven, and also to eight; for thou knowest not what evil shall be upon the earth.

anywaa: Kany wø näk mo maal ogääbö ki pøøl, ge wø puta lööny piny na køth; ni kany wø näk mo jaath opäth jï tier-piny wala jï wï-piny, wø puta bëëtö kanya näk mo eno päth yie.
english: If the clouds be full of rain, they empty themselves upon the earth: and if the tree fall toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falleth, there it shall be.

anywaa: Ŋat wø bëëdö ni køya jamø ba pïïdhö, ni ŋat wø bëëdö ni raŋŋa pøøl bäŋ caammi mo kaae.
english: He that observeth the wind shall not sow; and he that regardeth the clouds shall not reap.

anywaa: Kaawat man bëëdï en ni jöör jamø kuyï ki yi jöö man wø cwääc dhaanhø ec ki gø, kaawat manøgø thuwø ba løny ki man ŋäyï tïïe mo Jwøk, eni na tïïc jammi bëët.
english: As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit, nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child: even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.

anywaa: Piith köödhi moï ka amöölla, ni ba øc dëërï piny ki man pïïdhï ka abøøya thuwø, kiper kuyï ki man näk mo pïïdhö marï thura kare ka amöölla wala abøøya, wala kwörögø tïmö ni beyø bëët kiperï.
english: In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thine hand: for thou knowest not whether shall prosper, either this or that, or whether they both shall be alike good.

anywaa: Tar wøp, ni beeye gïn mo beer kiper waŋ ki man neen cäŋ.
english: Truly the light is sweet, and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to behold the sun:

anywaa: Ni näk mo dhaanhø bëëdö ki cwiiri mo thööth, beerra man ö eni ni mïn yie ki yïth cwiiyøgø bëët. 'Ba beerra man caar wïïe thuwø ki nïr muudhö, kiper nïne mo thööth mo muudhö løny ki man öge. 'Ba jammi bëët moo ööi poot bäŋ tietge.
english: But if a man live many years, and rejoice in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many. All that cometh is vanity.

anywaa: Ï na thiinh, iï mïnne kany poodï niï thiinh en; beerra man mïn cwïnyï yïth nïr thïnhö moï, ni caathï køør jap wø many cwïnyï ki mo wø neetï ki waŋï. 'Ba wär ŋäyï ni Jwøk ï pëënynye pëënynyö kiper japøge bëët.
english: Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth; and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thine heart, and in the sight of thine eyes: but know thou, that for all these things God will bring thee into judgment.

anywaa: Kiper manøgønø, män cwïnyï ka acaare mo reyø, ni mänï dëërï ki gïï wø leth. Kiper nïr thïnhö mo bëëtö marï ki nïra beyø mo met ec marï bäŋ tietge.
english: Therefore remove sorrow from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh: for childhood and youth are vanity.

anywaa: Par wïïï ki eni na cwääc ïïni ki yïth nïr thïnhö moï, kanyo poode ni nïra reyø poodi, ni kar cwiiri poot kär cäännö kanyo kööï, ni «Aani yia ba met ki bëëtö man;»
english: Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them;

anywaa: ni beeye kanyo poode ni cäŋ, ki tar, ki dwääy ki ceer poot kär tïïö ni cøl, ni pøøl maal poot käre cäŋ tïïyö ni cøl køør køth;
english: While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain:

anywaa: ni beeye dïcäŋo ö jø wø koor uudi noo tïm dëëtge ni kwanynyi, ni jøøa teek cäädhi no ogääŋ, ni jø wø gudö bäät kïte, ge dööŋ ni ge ba tïïö kiper ge nøk, ni jøøo lwïthi ki dha awëërnyeŋ, piny nëëni no onijïïm ki jïge;
english: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened,

anywaa: ni beeye kanyo ö dhøk uudi moa näk oløø nyeŋ jïëthe noo bëëtge no ocïëgö, ni dööt baabuure mo wø gudö wïnyi ni ena piny, ni jiy laara pää kanyo jwöŋ wenynyi, ni dudi mo wø wär wïnya mëëth.
english: And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought low;

anywaa: Maya thuwø, jiy tïmö ni lwäär ki man ethge kwöra  en maal, ni ge lwäär ki gïïo reyø noo tägi nyeŋ jïëthe; ni beeye kanyo tïm wïth jenni ni ŋøøk, na aditwie tuta dëëtge ki öölö, ni bäŋ gïr met ec mo many dhaanhe këët. Køøre nø, dhaanhø cøøa kar aŋuun bëëtö mare, ni ö jiyi moo kïmmi ni bëëtge ni ge wïïrö nyeŋ jïëthe jaak.
english: Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets:

anywaa: Par wïïï ki eni na Jwøk kanyo poode ni tiimme mana no otïïö ki gwel-bïrö poot kär cööt, ni dak mana no otïïö ki warkey poot kär keethø; ni gïr twøm pïï man wø en deŋ aguula poot kär nidhey, ni gïn wø käl pïï wøk ki yi iith poot kär ränynyö.
english: Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern.

anywaa: Køøre nø, tør døøa yïth ŋøøm na käl yi gø, ni ö jwïëyi ni døø baŋ Jwøk na cïp gø.
english: Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.

anywaa: Ni kö dïpööyi, ni «Bëëtö bäŋ tiere, bëëtö bäŋ tiere, ni jammi bëët bäŋ tietge!»
english: Vanity of vanities, saith the preacher; all is vanity.

anywaa: Dïpööy kär ŋuudö ki man bëëde ni leerra wïïe keere, 'ba eni, jiy apwönynye thuwø ki luup leec wïc, ni cäde ni määnye ni jiiŋ pwöc leec wïc mo thööth.
english: And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.

anywaa: Dïpööy amäänyö ni jïte ki luup mo met, ni luup moa gööre beege luup mo tiir na adïëri møn.
english: The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and that which was written was upright, even words of truth.

anywaa: Luup jøøa wïthge leer caala jaath man wø kwør lääc paac ki gø, ni kany wø cooŋ geni caala mucumääre mo ogurö ni teek. Ni luupögø cïpa dïkwääyi mana näk aciel ni beeye Jwøk.
english: The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails fastened by the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.

anywaa: 'Ba ï na wääda, beerra man gwøgï riï ki teeŋ luup møøk. Göör ki weeli mo thööth, aŋuunge bäŋgø, ni kwaan teeŋ weeli moøgø dëër dhaanhø di öölö.
english: And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.

anywaa: 'Ba ennø, jammi bëët anø wïnyö, na aŋuun luubö beeye en. Lwäär Jwøk, ni gwøgï ciik moe, kiper manøgø beeye gïna doo tïïc jiyi bëët.
english: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.

anywaa: Kiper Jwøk jammi bëët kïthe kar ŋøl mare, ni beege jammi bëët moa näk tietge okanø, nee raac wala beer.
english: For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.

anywaa: Duut man beeye obeec dudi mo Cølöman.
english: The song of songs, which is Solomon's.

anywaa: Beerra man ööï ni nuumï dhaa ki yi nuum dhøk marï, kiper mëër marï cïpö ki met ec mo kaala køøŋ nyïïomøki.
english: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for thy love is better than wine.

anywaa: Maar riia mana näk iï wïïrö, ŋwäänynye ec døøye mo met, ni wïny nyeŋ marï caala maaw mo ŋwäänynye met mo oøc piny ni muulö. Kiper manøgønø, nyïïakuue mëër ki ïïni.
english: Because of the savour of thy good ointments thy name is as ointment poured forth, therefore do the virgins love thee.

anywaa: Nyïï aani buutï, nøø putø aay ennø na aciel! Beerra man ö nyeya mara ni kïth aani yi øtø mare. Wa kanynyø kiperï ni yïthwa omïnnö; mëër marï pwøcwa pwøø ni kaala køøŋ nyïïomøki. Wui, mëër mar nyïïakuue ki ïïni kee kare møn!
english: Draw me, we will run after thee: the king hath brought me into his chambers: we will be glad and rejoice in thee, we will remember thy love more than wine: the upright love thee.

anywaa: Wui, u na nyïïakuk Jerucalem, aani, aana dhaanhø maa cøl, 'ba kïta mïërö, naa cøl kaamar oduŋkaare mo jø Këdar, naa mïërö kaamar abïïk gëëŋŋe mo øt Cølöman.
english: I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.

anywaa: A kär neetu ni nyeŋŋu you këël dëëra kiper cøl mara; kiper aani, dëëra cuula cäŋŋi. Nyïïmera moa näk cwøw gena gootø ki aani, ni tïïcge aani nee pwöth jer omøki koora; 'ba aani pwöth jer omøki mara kära koorø.
english: Look not upon me, because I am black, because the sun hath looked upon me: my mother's children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards; but mine own vineyard have I not kept.

anywaa: Wui, ï na mëëra ki ïïni, caanï jïra, ?A kaa ŋø ni wø kwaayï dïëk moï yie? ?Na kaa ŋø ni wø wëëgï dïëk moï jwöm yie ki dhöör? Caanï jïra, naa ba tïma kaamar dhaagø mo wïïe ee loobø kaamar kääbi, mo cäädhö yïthakic dïëk mo nyïïawäädi moï.
english: Tell me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou makest thy flock to rest at noon: for why should I be as one that turneth aside by the flocks of thy companions?

anywaa: Wui, ï na dhaagø mo mïërö døc dï mään, ni näk mo kar kwaath kuyï, løp køør tiet dïëk, ni wëëgï nyïï atëëe moï caam deŋ oduŋkaare mo dïkwääc dïëk.
english: If thou know not, O thou fairest among women, go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, and feed thy kids beside the shepherds' tents.

anywaa: 'Ba ki baŋa, ï no omëëya, ï caala okweeny ma maath mo ena dï okwëëc leny ma thwönhi mo Peerø.
english: I have compared thee, O my love, to a company of horses in Pharaoh's chariots.

anywaa: Täärnyïmï nëëni ni mïërö ki jap mïërö moa näk iï twöö, ni ö cwaagï ni bëëde ni mïërö ki tiik jëëthi moa en yie.
english: Thy cheeks are comely with rows of jewels, thy neck with chains of gold.

anywaa: 'Ba waani, wa tïïö ki jap mïërö møøk jïrï mo tïïc ka warkey ki gwel-bïrö.
english: We will make thee borders of gold with studs of silver.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya bëët nyeya mara ni ena kar cam mare, maar riia mara na näk ŋwäänynye met aput kadhø ki ŋwääö døc.
english: While the king sitteth at his table, my spikenard sendeth forth the smell thereof.

anywaa: Omëëya bëëdö jïra kaamar dwøø mo ŋwäänynye met mo okwøø yo opïr, ni wø but yïthakic thura.
english: A bundle of myrrh is my wellbeloved unto me; he shall lie all night betwixt my breasts.

anywaa: Omëëya nëëni jïra kaamar jaath mo oŋøøk mo ŋwääö ni met yi pwöth jer omøki mar paana cwøl ni Ayn-Gadi.
english: My beloved is unto me as a cluster of camphire in the vineyards of En–gedi.

anywaa: Omëëya, a teeŋ mïërö mo nyïëdi ni mïërï ki gø! Wui, a teeŋ mïëya ŋø ni en jïrï en! Nyeŋŋï nëëni ni mïërö kaamar akuuru.
english: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves' eyes.

anywaa: Omëëya, a teeŋ mïërö mo nyïëdi ni mïërï ki gø en! Wui, ec mïnnö ki ï døc! Pëëm marø otïmö ni beeye luum mo pulli.
english: Behold, thou art fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant: also our bed is green.

anywaa: Ni ö jera perge leth ni tïmge ni beege cööthe mo øtø marø, ni tïm cuge mo øtø marø na teeŋ jera perge leth møga.
english: The beams of our house are cedar, and our rafters of fir.

anywaa: 'Ba aani a caala jaath jaak mo oŋøøk ni mïërö yi ŋööm Carön, naa caala apiitø mar gool.
english: I am the rose of Sharon, and the lily of the valleys.

anywaa: Omëëya nëënö dï nyïïakuue kaamar apiitø mo oŋøøk ni mïërö yïthakic koodhi.
english: As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.

anywaa: Omëëya nëënö dï obwöc cwøw kaamar jaath mo bääte oninøn ki nyïëdi yïthakic jenni mo paap. Aani yia met ki man pïïa piny tïpö mare, ni kany wø cama nyïëdi moe, put dhaa ka jwør ni met.
english: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.

anywaa: Eni aana kïth yi øtø mare kiper atïya mana näk ee jiiŋŋø kipera, ni gïna näk ee tïŋ maal bääta kaamar bëëra, beeye mëër mare ki aani.
english: He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me was love.

anywaa: Caam aani ki cam mo dëëra nathïk ki gø. Wëëk dëëra tëënnö ki nyïïjaadho cama, kiper dëëra bëëdö no oööl mëërri.
english: Stay me with flagons, comfort me with apples: for I am sick of love.

anywaa: Beerra man ö cer caame ni thäänha ki gø, ni ö cer cwïïe ni gääm aani ki gø.
english: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand doth embrace me.

anywaa: Wui, u na nyïïakuk Jerucalem, a cäänna uuni, nou kööŋŋu ŋëët aŋeri ki purre mo wø en yi pwöla, nee mëër ba tuuŋŋu nee ö maal këël kanyo pïïc kare.
english: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.

anywaa: Cegu ïthu! Man beeye dwør omëëya ni wïnyi en. Raŋŋu, ena rïŋŋö ki bäät kïte, ni ööi ni pärö ki yïthakic thuuri ni ööa baŋa.
english: The voice of my beloved! behold, he cometh leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills.

anywaa: Omëëya caala aŋer ki thwønh purra mo teek. Raŋŋu, eni cuŋŋö deŋ øtø marwa ni eni rääŋö ki dha awëërnyeŋ ki yïthakic rïwe.
english: My beloved is like a roe or a young hart: behold, he standeth behind our wall, he looketh forth at the windows, shewing himself through the lattice.

anywaa: Omëëya acäänö ki aani ni kööe, «Ö maal nø, omëëya, ni ööï baŋa, ni bee ï omëër mara na mïërö.
english: My beloved spake, and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.

anywaa: Raŋï, cwiir anø pöödhö, ni ö køthi ni cuŋŋe.
english: For, lo, the winter is past, the rain is over and gone;

anywaa: Jenni anø ŋøøk yi ŋööm pøø, ni ö caa man jwöŋ wenynyi yie ni ööe. Dööt akuyi aløny ni wïnyö yi ŋöömö marø.
english: The flowers appear on the earth; the time of the singing of birds is come, and the voice of the turtle is heard in our land;

anywaa: Olämmi anø ŋweel ki nyïëdi, ni ö jer omøki moa no oŋøøk ni nø ŋwänyge ni met. Ö maal nø, omëëya, ni ööï baŋa, ni bee ï omëër mara na mïërö.»
english: The fig tree putteth forth her green figs, and the vines with the tender grape give a good smell. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.

anywaa: Wui, omëëya, ï ni caal akuuru mo ena yïth aleye ki yïth kïte, mo ree ee kanø kany mo diiny deŋ kïdi en, beerra man nyoothï täärnyïmï jïra, ni tïïyï dwørï nee wïnynya, kiper dwørï met ni täärnyïmï mïërö.
english: O my dove, that art in the clefts of the rock, in the secret places of the stairs, let me see thy countenance, let me hear thy voice; for sweet is thy voice, and thy countenance is comely.

anywaa: Magu othööe jïwa, ni beege nyïï othööe moa therø ni wø raany jer omøki, ni beege jer omøki mowa na näk oŋøøk.
english: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines have tender grapes.

anywaa: Omëëya beeye mara, ni aana mare; eni dïëk moe wø caame yïth apiite.
english: My beloved is mine, and I am his: he feedeth among the lilies.

anywaa: Wui, ï no omëër mara, beerra man luuï riï baŋa ni bëëdï ki aani, këël kanyo ruu øwi noo pööth muudhö mar wäär. Beerra man tïmï kaamar aŋer ki nyi purra mo teek mo ena bäät kïte mo gwalli.
english: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be thou like a roe or a young hart upon the mountains of Bether.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya ena kar niine mara, wäär bäre athööra naa cädö naa manynya ŋata mëëra ki gø ki cwïnya; aana bëëdö naa manynya gø, 'ba eni kära joodø.
english: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.

anywaa: 'Ba ennø, a ööa maal naa cøøa nyeŋ jïëthe mo pääny, ka agääk jïëthe. Aani, a cøøa kuna manynya ŋata mëëra ki gø ki cwïnya. 'Ba kanya nø cøøa ni manynya gø, eni kära joodø.
english: I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.

anywaa: 'Ba jø wø kurö ni ge wïdö dï pääny, aana jootge; ni puta ge pëënynyö ni kööa, ni «?Ŋata mëëra ki gø ki cwïnya ajootu?»
english: The watchmen that go about the city found me: to whom I said, Saw ye him whom my soul loveth?

anywaa: 'Ba kanya pöödha ki buutge mo thiinh, ŋata mëëra ki gø ki cwïnya aputa joot, ni puta gø mak ni mäna gø ki wääth, ni kïtha gø po mera, yi øtø mare, eni na nywøl aani.
english: It was but a little that I passed from them, but I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother's house, and into the chamber of her that conceived me.

anywaa: Wui! u na nyïïakuk Jerucalem, a cäänna uuni, nou kööŋŋu ŋëët aŋeri ki purre mo wø en yi pwöla, nee mëër ba tuuŋŋu nee ö maal këël kanyo pïïc kare.
english: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.

anywaa: Wui! ?Man aŋøøni ni ööi ki dï paap, ni ree wenyø kaamar jïrö en, ni ŋwäänynye met kaamar teeŋ jer wø jïcge ŋwääi ni met ni wø jääp dïgäthe?
english: Who is this that cometh out of the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the merchant?

anywaa: Ka adïëri møn, beeye pëëm man wø käär wälu ki gø mar Cølöman, no okoor jø lenynyi moa teek ma pïërabïciel røk jø leny moa teek mo Icriel.
english: Behold his bed, which is Solomon's; threescore valiant men are about it, of the valiant of Israel.

anywaa: Ni ge bëët ceŋge do opëëlle, ni geno kwänynyö døc ki leny; no opëëlle moge ege twöö ŋäthge, ni rege ege jiiŋŋø kiper gïn mo leth mo tägö ki wäär.
english: They all hold swords, being expert in war: every man hath his sword upon his thigh because of fear in the night.

anywaa: Pëëm mana tïïc nyeya ma Cølömanni kiper dëëre, tïïe ka jaath mo käla yi lur Libaanø.
english: King Solomon made himself a chariot of the wood of Lebanon.

anywaa: Ni tïïc tiet abïla mar pëëm manøgø ki gwel-bïrö, ni tïïc kany wø jääŋ røk ki gø ki warkey, ni kïth kany wø pï yie ka abïï ma dïmuur, ni jammi moa tïïc nyïïakuk Jerucalemmi ki mëër marge opeeth dïëre.
english: He made the pillars thereof of silver, the bottom thereof of gold, the covering of it of purple, the midst thereof being paved with love, for the daughters of Jerusalem.

anywaa: Wui! u na nyïïakuk Jerucalem, ööu wøk, ni neennu nyeya ma Cølöman ni wïïe okïthö ka aduda en, ni beeye adun nywöm mana kïth menni wïïe dïcäŋa nyöömme, ni beeye dïcäŋa näk cäŋ met ec mare.
english: Go forth, O ye daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon with the crown wherewith his mother crowned him in the day of his espousals, and in the day of the gladness of his heart.

anywaa: Omëëya, a teeŋ mïëyaŋø ni mïërï ki gø en! Wui, a teeŋ mïëyaŋø ni baŋï en! Nyeŋŋï nëëni ni mïërö kaamar akuuru tier abïï mana näk iï loop wïïï; ni jïëyï nëëni kaamar pïïth atëëe mo kööla piny ki bäät Kïn Gelät.
english: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves' eyes within thy locks: thy hair is as a flock of goats, that appear from mount Gilead.

anywaa: Lagï nëëni ni tar kaamar pïïth rööm mo jïëcge onyaarø mo ge ööi ki baŋ lwøk, ni gena cïp-jwøk, ni bäŋgø rege mo bëëdö na eni keere.
english: Thy teeth are like a flock of sheep that are even shorn, which came up from the washing; whereof every one bear twins, and none is barren among them.

anywaa: Buny dhiï ree atwøde ni kwaar kaamar waarø mo ocwääö na baap; ni dhiï nëëni ni mïërö. Pïtï nëënö tier abïï mana näk iï loop wïïï kaamar nya adikwala mo opääŋŋö na thäŋi ariiø.
english: Thy lips are like a thread of scarlet, and thy speech is comely: thy temples are like a piece of a pomegranate within thy locks.

anywaa: Ŋutï bäär kaamar øt koor mar Deebit, na näk ogeerø ni mïërö; ni kööt leny ma kuma olïër yie, ni beege kööde bëët mo jø leny moa teek.
english: Thy neck is like the tower of David builded for an armoury, whereon there hang a thousand bucklers, all shields of mighty men.

anywaa: Thurï moø na ariiø yøø mïërö ni caala nyïï purre ariiø ma cïp-jwøk, mo ge cämö yïthakic apiite.
english: Thy two breasts are like two young roes that are twins, which feed among the lilies.

anywaa: A bëëdö bäät kïnna näk bääte da dwøk, ni beeye bäät thuura näk bääte da jer wø ŋwääi ni met, këël kanyo ruu øwi, noo pööth muudhö mar wäär.
english: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.

anywaa: Wui, omëëya, dëërï mïërö bäre, ni bäŋ kany mo jøøŋŋi riï.
english: Thou art all fair, my love; there is no spot in thee.

anywaa: Wui, ï na dhaagø-thiinh mara, cøø piny na aciel ki bäät Kïn Libaanø. Wui, cøø piny na aciel ki bäät Kïn Libaanø. Løøyø piny ki bäät Kïn Amana, ni løøyø piny ki bäät Kïn Canër ki Armön, ni beege kwör bëëte mo ŋuuwe, na kïte mo wø bëët kwäänynye bäätge.
english: Come with me from Lebanon, my spouse, with me from Lebanon: look from the top of Amana, from the top of Senir and Hermon, from the lions' dens, from the mountains of the leopards.

anywaa: Wui coka, ni bee ï dhaagø-thiinh mara,  cwïnya atïmö ni pärö døc kiperï! Cwïnya atïmö ni pärö døc møn kiperï ki yi räŋŋö aciel mana raŋï jïra ki nyeŋŋï, ki tiin-jeth aciel mana jooda cwaagï.
english: Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, my spouse; thou hast ravished my heart with one of thine eyes, with one chain of thy neck.

anywaa: Wui coka, ni bee ï dhaagø-thiinh mara, a teeŋ met ec mo nyïëdi na jooda ki køør mëër marï! Wui, mëër marï ko opöödhö ki met ni kaala køøŋ nyïïomøki, ni ö maar wïïr marï ni ŋwääe ni met ni kaala teeŋ gïï wø ŋwääi ni met møga bëët.
english: How fair is thy love, my sister, my spouse! how much better is thy love than wine! and the smell of thine ointments than all spices!

anywaa: Wui, ï na dhaagø-thiinh mara, buny dhiï ŋweeth ni caala maar kïc; ni beege caak ki maar kïc ni en tier leebï. Abïïe moï ŋwääö ni met døc ni kaala ŋwääny jer wø ŋwääi ni met yi Lur Libaanø.
english: Thy lips, O my spouse, drop as the honeycomb: honey and milk are under thy tongue; and the smell of thy garments is like the smell of Lebanon.

anywaa: Wui coka, ni bee ï dhaagø-thiinh mara, ï caala ajïniina mo dhee odëëdö, ni beeye ajïniina mo kal mare othørø ki kïte, niï caala iith mo dhee odëëdö.
english: A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.

anywaa: Ïïna ajïniina mo yie da jer adïkwäle mo oŋweel ki nyïëdi mo beyø, ki teeŋ jer wø ŋwääi ni met ni wø tïïc na mäth wïïr;
english: Thy plants are an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits; camphire, with spikenard,

anywaa: ki teeŋ jer wø tïïc na mäth wïïr ki booya ma abäga, ki jer wø ŋwääi ni met ni wø kïth yi kadø, ki jaath man wø tïïc na maar wïïr, ki teeŋ jenni møøk mo ŋwääö ni met, ki jer dwøk, ki teeŋ jenni møøk thuwø mo perge leth mo ŋwääö ni met.
english: Spikenard and saffron; calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices:

anywaa: Ïïni, ï caala jøøro mo ena ya ajïniina, niï caala iith mo pïïe met, niï bëëdö kaamar waŋ naam mo kwönni ka yi Kïn Libaanø.
english: A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon.

anywaa: Wui, ï na jam wø ööi ki jï løø wïpiny, ö maal! Wui, ï na jam wø ööi ki jï løø tier-piny, ööï! Ööu ni kwötu dëër ajïniina mara, nee ŋwäänynye na näk met nee kwöt kany mo bäär. Beerra man ö omëërri mara ni døny ya ajïniina mare, ni cam nyïïjenni na beyø na en yie.
english: Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.

anywaa: Wui! coka, ni bee ï dhaagøthiinh mara, aana ö ya ajïniina mara, dwøk 'moa acooŋa, ki jenni 'moa mo wø ŋwääi ni met; aani, ogat kïc ki maar kïc mara acama, ni maadha køøŋ nyïïomøki ki caak 'moa.
english: I am come into my garden, my sister, my spouse: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk: eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.

anywaa: Wui! nyïïawäätwa, cämu ni mädhu. Wui! omëërri, mädhu ni rømmu.

'Ba ni aano butö, cwïnya abëëdö ni nëënö. 'Ba dwøl aputa wïnynyö, no omëër mara dööŋö dhi øtø, ni kööe, «Wui coka, nyimëëc cwïnya, na bëëtö mare beer, na mwöl kaamar akuuru, jap dhi øtø jïra. Aani wïïa atïmö ni thec ki thööy, ni tïm jïëc wïïa ni thec ki thööc wäär.»
english: I sleep, but my heart waketh: it is the voice of my beloved that knocketh, saying, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew, and my locks with the drops of the night.

anywaa: 'Ba aløøa, ni «Aani, abïï mara yaa nø gööny wøk; ?aŋø, cäŋa ka dwøk dëëra? Aani, tieta yaa nø lwøk; ?aŋø, ge cäŋa ka wëëk cullö?»
english: I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?

anywaa: 'Ba omëër mara cere aput rwää baŋa ki dhi øtø kanya ŋaam, ni put cwïnya tägö ki pärö kipere.
english: My beloved put in his hand by the hole of the door, and my bowels were moved for him.

anywaa: Køøre aana päny maal nee dhi øtø jaba jï omëër mara, ni ceŋŋa onijwöc ki maar riia, ni lweeta thec ki gø, ni put tøøn bäät dïdëët.
english: I rose up to open to my beloved; and my hands dropped with myrrh, and my fingers with sweet smelling myrrh, upon the handles of the lock.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya jaba dhi øtø kiper omëër mara, ree ee nø daak ni tøør këët; ni puta bëëtö ni cwïnya pärö ki køør mana cääne ki aani dïkwøŋ. Ni manynya gø døc, ni kära eni joodø, ni cwøla gø, 'ba eni kär duunnö jïra.
english: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself, and was gone: my soul failed when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.

anywaa: 'Ba jø koor mo wø kurö ni ge wïdö dï pääny, ni beege jø wø koor kiir, aana jootge ni putge aani pwöt, ni moocge dëëra ki ŋwiili, ni kälge aleeŋŋa mara ni aacge ki gø.
english: The watchmen that went about the city found me, they smote me, they wounded me; the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.

anywaa: Wui, nyïïakuk Jerucalem, a cäänna uuni, ni näk mo omëër mara jootu joodø, wär caannu jïre ni kööu, no «Omëër marï dëëre onøkiil ki mëër.»
english: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if ye find my beloved, that ye tell him, that I am sick of love.

anywaa: Wui, ï na dhaaŋŋa mïërö døc dï mään, ?aŋø, omëër marï okadhø ka ŋø ni kaala cwøw bëët? ?Aŋø, omëër marï okadhø ka ŋø døc, ni bëëdï ni wa iï cemø kipere en?
english: What is thy beloved more than another beloved, O thou fairest among women? what is thy beloved more than another beloved, that thou dost so charge us?

anywaa: Omëër mara kïte mïërö døc ni dëëre pulli, ni eni di ŋiiø yïthakic cwøw ma kume apaar.
english: My beloved is white and ruddy, the chiefest among ten thousand.

anywaa: Täärnyïme paŋŋi kaamar warkey mana tøŋ, ni jïëye na näynäy ni cøl kaamar okwör mo agaak.
english: His head is as the most fine gold, his locks are bushy, and black as a raven.

anywaa: Ni nyeŋŋe mïërö ni tar kaamar akuyi mo ena buut pïï mo kwödö, mo geno lwøk ki caak, ni ge mïërö kaamar nyeŋ kïte moa perge leth.
english: His eyes are as the eyes of doves by the rivers of waters, washed with milk, and fitly set.

anywaa: Ni mïërö mar pïte bëëdö kaamar pwöth jer wø ŋwääi ni met, ni buny dhee caala apiitø mo oŋøøk mo tøøn ki maar riia.
english: His cheeks are as a bed of spices, as sweet flowers: his lips like lilies, dropping sweet smelling myrrh.

anywaa: Bäädi moe nëëni kaamar athøc warkey mo otïïö ni mïërö ki nyeŋ kïte mo perge leth. Bäp yie mïërö kaamar lëëc liec mo otïïö ni pøøth, mo oŋwaŋŋø ni mïërö ki nyeŋ kïte mo perge leth.
english: His hands are as gold rings set with the beryl: his belly is as bright ivory overlaid with sapphires.

anywaa: Tiete nëëni kaamar were mo otïïö ki kïdi mo mïërö, mo ocwöth bäät warkey mana tøŋ, ni dëëre mïërö kaamar Lur Libaanø, ni leth pere rööma jenni mo gø.
english: His legs are as pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: his countenance is as Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.

anywaa: Eni buny dhee ŋweeth kiree, ni ena ŋat mo cwïny pärö kipere døc. Wui, nyïïakuk Jerucalem! Ŋatøgø beeye omëër mara, ni ŋatøgø beeye nyawatwa.
english: His mouth is most sweet: yea, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.

anywaa: ?Wui, ï na dhaaŋŋa mïërö døc dï mään, omëëyï ocøøa kaa? ?Aŋø, omëëyï ocøra jööraŋø, nee eni manynyø na aciel?
english: Whither is thy beloved gone, O thou fairest among women? whither is thy beloved turned aside? that we may seek him with thee.

anywaa: Omëëya aci ya ajïniina mare, dï jenni moa näk ŋwääi ni met. Ena ci kuna kwaac pïïth dïëk moe yïth jenni, na apiite moa no oŋøøk cooŋe.
english: My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.

anywaa: Aani, aana mar omëëya, no omëëya beeye mara; bee eni ni wø kwaac pïïth dïëk moe dï apiite moa no oŋøøk.
english: I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine: he feedeth among the lilies.

anywaa: Wui, omëëya, ï mïërö kaamar pääny Tirja, niï mïërö døc kaamar pääny Jerucalem, ni ec thäŋŋö ki ïïni kaamar jø leny mo bëëre ege tïŋ maal.
english: Thou art beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, comely as Jerusalem, terrible as an army with banners.

anywaa: Wec aani ki raŋŋø ki nyeŋŋï nø, kiper wïïa akierge. Jïër moï caala pïïth atëëe mo löönynya piny ki bäät Kïn Gelät.
english: Turn away thine eyes from me, for they have overcome me: thy hair is as a flock of goats that appear from Gilead.

anywaa: Lagï nëëni ni tar kaamar pïïth rööm, mo ge käla baŋ lwøk; ni gena cïp-jwøk, ni bäŋgø rege mo bëëdö na eni keere.
english: Thy teeth are as a flock of sheep which go up from the washing, whereof every one beareth twins, and there is not one barren among them.

anywaa: Pïtï nëënö tier abïï mana näk iï loop wïïï kaamar nya adikwala mo opääŋŋö na thäŋi ariiø.
english: As a piece of a pomegranate are thy temples within thy locks.

anywaa: Løny man bëët nyeya ni jïre da gwaae ma pïërabïciel, ki mään ma akwanye ma pïërabära, ki nyïïakuue mo dëët cwøw poot kucge mo ba kwaan.
english: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, and virgins without number.

anywaa: 'Ba aani, dhaagø mara bee eni keere, ni bëëtö mare beer, ni mwöl kaamar akuuru, ni bee eni na nyakøø mana pere leth jï menni, ni menni na nywøl gø mëër ki gø døc. Eni, ena joot nyïïakuue møga ni köge no ogwïëdhö; ni jooti ya gwaae thuwø, ki mään moa näk akwanye, ni pwøcge gø, ni köge,
english: My dove, my undefiled is but one; she is the only one of her mother, she is the choice one of her that bare her. The daughters saw her, and blessed her; yea, the queens and the concubines, and they praised her.

anywaa: na «A dhaaŋaŋø ni nëëni kaamar tiet-øw en, ni nëëni ni mïërö kaamar dwääy mo ena tar en, ni tøŋ kaamar cäŋ, ni ec thäŋŋö ki gø kaamar jø leny mo bëëre ege tïŋ maal!»
english: Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners?

anywaa: Aana løøc piny dï pwöth jer athaloommi kuna raŋa jenni moa no oløth yi gool, nee jooda ki man näk mo jer omøki othiew, wala jer adïkwäle oŋøøk.
english: I went down into the garden of nuts to see the fruits of the valley, and to see whether the vine flourished, and the pomegranates budded.

anywaa: Kanyøgø gïn mør aput tägö ni cwöba raa: jwïëy 'moa aana tïïcge keda aano pï piny bäät jään okweeny yïthakic jïëth okwëënyi mo jø powa mo kwörge døøŋŋø.
english: Or ever I was aware, my soul made me like the chariots of Amminadib.

anywaa: Wui, nyijø Cunem, duuï, duuï! Duuï, duuï, niï raŋwa!
english: Return, return, O Shulamite; return, return, that we may look upon thee. What will ye see in the Shulamite? As it were the company of two armies.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, aperŋø ni raŋŋu nyijø Cunem en kaamar meeŋ jø Maanayim?
Wui, ï na nyi ŋat mo kare dwøŋ! Tietï moø ni iï kïth yi war yøø mïërö marge ka akadhø døc, ni bathï pøøth ni caala jap mïërö mo wø tïïc jø wø nyeŋge reegø.
english: How beautiful are thy feet with shoes, O prince's daughter! the joints of thy thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a cunning workman.

anywaa: Peellï legø ni nëëni keda wïlli mo yie päŋ ki køøŋ nyïïomøki, ni yiï bäre nëëni ko omeenø ka apiite mo oŋøøk, ni caala acooŋ nyeŋ beel mo ogëëŋö.
english: Thy navel is like a round goblet, which wanteth not liquor: thy belly is like an heap of wheat set about with lilies.

anywaa: Thunh moï moø na ariiø yøø mïërö ni caala nyïï purre ariiø ma cïp-jwøk.
english: Thy two breasts are like two young roes that are twins.

anywaa: Ŋutï nëëni keda øt koor mo otïïö ki lëëc liec, ni nyeŋŋï nëëni keda pulli mo wø en pääny Ëcbön ni beege moa en buut dhi kiir man wø cwøl ni Bath-Rabim. Umï nëëni ni mïërö keda øt koor man wø en Libaanø ni raŋŋa Damacka.
english: Thy neck is as a tower of ivory; thine eyes like the fishpools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bath–rabbim: thy nose is as the tower of Lebanon which looketh toward Damascus.

anywaa: Wïïï nëëni ni mïërö kaamar Kïn Karmël, ni jïër moï rege døøllø ni mïërö, ni caala waare ma dïmuur, ni mïërö mar jïëyï, nyeya pute ka böötö.
english: Thine head upon thee is like Carmel, and the hair of thine head like purple; the king is held in the galleries.

anywaa: Ïïni, ï mïërö døc ni ec mïnnö ki ïïni. Wui omëëya! Bëëtö mar dëërï bäre mïërö døc møn!
english: How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!

anywaa: Yi cwääc marï tiir kaamar jaath twöö, ni thunh moï nëëni keda jwale mo nyïï twöö.
english: This thy stature is like to a palm tree, and thy breasts to clusters of grapes.

anywaa: Ni kööa, na «A etha maal bäät twöö, nee nyïï gø lema.» Beerra man tïm thurï kaamar jwale mo nyïïomøki, ni tïm jam dhiï ni ŋwääö ni luy,
english: I said, I will go up to the palm tree, I will take hold of the boughs thereof: now also thy breasts shall be as clusters of the vine, and the smell of thy nose like apples;

anywaa: ni tïm nuum dhøk marï kaamar køøŋ nyïïomøki mo nyään.
english: And the roof of thy mouth like the best wine for my beloved, that goeth down sweetly, causing the lips of those that are asleep to speak.

anywaa: Beerra man ö køøŋ nyïïomøki manøgø ni put aay ni coonya baŋ omëëya,ni møle ki bäät buny dhee ki lage.
Aani, aana mar omëër mara, ni eni cwïnye lääŋŋa aani.
english: I am my beloved's, and his desire is toward me.

anywaa: Omëëya, ööï, nøø aa wøk ki dï pääny; ö waa cøø yïth atude moa en wøk, ni thöörø wäär kunece.
english: Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field; let us lodge in the villages.

anywaa: Beerra man laarø møøl yi pwöth omøki nee neenø; kanymør geno nø ŋøø, wala geno nø nipäta, wala adïkwäle geno nø ŋøø. Køøre nø, mëër onyoodha jïrï kaace.
english: Let us get up early to the vineyards; let us see if the vine flourish, whether the tender grape appear, and the pomegranates bud forth: there will I give thee my loves.

anywaa: Nyïï ocøøk ŋwäänyge ajääŋge wøk; ni dhi øtø marø päŋ ki nyïëdi mo nyärö ki mo oruu, mo yaa cooŋ piny kiperï, ï no omëër mara.
english: The mandrakes give a smell, and at our gates are all manner of pleasant fruits, new and old, which I have laid up for thee, O my beloved.

anywaa: Wui, doo naa ï caala coka ma dïcwøø mana dhøøth thunh mera; aani ni näk miï yaa joodø wøk, dhiï daa nuumö, ni bäŋ ŋat mo jääl aani.
english: O that thou wert as my brother, that sucked the breasts of my mother! when I should find thee without, I would kiss thee; yea, I should not be despised.

anywaa: Aani, ï daa kälö ni kïtha ïïni yi øt mera na pwöny aani. Aani, ï daa mooø ki køøŋø mo ŋwääi ni met nee maathï, ni beeye køøŋø mo tïïc ka pï nyïï adïkwäle 'moa.
english: I would lead thee, and bring thee into my mother's house, who would instruct me: I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine of the juice of my pomegranate.

anywaa: Beerra man ö cer caamï ni thäänha ki gø, ni ö cer cwïïï ni gäämï aani ki gø.
english: His left hand should be under my head, and his right hand should embrace me.

anywaa: Wui, u na nyïïakuk Jerucalem, a cäänna uuni, nee mëër ba tuuŋŋu nee ö maal këël kanyo pïïc kare.
english: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, until he please.

anywaa: ?Aŋø, man aŋa ni ööi ki dïtëën en, ni cäädhi ni ree ee nyaaŋ bäät omëër mare en?
english: Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved? I raised thee up under the apple tree: there thy mother brought thee forth: there she brought thee forth that bare thee.

anywaa: Aani, mëër mara anyoodha jïrï tier jaath;ni beeye tier jaadha ö meru ni put cäädhö yie ki mäc lwaar, ni put lwaar ki ïïni.

Gum aani cwïnyï kaamar ogut lweedø mar ŋïï mo pere leth jïrï, ni tïïyï aani kaamar ogut lweedø mar ŋïï mo ena cerï; kiper mëër teek døc kaamar thøø, ni këëyö mare leth ni caala yi bwörö, ni mëër liel kaamar maac, ni nitära ni caala leep maa Jwøk.
english: Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm: for love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as the grave: the coals thereof are coals of fire, which hath a most vehement flame.

anywaa: Pïï mo thööth maa-mëër ba jwöe; ni bäŋe näm mo wëëga gø køøl. Ni näk mo da dhaanhø mo cïpa jap kwärö mo paare bëët kiper nyeŋ mëër, jammi moe bëët di taa.
english: Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it: if a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be contemned.

anywaa: Waani, jïwa da cöökwa ma nyakøø mo poot thiinh, mo thure poot kär døøŋŋø. ?Agïnaŋø noo tïïcwa kiper cöökwa nø, kiper cäŋ mano pëënynyi yie ki nywöm?
english: We have a little sister, and she hath no breasts: what shall we do for our sister in the day when she shall be spoken for?

anywaa: Doo naa ena kal, dewa gëënnö ki øt koor mo teek mo tïïc ka gwel-bïrö. 'Ba doo naa ena dhi øtø, dewa gëëŋö ko opäp jaadha teek.
english: If she be a wall, we will build upon her a palace of silver: and if she be a door, we will inclose her with boards of cedar.

anywaa: Aani, a caala kal mo teek, ni ö thunhnhi 'moa ni caalge uut koor moa no ogeerø ni ena maal; ni ö omëërri mara ni jïte ki met ec baŋa.
english: I am a wall, and my breasts like towers: then was I in his eyes as one that found favour.

anywaa: Cølöman da pwöth omøki jïre kanya cwøl ni Baal-Amön. 'Ba eni pwöth omøki manøgø ee cïp ceŋ jiy mo gwøga gø jïre, ni ŋati man nø kännö jïre ki gwet-bïrö ma kuma ki røk nyïëdi mo wø gath.
english: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal–hamon; he let out the vineyard unto keepers; every one for the fruit thereof was to bring a thousand pieces of silver.

anywaa: 'Ba pwöth omøki mara beeye kipera; ni gwet-bïrö ma kuma beeye kiperï, ï na Cølöman. 'Ba gwet-bïrö ma dïpe ariiø beeye kiper jøøa gwøk nyïïjenni.
english: My vineyard, which is mine, is before me: thou, O Solomon, must have a thousand, and those that keep the fruit thereof two hundred.

anywaa: Wui, ï ni en yïth ajïniine, nyïïawääta yïthge ege ciiø ki dwørï; beerra man wïnynya dwørï.
english: Thou that dwellest in the gardens, the companions hearken to thy voice: cause me to hear it.

anywaa: Wui, omëëya, laar ö baŋa, ni tïmï kaamar purra wala thwønh aŋer mo ena bäät kïte moa näk bäätge da jer wø ŋwääi ni met.
english: Make haste, my beloved, and be thou like to a roe or to a young hart upon the mountains of spices.

anywaa: Moi beege luup mo wø nyooth ki yi wïc na nyooth Jwøki jï Aydheea wär Amöth kiper jø Juuda ki jø Jerucalem yïth nïr Udhaya, ki Jötham, ki Eeyeth, ki Edhekaya, kanya bëëtge ni gena nyeye mo Juuda.
english: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

anywaa: Wuuö Jwøk aköö, ni «Wui, Maal, cek ïthï! Wui, Piny, wïnynyï! Obwöre moa piidha na døøŋŋø cera, gena ö maal bääta ni gëëmge ki aani.
english: Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth: for the Lord hath spoken, I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me.

anywaa: Dhieŋ wänni ŋääe, ni ö arëënni ni ŋäc kar cam mana jiiŋ wänni jïre; 'ba jiya ma jø Icriel, a na wääge a kucge, ni tier luumma ba kwanyge.»
english: The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's crib: but Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider.

anywaa: Wui, u na wï jur ma jø raay en, u na jiy mo raay löör ŋäthu kaamar tëër en, ni bee u nyïïkwaac jiy mo wø tïïö ki gïï mo reyø, ni uuno obwöre mo temma raay møn! Wuuö Jwøk, eni na Jwø Icriel na en kur keere, aweyu, ni taagu gø, ni løøu ŋäthu wøk ki eni.
english: Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the Lord, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward.

anywaa: ?Aperŋø ni poot bëëdu ni uuno nieŋ yïth raay en? ?U poot manynya man pwöt uuni? Wïthu moø bëët bëëdö no opääŋ täwi, ni ö cwïnynyu ni kwääli ya raayi;
english: Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more: the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.

anywaa: ki mana täge ki thäc tietu këël wïthu, bäŋ kany mo jööt; 'ba beege ŋwiili keerge; ni beege kwör mo okwöt, ka atwøt mo onilwäk piny, mo bëëdö no odheeth, ni kär bääö, ni kär julö ki maaw.
english: From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.

anywaa: Ŋöömö maru araanynyi, ni waaŋ päänye mou ki maac; ni ö pwöthi mou ni lwøri ya jøøa pathi ni nëënö jïïu, ni wëëkge jammi mou bëët ränynyö.
english: Your country is desolate, your cities are burned with fire: your land, strangers devour it in your presence, and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers.

anywaa: 'Ba Dhayan awec ni dööŋe ni caala abïl koor man wø dööŋ yi pwödhö, ni caala pääny mo ociel dëëci dïër.
english: And the daughter of Zion is left as a cottage in a vineyard, as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged city.

anywaa: 'Ba onää Wuuö Jwøk, eni na wïth jammi bëët, bäŋ jiy mo ee wiiø ni kwøw dëëtø, doo na øøno tïmö kaamar Cødam ki Gømöra en.
english: Except the Lord of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah.

anywaa: Wui, u na bwöthe mo Jerucalem, ki jø Juuda, u ni bëëtö maru caala bëët jø Cødam ki jø Gømöra, Wïnynyu luum Wuuö Jwøk, ni cegu ïthu ki pwöc mar Jwøk marø,
english: Hear the word of the Lord, ye rulers of Sodom; give ear unto the law of our God, ye people of Gomorrah.

anywaa: Wuuö Jwøk aköö, no «?Olämme mou na thööth kønyge ŋø kipera? Aana jøøm ko olämme mo wø waaŋ bäre mou moø ni thööth yøø, ni beege olämme mo nyöök rööm ki dwäle mo dhäk. Yia ba mïnni ki rem mo rwädhe ki mo nyïïdïëk, wala rem atëëe.
english: To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me? saith the Lord: I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats.

anywaa: ?Kany wø ööu nyïma baŋ lam, aŋa na kööm uuni nou wïdu yi kal mara jaak?
english: When ye come to appear before me, who hath required this at your hand, to tread my courts?

anywaa: Muuce mou moø ni bäŋ tietge yøø kär cïpu këët! Gïï wø jïcge ŋwääi ni met mou, yia raac ki ge døc. Wödö man wø wøørru cäŋ man wø päär dwääyi yie, ki wøør cäŋ jwömö, ka acooŋe mo wø cwøllu, a ba jïëy ki ge; kiper acook lam mo wø tïïyu, tïïyu ni bëëtö maru patha kare.
english: Bring no more vain oblations; incense is an abomination unto me; the new moons and sabbaths, the calling of assemblies, I cannot away with; it is iniquity, even the solemn meeting.

anywaa: A män ka ajwöm mo wø wøørru kany wø päär dwääyi, ka ajwöm mou møga mo wø wøørru. Gena tïmö na tëër bääta, ni ööla ki käär ge.
english: Your new moons and your appointed feasts my soul hateth: they are a trouble unto me; I am weary to bear them.

anywaa: Kiper manøgønø, kany wø thaaŋu ceŋŋu maal nou lämö, waŋa kana kanø ki uuni. U këël doo lämö ki lam mo dwøŋ døc, aani, ïtha ba ciia; Kiper uuna jiy mo uuno kuny piny ki rem jiy.
english: And when ye spread forth your hands, I will hide mine eyes from you: yea, when ye make many prayers, I will not hear: your hands are full of blood.

anywaa: «Lwøgu dëëtu, ni tïïyu dëëtu ni waany, ni ö tïïe mou moa reyø ni daagu ge nyïma. Weyu tïï jammi moa reyø,
english: Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil;

anywaa: ni kwänynyu ki man tïïyu jammi moa beyø. Bëëdu nou tïïya ŋøl ma kare, ni joogu jøøa no ogäy. Cuŋŋu løø kïïe ki määr thuunhnhi.»
english: Learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.

anywaa: Wuuö Jwøk aköö, ni «Ennø, ööu nøø dwätø na aciel ri luubö. Këël na bëëde ni raay mou kwayø kaamar remø, di tïïö ni tar ni caala piiø, këël ge doo kwayø døc, di tïïö ni tar ni caala jïëc røømmø.
english: Come now, and let us reason together, saith the Lord: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.

anywaa: Ni näk mo u jïëy ni kïthu luumma bäät tïïc, gïïa beyø moo ciek yïth ŋøøm cammu camø;
english: If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land:

anywaa: 'ba ni näk mo u kweer ni gëëmu, u thöör opëëlle thöörö.» Luummögø caana Wuuö Jwøki ki dhee kiree.
english: But if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword: for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it.

anywaa: Raŋŋu, päänya beer atïmö kaamar kääbi, ni beeye päänya wara bëëdö ni tïïya ŋøl ma kare, na bëët jøøa beyø yie; 'ba ennø atïmö ni nuta dïnäge yie.
english: How is the faithful city become an harlot! it was full of judgment; righteousness lodged in it; but now murderers.

anywaa: Wui, Jerucalem, gwet-bïrö moï aränynyö ni dööŋge na nyal, ni ö kwøk nyïïomøki mo wø maathï ni jääpge rege ki pïï.
english: Thy silver is become dross, thy wine mixed with water:

anywaa: Kwääri moï gena jø ageem, ni rege ege dwalø ki kuuwe; ge bëët, ge mëër ki man cun geni ki gwel ki piny, ni ge rïïŋö køør muuce nee camge. Ge bëëdö ni kïïe ba gwøkge, ni ïthge ba cekge ki luup määr thuunhnhi kany wø pëëge kiper køny.
english: Thy princes are rebellious, and companions of thieves: every one loveth gifts, and followeth after rewards: they judge not the fatherless, neither doth the cause of the widow come unto them.

anywaa: Kiper manøgønø, Kwäärö Wuuö Jwøk, eni na wïth jammi bëët, eni na teek na näk Jwø Icriel, ena köö, ni «Aani kwör japa tïïc nyïïmän 'moa dëëra, coola coolø dëëtge, naa jïta ki jwöm.
english: Therefore saith the Lord, the Lord of hosts, the mighty One of Israel, Ah, I will ease me of mine adversaries, and avenge me of mine enemies:

anywaa: 'Ba aani da gïn mo tïïa tïïö dëërï thuwø, ï na Jerucalem, gïïa reyø dëërï na caal apøk nyal, twöna wøk, kaawat man wø ö apøk nyalli mo wø en dëër nywïënyö wø twöni wøk kany wø leeny nywïënyö ki maac.  Gïïa reyø bëët moa en dëërï käla wøk.
english: And I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin:

anywaa: Køøre a tïŋŋa maal jïrï ki pïëmme kaawat mana dïkwøŋ, ni tïŋŋa maal jïrï ki jø wø cïpi ka acaare kaawat mana tïïa ya acääŋŋe. Kanyøgø nø, ï na Jerucalem, ï di cwølø ni Pääny Bëënynyö, ni Pääny mo Bëënna Adïëri.»
english: And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness, the faithful city.

anywaa: Dhayan di piemø, ki jiye moo køp raacge, ki køør adïëri mar Jwøk ki bëënynyö mare.
english: Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and her converts with righteousness.

anywaa: 'Ba jø ageem ki jø raay ge di raanynyø na aciel bëët, ni ö jø wø wec Wuuö Jwøk ni ränyge.
english: And the destruction of the transgressors and of the sinners shall be together, and they that forsake the Lord shall be consumed.

anywaa: Uuni wïthu lääö kiper mana bëëdu nou lama jenni mo wø en cwïnynyu køørge, ni bëëdu ni wïthu lääö ki lam mana tïïyu kwöra näk you jierø yïth ajïniine.
english: For they shall be ashamed of the oaks which ye have desired, and ye shall be confounded for the gardens that ye have chosen.

anywaa: Kiper u tïmö kaamar jaath mo bøøge otal ni tïmu kaamar ajïniina mo ba jøøyi ki pïï.
english: For ye shall be as an oak whose leaf fadeth, and as a garden that hath no water.

anywaa: Jiy moa teek dëëtu otïmö kaamar akaraac mo otal, ni ö tïïe moge ni tïmge kaamar maac mo pätha yie, ni putge waaŋ bëët ni bäŋ ŋat mo lønye jïre ki man bïp gø.
english: And the strong shall be as tow, and the maker of it as a spark, and they shall both burn together, and none shall quench them.

anywaa: Man beeye luubö mana nyooth jï Aydheea wär Amöth kiper jø Juuda ki jø Jerucalem.
english: The word that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.

anywaa: 'Ba kanyo tïme na aŋuun nïne, kïdi mana en Øt Wuuö Jwøki bääte okëël piny ni teek, ni tïme na wïth kïte; eno tïŋ maal ni kaala thuuri, ni ö wïth juurre bëët ni rwäthge bääte.
english: And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the Lord's house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it.

anywaa: Wïth juurre mo thööth öö ni köge, ni «Ööu, owaa cøø bäät Kïn Wuuö Jwøk yi Øt Jwø Jeekap, kiper nee ø pwönynye ki jööre, nee ø cäädhø øtjööre.» Kiper luum ciik Jwøk wø caan ka yi Dhayan, ni beeye Jerucalem ni wø ö luup Wuuö Jwøki ki yie.
english: And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

anywaa: 'Ba eni luup ŋøle ŋølø yïthakic wïth juurre, ni ö wïth juurre mo thööth ni dwøk ge kanya ciel. Ni ö geni ni thääthge opëëlle moge na jap puur, ni thääthge tøøŋi moge na jap goor wïth jenni ki ge, ni bäŋe wï jur mo kwany tøŋ ki wï jur mør, ni ge ba pwönynyi këët ki leny.
english: And he shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.

anywaa: 'Ba ennø, u na nyïïkwaac Jeekap, ööu, nøø cäädhø ki yi tar mar Wuuö Jwøk.
english: O house of Jacob, come ye, and let us walk in the light of the Lord.

anywaa: Wui Wuuö Jwøk, jiyï ma jø dhi øt Jeekap aweyï, kiper mana caathge køør ajuuk mo jø kur tuul-cäŋ, ni tïmge ni ge tïïö ki jap adïëda kaamar jø Pilitin, ni dwätge ki juurre møøk.
english: Therefore thou hast forsaken thy people the house of Jacob, because they be replenished from the east, and are soothsayers like the Philistines, and they please themselves in the children of strangers.

anywaa: Yi ŋöömö marge opäŋ ki warkey ki gwet-bïrö, ni jap kwärö moge ba løny ki kwaan; ni ŋöömö marge thuwø päŋ ko okwëëc leny, ki jïëth okwëëc leny mo ba løny ki kwaan.
english: Their land also is full of silver and gold, neither is there any end of their treasures; their land is also full of horses, neither is there any end of their chariots:

anywaa: Ŋöömö marge bëëdö no opäŋ ki gïï wø lam na tïïcge ki ceŋge,  ni ge wøøra gïïögø na tïïcge ki lweetge.
english: Their land also is full of idols; they worship the work of their own hands, that which their own fingers have made:

anywaa: Ki køør japøge, jiy wïthge adwøk piny, ni ö jøøa kwörge døøŋŋø ni dwøgi piny. 'Ba kär niï wëënna ge.
english: And the mean man boweth down, and the great man humbleth himself: therefore forgive them not.

anywaa: Cou yïth agäp-kïte, ni kannu dëëtu kwöra ŋammø yïth ŋøøm, nou lwäära wëëc Wuuö Jwøk ka ajiem mare na dwøŋ.
english: Enter into the rock, and hide thee in the dust, for fear of the Lord, and for the glory of his majesty.

anywaa: 'Ba nyøth røk ka atöör mar jiy odwøk piny, ni ö bëëtö mar jø wø tïŋ dëëtge maal ni dwøgi piny. 'Ba Wuuö Jwøk keere beeye noo bëëdö ni di jiemø dïcäŋöce.
english: The lofty looks of man shall be humbled, and the haughtiness of men shall be bowed down, and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day.

anywaa: 'Ba Wuuö Jwøk, eni na wïth jammi bëët, da cäŋ ajäla mare mo ööa bäät jø atöör ki jø wø tïŋ dëëtge maal mo ge dwøge piny yie,
english: For the day of the Lord of hosts shall be upon every one that is proud and lofty, and upon every one that is lifted up; and he shall be brought low:

anywaa: ni ö ajäla mare bäät jenni bëët mo lur Libaanø moa bäyö na näk wïthge opööth maal, ki bäät jera teek mo Baacan,
english: And upon all the cedars of Lebanon, that are high and lifted up, and upon all the oaks of Bashan,

anywaa: ki bäät kïte bëët moa bäyö, ki bäät thuuri bëët moa bäyö,
english: And upon all the high mountains, and upon all the hills that are lifted up,

anywaa: ki bäät uut koor bëët moa no ogeerø ni ena maal, ki bäät kwör gwøk røk bëët moa no ogeerø ni teek,
english: And upon every high tower, and upon every fenced wall,

anywaa: ki bäät baabuure bëët moa näk mo gath, ki bäät jïëth näm bëët moa beyø.
english: And upon all the ships of Tarshish, and upon all pleasant pictures.

anywaa: 'Ba atöör mar jiy odwøk piny, ni ö bëëtö mar jø wø tïŋ dëëtge maal ni dwøgi piny. 'Ba Wuuö Jwøk keere beeye noo bëëdö ni di jiemø dïcäŋöce.
english: And the loftiness of man shall be bowed down, and the haughtiness of men shall be made low: and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day.

anywaa: 'Ba kït gïï wø lam rwäänyö na bäre bäre.
english: And the idols he shall utterly abolish.

anywaa: 'Ba jiy oreŋ kwöra ŋammø yïth kïte ki kwöra ŋammø yïth ŋøøm, ni ge lwäära wëër mar Wuuö Jwøk ka ajiem mare na dwøŋ, kanyo ö maal noo jäŋ piny.
english: And they shall go into the holes of the rocks, and into the caves of the earth, for fear of the Lord, and for the glory of his majesty, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth.

anywaa: 'Ba dïcäŋöce kït gïï wø lam moa tïïcge kiper dëëtge nee wøørge, na no otïïö ki gwet-bïrö ki warkey, oleeŋge piny, ni tïmge na mo adule ka adïlïge.
english: In that day a man shall cast his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which they made each one for himself to worship, to the moles and to the bats;

anywaa: Geno reŋ kwöra ŋammø yïth kïte ki kwöra no okaaŋŋø yïth kïte, ni ge lwäära wëër mar Wuuö Jwøk ka ajiem mare na dwøŋ, kanyo ö maal noo jäŋ piny.
english: To go into the clefts of the rocks, and into the tops of the ragged rocks, for fear of the Lord, and for the glory of his majesty, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth.

anywaa: Weyu ŋääth dhaanhø, man ni jwïëy ka ume keere jaak en. ?Aŋø, da kare cøøn?
english: Cease ye from man, whose breath is in his nostrils: for wherein is he to be accounted of?

anywaa: 'Ba ka adïëri møn, Kwäärö Wuuö Jwøk, eni na wïth jammi bëët, ena bäät man käl køny mare wøk ki bäät Juuda ki Jerucalem, ni beege caammi ki pïï mo wø kønyge dëëtge ki ge;
english: For, behold, the Lord, the Lord of hosts, doth take away from Jerusalem and from Judah the stay and the staff, the whole stay of bread, and the whole stay of water,

anywaa: ki cwøw leny moa teek, ki jø leny møga, ki dïŋut luup ki nyïïkuk Jwøk, ki jø adïëda ki jø døøŋŋø,
english: The mighty man, and the man of war, the judge, and the prophet, and the prudent, and the ancient,

anywaa: ki kwääc lwaa pïërabïïc, ki jøøa kwörge døøŋŋø, ki jø wø cïpi ka acaare, ki jø wø nyeŋge reegø ki tïïe mo wø tïïc ki ceŋ, ki jø thïëth.
english: The captain of fifty, and the honourable man, and the counsellor, and the cunning artificer, and the eloquent orator.

anywaa: Aani obwöc cwøw tïïa tïïö na kwääri bäätge, ni tïmge ni ge ena tiet obwöre mo wïthge känni.
english: And I will give children to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them.

anywaa: Ni tïm jiyi ni ŋati man nø watge thiele piny, ni ö ŋat atut man nø ni dïïm ŋat atut mare. Wøpe ge ööa maal bäät jø døøŋŋø, ni tïm ŋata no otaaø ni töödö bäät ŋata no owøørø.
english: And the people shall be oppressed, every one by another, and every one by his neighbour: the child shall behave himself proudly against the ancient, and the base against the honourable.

anywaa: 'Ba ŋati man nø ki røk nyïïmenni ki dhi øt wänni keere, dhaanhø aciel omaae ni kööe jï gø, ni «Nyie, ïïni abïï dagø jïrï; tïmï ni ïïna dïbwödhi marwa, nee paani no oränynyö en nee tïme ni ena cerï!»
english: When a man shall take hold of his brother of the house of his father, saying, Thou hast clothing, be thou our ruler, and let this ruin be under thy hand:

anywaa: 'Ba dïcäŋeca, ŋatøgø ojwöŋi ni dwøre ee tïŋ maal, ni kööe, ni «Aani a ba tïmö na dïkunyi maru; bäŋ cam jïra wala abïïe mo ena paara. Kär a tïïyu na dïbwödhi mar jiy.»
english: In that day shall he swear, saying, I will not be an healer; for in my house is neither bread nor clothing: make me not a ruler of the people.
