english: And when they heard these sayings, they were full of wrath, and cried out, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.

anywaa: Ni tïm paaci bäre ni döönni. Ni reŋge kar acooŋa karge bëët, ni ge pieya Geea ki Aritarka, jak Macedönia mo wø cäädhi ki Pøøl na aciel.
english: And the whole city was filled with confusion: and having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul's companions in travel, they rushed with one accord into the theatre.

anywaa: 'Ba Pøøl manynya man ci dï lwaaøgø, 'ba ena män bääŋi.
english: And when Paul would have entered in unto the people, the disciples suffered him not.

anywaa: 'Ba jø Eecia møøk thuwø mo kwörge døøŋŋø, moa näk nyïïawääte, gena öön baŋe ni ge kwaya gø nee ba ci yi kar acooŋa.
english: And certain of the chief of Asia, which were his friends, sent unto him, desiring him that he would not adventure himself into the theatre.

anywaa: 'Ba jøøgø rëëdi ni ge cara luup ma teeŋi. Kiper acooŋa manøgø wïïe ree akiere, ni ö thööthge ni kucge gïna öge kanya ciel kipere.
english: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another: for the assembly was confused; and the more part knew not wherefore they were come together.

anywaa: 'Ba jø Juuth ŋat poge ma Alekdhander akïthge nyïm, nee tier luummögø caane. Ni ö Alekdhander ni tïŋ cere maal, ni manynya man piem jø poge ki luummögø.
english: And they drew Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. And Alexander beckoned with the hand, and would have made his defence unto the people.

anywaa: 'Ba na ŋecge gø ni ena ŋat Juuth, gena rëëdö ki dwøl aciel ki kany mo jïtö ki kar caae ariiø, ni ge rëëdi, ni «Dwøŋŋa Artema jwø jø Epeca!»
english: But when they knew that he was a Jew, all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya ö kwääy päänynyi na nø jook lwaaøgø, ena köö, ni «?Wui jø Epeca, aŋø, da ŋat mo kuc gø ni beeye jø Epeca wø koor øt jwøk mar Artema na dwøŋ, ki kïn jwøk mana pänhnhö ki maal?
english: And when the townclerk had appeased the people, he said, Ye men of Ephesus, what man is there that knoweth not how that the city of the Ephesians is a worshipper of the great goddess Diana, and of the image which fell down from Jupiter?

anywaa: Na ŋäyu gø nø, ni gïïögø ba maar piem, u dou lïŋö nø, ni bäŋ gïn mo tïïyu.
english: Seeing then that these things cannot be spoken against, ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly.

anywaa: Kiper jøøi ii akälu kany ni gena jiy mo bäŋ gïn mo raac mo ege tïïö dëër øt jwøk, wala ajaany mo ege tïïö dëër jwøø.
english: For ye have brought hither these men, which are neither robbers of churches, nor yet blasphemers of your goddess.

anywaa: Kiper manøgønø, ni näk Dimitaria ki jø wø tïïc tïïögø na en buute yøøgø, nee jïge da luubö ki dhaanhø mør, kwör løøe nutö, ni kwääri dagø. Wär cige baŋ løøk.
english: Wherefore if Demetrius, and the craftsmen which are with him, have a matter against any man, the law is open, and there are deputies: let them implead one another.

anywaa: 'Ba nee poot da gïn mør mo manynyu manynyø, ocaan ya acooŋa mano cooŋ.
english: But if ye enquire any thing concerning other matters, it shall be determined in a lawful assembly.

anywaa: Kiper kanymør ø di jäälö ni pøø da dïŋaŋ dïcäŋi, ni tïme ni bäŋ gïn mo maarø caan kiper luummi ni kierø wïthø ki gø en.»
english: For we are in danger to be called in question for this day's uproar, there being no cause whereby we may give an account of this concourse.

anywaa: 'Ba na nø caan gïnögø, acooŋa manøgø awëëk keethø.
english: And when he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.

anywaa: 'Ba na pï dïŋaŋ manøgø piny, Pøøl ajääk baŋ bääŋi. 'Ba na nø luum geni døøc, gena wiie ni aa Macedönia.
english: And after the uproar was ceased, Paul called unto him the disciples, and embraced them, and departed for to go into Macedonia.

anywaa: 'Ba na nø caath kwörögø bëët ni cøma cwïny jiy døøc, ena ci po jø Gïrïïk.
english: And when he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece,

anywaa: Ni bëëde kaace ki dwäde adäk. 'Ba kanya dee aa Ciria ki jää naam, luubö mør aput jø Juuthi tuut kipere. Ni caar wïïe ni beerra man døøe ni cøra Macedönia.
english: And there abode three months. And when the Jews laid wait for him, as he was about to sail into Syria, he purposed to return through Macedonia.

anywaa: 'Ba jøøa aay ki Pøøl beege Cöpater o Payra ma nyï Beria, ki Aritarka ki Cekunda ma jak Thecalönika, ki Geea ma nyï Derbe, ki Timöthi, ki jaak Eecia na näk Taykika ki Taröpima.
english: And there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timothy; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.

anywaa: Jøøgø gena aay ni koorge waani yi Tarööa.
english: These going before tarried for us at Troas.

anywaa: 'Ba køør nïr Ajwöma mar Møga Näk Ree Bäŋ Thømmø, waana läw tïŋŋö Pilipay ki jää naam. 'Ba na tïme na ri nïne abïïc, waana pïï buutge Tarööa. Ni bëëtwa kaace ki nïne abïriiø.
english: And we sailed away from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and came unto them to Troas in five days; where we abode seven days.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïme na täk tïïc, ni dëëtwa ewa cooŋ kanya ciel nee wa cämwa ki møø, Pøøl acäänö ki geni, ni ee cooŋø ki cwïnye ni eni tïŋŋö ka aruunnø. Ni tïïc luumme ni yie bäär ni këët dï wäär.
english: And upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them, ready to depart on the morrow; and continued his speech until midnight.

anywaa: 'Ba øt pööki mana en maal na cooŋwa yie, yie da lambae mo thööth.
english: And there were many lights in the upper chamber, where they were gathered together.

anywaa: 'Ba nyen ma wøp mo cwøl ni Yutika opï piny dha awëërnyeŋ. 'Ba kanya ruu Pøølli ni poot cäänö, eni nyeŋŋe amägö døc, ni bute, ni put päth piny ki yi dää øt pööki maal. Ni tïŋi maal no othøw.
english: And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third loft, and was taken up dead.

anywaa: 'Ba Pøøl aci piny baŋ gø ni guuŋe bäät gø, ni tïŋ gø ni kïth gø kööre, ni kööe, ni «Käru lwäyö. Jwïëye poot nut dëëre.»
english: And Paul went down, and fell on him, and embracing him said, Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him.

anywaa: 'Ba na nø døø Pøølli maal, ni pøt møø ni cäme, ena wääö ki geni ki kany mo yie bäär, gøøc mana tuul cäŋŋi. Køøre, ena aay.
english: When he therefore was come up again, and had broken bread, and eaten, and talked a long while, even till break of day, so he departed.

anywaa: Ni kälge nyenøgø no okwøw, ni yïthge omïnnö døc.
english: And they brought the young man alive, and were not a little comforted.

anywaa: 'Ba na ciwa yi jää naam, waana tïŋŋö ki gø ni ciwa Eecø, ni ewa caarø ni Pøøl kïthwa yi jääy kaace, kiper na kwøŋ gø caan. Kiper eni ki dëëre ee caarø ni eno cäädhi ki wøk.
english: And we went before to ship, and sailed unto Assos, there intending to take in Paul: for so had he appointed, minding himself to go afoot.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya røømme ki waani yi Eecø, ena kïthwa yi jääy ni ciwa Mitilin.
english: And when he met with us at Assos, we took him in, and came to Mitylene.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïŋwa kaace ka aruunnø man, waana pïï nyïm Kiø. 'Ba na tïme na aruunnø maya, waana mäk piny yi Cemø. 'Ba na tïme na amöölla maya, waana pïï Milita.
english: And we sailed thence, and came the next day over against Chios; and the next day we arrived at Samos, and tarried at Trogyllium; and the next day we came to Miletus.

anywaa: Kiper ocaar Pøølli ni eni pöödhö ki buut Epeca, kiper eni ba many man ruue Eecia. Kiper eni läädö nee tïme ni ena Jerucalem ki cäŋ Pentikø, ni näk mo løny jïre.
english: For Paul had determined to sail by Ephesus, because he would not spend the time in Asia: for he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost.

anywaa: 'Ba na pïïe Milita ena jääk Epeca, ni eni cwöla jaak acooŋ Jwøk baŋe.
english: And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called the elders of the church.

anywaa: 'Ba na nø öge, ena köö jïge, ni «Uuni ki dëëtu, bëëtö mara mana beeda dïïu, këël dïcäŋa kwøŋa tiera këël yi Eecia, ŋäyu,
english: And when they were come to him, he said unto them, Ye know, from the first day that I came into Asia, after what manner I have been with you at all seasons,

anywaa: naa tïnynya Wuuö ni dëëra yaa dwøk piny naa jwöŋö, ni jït dëëra ki gïï mo leth ki køør luup moa tuut jø Juuthi bääta.
english: Serving the Lord with all humility of mind, and with many tears, and temptations, which befell me by the lying in wait of the Jews:

anywaa: Ni kära lwäyö ki man køba jammi bëët jïïu moa doo beyø kiperu ki man wïnynyu gø. Ni pwönynya uuni nyïm jiy bëët, ni cäŋa pöö naa cøøa yi ødi nø ki ødi nø,
english: And how I kept back nothing that was profitable unto you, but have shewed you, and have taught you publickly, and from house to house,

anywaa: naa cäänna jø Juuth ki jø Gïrïïk bëët kiper løk cwïny baŋ Jwøk, ki ŋääth Kwääyø ma Jecu Krictø.
english: Testifying both to the Jews, and also to the Greeks, repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.

anywaa: «'Ba kawaane, neennu, a aa Jerucalem ni aano mak Jwïëc Jwøki, ni kuua gïno pïï dëëra kunöce,
english: And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there:

anywaa: 'ba tiirra man wø køp Jwïëc Jwøki na en kur keere jïra yïth mïëri bëët, ni tööc ki jwør gïï mo leth ena nyïma.
english: Save that the Holy Ghost witnesseth in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me.

anywaa: 'Ba jwïëya patha yaa caarø ni gïn mo pere leth jïra, mo daa gwøø. 'Ba mana manynya keere beeye ki man thööra tïïc mara, ki tïïc mana wëëk Kwäärö ma Jecu aani ki man køba gïr luumma nyään na met mar met yi Jwøk.
english: But none of these things move me, neither count I my life dear unto myself, so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God.

anywaa: «'Ba kawaane, neennu, ŋääa ni uuni bëët, u na dïïu caadha naa køpa luum buc Jwøk, waŋa ba jootu këët.
english: And now, behold, I know that ye all, among whom I have gone preaching the kingdom of God, shall see my face no more.

anywaa: Kiper manøgønø, a cäänna uuni dïcäŋi, naa tøør ri remmu karubëët.
english: Wherefore I take you to record this day, that I am pure from the blood of all men.

anywaa: Kiper a kär lwäyö ki man caana luup Jwøk bëët jïïu.
english: For I have not shunned to declare unto you all the counsel of God.

anywaa: 'Ba kawaane gwøgu rou, ni gwøgu pïïth bäre, pïïdha cïp Jwïëc Jwøki na en kur keere ceŋŋu ni uuna dïkuye, na acooŋ Jwøk na joode ki køør remme caammu.
english: Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the which the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers, to feed the church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood.

anywaa: Kiper ŋääa, ni køøra noo aaa, orude mo reyø døc ööa dïïu ni ba wecge pïïth.
english: For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.

anywaa: 'Ba jø møøk dïïu røkge othïïŋge, ni kierge wïthu nee cwïny bääŋi løøge køørge.
english: Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them.

anywaa: Kiper manøgønø, gwøgu rou, ni parru wïthu ki cwiiya näk adäk na thööra cääŋŋe ki wärre naa köömma uuni bëët ki luubö mo teek, naa jwöŋö.
english: Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears.

anywaa: 'Ba kawaane, uuna wiia cer Jwøk, ki luum met ec mare, ni beeye noo wëëk u tëënnö, ni mëëk olaawi uuni na aciel ki jøøa näk ocïp kur keerge bëët na mo Jwøk.
english: And now, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified.

anywaa: Bäŋ ŋat mo gwete yaa parø, wala warkey, wala abïïe.
english: I have coveted no man's silver, or gold, or apparel.

anywaa: Uuni ki dëëtu ŋäyu ni ceŋŋi ii beege na tïny aani ki jøøa öö ki aani na aciel.
english: Yea, ye yourselves know, that these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me.

anywaa: 'Ba ki yïth japøgø bëët, a nyuunhnha uuni, ni dhaanhø doo tïïö døc na enøgønø ni køny jøøa can, ni para wïïe ki luupa caan Kwäärö ma Jecu, na kööe, ni ‹Beerra mar ŋat wø cïpi, ni kaala ŋat wø mooc.› »
english: I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.

anywaa: 'Ba na nø caan luummögø, cøŋŋe akëël piny ni läme ki geni bëët.
english: And when he had thus spoken, he kneeled down, and prayed with them all.

anywaa: Ni jwöŋge bëët, ni gämge gø, ni nuumge dhi gø.
english: And they all wept sore, and fell on Paul's neck, and kissed him,

anywaa: Ni cwïnyge opädhö døc ki luumma caane, ni waŋe ba cäŋge jootø këët. Ni öge ni jiethge eni bäät jääy.
english: Sorrowing most of all for the words which he spake, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him unto the ship.

anywaa: 'Ba na nø pääwa ki geni ni tïŋwa ki jää naam, waana put pööth Køc. 'Ba na tïme na aruunnø man, waana pïï Röd. Køøre na jöökwa kunöce, waana pööth Patara.
english: And it came to pass, that after we were gotten from them, and had launched, we came with a straight course unto Coos, and the day following unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara:

anywaa: 'Ba na nø jïtwa ki jääy mo ŋuta løø Pönicia, waana ci yie ni aacwa.
english: And finding a ship sailing over unto Phoenicia, we went aboard, and set forth.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïm Caypara ni nëënö, ni ewa wii bäät caam, waana ci Ciria, ni mäkwa piny Tayar. Kiper beeye kanya käl jammi wøk ki yi jääy.
english: Now when we had discovered Cyprus, we left it on the left hand, and sailed into Syria, and landed at Tyre: for there the ship was to unlade her burden.

anywaa: 'Ba na nø jootwa kar bääŋi waana bëëdö kaace ki geni ki nïne abïriiø. Ni cäänge Pøøl ki køør Jwïëc Jwøk, ni köge, ni «Kärï ci Jerucalem.»
english: And finding disciples, we tarried there seven days: who said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya thum nïrögø, waana tïŋŋö ni cäŋwa døø ri wääth marwa. 'Ba geni bëët ki määrge ko obwöre, waana jiethge këël mana pïïcwa ŋää paac. Ni këëlwa cøŋwa piny lak ageela, ni lämwa, ni määthwa dëëtwa.
english: And when we had accomplished those days, we departed and went our way; and they all brought us on our way, with wives and children, till we were out of the city: and we kneeled down on the shore, and prayed.

anywaa: Køøre waana ci yi jääy, ni døøge paac.
english: And when we had taken our leave one of another, we took ship; and they returned home again.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïŋwa wääth ki Tayar, waana pïï Tølame, ni määthwa nyïïmëëe ni bëëtwa ki geni ki dïcäŋ aciel.
english: And when we had finished our course from Tyre, we came to Ptolemais, and saluted the brethren, and abode with them one day.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïme na aruunnø man, waana tïŋŋö ni ciwa Cecaria ni dønywa øt Pilip, ŋat wø køp luum Jwøk na näk dhaanhø aciel dï Jøøa näk Abïriiø, ni bëëtwa buute.
english: And the next day we that were of Paul's company departed, and came unto Caesarea: and we entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, which was one of the seven; and abode with him.

anywaa: 'Ba jïre da nyïïe aŋween ma nyïïakuue mo poot kär nywømø, ni ge wø køpa gïï mo poot ena nyïm.
english: And the same man had four daughters, virgins, which did prophesy.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya bëëtwa kaace ki nïne møøk, nyikuŋ Jwøk mør mo nyeŋŋe Agaba aöö ki yi Judia.
english: And as we tarried there many days, there came down from Judaea a certain prophet, named Agabus.

anywaa: 'Ba na ö baŋwa, kaw mar Pøøl alwøre ni twöc tiete ki ceŋŋe keere ki gø, ni kööe, ni «Man beeye gïna caan Jwïëc Jwøki na en kur keere, ni ‹Wää kaw man en otwöc jø Juuthi mo wø en yi Jerucalem na ennø nø, ni cïpge gø ceŋ juurre.› »
english: And when he was come unto us, he took Paul's girdle, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus saith the Holy Ghost, So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owneth this girdle, and shall deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.

anywaa: 'Ba na wïnywa gïnögø, waani ki jøøa en kaace, Pøøl akwaacwa nee ba ci yi Jerucalem.
english: And when we heard these things, both we, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem.

anywaa: 'Ba Pøøl ajutö, ni kööe, na «?Agïnaŋø ni tïïyu enøgø, nou jwöŋö nou thääŋa cwïnya? Kiper yaa nø caar ni paa tööc keere, 'ba këël a doo thøw thuwø yi Jerucalem kiper nyeŋ Kwäärö ma Jecu, yia doo met.»
english: Then Paul answered, What mean ye to weep and to break mine heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.

anywaa: 'Ba na jootwa gø ni luumwa ba wïnynye, waana lïŋö, ni köwa, ni «Mana many Wuue, wëëk tïïc.»
english: And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be done.

anywaa: 'Ba køør nïrögø dëëtwa ajiiŋwa ni ciwa Jerucalem.
english: And after those days we took up our carriages, and went up to Jerusalem.

anywaa: Ni ö bääŋi møøk mo käla Cecaria ni jiethge waani, ni ge kïtha wa po Manecan ma nyï Caypara, ŋat ma bääŋ mo okwøŋ jïëy cøøn, ni beeye ŋato bëëtwa buute.
english: There went with us also certain of the disciples of Caesarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, with whom we should lodge.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya pïïcwa yi Jerucalem, waana pänh nyïïmëëe ki met ec.
english: And when we were come to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïme na aruunnø man, Pøøl aci øt Jeemeth ki waani. 'Ba jaak acooŋ Jwøk bëët ena kaace.
english: And the day following Paul went in with us unto James; and all the elders were present.

anywaa: 'Ba na nø määthwa geni, Pøøl gïïa tïïc Jwøki dï juurre ki ree, apare jïge no oceele oceele.
english: And when he had saluted them, he declared particularly what things God had wrought among the Gentiles by his ministry.

anywaa: 'Ba na wïnyge gø, Jwøk apwøcge. Ni köge ki eni, «Neenï nø, cöökwa, da jiy mo ojïëy dëët jø Juuth mo jïtö ki kume mo thööth, mo ge bëëdö ni cwïnyge caya ciik Jwøk døc.
english: And when they heard it, they glorified the Lord, and said unto him, Thou seest, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are which believe; and they are all zealous of the law:

anywaa: 'Ba gïrï acaan jïge, ni jø Juuth bëët moa bëëdö dï juurre wø pwönynyï pwönynyö ki man wecge ciik Modhe, ni köömmï geni ni kär nyïïge daŋge, wala ki man gwøkge kööŋŋe moa cääŋŋe.
english: And they are informed of thee, that thou teachest all the Jews which are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs.

anywaa: ?Agïnaŋø nø noo tïïc? Kiper wïnyge wïnynyö ni ïïna nø ö kany.
english: What is it therefore? the multitude must needs come together: for they will hear that thou art come.

anywaa: Kiper manøgønø, tïïc gïno caanwa jïrï. Da jiy aŋween mo okööŋ dïwa.
english: Do therefore this that we say to thee: We have four men which have a vow on them;

anywaa: Käl jøøgøøni ni døøyï dëërï mo waany ki geni na aciel, ni coolï gweta dege cïbö, kiper nee wïthge gwäärge wøk. Kanyøgø nø, oŋäc jøw bëëti ni gïïa caan jïge kiperï, bäŋ tietge, 'ba oŋäcge ni ïïni ki dëërï ï bëëdö ni ciik Jwøk iï gwøø.
english: Them take, and purify thyself with them, and be at charges with them, that they may shave their heads: and all may know that those things, whereof they were informed concerning thee, are nothing; but that thou thyself also walkest orderly, and keepest the law.

anywaa: 'Ba mar juurre moa näk ojïëy, waana nø jääk baŋge ki wëëlö kiper dwøna ŋølwa piny, ni ge doo bëëdö ni karge bäyö ki gïï mo onää jï juu, ki cam remø, ki gïn mo odeeø, ki käp.»
english: As touching the Gentiles which believe, we have written and concluded that they observe no such thing, save only that they keep themselves from things offered to idols, and from blood, and from strangled, and from fornication.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïme na aruunnø man, Pøøl jøøgø na aŋween yøø akäle, ni døøc dëëre mo waany ki geni na aciel, ni ci Øt Jwøk Mana Dwøŋ kuna caan cäŋ mano thum nïr døøc dëël mo waany marge yie, ki kanyo cïp olämme kiperge bëët.
english: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself with them entered into the temple, to signify the accomplishment of the days of purification, until that an offering should be offered for every one of them.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïm nïne moøgø na abïriiø ni karge cään ki thumö, jø Juuth moa öö ki Eecia, na neenge Pøøl yi kal mar Øt Jwøk Mana Dwøŋ, yïth jøøa thööth na en kaace bëët acoonge, ni makge Pøøl,
english: And when the seven days were almost ended, the Jews which were of Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the people, and laid hands on him,

anywaa: ni ge rëëdö, ni «Jø Icriel, kunynyu! Ŋati en beeye nyena pwöny jiy bëët bäät piny bäre ki man taakge luup jø pøø, ki ciik Jwøk, ki Øt Jwøk marø man en, ni käl jø Gïrïïk yie thuwø, ni tïïc kany ni en kur keere na mar Jwøk en ni ba waany.»
english: Crying out, Men of Israel, help: This is the man, that teacheth all men every where against the people, and the law, and this place: and further brought Greeks also into the temple, and hath polluted this holy place.

anywaa: Kiper Taröpima nyï Epeca akwøŋge joot pääny ki eni na aciel, ni ege caarø ni eno käl Pøølli yi kal mar Øt Jwøk Mana Dwøŋ.
english: (For they had seen before with him in the city Trophimus an Ephesian, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)

anywaa: Kanyøgø paac bäre apäy, ni ö jiyi bëët ni reŋge kanya ciel, ni makge Pøøl, ni peege gø wøk ki yi Øt Jwøk. Ni ö dhøk kiiri ni puti cïëgö.
english: And all the city was moved, and the people ran together: and they took Paul, and drew him out of the temple: and forthwith the doors were shut.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya tïmge ni ge caya man 'näkge Pøøl, awïny kwääy dïkuye, ni Jerucalem bäre atïmö ni döönni.
english: And as they went about to kill him, tidings came unto the chief captain of the band, that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.

anywaa: Ni puti ya jø tøŋ käl ki kwääc lwaae, ni reŋge baŋ jiy. 'Ba jiy na raŋge kwääy jø tøŋ ki jø tøŋ, ceŋge awecge ri Pøøl ki pöödö.
english: Who immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran down unto them: and when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, they left beating of Paul.

anywaa: Kanyøgø kwääy dïkuye acøø ni mak gø, ni cïpe ki dwøl, ni eni twöc ko oguudi ariiø. Ni pëëe, ni ena ŋa, na agïnaŋø na tïïe.
english: Then the chief captain came near, and took him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains; and demanded who he was, and what he had done.

anywaa: 'Ba jø møøk dï lwaaøgø rëëdi ni ge cara luup ma teeŋi. 'Ba na tïme ni tier luubö ba maar kwany kiper dïŋaŋ, ena cïpö ki dwøl ni Pøøl kïth kar dïkuye.
english: And some cried one thing, some another, among the multitude: and when he could not know the certainty for the tumult, he commanded him to be carried into the castle.

anywaa: 'Ba na iith thudhi mana en dhi øtø, Pøøl atïŋ jø tøŋŋi ni käärge gø, kiper gootø mar lwaaøgø.
english: And when he came upon the stairs, so it was, that he was borne of the soldiers for the violence of the people.

anywaa: Kiper lwaak cäädhi ni ge rëëdö køøre, ni «'Nägï! 'Nägï!»
english: For the multitude of the people followed after, crying, Away with him.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya ö Pøølli na tïme ni eni kïtha kar dïkuye, ena köö jï kwääy dïkuye, ni «?Løny ki man caana gïn mør jïrï?» 'Ba kwääy dïkuye aköö, na «?Aŋø, dhi Gïrïïk ŋäyï?
english: And as Paul was to be led into the castle, he said unto the chief captain, May I speak unto thee? Who said, Canst thou speak Greek?

anywaa: ?Ï paa nyï Ijep cøøn, na coon yïth jiy ya awääre maya, na bwøth dïnäge wøk dï paap moa näk kume aŋween?»
english: Art not thou that Egyptian, which before these days madest an uproar, and leddest out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers?

anywaa: 'Ba aløk Pøølli, ni «Aana ŋat Juuth naa käla Tarca yi Cilicia. Aana o thwønh paana ŋäc døc. A kwaya ïïni, nee jiy cäänna.»
english: But Paul said, I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and, I beseech thee, suffer me to speak unto the people.

anywaa: 'Ba na nø jïëc gø nee cäänne, Pøøl acuŋŋö bäät thudhi ni tïŋ cere maal ni jooga jiy. 'Ba na nø lïŋge bëët, gena cäänne ki dhi Ibaru, ni kööe,
english: And when he had given him licence, Paul stood on the stairs, and beckoned with the hand unto the people. And when there was made a great silence, he spake unto them in the Hebrew tongue, saying,

anywaa: «Nyïïmera ki wëëga, wïnynyu mara noo caana jïïu en.»
english: Men, brethren, and fathers, hear ye my defence which I make now unto you.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya wïnyge gø ni eni cäänö ka geni ki dhi Ibaru, gena put lïŋŋe døøc. Ni ö Pøølli ni kööe,
english: (And when they heard that he spake in the Hebrew tongue to them, they kept the more silence: and he saith,)

anywaa: ni «Aana ŋat Juuth, naa nywølla Tarca yi Cilicia. 'Ba a piitha paani en, ni aano pwönynyö cer Gameeliel ki pwöc mo teek kiper ciik Jwøk mar kwäyø, ni cwïnya wø caya Jwøk kaawat man tïïyu dïcäŋi en.
english: I am verily a man which am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, and taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous toward God, as ye all are this day.

anywaa: Ni gëëma ki Jöör Lam manøgø, naa nääö ki jiy, naa töö ni kïtha geni øt twöc, ni beege cwøw ki mään bëët.
english: And I persecuted this way unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.

anywaa: Ni manøgø ŋäc Kwääy Lammi Mana Dwøŋ ki jaae bëët moa en dï jiy. Ni bee geni na lwøra weeli baŋge moa göörge baŋ nyïïmëëkge moa en Damacka, ni cøøa kuna øømma jø wø caath køør Jöör Lam manøgø, nee ge käla yi Jerucalem ni geno twöö, nee ge jääl.
english: As also the high priest doth bear me witness, and all the estate of the elders: from whom also I received letters unto the brethren, and went to Damascus, to bring them which were there bound unto Jerusalem, for to be punished.

anywaa: «'Ba yi wääth mara na aa, na tïm kara ni cään ki Damacka ki dïcäŋ, tar mo dwøŋ mo ööi ki maal aput rieny bääta.
english: And it came to pass, that, as I made my journey, and was come nigh unto Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me.

anywaa: Ni pädha ni wïnynya dwøl mo cäänö ka aani, ni ‹?Cøøl, Cøøl, aŋø ni gëëmï ki aani en?›
english: And I fell unto the ground, and heard a voice saying unto me, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?

anywaa: «'Ba aana köö, ni ‹?Ïïna ŋa, Kwäärö?› «Ni kööe jïra, ni ‹Aana Jecu nyï Nadhareth ni gëëmï ki gø enø.›
english: And I answered, Who art thou, Lord? And he said unto me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom thou persecutest.

anywaa: 'Ba jøøa en buuta, tar manøgø aneenge, 'ba dwør ŋata cäänö ki aani, kärge wïnynyö.
english: And they that were with me saw indeed the light, and were afraid; but they heard not the voice of him that spake to me.

anywaa: «Ni kööa, na ‹?Agïnaŋø noo tïïa, Kwäärö?› «Ni kö Kwäärö ki aani, ni ‹Ö maal ni ciï Damacka. Gïno tïïyï ocaan jïrï kaace.›
english: And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said unto me, Arise, and go into Damascus; and there it shall be told thee of all things which are appointed for thee to do.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïma naa ba nëënö kiper tayøgøøni na tar døc, jøøa öö ki aani aana piecge ki cera, ni kïthge aani yi Damacka.
english: And when I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that were with me, I came into Damascus.

anywaa: «'Ba nyen mør mo nyeŋŋe Ananaya aö baŋa, ŋat mo cwïnye ena køør Jwøk kaawat man wø caani ri ciik Jwøk, ni wø pwøc jø Juuthi bëët mo wø bëëdö kaace.
english: And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt there,

anywaa: Ni ö eni ni cuŋŋe buuta, ni kööe jïra, ni ‹Cøøl, coka, nyeŋŋï døøge karge!› 'Ba yi caannøce kiree nyeŋŋa aput døø karge, ni neena eni.
english: Came unto me, and stood, and said unto me, Brother Saul, receive thy sight. And the same hour I looked up upon him.

anywaa: Ni kööe, ‹Jwø kwäyø ïïna jiere ki man ŋäyï mana manynye, ni neenï ŋata mare beer, ni wïnynyï dwøl mana öö ki dhee.
english: And he said, The God of our fathers hath chosen thee, that thou shouldest know his will, and see that Just One, and shouldest hear the voice of his mouth.

anywaa: Kiper ïïno tïmö ni ïïna lïŋi kipere jï jiy bëët, kiper gïna neeni na wïnynyï.
english: For thou shalt be his witness unto all men of what thou hast seen and heard.

anywaa: ?'Ba kawaane agïnaŋø ni koorï? Ö maal, niï lwøk na nyuudhi, niï penya raayï wøk, niï cwøla nyeŋŋe.›
english: And now why tarriest thou? arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on the name of the Lord.

anywaa: «'Ba køøre na nø duua yi Jerucalem, dïcäŋ aciel naa lämö Øt Jwøk Mana Dwøŋ, gïn mo keda lääk aö wïïa.
english: And it came to pass, that, when I was come again to Jerusalem, even while I prayed in the temple, I was in a trance;

anywaa: Ni neena Jecu ni kööe ki aani, ni ‹Ö maal ni laarï aa wøk ki yi Jerucalem, kiper ge ba maar jïëy ki marï na diï caanø kipera.›
english: And saw him saying unto me, Make haste, and get thee quickly out of Jerusalem: for they will not receive thy testimony concerning me.

anywaa: «'Ba aana köö, ni ‹Kwäärö, geni ki dëëtge ŋäcge ni ki yïth uut acook lam bëët aana wara töö ni pwöda jøøa näk ojïëy ni ŋääthge ïïni.
english: And I said, Lord, they know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue them that believed on thee:

anywaa: Ni këël kanya ö rem lïŋi marï ma Ectipen na kønynyi piny, a cuŋŋö kaace thuwø, ni aano jïëy ki mana tïïcge, naa koora abïïk jøøa 'näk gø.›
english: And when the blood of thy martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting unto his death, and kept the raiment of them that slew him.

anywaa: «'Ba ena köö ki aani, ni ‹Tïŋŋï, kiper ïïno jääŋŋa kany mo bäär baŋ juurre.› »
english: And he said unto me, Depart: for I will send thee far hence unto the Gentiles.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya poot Pøølli ni luum juurre poot käre caanø, lwaak ïthge ege ciiø jïgø. 'Ba kanyøgø döötge atïŋge maal, ni köge, ni «Aayï ki teeŋ ŋat ma enøgønø nee tïme ni tøør bäät piny! 'Nägï, kiper ba doo beer ki man kwøe!»
english: And they gave him audience unto this word, and then lifted up their voices, and said, Away with such a fellow from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya rëëtge, ni ge kiinynya abïïkge ni tør jøøpge maal,
english: And as they cried out, and cast off their clothes, and threw dust into the air,

anywaa: kwääy dïkuye acïpö ki dwøl, ni Pøøl kïth kar dïkuye, ni caan gø ni eni doo tetø ki pöödö, nee tier gïna rëët jøøgø na enøgønø kipere nee joot.
english: The chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bade that he should be examined by scourging; that he might know wherefore they cried so against him.

anywaa: 'Ba na nø twöcge gø ki kaae, Pøøl aköö jï kwääy jø tøŋ ma dïpa mo cuŋŋa buute, na «?Aŋø, beer jïrï ki man pwötï ŋat ma o thwønh Röm, ni luumme poot kär ŋøl piny?»
english: And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?

anywaa: 'Ba na ö kwääy jø tøŋ ma dïpa na wïny gïnögø, ena ci baŋ kwääy dïkuye mana dwøŋ ni kööe jïgø, na «?Agïnaŋø ni tïïyï en? Kiper nyenøgø ena o thwønh Röm.»
english: When the centurion heard that, he went and told the chief captain, saying, Take heed what thou doest: for this man is a Roman.

anywaa: Kanyøgø kwääya dwøŋ aöö ni kööe jïgø, ni «?Caanï jïra, ïïna o thwønh Röm møn?» Ni kööe, ni «Yaa.»
english: Then the chief captain came, and said unto him, Tell me, art thou a Roman? He said, Yea.

anywaa: Ni dwøgi ya kwääya dwøŋŋi, ni «Aani, thwønh paac manøgø ŋeea ka jammi mo thööth.» 'Ba Pøøl aköö, «'Ba aani, a nywöli ni aana o thwønh Röm.»
english: And the chief captain answered, With a great sum obtained I this freedom. And Paul said, But I was free born.

anywaa: Kanyøgønø, jøøa doo tet eni gena put keethø buute. Ni ö kwääya dwøŋŋi thuwø ni lwäye, kiper na joot gø ni Pøøl a o thwønh Röm, ni ee nø twöc.
english: Then straightway they departed from him which should have examined him: and the chief captain also was afraid, after he knew that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïme na aruunnø man, ni kwääy dïkuye manynya man ŋäc tier luubö na adïëri kiper gïna caan jø Juuthi dëër Pøøl, Pøøl apäde, ni cïpe ki dwøl jï kwääc laam ki kwääc løøe bëët nee rege cooŋge. Ni käl Pøøl baŋge ni cïp gø nyïmge.
english: On the morrow, because he would have known the certainty wherefore he was accused of the Jews, he loosed him from his bands, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to appear, and brought Paul down, and set him before them.

anywaa: 'Ba Pøøl nyeŋ kwääc løøe aneene ni ee kemø, ni kööe, ni «Nyïïmera, aana bëëdö nyïm Jwøk ki cwïny mo leer bäre këël dïcäŋi en.»
english: And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day.

anywaa: 'Ba Kwääy Lam Mana Dwøŋ ma Ananaya acïpö ki dwøl jï jøøa cuŋŋö buut gø, ni eni dhööŋ ki dhee.
english: And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.

anywaa: Kanyøgø Pøøl aköö jïre, ni «Ïïno dhööŋ Jwøki, ï na caal dëër øtø mo orwødhø ki booya mo tar. Ïïno pï piny kaagø, niï ŋøla luubö mara piny ki køør ciik Jwøk. ?Aŋø, ï doo köö naa dhööŋ, niï raanynya ciik Jwøk?»
english: Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall: for sittest thou to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?

anywaa: 'Ba jøøa cuŋŋö buute gena köö, na «?Aŋø, ï doo cäänö ki luubö mo raac jï Kwääy Lam Mana Dwøŋ mar Jwøk?»
english: And they that stood by said, Revilest thou God's high priest?

anywaa: 'Ba adwøk Pøølli, ni «Kuua cøøn, nyïïmera, ni ena Kwääy Lam Mana Dwøŋ. Kiper ogöörö, ni ‹Ï ba doo cäänö ki gïn mo raac dëër kwääy pou.› »
english: Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.

anywaa: 'Ba na jooti ya Pøølli ni jø møøk a jø Cajucith, ni jø møøk a jø Paricith, ena köök døc nyïm kwääc løøe ni kööe, ni «Nyïïmera, aana ŋat Paricith, ni aana wäät jø Paricith, ni beeye kiper ŋäädhe mar duun wøk ki yi thøø ni tïm løøki ni dagø bääta en.»
english: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.

anywaa: 'Ba na nø caan gïnögø, pïëm mo dwøŋ atägö yïthakic jø Paricith ki jø Cajucith. Ni ö acooŋa manøgø ni pääŋ ree.
english: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided.

anywaa: Kiper jø Cajucith wø köö, ni bäŋ duun wøk køør thøø, ni bäŋ nyïïatwiel maal, wala jwïëy. 'Ba jø Paricith gïïögø ege jïëö bëët.
english: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.

anywaa: Kanyøgø dïŋaŋ mo päl atägö yïthakicge. Ni ö dïpööye møøk mo ciik Jwøk dëët jø Paricith ni öge maal ni pïëmge, ni «Bäŋ gïn mo raac mo ewa joodø baŋ nyeni. ?Otïme nidïï ni näk mo eni cäänna jwïëy mør wala nyïïatwiel maal?»
english: And there arose a great cry: and the scribes that were of the Pharisees' part arose, and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man: but if a spirit or an angel hath spoken to him, let us not fight against God.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïm pïëmmi na dïŋaŋ mo dwøŋ døc, kwääy jø tøŋ alwäyö ni kanymør Pøøl cöötge cöötö na thäŋi, ni cïpe ki dwøl jï jø tøŋ nee cige ni kälge eni wøk ki teek dï lwaak ni dwøkge gø kar jø tøŋ.
english: And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of them, commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring him into the castle.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïme na wäär, Wuuö acuŋŋö buut Pøøl ni kööe, ni «Mak cwïnyï. Kiper gïra okøpï yi Röm thuwø, kaawat mana køpï gïra yi Jerucalem.»
english: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as thou hast testified of me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïme na amöölla, jø Juuth atudö ki luubö ni lamge røkge, ni ge ba cämö wala maath këël mano 'näkge Pøøl.
english: And when it was day, certain of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.

anywaa: 'Ba jøøa tuut luummögø jïtö ki pïëraŋween ki wïthge.
english: And they were more than forty which had made this conspiracy.

anywaa: Ni cige baŋ kwääc laam ki jaae, ni köge, ni «Dëëtwa alamwa døc ni cam ba maarwa bel, këël mano 'näkwa Pøøl.
english: And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, that we will eat nothing until we have slain Paul.

anywaa: Kiper manøgønø, uuni ki kwääc løøe bëët, cïpu ennø ki dwøl jï kwääy jø tøŋ, nee eni käl baŋu, keda u cäŋa luumme neennø døøc. 'Ba waani dëëtwa ewa nø jek ki man 'näkwa gø kanyo poode ni kär pïï buutu.»
english: Now therefore ye with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down unto you to morrow, as though ye would enquire something more perfectly concerning him: and we, or ever he come near, are ready to kill him.

anywaa: 'Ba møør-piny marge awïny o cöök Pøølli, ni cøøe ni døny kar dïkuye ni caan gø jï Pøøl.
english: And when Paul's sister's son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle, and told Paul.

anywaa: Ni ö Pøølli ni cwöte ki dhaanhø aciel dëët kwääc dïkuye ma dïpa, ni kööe, ni «Kïth nyilaari baŋ kwääy jø tøŋ mana dwøŋ, kiper da gïn mo caane caanø jïgø.»
english: Then Paul called one of the centurions unto him, and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain: for he hath a certain thing to tell him.

anywaa: Kanyøgø nyilaarøgø akäle ni kïth gø baŋ kwääy jø tøŋ mana dwøŋ, ni kööe, ni «Aana cwøl Pøølli manø no otwöö enø, ni kööm aani ni käla nyilaari baŋï, kiper da gïn mo caane caanø jïrï.»
english: So he took him, and brought him to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto him, and prayed me to bring this young man unto thee, who hath something to say unto thee.

anywaa: Kanyøgø cere amak kwääya dwøŋŋi ni pee gø kur keere, ni pëëny gø, na «?Agïnaŋø ni manynyï nee caanï jïra?»
english: Then the chief captain took him by the hand, and went with him aside privately, and asked him, What is that thou hast to tell me?

anywaa: Ni kööe, ni «Jø Juuth gena tudö ki luubö niï pëënyge ki man kïthï Pøøl baŋge diøø nyïm kwääc løøe, kee ge manynya man cäŋge gø pëënynyö døøc nee mare cäŋge wïnynyö.
english: And he said, The Jews have agreed to desire thee that thou wouldest bring down Paul to morrow into the council, as though they would enquire somewhat of him more perfectly.

anywaa: 'Ba kär niï jïëy ki luumge. Kiper da jiy røkge mo jïtö ki pïëraŋween ki wïthge, mo geno møør piny, ni ge koora Pøøl, ni rege ege lamø ni ge ba cämö wala maath këël mano 'näkge gø. 'Ba kawaane dëëtge ege jiiø, ni ge koora luummo caanï.»
english: But do not thou yield unto them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, which have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from thee.

anywaa: Kanyøgø nyilaal awëëk kwääy jø tøŋ wääth, ni kööm gø, ni «Kär dee ŋat mo caanï gø jïre ni gïnögø iï nø caan jïra.»
english: So the chief captain then let the young man depart, and charged him, See thou tell no man that thou hast shewed these things to me.

anywaa: Kanyøgø kwäärö mana dwøŋ mar jø tøŋ kwääc jø tøŋ ariiø acwøle, ni kööe, ni «Kanyo tïme na caae abïŋween ki wäär, wäru lwötu ki jø tøŋ ma dïpe ariiø, ki jø wø cääthi ki bäät okwëënyi ma pïërabïriiø, ki jiy ma dïpe ariiø mo käära tøøŋi, nee cige këël mano pïïcge Cecaria.
english: And he called unto him two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Caesarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night;

anywaa: Ni cïpu ko okwëënyi nee Pøøl cäädhe ki bäätge thuwø, ni kïthu gø baŋ kwäärö ma Pilik ni you gwøø døøc.»
english: And provide them beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring him safe unto Felix the governor.

anywaa: Ni ö eni ni gööt baŋ Pilik ki wëëlö na ennø nø,
english: And he wrote a letter after this manner:

anywaa: «Aana Kalødia Licia ni göön baŋï en, ï na kwäärö ma Pilik. «Ï na nyigwaak, a määtha ïïni.
english: Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix sendeth greeting.

anywaa: «Ŋati en amak jø Juuthi, ni dege gø nääö, 'ba bøth ka kany mo thiinh, 'ba aana ö baŋe ki dïkuye 'moa ni piemwa gø, kiper na jooda gø ni ena o thwønh Röm.
english: This man was taken of the Jews, and should have been killed of them: then came I with an army, and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya manynya man ŋääa tier luumma caange dëëre, ena kïtha nyïm kwääc løøe moge.
english: And when I would have known the cause wherefore they accused him, I brought him forth into their council:

anywaa: Ni jooda gø ni ge cäänö ka gø kaper luup mo ena ri ciik Jwøk marge. 'Ba luupa caange dëëre paa gïï mo doo rømø ki thøø wala tööc.
english: Whom I perceived to be accused of questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.

anywaa: 'Ba na wïnynya gø ni da luubö mo otuut jø Juuthi kipere nee eni 'näk, beeye ni puta gø jääŋ baŋï en, ni cïpa ki dwøl thuwø jï jøøa löö ki eni, nee gïna manyge nee caange dëëre caange nyïmï.»
english: And when it was told me how that the Jews laid wait for the man, I sent straightway to thee, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before thee what they had against him. Farewell.

anywaa: Kanyøgø jø tøŋ Pøøl akälge ni kïthge gø yi Antipatari ki wäär, kaawat mana caani jïge.
english: Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul, and brought him by night to Antipatris.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïme na aruunnø, gena duu kar dïkuye, ni wecge jø wø cääthi ki bäät okwëënyi nee aacge ki gø.
english: On the morrow they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle:

anywaa: 'Ba na pïïcge Cecaria ni cïpge wëëlö cer kwäärö ma Pilik, Pøøl akïthge nyïme thuwø.
english: Who, when they came to Caesarea, and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.

anywaa: 'Ba na nø kwaan wëëlö, Pøøl apëënynye, ni kööe, ni «?Ïïna dhaanh kwäänynye mane?» 'Ba na wïny gø ni eni käla Cilicia,
english: And when the governor had read the letter, he asked of what province he was. And when he understood that he was of Cilicia;

anywaa: ena köö, ni «Luummï owïnynya kanyo pïïc jøw olöö ki ïïni.» Ni cïpe ki dwøl, ni eni koor yi øt Eerat.
english: I will hear thee, said he, when thine accusers are also come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod's judgment hall.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïme na køør nïne abïïc, Kwääy Lam Mana Dwøŋ ma Ananaya apïï, ki jaae møøk, ki dïcääni aciel mo nyeŋŋe Tertula. Ni peethge luup løøk marge mana caange dëër Pøøl nyïm kwäärö ma Pilik.
english: And after five days Ananias the high priest descended with the elders, and with a certain orator named Tertullus, who informed the governor against Paul.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya cwøl Pøøl, Tertula atägö ki man lööe ki Pøøl, ni kööe, ni «Ï na Pilik, nyigwaak, beeye ki køørï na jïtwa ki bëët-mëër, ni beeye käädö marï na beer na jït paaci ki bëëtö mo beer.
english: And when he was called forth, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, Seeing that by thee we enjoy great quietness, and that very worthy deeds are done unto this nation by thy providence,

anywaa: 'Ba ki yïth luup bëët paac bäre ajïëy ki gø, ni yïthwa met døc.
english: We accept it always, and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness.

anywaa: 'Ba ï ba ööla ki man cööpa kany mo bäär, 'ba a kwaya ïïni ki met ec marï, nee ïthï cegï ki luumwa ki kany mo thiinh.
english: Notwithstanding, that I be not further tedious unto thee, I pray thee that thou wouldest hear us of thy clemency a few words.

anywaa: Kiper nyeni en, ajootwa ni ena dhaanhø mo raac, ni cøønna yïth jø Juuth yi piny bäre, ni ena bwödhi mar lwaa Nadharin ni wø lämö ki teeŋ lam mør.
english: For we have found this man a pestilent fellow, and a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes:

anywaa: Ni eni manynya man tïïc Øt Jwøk Mana Dwøŋ thuwø ni ba waany. ['Ba amakwa ni luumme dewa ŋøla piny ki køør ciik marwa.
english: Who also hath gone about to profane the temple: whom we took, and would have judged according to our law.

anywaa: 'Ba kwääy dïkuye ma Licia aöö ni käl gø wøk ceŋwa ki teek.
english: But the chief captain Lysias came upon us, and with great violence took him away out of our hands,

anywaa: Ni kööm jøøa löö ki eni, ni öge nyïmï.] 'Ba ennø, noo pëënynyï gø ki dëërï, tiet jammi bëët moa caanwa dëëre owïnynyï baŋe.»
english: Commanding his accusers to come unto thee: by examining of whom thyself mayest take knowledge of all these things, whereof we accuse him.

anywaa: Ni ö jø Juuthi møga thuwø ni dwalge dhøkge ni gïïögø bëët beege karge.
english: And the Jews also assented, saying that these things were so.

anywaa: Kanyøgø kwäärö Pøøl anyoodhe ki cere nee cääne. Ni ö Pøølli ni jute ni kööe, ni «Ï ŋääa niï bëëdö kany ki cwiiri mo thööth ni ïïna kwääy løøk paani. Kiper manøgønø, yia amïnnö ki man caana luumma nyïmï.
english: Then Paul, after that the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, answered, Forasmuch as I know that thou hast been of many years a judge unto this nation, I do the more cheerfully answer for myself:

anywaa: 'Ba ojootï, naa jïtö ki nïne apaar kurriiø keerge ki mana cøøa yi Jerucalem baŋ lam.
english: Because that thou mayest understand, that there are yet but twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem for to worship.

anywaa: Ni kärge a joodø naa pïëmö ki dhaanhø mør, wala yi lwaak mo yaa coonø yi Øt Jwøk Mana Dwøŋ, wala yïth uut acook lam, wala dï pääny.
english: And they neither found me in the temple disputing with any man, neither raising up the people, neither in the synagogues, nor in the city:

anywaa: Ni bäŋe nyuudhi mo maarge nyooth jïrï, kiper luupa kïthge bääta kawaane en.
english: Neither can they prove the things whereof they now accuse me.

anywaa: 'Ba mano jïëa jïrï beeye ni a wø lämö ki Jwøk mar kwäcwa ki Jöör Lam man wø cwølge ni teeŋ lam mør, ni aano jïëy ki jammi bëët moa näk ocaanø ri ciik Jwøk ki moa näk ogöörö yïth weet nyïïkuk Jwøk.
english: But this I confess unto thee, that after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets:

anywaa: Ni Jwøk yaa ŋäädhö ni da duun wøk køør thøø jï jøøa beyø ki jøøa reyø bëët, na näk ege jïëö thuwø.
english: And have hope toward God, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.

anywaa: Kiper manøgønø, raa yaa gwøø cooth ki man bëëda ni cwïnya tar nyïm Jwøk ki nyïm jiy.
english: And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.

anywaa: 'Ba na nø thöödha ki cwiiri mo boop, aana öö naa käla jap cane jï jø powa, naa cïpa ko olämme thuwø.
english: Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya tïïa gïnögø, aana jootge yi Øt Jwøk ni dëëra yaa døøc mo waany, ni bäŋ lwaak buuta wala dïlweel.
english: Whereupon certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with multitude, nor with tumult.

anywaa: 'Ba da jø Juuth møøk mo käla Eecia, mo ge doo ena kany thuwø nyïmï kiper luumma dege caanø dëëra, ni näk jïge da løøk ki aani.
english: Who ought to have been here before thee, and object, if they had ought against me.

anywaa: Wala jøøi ii ki dëëtge beerra man caange gïna raac na tïïa na jootge kanya cuŋŋa nyïm kwääc løøe.
english: Or else let these same here say, if they have found any evil doing in me, while I stood before the council,

anywaa: Kiper beeye gïrpiny aciel keere, mana kööa ki gø ni dwøra yaa tïŋ maal kanya cuŋŋa dïge, ni ‹Beeye gïr duun wøk køør thøø ni tïm løøki ni dagø bääta dïcäŋi en.› »
english: Except it be for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Touching the resurrection of the dead I am called in question by you this day.

anywaa: 'Ba Pilik kiper na ŋäc tier Jöör Lam manøgø ki mo thiinh, gena wëëk ciin wøk, ni kööe, ni «Kanyo ö Licia na näk kwääy dïkuye, luummu oneena.»
english: And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of that way, he deferred them, and said, When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will know the uttermost of your matter.

anywaa: Køøre ena cïpö ki dwøl jï kwääy jø tøŋ ma dïpa, nee Pøøl bëëde yi øt twöc, ni patha twöc mo raac, ni ba män nyïïawääte ki ciin baŋe kiper gïno manynye.
english: And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul, and to let him have liberty, and that he should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister or come unto him.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïme na køør nïne møøk Pilik aöö, ki cïïe ma Darucila ma nyijø Juuth. Ni jääk baŋ Pøøl ni wïny luumme na caane kiper tier ŋäädhe na en ri Krictø Jecu.
english: And after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, which was a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya ö Pøølli na piem gïr bëëtö mo beer, ki gïr män røk ki raay, ki kanya caan gø ni da kany mo luup jiy ŋøla piny yie mo poot ena nyïm, Pilik cwïnye abwøk ni kööe, ni «Ci wøk dïciel. Aano jïti ki kany cwøla ïïni yie.»
english: And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee.

anywaa: Ni ee ŋäädhö thuwø, ni kanymør eno mooc Pøølli ki jammi. Kiper manøgønø, ena tïmö ni jääga baŋe kwöre mo thööth ni wääge ki gø.
english: He hoped also that money should have been given him of Paul, that he might loose him: wherefore he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him.

anywaa: 'Ba na nø thum cwiiri ariiø, Pilik awiil Pörcia Pecta. 'Ba Pilik kiper na many man døøc yïth jø Juuth mo met, Pøøl awii øt twöc.
english: But after two years Porcius Festus came into Felix' room: and Felix, willing to shew the Jews a pleasure, left Paul bound.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya tïïc Pecta na kwäärö mar Cecaria, ena ci yie. 'Ba na pïïe paanøgø, køør nïne adäk ena tïŋŋö ni aa Jerucalem.
english: Now when Festus was come into the province, after three days he ascended from Caesarea to Jerusalem.

anywaa: Ni ö kwääc laammi ki jøøa døøŋŋø røk jø Juuth ni caange gïr Pøøl jï Pecta, ni kwaacge eni døøc,
english: Then the high priest and the chief of the Jews informed him against Paul, and besought him,

anywaa: nee Pøøl cwöl yi Jerucalem ki met ec mare, kiper gïre ege nø cooŋ ki cwïnyge ni ge møøra piny waŋjöö nee 'näkge.
english: And desired favour against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem, laying wait in the way to kill him.

anywaa: 'Ba aløk Pecta, ni «Pøøl ena Cecaria no otwöö, ni aani ki dëëra, a døøk kany mo cään.
english: But Festus answered, that Paul should be kept at Caesarea, and that he himself would depart shortly thither.

anywaa: Kiper manøgønø, beerra man ö jøøa näk ocuumö dïïu ni lööpge ki aani. 'Ba noo näk da gïn mo raac jïre, geno löö ki eni.»
english: Let them therefore, said he, which among you are able, go down with me, and accuse this man, if there be any wickedness in him.

anywaa: 'Ba na nø bëët Pecta ki geni ki nïne mo jïtö ki kar abära wala apaar, ena døø Cecaria. 'Ba na tïme na aruunnø man, ena ci kar løøk ni cïpe ki dwøl, nee Pøøl käl nyïme.
english: And when he had tarried among them more than ten days, he went down unto Caesarea; and the next day sitting on the judgment seat commanded Paul to be brought.

anywaa: 'Ba na ööe, jø Juuth moa öö ki yi Jerucalem acuŋŋö buute, ni ge kïtha bäät Pøøl ki luup mo reyø døc, mo kär maar lønyø jïge ki man nyoothge tietge.
english: And when he was come, the Jews which came down from Jerusalem stood round about, and laid many and grievous complaints against Paul, which they could not prove.

anywaa: 'Ba Pøøl mare aläw caan ni kööe, ni «Aani bäŋ gïn mo yaa baa bäre bäre dëër ciik Jwøk mar jø Juuth, wala dëër Øt Jwøk Mana Dwøŋ, wala dëër Cidhar.»
english: While he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, neither against the temple, nor yet against Caesar, have I offended any thing at all.

anywaa: 'Ba Pecta na many man døøc yïth jø Juuth mo met, aköö jï Pøøl, ni «?Ï manynya man ciï yi Jerucalem, nee luupi ii na caan dëërï nee caan nyïma kaace?»
english: But Festus, willing to do the Jews a pleasure, answered Paul, and said, Wilt thou go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me?

anywaa: 'Ba Pøøl aköö, ni «Aani, a cuŋŋa kar løøk mar Cidhar, kanya di mara caanø yie. Bäŋ gïn mo raac mo yaa tïïö dëët jø Juuth, ni manøgø ŋäyï ki dëërï.
english: Then said Paul, I stand at Caesar's judgment seat, where I ought to be judged: to the Jews have I done no wrong, as thou very well knowest.

anywaa: Kiper manøgønø, ni näk mo aana dhaanhø mo raac, ni da gïn mo raac mo yaa tïïö maa doo thøw kipere, a ba doo kweer ki thøø. 'Ba ni näk luupa kïth jø Juuthi bääta bäŋ tietge, doo bäŋ ŋat mo cïp aani ceŋge. Aani, mara ocaana nyïm Cidhar.»
english: For if I be an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Caesar.

anywaa: Kanyøgø Pecta na nø løøŋ tier gïnögø ki jaae moe, ena köö jï Pøøl, ni «Ïïna köö niï cøøa nyïm Cidhar. Beer nø, ïïno ci nyïm Cidhar.»
english: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Hast thou appealed unto Caesar? unto Caesar shalt thou go.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïme na køør nïne møøk, nyeya ma Agaripa ki Bernice gena pïï Cecaria kuna määthge Pecta.
english: And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Caesarea to salute Festus.

anywaa: 'Ba na bëëtge kaace ki nïne mo thööth, Pecta luum Pøøl apare jï nyeya, ni kööe, ni «Da dhaanhø kany mo owii Piliki øt twöc.
english: And when they had been there many days, Festus declared Paul's cause unto the king, saying, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix:

anywaa: 'Ba kanya cøøa yi Jerucalem, kwääc laam ki jaak jø Juuth, gïre aparge jïra, ni pëënyge aani ni ŋøla eni wøk.
english: About whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, desiring to have judgment against him.

anywaa: 'Ba adwøga jïge ni manøgø ba beer jï jø Röm ki man ŋøl dhaanhø wøk ni eni poot kär pï kanya ciel ki jøøa löö ki eni, nee jïte ki kar dhee kiper luummo caange dëëre.
english: To whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before that he which is accused have the accusers face to face, and have licence to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him.

anywaa: Kiper manøgønø, kanya öge kany ki aani, raa kära gaalø. Aana put ci kar løøk ka aruunnø man ni cïpa ki dwøl ni nyenøgø käli.
english: Therefore, when they were come hither, without any delay on the morrow I sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought forth.

anywaa: 'Ba na ö jøøa löö ki eni ni öge maal, bäŋ gïn mo raac mo ege caanø yi løøk mare, kaa mana näk yaa gø caarø ni dege caanø.
english: Against whom when the accusers stood up, they brought none accusation of such things as I supposed:

anywaa: 'Ba ge cara luup møøk mo ge pïëmö ki eni kiper lam marge, ki gïr nyen mør ma Jecu mo othøw, mo ocaan Pøølli na acäŋ kwøw.
english: But had certain questions against him of their own superstition, and of one Jesus, which was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.

anywaa: 'Ba na dhäth gïïögø jïra ki ŋøl, ena pëënynya ki man näk mo eni manynya man ci Jerucalem, nee luupögø cäŋge løøgø kunöce.
english: And because I doubted of such manner of questions, I asked him whether he would go to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these matters.

anywaa: 'Ba na kö Pøølli ni eni bëëde no otwöö ni koora luubö mano ŋøl nyeya mana dwøŋŋi piny, ni beeye Cidhar, aana cïpö ki dwøl ni eni bëëde no otwöö, gøøc kanyo jïta ki jöö mano kïtha gø nyïme.»
english: But when Paul had appealed to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Caesar.

anywaa: 'Ba Agaripa aköö jï Pecta, na «A doo manynya man wïnynya dwør nyenøgø ki dëëra.» Ni dwøk gø, ni «Beer, mare owïnynyï diøø.»
english: Then Agrippa said unto Festus, I would also hear the man myself. To morrow, said he, thou shalt hear him.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïme na aruunnø man, Agaripa ki Bernice, gena öö ni geno ruyö døøc. Ni dønyge øt wø kuut jøwi yie, ni ge cäädhi ka kwääc dïkuye ki jøøa kwörge døøŋŋø mo paac. Ni ö Pecta ni cïpe ki dwøl, ni put Pøøl käl nyïmge.
english: And on the morrow, when Agrippa was come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and was entered into the place of hearing, with the chief captains, and principal men of the city, at Festus' commandment Paul was brought forth.

anywaa: Ni kö Pecta, ni «Ï na nyeya ma Agaripa, ki uuni bëët ni en kany ki waani en, neennu nyena ö jø Juuthi bëët moa en Jerucalem ki moa en kany na kwaacge aani kipere, ni ge rëëdö ni eni ba doo beer ki man kwøe këët.
english: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men which are here present with us, ye see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews have dealt with me, both at Jerusalem, and also here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.

anywaa: 'Ba bäŋ gïn mo yaa joodø mo ee tïïö mo doo rømø ki thøø. 'Ba na kööe ni eni cøøa nyïm nyeya mana dwøŋ, aana jïëy ni eni jääŋŋa jääŋŋö.
english: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself hath appealed to Augustus, I have determined to send him.

anywaa: 'Ba aani, jïra bäŋ tier luubö mo beer mo gööra baŋ nyenynya kipere, ni beeye tiere ni käla gø nyïmmu en, ni beeye nyïmï røk, ï na nyeya ma Agaripa en, kiper noo nø pëënynyø gø, naa jïta ki gïn mo gööra.
english: Of whom I have no certain thing to write unto my lord. Wherefore I have brought him forth before you, and specially before thee, O king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I might have somewhat to write.

anywaa: Kiper nëëni kee paa gïn mo beer jïra ki man wëëga ŋat mo otwöö käl, ni bäŋ gïn mo onyooth tiet luupa caan dëëre.»
english: For it seemeth to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not withal to signify the crimes laid against him.

anywaa: Kanyøgø Agaripa aköö jï Pøøl, ni «Ïïna wec nø ki man caanï marï.» Køøre Pøøl cere atïŋ maal ni caan mare, ni kööe,
english: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself:

anywaa: na «Acaara ni yia met na tïme ni beeye ïïni, ï na nyeya ma Agaripa en, noo caana mara nyïmï dïcäŋi kiper luup bëët moa kïth jø Juuthi bääta.
english: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before thee touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews:

anywaa: Kiper ïïni kööŋŋe mo jø Juuth bëët ki pïëm marge ŋäyï døøc. Kiper manøgønø, a kwaya ïïni nee luumma wïnynyï mëëth.
english: Especially because I know thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.

anywaa: «Bëëtö mara kanya ööa ki thïnhö na bëëda dï jø powa, ki kanya bëëda yi Jerucalem, ŋäc jø Juuthi bëët.
english: My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among mine own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews;

anywaa: Ni ŋäcge ki kany mo bäär, ni dege caanø onää ge caya gø, ni bëëtö mara ena køør jøøa en ri jöör lam marwa mana teek døc, ni aano bëëdö ni aana ŋat Paricith.
english: Which knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.

anywaa: 'Ba kawaane a cuŋŋö kar løøk kany en kiper mana ŋäädha luumma kwøŋ Jwøki buuk jï kwäcwa.
english: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers:

anywaa: Ni beeye luum wø ŋääth dhøk uudi mowa na apaar kurriiø nee ci jïge, kany wø tïnyge Jwøk døøc ki wärre ki cääŋŋe. Ni beeye kiper luum ŋäädhe manøgø ni ö jø Juuthi ni lööge ki aani, ï na nyeya.
english: Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come. For which hope's sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews.

anywaa: ?Aŋø ni tïme keda gïn mo ba maaru jïëc en, ki man ŋääth Jwøk ni jiy wø tïŋe maal ki yi thøø?
english: Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?

anywaa: «Këël aani ki dëëra acaara ni doo beer jïra ki man tïïa ki gïï mo thööth naa raanynya nyeŋ Jecu nyï Nadhareth.
english: I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

anywaa: Ni tïïa gø møn yi Jerucalem. Ni kïtha jø Krictø mo thööth øt twöc ki teek mana wëëk kwääc laammi aani. 'Ba na wara nääŋ geni, aano jïëy thuwø ni cïba dwøra.
english: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.

anywaa: Ni ge wø pööta pöötö cooth yïth uut acook lam bëët, naa manynya man wëëga geni jany nyeŋŋøgø. Ni gëëma ki geni këël mana pïïa tiet mïëc juurre, naa män ki geni døc.
english: And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.

anywaa: «Ni beeye na aa naa cøøa Damacka ki teek mana wëëk kwääc laammi aani.
english: Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,

anywaa: 'Ba na tïme na dhöör cäŋ, ï na nyeya, kanya ena waŋjöö, da tar ma araŋa mo ööi ki maal, ni tar døc ni kaala tac cäŋ, ni put rieny bääta ki jøøa cäädhö ki aani.
english: At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.

anywaa: Ni putwa pädhö bëët, ni wïnynya dwøl ni cäänö ka aani ki dhi Ibaru, ni ‹?Cøøl, Cøøl, aŋø ni gëëmï ki aani en? Beeye gïn mo leth kiperï ki man cäpï gïï mo cööba ïïni.›
english: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.

anywaa: «Ni kööa, ni ‹?Ïïna ŋa, Kwäärö?› «Ni ö Kwäärö ni løk gø, ni ‹Aana Jecu ni gëëmï ki gø en.
english: And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.

anywaa: Ö maal ni cuŋŋï ki tietï. Kiper dëëra anyoodha jïrï kiper niï jiera naa tïnynyï, nee gïïa nø jootï aani dëëtge, ki moo nyoodha raa jïrï yïthge nee gïrge køpï.
english: But rise, and stand upon thy feet: for I have appeared unto thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness both of these things which thou hast seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto thee;

anywaa: 'Ba ïïno gwøa ceŋ jø Juuth ki ceŋ juurre, jøw ojääŋŋa ïïni baŋge en,
english: Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee,

anywaa: kiper nee nyeŋge japï, nee muudhö wecge ni løøge rege baŋ tar, ni wecge teek Ceethan ni løøge rege baŋ Jwøk, kiper nee raay moge wec Jwøki, ni jïtge ki karge dï jøøa näk ocïp kur keerge na mo Jwøk, ki køør ŋäädhe man wø ŋääthge aani.›
english: To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.

anywaa: «Kiper manøgønø, ï na nyeya ma Agaripa, wïïa kär teek ki mana neena na öö ki maal.
english: Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:

anywaa: 'Ba akwøŋa køp jï jøøa en Damacka, køøre akøba yi Jerucalem ki yïth mïëri bëët mo Judia, ki jï juurre thuwø, nee wïthge cäŋge caarrø ni løøge rege baŋ Jwøk, ni tïïcge gïï mo orømø ki løk cwïny marge.
english: But shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judaea, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.

anywaa: Beeye gïnögø nø, na ö jø Juuthi ni makge aani yi Øt Jwøk Mana Dwøŋ, ni ge manynya man 'näkge aani.
english: For these causes the Jews caught me in the temple, and went about to kill me.

anywaa: 'Ba a wø køny Jwøki kønyø këël dïcäŋi en. Ni beeye ni cuŋŋa kany en, naa cäänna jøøa kwörge therø ki jøøa kwörge døøŋŋø, naa para luupa car nyïïkuk Jwøki ki moa car Modhe ni doo tägö, ni bäŋ gïn mør mo kïtha bäätge,
english: Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come:

anywaa: ni beeye ni Krictø gïï mo leth jwøre jwørø, 'ba kiper mano tïme ni bee eni noo kwøŋ duu wøk ki yi thøø, eni luum tar købe købø jï jø poge ki juurre bëët.»
english: That Christ should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should shew light unto the people, and to the Gentiles.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya poot Pøølli ni caana luumme na enønø, Pecta dwøre atïŋ maal døc ni kööe, ni «Pøøl, ïïna bøøl, luupa thööth na kwanyï ïïna døøcge bøøl.»
english: And as he thus spake for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad.

anywaa: 'Ba Pøøl aköö, ni «Mara paa bøølø, ï na Pecta, nyigwaak. 'Ba a cara gïï ma adïëri.
english: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness.

anywaa: Kiper nyeya gïïögø ŋääe, ni beeye ni lämma gø døøc en. Kiper ŋääa døøc ni gïïögø bëët bäŋgø mo obøth jïre mo käre kwøŋ wïnynyö, kiper gïnögø kär tïïö gøøt.
english: For the king knoweth of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner.

anywaa: ?Ï na nyeya ma Agaripa, aŋø, ï patha ojïëy ki luup nyïïkuk Jwøk? Ŋääa ni ïïno jïëy.»
english: King Agrippa, believest thou the prophets? I know that thou believest.

anywaa: 'Ba Agaripa aköö jï Pøøl, na «?Aŋø, iï caarø naa diï døøc dhaanh Krictø ki nyi kany mo thiinh en nø?»
english: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.

anywaa: 'Ba Pøøl aköö, ni «Nee kany mo thiinh wala kany mo bäär, ki nyeŋ Jwøk yia doo met ni paa ïïni keerï, 'ba këël jøøi bëët thuwø ni wïny dwøra dïcäŋi en, mana dege tïmö kaamara, ba tiirra oguuti ii.»
english: And Paul said, I would to God, that not only thou, but also all that hear me this day, were both almost, and altogether such as I am, except these bonds.

anywaa: 'Ba kanyøgø nyeya aö maal, ki kwäärö, ki Bernice, ki jøøa näk opï piny ki geni.
english: And when he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them:

anywaa: 'Ba na nø aage wøk, gena cäänö keerge, ni «Nyenøgø bäŋ gïn mo ee tïïö mo doo rømø ki thøø, wala tööc.»
english: And when they were gone aside, they talked between themselves, saying, This man doeth nothing worthy of death or of bonds.

anywaa: 'Ba Agaripa aköö jï Pecta, ni «Nyenøgø doo pädö, onää eni kär nø köö ni eni cøøa nyïm Cidhar.»
english: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Caesar.

anywaa: 'Ba køøre na nø caani ni wa kïth yi Itali ki jääy mo dwøŋ mar naam, Pøøl ki jø tööc møøk acïpge cer kwääy lwaa dïkuye mar nyeny Röm ma Agacta mo nyeŋŋe Julia.
english: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus' band.

anywaa: Ni ciwa yi jää paana cwøl na Adarmitiem na many man tïŋŋe ni cøøa yïth mïëc Eecia, ni aacwa ki gø, ni ö Aritarka ma nyï Macedönia mo käla Thecalönika, ni lööbe ki waani.
english: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïme na aruunnø man, waana mäk piny Caydan. 'Ba Julia, Pøøl atïïe na wøp, ni wëëk gø ciin baŋ nyïïawääte kiper gïno manynye.
english: And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïŋwa kaace, waana ci buut acuul Caypara, kiper jamø atïmö ni kwönna baŋwa.
english: And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.

anywaa: 'Ba na nø ŋutwa løø Cilicia ki Pampilia, waana pïï Mayra na en Licia.
english: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.

anywaa: Kaace kwääy jø tøŋ ajïtö ki jää Alekdhandaria mo aa Itali, ni kïth waani yie.
english: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.

anywaa: Ni cääthwa mëëth ki nïne mo thööth, këël mana pïïcwa buut Nida ki wääth mo raac. 'Ba na ö jame na män waani ki wääth, waana ci buut Kariit nyïm Calmöne.
english: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone;

anywaa: 'Ba na nø cääthwa ki wääth mo raac, waana pïï kany mo cwøl ni Peer Eeben na näk kare cään ki paana cwøl ni Laceea.
english: And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called The fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.

anywaa: 'Ba na nø gaal wääthi marwa ki nïne mo thööth, ni tïm pinynyi na arïïa ni paa kany mo beer kiper wääth naam, kiper nïr lam-wödö onø pöödhö, Pøøl acäänö ki geni,
english: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them,

anywaa: ni kööe, ni «Jaay, ajooda ni wääthi en kännö ki ŋwiili ki ränynyö mo dwøŋ døc, ni paa jammi mo en yi jääy ki dëër jääy keerge noo ränynyi, 'ba këël jwïëyø thuwø.»
english: And said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives.

anywaa: 'Ba kwääy jø tøŋ leŋa luup mo wø caan kwääy jääyi ki wää jääy, ni käre ïthe ciiø ki luup moa caan Pøølli.
english: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.

anywaa: 'Ba kiper mana tïme ni dhi wääth manøgø paa kany mo beer ki man ruu jääyi yie ka arïïa, jiy mo thööth aköö, ni jääy laar aay kaace, ni ege caarø ni kanymør ge pïï Pinik, na näk dhi waath Kariit na näk raŋŋa rege ki jï løø kur pänh-cäŋ bäät cwiic ki bäät caam, nee put bëëte kaace ka arïïa.
english: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the south west and north west.

anywaa: 'Ba na ö jam wø rïïw piny ni kwönne mëëth, acaarge ni kanya koorge athur kare, ni gøønyge jääy, ni cääthge ki deŋ ageel Kariit.
english: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence, they sailed close by Crete.

anywaa: 'Ba ki nyi kany mo thiinh jam aŋalakiir mo raac døc aput kwönnö ki wøk ki jï løø wï-piny kur tuul-cäŋ.
english: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïm jääyi ni käär jame käärö ni ba løny ki man kem jamø, awëëkwa køøl, ni puti ya jame käärö.
english: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive.

anywaa: 'Ba na nyiikwa buut acuula mo thiinh mo cwøl ni Køda, jääna thiinh adwøkwa yi jääy ni twöwa gø piny ki tïïc mo leth.
english: And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat:

anywaa: 'Ba na nø tïŋge gø maal, dëër jääna dwøŋ ameenge ki thøør nywïënyö. 'Ba køøre na lwäcge ni jääy køøla ya akwöny Cirti, abïï jamø aduuge piny, ni wëëkge jääy køøl.
english: Which when they had taken up, they used helps, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïme ni wa leeŋ athage leeŋŋø, na tïme na aruunnø man gena tägö ki man leeŋge jammi yi naam moa käär jääyi.
english: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship;

anywaa: 'Ba na tïme na dää nïne, thøør jääy kiree aleeŋge yi naam ki ceŋge keerge.
english: And the third day we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïme ni cäŋ ki ceer ba nëëni ki nïne mo thööth, na atuunna mo ba thiinh ena bäätwa, ŋäädhe marwa ki man näk mo wa kwøw këët arwäänyö jïwa na bäre.
english: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya nø bëëtge ki nïne mo thööth ni ge ba cämö, Pøøl aci dïge, ni kööe, ni «Onää luumma you leŋø, ni ba tïŋŋu ki Kariit, u ba doo jïtö ki ŋwiili ki ränynyö man en.
english: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.

anywaa: 'Ba kawaane a kwaya uuni ki man magu cwïnynyu. Kiper bäŋ ŋat mo thøw dïïu, 'ba beeye dëër jääy keere noo ränynyi.
english: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man's life among you, but of the ship.

anywaa: Kiper yawïtïn kiree, nyïïatwiel maal mør mar Jwøk, ni näga dhaanhnhe en ni wø wøøra, acuŋŋö buuta.
english: For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve,

anywaa: Ni kööe, ni ‹Kärï lwäyö, Pøøl. Ïïni, ï cuŋŋö nyïm Cidhar. Ni Jwøk thuwø yie met ki ïïni ki man gwøk jøøi bëët ni en yi jääy ki ïïni na aciel en.›
english: Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Caesar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.

anywaa: Kiper manøgø nø, jaay, magu cwïnynyu. Kiper Jwøk yaa ŋäädhö ni gïnögø thura kare na adïëri, kaawat mana caani jïra.
english: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.

anywaa: 'Ba ø kwøŋ ka leeŋ ya acuula.»
english: Howbeit we must be cast upon a certain island.

anywaa: 'Ba wääna tïm nïne na apaar kurŋween ni jääy marwa okøøl jamø løø naam Eedaria, kanya tïm pinynyi ni dï wäär, dïkïïwe acaarge ni karge ocäännö ka ageela.
english: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country;

anywaa: Kanyøgø naam arømge ni jootge gø na rumme ma pïërariiø. 'Ba na nyiikge nyïm mëëth gena cäŋ rummö, ni jïtge ki rumme ma apaar kurbïïc.
english: And sounded, and found it twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found it fifteen fathoms.

anywaa: 'Ba kiper mana lwäcge ni kanymør wa cøøa bäät kïte, alïŋe aŋween mo jääy aleeŋge piny thar jääy, ni kwacge Jwøk nee øw laar ruuö.
english: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.

anywaa: 'Ba dïkïïwe atïmö ni ge manynya man kwalge dëëtge yi jääy ni jääy mana thiinh ege nø kïth naam, ni ge tïïya riek waŋ kede ge leeŋa alïŋe mo wï jääy piny.
english: And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under colour as though they would have cast anchors out of the foreship,

anywaa: 'Ba Pøøl aköö jï kwääy jø tøŋ ki jø tøŋ, ni «Ni näk jøøgø ba bëëdö yi jääy, u ki dëëtu, u ba maar piem.»
english: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.

anywaa: Kanyøgø jø tøŋ thøøth jääna thiinh aputge ŋøørø ni wëëkge gø tharø.
english: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.

anywaa: 'Ba na tïm kar øwi ni cään, gena kwaac Pøølli bëët nee ge cämge, ni kööe, ni «Dïcäŋi jïïu da nïne apaar kurŋween nou bëëdö nou lwäär nou ba cämö, ni bäŋ gïn mo maaru kïth dhøgu.
english: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought them all to take meat, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that ye have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing.

anywaa: Kiper manøgø nø, a kwaya uuni nou cämu, nee dëëtu tëënge, kiper bäŋ jëën wï dhaanhø aciel dïïu mo rwäänyi.»
english: Wherefore I pray you to take some meat: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.

anywaa: 'Ba na nø caan gïnögø, ena lwötö ki møø. 'Ba na nø dwøk met ec jï Jwøk nyïmge bëët, møø apøte ni put tägö ki cam.
english: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all: and when he had broken it, he began to eat.

anywaa: Kanyøgø gena jïtö ki cøm cwïny bëët, ni cämge thuwø.
english: Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took some meat.

anywaa: 'Ba wa na en yi jääy bëët, waana dïpe ariiø ki pïërabïriiø ka abïciel.
english: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.

anywaa: 'Ba na nø cämge ni jäŋge, beel awetge yi naam, ni ge døøya jääy mo jööt.
english: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya ruu øwi, kaace kärge ŋiiø, 'ba gena jïtö ki cwøny mo opäär ka akwöö, ni caarge gø ni ni näk mo løny, jääy dege kïtha yie.
english: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.

anywaa: Kanyøgø alïŋe apätge ni wiige ge yi naam, ni jø møøk päta thøøtha en dëët ogeelle. Køøre na nø tïŋge abïï jamø maal kiper jamø, gena cääth baŋ ageela.
english: And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed themselves unto the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoisted up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore.

anywaa: 'Ba kanya ö jääyi ni gööc kany mo cwøk, anigëëk, ni magi ya pinynyi. Ni ö wïïe ni këët piny ni tïme ni ree ba maar tuk. 'Ba jïp jääy atoor athage.
english: And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.

anywaa: Kanyøgø jø tøŋ aköö ni jøøa näk otwöö 'näk, nee bäŋe dhaanhø mo kwaŋ wøk ni kwala ree.
english: And the soldiers' counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.

anywaa: 'Ba kwääy jø tøŋ ma dïpa, kiper mana näk mo eni manynya man gwøk Pøøl, gena mäne ki mana dege tïïö. Ni cïpe ki dwøl jï jøøa ŋäc kwaaŋ ni kwøŋge rege leeŋ yi naam, nee cige wøk,
english: But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast themselves first into the sea, and get to land:

anywaa: ni ci jø møga wøk ki bäät opämi wala ki bäät thäk jääy moa no otøyø. Ni pïïcge bäät ageela ni bäŋ gïn mo otägö dëëtge.
